review_text:
Get in line now. Excellent bagels and surprisingly even better cookies.

The bagels are on the small side ($2 each) a la a Black Seed and the cookies are on the incredible, super soft and chewy side. Even the Oatmeal Raisin is excellent ($2).

Unfortunately they already were out of he Everything and Everything 2.0, but the Pumpernickel Everything with Salmon and Cream Cheese was perfect ($12).

Also, the Chocolate Babka was incredible ($15). Very different from the current champion Breads Bakery, as this one is coated in chocolate and is a bit fluffier and softer. Definite contender.

I'll be back soon for the rest of the bagels and the full menu once the seating area is open.

The Torrisi Brothers are genus, expanding their Italian American comfort into Jewish American classics. Bagels are hot! At the soft opening hot bagels are greeted with hot bagel shout outs by the staff- love it! This is an elegant spot like Kutschers Tribecca was and the bagels are small, crunchy and outstanding! Lox is smoked in house natch- and is delicately flavored.

The baked goods in general looks amaze. Particularly outstanding was the chocolate chip loaf. Perfection! On to my tuna sandy. Did I mention bagels are $2 each-  perfection has a price. The onion bagel elevates this sandwich classic. The tuna itself was pedestrian, but the small crisp bagel took it to a whole other level. Just in time for the Jewish holidays.
 1001 review!

It's the second day of business and it already takes an hour minimum from the time you get on line (which will be out the door at 8:30am) to getting your bagel. And it's totally worth it. 

This was actually without a doubt the best bagel I've ever had. They're smaller than the usual bagels but I'm grateful for that because it was just the right amount of food when loaded up with lox and all the other fixings. The lox is amazing. The rugelach is amazing. Everything is amazing. 

The space is huge and super nice. Only negative is they've got some dripping air conditioning vents that you have to watch out for when you're waiting in line, but I'm sure they'll sort that out soon. The staff is incredibly professional and personable; they threw in not 1, not 2, but 3 extra rugelach for me to try. A++

Go for the gold: toasted everything bagel loaded up with lox, cream cheese, onions, and tomatoes. It'll be $12 entirely well spent.

** UPDATE
The manager reached out to me apologizing and offered me to come by to skip the line for the bagel done right.

****
For the amount of time I waited for the bagel and money I spent I expected my order to be right.  

Excited by the hype I went this afternoon to grab a bagel. There was line about 15 people long. After waiting roughly 30 minutes to order (yes that's about 2 minutes per person JUST to order) I was pleasantly surprised that my $15 bagel was ready quickly after I placed the order. I got back to my office to discover that my bagel was missing the lox (the main ingredient). So I paid $15 for a bagel that was missing the star ingredient.  I'm furious that I waited and did not receive the right order. I am still waiting for the management to get back to me.

"Hot bagels!"

Every time one of the staff walks up to the counter with a new batch of bagels,  the whole team will shout back to them that catchphrase. And what great bagels they are!

My boyfriend Mike and I heard about the soft opening and decided to try our luck their second day. We arrived close to 9:00am and there was already a line out the door. It seemed short enough, but we ended up waiting about 20 minutes just to order.

Our bounty: An Everything 2.0 bagel with chive cream cheese and house lox, a Salt and Pepper bagel with chive cream cheese and house lox, 3 bagels to go (Everything Pumpernickel, Cinnamon Raisin, Onion), a 1/4 pound of sable, a chocolate babka, a chocolate chip cookie, a chocolate chip loaf slice, a cheese danish and a sticky bun - they ended up throwing in 2 bear claws for us too since we bought so much stuff. 

As other Yelpers have mentioned, they were having pretty severe hiccups which impacted their service. We were told to wait for our pastries on one side of the store and for our bagels on the other side and received an order number to wait for them to call out for. Mike and I split up - him taking the bagel side and I the pastry side. A woman, without calling our number, walked up to another couple and tried to give them a pastry package. The other couple was confused and I went up to the woman asking what it was - she said a chocolate babka. I told her that was ours and all was fine, but I checked the package just in case and it was NOT the chocolate babka, but the other pastries we ordered. She didn't even know what she was handing out.

Cut to 20 minutes later, Mike looks at me across the room and mouths to me if we got all our pastries yet. We were still waiting on the chocolate babka. I went up to the counter and politely asked when the chocolate babka would be ready and the same woman said, "Oh, it's been sitting right here." What? Wasn't that supposed to be brought to me? Has it been hanging out there for 20 minutes? There was so much confusion amongst the staff, they didn't even know who to hand things out to or what was being given out. Complete chaos.

Mike finally got our bagels and we left for the park to eat them, only to sit down and see that our bagel package was missing our 3 bagels to go. We went back and the guy on the bagel side he said that any bagels just to go were to be given out on the pastry side, and they were never given to us...We were baffled to say the least.

Once we sat down to try everything, we were SUPER impressed. The bagels themselves are very unique - they have a crunchy exterior and soft interior. I suspected they did not give me the Everything 2.0 bagel because mine did not have caraway or fennel seeds on it, but it was still delicious. The Salt and Pepper bagel was probably my favorite of the bunch - containing bits of black pepper in the dough itself with large crystals of salt on the outside. The house lox is almost creamy, very soft, fresh and flavorful - possibly one of the best cures I've had on salmon. We had the 3 bagels a day later and they held up all right. The Everything Pumpernickel is VERY deep in flavor and I would recommend it to someone who likes Pumpernickel a lot since it is so pronounced. The Onion bagel was lovely, also with several types of onion in the dough throughout. Mike ate the Cinnamon Raisin and told me it was all right. The sable was incredible - it melt in your mouth and was very flavorful.

We purchased the chocolate babka for a dinner party we were having with friends that evening and it was a HIT! People were saying it was the best babka they have ever had. While it was my first time ever having babka, I would definitely purchase it again. This sweet bread pulls apart beautifully and has lovely swirls of chocolate in it - not too bitter, sweet or overpowering. Just perfect. The chocolate ganache spread on top is the pièce de résistance. If you only get one pastry from Sadelle's - GET THIS.

The rest of the items ranged from good to great. I highly recommend the chocolate chip cookie - it was chewy with a soft center and the crust was almost caramel-tasting. I wish I had purchased more of them. I enjoyed the chocolate chip loaf, but Mike was not as big a fan. He liked it more as he ate it, but he felt that the chocolate was too bitter and was best eaten with a glass of milk. The cheese danish was good - almost cheesecake-like. I felt that the Sticky Bun was a little too sweet (my teeth hurt just biting into it), but it also had a very nice caramel taste to it - Mike thought it was fantastic. The only item we were both underwhelmed by were the free bear claws - they were simply okay. 

All in all - we will return once their service improves. We felt that these problems all stemmed from the fact they just opened and are trying to get themselves organized. Mike and I are looking forward to trying their sit down restaurant soon!

Somehow zero line on 'openign day' amidst huge hype and a site listing all prices by the dozen. Solid sesame bagel (untopped), and some tasty cookies, but overpriced beyond belief.

http://gothamist.com/2015/09/15/sadelles_deli_sandwich.php#photo-4

First off, Sadelle's is eventually going to be a hit and a surefire 5-star place. My friend and I went this morning at 8:15am and of course expected a pretty empty place. We were some of the first people to get a table but as soon as we did a crowd came in. Our server was very friendly and accommodating, but seemed a little bit overwhelmed. I'm sure it's just the first couple days and they'll work out the kinks with that. Anyway, we weren't incredibly adventurous so we decided to just try the bagels because we had heard such good things. My friend ordered an Everything 2.0 (everything bagel with fennel and something else I don't remember) with Chive Cream Cheese, Sable and tomatoes. Sadelle's hasn't quite figured out pricing yet so they didn't technically have this as an option...usually bagels with Sable are $25 there but they come with a huge spread, and he just wanted a single bagel. So they did that for him, which was very nice. I ordered a simple Sesame Bagel with Plain Cream Cheese. 

Our orders came, and they do not construct the bagels for you. They gave us the bagels on a stick, and also all the spreads and toppings separately. It's great that you can personalize your own, but I wish they would have given us an option for them to do it. It just feels a little safe for them to not want to risk getting your bagel wrong, but nevermind that--these bagels were amazing. Like in conversation for best in the city amazing. They're much different than your H&H or other popular NY bagels. Super soft and melt in your mouth. Really tasty. We ordered another round. 

All in all, really great place with a lot of potential. Once they get off the ground and don't have the problems of a new place, they'll be just as special as Carbone and the rest of the Major restaurants.

Went downtown this morning especially to pick up some bagels after reading all the hype about this spot this week - was told at the door that they were out of all bagels and wouldn't have any more for an hour.  This was at 10:20 AM on a Sunday morning.  I'm still looking forward to trying this place, and will update this review when I do, but - no bagels at a bagel place on a Sunday morning is a little weird and a little disappointing.

"Hot bagels!"....more like "NO bagels."  I went there this weekend and wanted the Everything 2.0 and smoked salmon -- but they had no bagels!  I wasn't about to eat the salmon on some sourdough bread, so...instead I ended up ordering poorly poached eggs, generic potatoes and sourdough bread (it was supposed to come with a bagel...) for about $20.  (Sidenote: How can a restaurant known for its bagels not have any bagels??!) Way over priced! Despite all these mishaps, the experience wasn't a total loss because my server Richard was great! So funny and helpful. But overall, I was very disappointed at Sadelle's and probably won't go again anytime soon.

I came last Friday around 2pm on the hunt for Chocolate Babka. I'd seen the photos popping up on food blogs so I had to have some. My plan was to share with my coworkers in order to keep my inner fatass in check. When I arrived there wasn't much of a line and the bakery items had been depleted. They only had a few cookies and cakes left. The girl behind the counter told me they sold out of babka at 10am. I guess that teaches me to never go on the Friday before a Jewish holiday. Anyway, they still had some chocolate pecan cookies left so I took 10 back to my team. The girl was sweet in only charging me for 6 since I didn't get any babka. Major points on that. 

The cookies did not last long around my team. They were seriously some of the best cookies I've ever had and they all agreed. The cookies were soft, had the consistency of a brownie, and I swear I tasted a hint of caramel. I'm planning to go back for the babka and this time I'm getting there early! I also can't wait to try brunch.

Luckily, I didn't experience the long wait like most some Yelpers have. I arrived at 7:30AM expecting a line for what I thought was their 8AM opening time, but it was open and I walked right in!
The menu is short sweet and to the point. I ordered an everything pumpernickel with lox, tomato, onions, and capers.
A few minutes later, my order came out in a cute to-go bag.
The bagel itself was good, but small. A tad overpriced at $13+ but I'll chalk that up to NYC pricing as well as the smoked salmon.
I could definitely recreate this at home, but still a nice treat every once in awhile.

Wow. Such a cool joint with great natural light! Fun atmosphere and awesome-looking smoked fish. Everybody seemed to be having a good time which created a great vibe. I was by myself so just had the bagel with smoked sturgeon platter - it was delicious. Can't wait to go back and try the sable and enticing entrees. Will be a huge hit. I can eat like this twice a week!

Bagels & lox by way of "Portlandia."  An overly precious, preening perversion of traditional Jewish appetizing, served on three-tiered trays a la English high tea service.  Ludicrous prices: $12 and up for a smoked fish sandwich, $2 for just a bagel to go.  Even more expensive than Black Seed, and certainly not any better.  

I don't know what's more pathetic: this self-parody of foodie scene-mongering, or the long line of Instagramming sheep waiting on line to get in on a Saturday afternoon.  

Hats off to Torrisi & Carbone's publicists, but I think you guys have jumped the shark this time.  By next Spring, when actual Jews have to clean their houses of bagels and other bread products, this place will be toast.

P.s. If you really want high end fancy bagels and smoked fish, go across town to Russ & Daughters where they actually know about this stuff. Otherwise stick to Barney Greengrass uptown.

P.p.s. The good folks at Major Food Group tried to have this review taken down. When that didn't work, they posted a handful of obviously fake, totally generic 5-star reviews. More proof that these guys are more interested in their social media image than the actual food. News flash: if the food is good, the social media will follow. Not the other way around. The food has a ways to go.

Wow.  I felt that writing this review as soon as I tried the plethora of goods that I purchased at Sadelle's this morning was exigent.  After each bite, I kept saying out loud, "This is so disappointing.  Did they run out of sugar or something?"  Is it possible that a babka enveloped in a lair of chocolate could be this tasteless?  

I arrived at Sadelle's around 8:30 and the line was slightly out the door.  I was probably 10 people from the front.  I did not get to the front until 9:15.  The funny thing about the line was that it grew to a point, and although it was not moving, enough people exited the line from frustration such that it maintained a fairly consistent length.  Once we made it to the front, our hunger bested us so we ordered one of everything.  We spent over $50 just on baked goods.  

We sampled every baked good, but to illustrate the experience, I only need to discuss the cheese danish. It looks appetizing in appearance albeit a bit small.  Yet, upon biting into it, it simply lacks any notable rich cheese flavor one would expect, in fact, it was tasteless.  Honestly, I found myself sentimentally yearning for the Entenmann's cheese danish of my youth.  While beautiful, the devoid flavor profile was reminiscent of a movie a prop (or a poor actor).  Unfortunately, this was quintessential of each baked good at Sadelle's, save for the sticky bun. That coupled with above average bagels saves this from being a 1 (or 0) star review. 

I've been to every Torrisi/Carbone group establishment, and this was definitely the biggest let down.  Often they push the envelope or do something new with each establishment, but this just seems like complacency and poorly executed "high end" homage to the classic NY appetizing store.  Frankly, it seems like they are just riding on the coattails of their more worthwhile restaurants.  

I just want a Breads Bakery babka right now.

Over all this restaurant was ok and that coupled with a few major annoyances left my girlfriend and I with the consensus that it's not worth the time and we wouldn't go back.

We arrived after reading the glowing reviews of hot bagels and had a line of about 10 people to the takeout counter, at any other place in nyc this would take 15 mins tops, not here!

Due to either horrible management or managements attempt to maintain a line outside, they only have 1 register open and take about 5 to 7 mins for each person. The cashier slowing gets the order, inputs it - walks over to tell the other employee what to make and then you pay. It took about an hour to get through the 10 person line.

Based on an hour wait for a 3 dollar bagel - 12 for house lox and 6 for an iced coffee, we had high expectations. The bagel is small, cold and about average at best. Nothing stood out here and I would say there are lot better bagels places for you to spend you $ and time. Go up town to bagel talk in the 70's or absolute at 107th if you want a real ny bagel and not to waste your time.

I bet this place goes out of business in a year or two once the hype wears off bc I can't see anyone visiting a second time.

My BF took me to this place for bagels. It's a complete surprise. The servant dressed up in 1950s and serve amazing bagels on a stacked serving rack. We both tried the house tuna bagel. Comes with free additional bagels . They even have gluten free ones. Nice find , come before free additional bagels.

The food is good but they have some weird logistical issues. 

Arrived at 7:50 on a Sunday, they open at 8am. About 10 people in line. There is only one cashier so I waited about 15 minutes to get to the register/ order area. The cashier gave us a number and it turns out she gave us the number for the order before ours. She was a bit disorganized. 

Also, there is a huge dining room, which does not open until 9am. The entire dining room staff including hostesses were there and in place so it was very odd that it did not open until an hour after the bagel counter opened. I would have paid more for table service, to have been able to have a place to sit while eating.

Back to to food: The guys who make the bagel sandwiches and slice the fish are fantastic and very organized unlike the cashier. I especially liked the smoked salmon (in a bagel sandwich) and the cinnamon raisin bagels. The smoked salmon tasted very rich - like Acme's Belly Lox- even though it was sliced very thin. The cinnamon raisin bagel had raisins that had been presoaked so they were very juicy and plump.
Chaos after 3 weeks.  Bagels are good, not really worth the wait in line and the screwed up orders.  Very nice staff though.

How not to manage a restaurant....Consider this a take out shop and not a real restaurant. Had a 3pm reservation, just got a call to say they've run out of all bagels and all pastries.  Thanks Sadelle's for ruining our holiday.

For the recent holiday I ordered from 5 of the top establishments in NYC - Barney Greengrass, Russ & Daughters, Tal Bagel, Zucker's and Sadelle's -- everyone has their specialties and those cannot be duplicated.  The newcomer Sadelle's has interesting twist on Jewish classics including some of the best Jewish inspired baked goods the city has to offer.  Their packaging is outstanding!!!

This place is a destination !!!
Its going to be like Murray's bagels is but in the SOHO .
Bagels texture wise are the same as Murray's  , can be serve toasted (like Murray's started lately) though prefer as non toasted if just came out of the oven, 
( you will hear it - trust me :)
The Place is beautiful , great atmosphere, 
Excellent service !!!
Bagels (assortment , you can chose) are slightly smaller then usual which make it right with no regrets .
Their Foie gras on Challa bread is exceptional, they might need to add an ice wine or Botrytis option to complete this dish .

Love this place, fresh orange juice, great bloodymary. The bagels are deliciously fresh and they have the perfect size. Smoke salmon was amazing, eggs and potatoes were perfectly cooked. 
And the blueberry cheesecake was incredible 

If you don't like to wait I recommend to make reservations and then not need to complain about waiting time. 
It is a pretty busy place but totally worthy.

Awesome bagels and breads and cakes and smoked fish, but repugnant service! I was waiting in line behind a lady who wasn't given a number or a receipt, and the woman behind the counter refused to give the customer anything without a receipt or a number even though it was she who had forgot to give these things to the customer, meanwhile she was saying the downright most disgusting comments and remarks to the customer (who was a polite, disabled elderly lady) which were not just condescending and inappropriate but also incredibly mean and unforgivable. Then when it was my turn, the woman behind the counter said "What do YOU want!" as if I had done something wrong, which I definitely didn't, and when I asked if they were out of anything, she yelled JUST TELL ME WHAT YOU WANT, I said Pumpernickel Everything, and she said WE DONT GOT THAT, and I asked what DO they have and she said JUST TELL ME WHAT YOU WANT and I said Everything Bagel with Salmon and Chive and Tomato, she said THERE IS NO TOMATOES, I said then Capers please, she threw my receipt at me, scoffed and laughed at me when I didn't leave her a tip, then when my order was ready they just threw it on the counter and said HERE, no bag or napkin or anything, and of course they gave me a Plain Bagel rather than the Everything Bagel I ordered, but the sandwich itself was without a doubt the best Salmon Chive Caper bagel I've ever ever ever had.

Hello I'm Karen and I'm a bagelaholic. 

Three stars, three comments:
1. Bagels are on point - their everything is EVERYTHING. Both top and bottom are decked out in everything bagel goodness. Especially enjoyed the salt crystals. Perfectly chewy, just the right size, and toasted to perfection. This is what everything bagel dreams are made of.

2. Chive cream cheese and scottish salmon - I can't say it was bad...but i do find their competitor (R&D) better. The flavor of the chive CC and the scottish salmon - very high quality but the depth of flavor just did not compare. 

3. Very expensive.

This is not your average bagel grabbing establishment. I get it - the place is beautiful and the rent must be high...but $8 for a side of avocado? WHAT?! You can only imagine how things go up from there...

Oh Sadelle's, I'll come back and sit down if I celebrate some spectacular bagelversary of some kind...but until then I'll just grab an occasional take-away everything bagel and relish in this one time visit.

They clearly have no idea what a "bear claw" is.

On this basis alone, I'm giving the a low rating. I'm not even holding them to a high standard, I just expect them to make this one pastry properly.

Instead of a bear claw, it was more like a "bear cub claw" - it had the right shape but was at least one third the size of what it should have been and had barely any filling or anything on the outside. Pathetic.

Perhaps their other offerings are better quality, but I just wanted this one thing and they couldn't deliver.

The bagel i had was amazing and the salmon i chose was about the best i have ever had in the city. The wait was long, but worth it on a Sunday morning. Only thing that ruined my visit was the snotty little black woman and the way that she spoke to her counterparts, they were doing their best and obviously were trying but the way she spoke to them was disgusting, if that were me I would have lost my mind! It totally ruined my visit and we had been waiting to try Sadelle's out since in opened.  Two thumbs way down

Their bagels are fabulous.  Not bombs but right-sized, old school crispy on outside, soft and chewy on inside.  Feasted on plain, poppy and pumpernickel and all were excellent.  The lox, or should I say smoked salmon as it is not salty, is silky, fresh and delicious and when put on a bagel with chive cream cheese is out of this world. I'm a bagel expert, having eaten fresh ones for 50 years, andthese are great.

A beautiful space and a restaurant with a lot of potential but it all falls flat. Service is abysmal. They hype you on the "non stop bagels" but good luck trying to find your server to get you more when you need them. Your breakfast will come with one half sized normal bagel per person and then you'll sit there with all your food waiting to find someone to bring you more. Coffee? Same problem. Be ready to sit there with cold coffee waiting for someone to pour you more. Why isn't someone walking around the room with a pot of regular in one hand and decaf in another? Why isn't someone going from table to table with bagels so your meal doesn't stop for 10 minutes waiting for another bagel? Instead of the gimmick of someone shouting out "hot bagels" every time some new ones come out perhaps working on improving the service would be time better spent. If you want a far better experience go to Russ and Daughters. We won't be back.

Update: happened to be in the area and thought I'd give it another try. It's actually worse than I remembered it. Service is horrific. I have to believe our waiter quit or was fired during our meal because we never again saw him after taking our order. $7 per person for unlimited water yet no one bothers to come around to refill your glass and much more to complain about. Don't waste your time here.

Very disappointed with this restaurant.  Bagels may be good but there are wonderful , many better, and comparable places for bagels in the bagel capital of the world, NYC.  What was most distressing is their total lack of customer service.  Food is important but customer service is as well.  When I contacted them by phone to make a reservation, the woman who answered could not have been ruder and unhelpful.  In fact she made me feel like I was taking up her "valuable" time, and yet not even answering my question.  One strike.  I followed up with an email to the restaurant owners, Major Food Group, regarding my experience, and heard nothing back.  I don't care if they might have even disagreed with me on my experience which would be hard to do but the total failure to even respond is inexcusable.  Perhaps their ego is getting too big.  Again, outstanding bagels can be found many places in NYC, but customer service is an earned benefit. This place has none of the latter.  Will not return.

Took me two attempts, but I finally got my grubby little mittens on the babkas this place will be (and is, I guess) infamous for. I last rocked up around 2pm and they were completely out of everything. Was not a happy camper. This past weekend I turned up at 10am to ensure I got something, and thankfully they had everything.

Lets get this out the way, the bakas are both awesome, and I can't believe I am saying this but I think I enjoy the cinnamon raisin babka a lot more than the chocolate. Controversial, I know, but apparently true. Next up, the inevitable comparisons to Breads' babkas. Right now, after a single experience with each, I am leaning towards Breads being superior though I am always willing to re-trial for further assessment. 

The bear claw was particularly great also, I just want to add.

Didn't try the bagels, but would another time.

Sadelle's is house in a BEAUTIFUL space right in the heart of Soho.  I went this past weekend after a barre class and picked up a bagel with lox and chocolate chip loaf to go.  We had originally wanted to dine-in, but as with any new Torrisi brother's venture, it was packed and we were quoted a 1.5 hour wait at around noon on Saturday.  

This bakery specializes in Jewish American classics, and there's a wide selection of baked loaves and buns to choose from.  A lot of the baked goods are not sold by the slice - we had wanted to try the chocolate babka but settled for the chocolate chip instead since that was available by the slice.  

The loaf was good but the star was probably still the bagel.  I would say it was almost like a cross between the HUGE doughy bagels you get at Ess-a-bagel and the flat Montreal-style bagels at Black Seed.  It was just the right amount of chewy, and the bagels are baked fresh every 30 mins or so.  I had the chive cream cheese with lox and there was a generous amount of fish in there.  

At $12 for a bagel and $3+ for a loaf this place isn't cheap since there's definitely a premium for the ambiance, but still worth checking out if you're in the area and want a quick breakfast to go.

The newest restaurant from Major Food has arrived, and it's another instant success. I came here for an early breakfast/late lunch and immediately loved the space. 

The menu was a bit confusing as the dishes are not really explained but I love that they serve breakfast all day and lunch starting after 11:30. 

My friend ordered the eggs any style. While this might sound like a boring dish, I can assure you it was far from it. She ordered her eggs scrambled and they came with the most incredible fried potatoes, a warm bagel and a piece of buttery, thick toast. I took a few bites and was really impressed. 

The waiter really pushed the grilled shrimp and coconut rice and I took his advice and went with it. Wow, it was insane. Perfectly succulent shrimp were covered in herbs and served on a bed of a slightly sweet coconut rice. I devoured this! 

I cannot wait to come back and try more of the menu, but to be honest, I'll probably just want to order the shrimp again!

Had high hopes for this place after seeing the glowing article in Businessweek and seeing a line out the door one sunday afternoon. Dropped by early one weekday morning, and there was no line. Ordered an onion bagel with chives cream cheese, lox, tomatoes, onions, and capers (yeah we went all in) and it came out to be $13 so I split it with a friend. The bagel itself was yummy, and the ratio and arrangement of ingredients was on point. However, $6.50 for a measly half of a tiny bagel to begin with, hurt a little. I'd say it's a good bagel, and a swanky place, but doesn't live up to the hype.

Wow, this venue is BEAUTIFUL with high ceilings.  Great and lively atmosphere if you are dining in.  Everyone here is incredibly friendly and sweet.  

I came here to grab a loaf of their famous chocolate babkas for $15.  I was able to grab one of their last loaves on a Saturday afternoon back in early/mid September.

I really wanted to like the babka but it was dry and tasteless, highly overrated.  My foodie friend (who loves the babka at Breads Bakery) was disappointed.

Disappointing. Space itself is beautiful but that's about it. We had the strangest server who was clearly bothered we were there and it felt like he was intentionally omitting information to just keep the day going and get us out of his hair. Asking what kind of bagels they had to offer to accompany our smoked salmon platter could not have irritated him more and it took three times as long as it could have to order.  

Unfortunately, the bagels are not that great. They come toasted (unheard of at the best bagel spots) and  tasteless. Because they were toasted once the bagels were cold had even less flavor. The everything and salt and pepper bagel we are but the sesame was not worth consuming despite the fact that we had an abundance of cream cheese. The salmon was fine but nothing you can't get at a deli. 

The icing on the cake was when we ordered a loaf of
 babka and asked for a slice to have while we sat. When I started to ask what kinds of babka they had the waiter turned his back and left bringing two chocolate slices and a box that had chocolate all over the side. Clearly careless and rushing. When I asked the hostess re babka flavors she told me there was a cinnamon option. I told the waiter I would have liked that instead of what he gave us without asking, when he came over to pick up our signed bill, and I was told "yeah our cinnamon babka is pretty great" before getting his back and never seeing him again. 

Lastly, two-top tables are so small that you can't have more that one main plate and your drinks on the table at a time. 

We are usually major food fans - Carbone and Santina are miles above Sadelles. Please save your time and money. If you need a good NYC bagel, hit up Essa, they know what they're doing n

All I have to say, is thank goodness we had a reservation because the wait was 2 hours. Yes, you can make online/email reservations, but don't bother. Instead, go to one of the thousand other bagel places in the city and you'll be sure to have better food and better service. Sadelle's tried to make bagels fancy--which is the exact opposite of what a bagel should be. With this attempt also came a snotty waitress who was annoyed that we asked what kind of bagels they had. If you specialize in bagels, shouldn't your offerings be on the menu or the first thing your waitress tells you about? Nope. Not at the fanciest bagel place in NYC. Same went for the cream cheese, of which they only have two options: 1. plain, 2. chive. Again, the waitress was annoyed we asked. I guess we should have done more research for our breakfast experience. I didn't know we were at the soup nazi. After loving Torrisi Italian Specialties and Carbone, I seriously expected a lot more from this restaurant group. Even more disappointing? The bagels aren't even good! They are small (for NYC Bagel standards) and pretty flavorless. If you specialize in bagels--get the bagels right! The cream cheese was fine--normal cream cheese. We also ordered lox, which my husband said was very fresh and very tasty. The egg salad was very good as well. But nothing to ever go back for. We also got a side of cucumbers and tomatoes. This came with about 10 slices of cucumber and 3 thin, fragile slices of tomato. The pathetic tomato portion was definitely not enough for 2 people. And when I asked for more, it took them about 15 minutes to bring another order out. Of tomatoes. Is this for real? To end the meal, we ordered a babka loaf. Why a loaf for 2 people? Well, at Sadelle's they don't sell the Babka by the slice. It's "too messy to cut," our waitress told us. Well, the babka was dry and unimpressive. The only thing impressive about Sadelle's is the space. It's absolutely beautiful. But for bagels? Save your money and your time.

Happy to report that since my reviews, Sadelle's management has reached out to address my concerns. They apologized for my experiences thus far and were kind enough to send me a wonderful spread of their goodies to try. More than anything, I appreciate that they are recognizing the frustrations of their customers and taking actions to rectify shortcomings. The food package aside, they assured me that they are looking into adding social media accounts as part of their communication strategy in the future. I look forward to visiting Sadelle's again soon as I now believe they are committed to providing positive experiences for their customers.

$13 is too much for a small bagel with smoked salmon and cream cheese. If the bagel were bigger or the flavors were outstanding, it'd be worth the $$, but even Russ & Daughters' bagels seem slightly bigger for less $$. Brooklyn Bagel & Coffee Co. have bigger, tastier bagels that are cheaper.

I have to say I was pleasantly surprised! Though pricey, the experience here is truly lovely. The decor is delightful (think teal decor and tableware, wood and white furniture), service is extraordinary and attentive, and the food is delicious. It's also a super spacious place for those of you who are trying to plan a massive group brunch. I ordered the blueberry pancakes - now, Yelp reader, it pained me to order these because it's $18 for PANCAKES. But I have to say they were some of the best pancakes I've ever tried. So if your parents are taking you out I highly recommend it. The bagels and spreads were also divine and beautifully arranged. 

Also, this is a testiment to how cheesy I am, but I adore that whenever the fresh hot bagels are en route from the kitchen to the front bakery, the waitstaff screams "HOT BAGELS!"

TL; DR: Tasty and probably overpriced; come here with your Jewish parents.

Love love love Sadelle's! I agree with other Yelpers that this place is expensive, but the food is great and service is beyond amazing. We had the chocolate babka, salmon salad, everything bagel with salmon and chives cream cheese, and the grapefruit cocktail. The babka was tender and chocolate-y without being too sweet, and everything else was delicious as well. The best part was the staff, who generously offered us compliments throughout our meal there. Needless to say, we were happily stuffed leaving Sadelle's!

This place is awful.  Overpriced, mediocre food, awful service.  The wait staff looks miserable.  Was so excited about trying it for the first time.  What a let down.  Don't even want to give it one star.

I hate to say it, but I was not really impressed with the bagels here. I really enjoyed the pastries though. 

I got there around 11am and asked how long the wait was for two, and they said I could be seated around 12:30. Since my friend wasn't there yet I put my name down and they took my number to text me when the table was ready. When my friend showed up we just decided to do take out and not wait for the table. Luckily there wasn't too much of a line for take out. My friend ordered a bagel and a few pastries, and I ordered an everything bagel with chive cream cheese, a black and white cookie and piece of pumpkin loaf.. You can't order babka by the slice at the counter, womp. 

So we wait for our orders and it doesn't take too long. We take it outside and walk a little to find somewhere to sit and we take out all our goodies when my friend discovers they didn't actually give him his bagel. So back we went and they made him a bagel. Then went outside again to eat and I discovered they gave me the wrong order.. they gave me an everything 2.0 and plain cream cheese. At that point I didn't feel like going back again so I kept it. The bagels are pretty small, and mine at that point was not warm and kind of hard. So yea I was not impressed. My friend was nice enough to take my second half and gave me his. His was much better, since it was warm and soft.  

I definitely wasn't that full after my bagel, so I was happy we had pastries, which were really good.  Of everything I tried probably the pumpkin loaf and the fruit/cheese danish my friend had gotten were the best.  I definitely think the pastries redeemed this place a little bit for me.  The inside looked really cute, so maybe I'd give it another shot sitting down.  But as far as the bagels go, if they're warm and they get your order right they are good, but there are a lot of good bagel places in the city.  So not sure I'd go back just for that.

The bagel restaurant OF MY DREAMS. Between Billy Joel playing in the background, sunshine coming through the skylight, people yelling "Hot Bagels" after fresh ones come out of the oven, and the gorgeous design, I am just in love. We got the seafood tower which is a bit expensive but so worth it for a group of people. The bagels are delicious and anyone here who said they've had better must not have had them hot. The way the salads are created is so smart and beautiful I didn't want to mess it up by eating it (but then I did). Lastly: Don't miss the salmon salad or the chocolate babka. I wish there was a Sadelles in BK!

funny, just last night i watched the mind of a chef episode where gabrielle hamilton talks about the only nod modern chefs give to tradition is an ironic one.  clearly she was talking about ridiculous places like this.   i really couldn't have hated this place more.  first there was the annoying hostess who wanted to know if we had reservations.  seriously?  it was 10am, we wanted to grab a quick breakfast and the place barely had three tables full.   i found the menu uninspiring and finally settled on salmon salad which came served atop a weird silver tray with three tiers--a  bit of overkill for the homely slices of cucumber, tomato, onion shreds and caper it carried.  my bagel was just this side of burnt, dry, and so dense i could barely chew it.   luckily, the ladies at the next table provided some distraction when their tower of smoked salmon slipped off the glass table and it's three heavy china plates crashed loudly to the floor - we were able to get our check and flee without the waiter asking why we had barely touched our food.   hey sadelle's in case you were wondering:  because it was absolutely inedible.  and just in case my review doesn't keep you away, make sure you bring a credit card with a hefty balance; our simple breakfast was fifty dollars and they don't take cash.

Short: The bagels were somewhat small, but the house salmon and cream cheese were both incredible. Sadelle's is pretty pricey--about $13 for a bagel, cream cheese, and lox. The restaurant is pretty small, so if you go on the weekend prepare for a wait. Four stars for taste, quality of product, and packaging of the bagel, lox, and cream cheese.
 
Long: I came here on a Sunday at 12:30 PM with a friend and the wait was 2.5 hours, so we decided to get our bagels to-go from the counter on the left side of the restaurant. The restaurant is very pretty, but honestly seems somewhat overrated--I mean 2.5 hours?! That is crazy for bagels. By 12:30, selection was somewhat low (I am not sure if they restock throughout the day). I ordered a sesame seed bagel (they were out of everything and everything 2.0) with plain cream cheese and the house salmon. The bagel was somewhat small and was chewy, but there was a relatively thick crust in comparison to the bagel itself. The lox was amazing. It was smooth as butter and was incredibly fresh. 

Since my friend and I didn't actually dine in I would rate the bagel and lox itself at 4 stars. The wait time to sit and the price make it less of a must have, but if you are in the area and are craving a quality bagel I would definitely suggest stopping by. Even though the bagel was somewhat small it was filling and the lox is incredible. At $13 for a bagel and lox, Sadelle's is not a place I would regularly dine but it is a great place to go for a yummy treat.

This place is the best! I said yes every time they offered me a hot bagel (I lost count around 6...everything 2.0 was the jam) and didn't regret a single delicious bite. The Scottish salmon is the best I've ever had, served with beautiful tomatoes (I was wary since they are definitely not in season) and the people watching in the awesome space was pretty killer too. I literally went back the next day for more and can't even bring myself to feel a little bit embarrassed.

Amazing food and definitely worth checking out. All bagels are made in house, which you can see and the salmon is amazing. Great decor and ambiance too. On the downside I'd say is that the food was a bit salty and the service was a tad slow, however they are a new restaurant. Apparently they will have a dinner menu soon but I wonder how the prices will be seeing that my small meal cost about $20 including tip. Hope to go back in a few months.

Great decor, beautiful peoples do long lines/waiting time to sit.

If you seek to over pay for a bagel with smoked fish, Sadelles is  definitely the place to go!

For the 1% ! Simply keeping it !

I dropped by during one of the first weekends after it opened, and they were out of bagels by 10:30am on a Sunday. While it wasn't completely surprising given the amount of traffic and hype they'd received, I wished that they could have better predicted the demand on their star item. Instead I picked up a couple of their rugelach, which were admittedly delicious. The rest of the bakery goods looked standard. There was an impressive chocolate-covered babka on display, if that's your thing. I got the impression that this is good spot if you're in the neighborhood but nothing special enough to come out of your way for.

Super pretty and cute ambiance with miniature rose floral arrangements and a vintage feel. It's a Jewish deli best known for their triple decker sandwich. I feel this place as beautiful as it is- is overrated and overpriced. The menu had very few choices except for salads, small breakfast menu and simple sandwiches. I.e oatmeal for $11. I think this place is best for just pick up for bagels. 

I also tried their sticky buns and tuna melt. Good but not all that impressed especially at this price point.

I went last week for brunch and was really impressed with the food, the decor, and the waitstaff - which if you've ever been to another of their restaurants is not at all surprising. We went with scottish smoked for the table with a few different types of bagels which were all hot and great, and also got the bacon, egg, and cheese on challah for the table - possibly tastiest BEC I've ever had. Definitely should be placed on anyone's brunch list who enjoys a good bagel and lox.
The food is phenomenal with amazingly beautiful presentation. Quality product. Stellar service. Good for people watching.

Best scrambled eggs - bar none - I have ever eaten.  Bagels baked on the premises.  Everything was cooked to perfection.  Service is top notch.  The pastries displayed in the front all looked delicious - wish I had room to try them.

Go here during the week off peak hours and you'll have a perfectly pleasant experience (a friend and I dined around 11:30am on a Tues). The ambiance is lovely - I'd call it a mix of jewish deli, 50s diner, and frenchy bistro. 

The presentation of food is top-notch with a slight caveat; some of the tables off the side are too small for the serving towers, creating an awkward eating arrangement should you and companion also have a beverage on the table. 

The wait staff is eager and amicable, but after the third request for a cup of coffee, I thought perhaps a bit forgetful or stretched thin. 

Despite that small glitch, the food was impeccable and delicious. My everything bagel was, in fact, everything! It was the proper size (bagels are not meant to be these behemoths you find in other shops), correct consistency, and flavored well. The smoked salmon was divine and the sticky bun was confection perfection. My friend's salmon eggs benedict looked delicious and a bite of her cream cheese + blueberry danish did not disappoint. 

Prices seemed steep, but given the location and use of high-quality ingredients, it's worth the splurge for an unexpectedly fun lunch date. I'd love to try dinner sometime soon!

Sadelle's is delicious and has an amazing cozy and buzzy vibe. I loved the fresh hot bread straight from the oven. 

I especially loved the veal dumplings and tuna tartar. The fried chicken with truffle honey is out of this world. 

Cocktails are also delicious. I had one with shiso infused vodka and apple that was so perfect for the fall season. 

Can't wait to come back and try the caviar service!

Sadelles joins Carbone & Dirty French in the pantheon of below average overpriced offerings from the Major Food Group. We came for dinner, and it can only be described as a disappointment.  While the decor and candles were cute, the food was overpriced and underwhelming. Somehow each restaurant opened by the Torrisi team seems more gimmicky than the last. We are being taken for a ride, by the emperor and his new clothes. The tuna tartare was extremely meh, although the veal dumplings were pretty good. The fried chicken was nice, but you can get far better (and cheaper) at Root and Bone or Blue Ribbon. The Romanian steak was fine, but for $32 you'd expect a side dish (and no, the absurdly salty spoonful of dill salad on the side does not count). Limited drink menu consists of only vodka based drinks and a boring (and expensive) wine list. Will not be returning.

Much improved since my last visit.  Coffee still pricey, though slightly cheaper and still amazing. No more vegetable cream cheese makes me sad but bagels are still one of the best in the vicinity. No wait at all, but maybe I got lucky.

I was really looking forward to trying this vey charming restaurant. While the decor and presentation is lovely, the decent food is way overpriced, and the service was the worst part of our experience. 
We ordered the house cured salmon, poached eggs with potatoes, and an omelette. Food was good, but nothing to scream about. $22-30+ for a salad? $8 for a side of potatoes? $7 for a side of avocado (that's like, half an avocado!!!)? LOL This is literally the cheapest food to purchase: eggs, bagels, potatoes... Get it together, people! 
As for the service.... The waitress took away our food before we were even finished, and then slammed the bill on the table. We didn't even ask for the bill, we weren't done eating our meal, and we were waiting to see the dessert and tea menu (which she never even offered!). 
Put off by this, we just paid and went to the bakery section to get rugelach. Seriously, don't even bother. $2 a piece and it's really not even remotely close to good, Jerusalem rugelach.

I came here for a unique experience and that's exactly what I got, a uniquely bad experience! Everything is so expensive and and not worth what you pay for. Place is trying to benefit of yuppies with their decor and lame paintings. Everything is so slow and place isn't near functional. I went to the bathroom and had to wait in a long line because they only have 2 small bathrooms for a place that seats maybe a 100 people. While on line I noticed the kitchen which was smaller than my kitchen which makes me think that the people running this are delusional if they think that kitchen can feed a full restaurants in a timely manner. Servers try to be helpful but from how everything is set up they are doomed for failure and a stressful day regardless. Basically everything about this place is "meh" and I would not ever come back again for the long waits and mediocre bagels. Try fooling people who have money to throw away for inferior quality everything. 

BTW they pay people to give fake reviews because they are desperate and know that what they have actually is lame and is getting old really fast!!

This is a great new restaurant in the spot. Really suggest coming in with a reservation or you'll have to wait about 2 hours to be seated. My friend and I came over and were lucky to be seated in about an hour. The lace was very busy so we had to flag down a waiter. She ordered the Scottish salmon and I went for the customized omelette. We had to wait about 40 minutes before our food arrived - we were starving. The waiter was nice to apologize but we were ravenous. Once the food did arrive, our cream cheese order was messed up. We ordered 2 choice cream cheeses and one was plain. We told the waiter that we originally ordered the choice cream cheese and he picked up the plain stating he'd return with the other cream cheese. Throughout the course of our meal  no one had returned to with the extra cream cheese. 

That being said, the food was delectable. Every 20 minutes or so, a man with a long stick filled with bagels would walk around the tables yelling "HOT BAGELS" and giving them out which was a nice touch. Let me mention that bagels are free when you dine in and water is flowing. The bagels are salted to PERFECTION. The omelette was well done as I liked it. 

Since this is a new establishment, I'm supposing they were still figuring out kinks in their technology as we had received two wrong checks before the original. The food and atmosphere are worth the price. However, I would rather come when it is less busy so that I can actually hear the convo I'm having with a friend.

The reason I gave three stars are for the kinks I the system, the wait time and the missing cream cheese. I'll come again when it's quieter and post an update of my experience.

Cramp spaces. Long waits. Food is, good.  Server forgot our coffee didn't send us the bagels we ordered as well as one of the cream cheeses we asked for.

Really? Is it that hard to ask the kitchen for two different types of bagels with the fish tower.  I'm convinced MFG management has no attention to detail.

Honestly the food isn't even that exciting.  It's bagels and salmon, nothing thrilling.

One more thing $17 for a Mimosa.  WHAT!!! That's hilarious and deplorable.  It's OJ and sparkling wine.  They could both be the cheapest quality and it would taste good.   No reason to charge that much for a simple cocktail.

Poor form MFG, really poor form.

I went to this restaurant for brunch on my sisters birthday. The wait time (even with reservations) is ridiculous. They don't have a seating area for waiting so everyone ends up smushed together annoyed with the wait. First impression wasn't great; however, once we got seated everything went uphill. Our waitress was one of the kindest people I ever met. They were incredibly busy but she paid attention to our table and was such a delight. The food was great but the customer service was even better. They comped all of our drinks by the end of it which was very considerate (not sure if our waitress knew about the wait time). When I walked out I was such a fan of the place. Don't let the wait time scare you- the food and customer experience is very worth the wait!
Want to be kept waiting for ten minutes when there are ten free tables in the restaurant? You've come to the right place. Do not go here!

I came in for a late breakfast with a friend about two weeks ago. We were both extremely impressed by the space and decor - it's a very large restaurant, is decorated well, and all the waiters are dressed in clean, white uniforms. The menu features standard bagels as well as omelettes and other breakfast specialties. We decided on the bagels and lox. You get unlimited bagels (of which there are many varieties) as well as a tower of lox and onions, tomatoes, and capers. The bagels are on the small side, but very tasty with the accompaniments. 

My biggest complaint is that everything is WAY overpriced. The bagels and lox are upwards of $20 which to me is ridiculous. Though the service was attentive and food tasty, I probably won't return as I feel that it's not worth the price.
Overpriced and not much of a selection.  The babka has too much icing and not enough flavor inside.  It's not even on the same planet as Russ & Daughters.

After going here twice this place is the real deal!  Their presentation is lovely and the food is super fresh.  At times there are lines but they do take reservations even for 2 people which isn't very common for restaurants so i would suggest making one before you go there.

I usually get their house salmon platter which is plentiful and they make the best omelettes around,  they take a bit longer to get but worth the wait.  The staff is friendly, attentive and Nattie the manager is so nice,  The salmon slicer Jay is one of a kind as he really knows how to slice and dice up that salmon.  Another outstanding person there is Avacado, yes that is her real name, she works near the take out area and has a smile that can light up a room. 

I would highly recommend eating there and also taking out some of their amazing food selections, I can't wait to go back, the place is spacious and does have communal tables for big parties or small tables if you just wanted to come in by yourself, they make you feel welcomed either way.  .

Sadelle's in Soho is so popular that the lines form outside at 6:30 AM, well before the store opens. The bakery-restaurant hybrid houses bagels, cheese danishes, pastries and walnut or chocolate babka. The lines are long and the goods are pricey. Go there with a lot of patience and a fat wallet. The chocolate babkas are great!

Love the spinach and goat cheese omelet. I come back every time and order the same thing. Service is fast but the servers are pretty monotoned not very nice and welcoming. Coffee is blah! But sarabeths is a classic place for breakfast in the city

The restaurant is transformed at night with candles and is quite stunning. The Eastern European menu is an interesting one, and some of the dishes are extremely good such as the Veal Palmeni appetizer (Russian dumplings) and the Chicken Paprika. Other dishes such as the pigs in a blanket don't taste much different than what you could get in the frozen food department of your local grocery store. However, the service, although pleasant, is beyond amateurish.It took thirty minutes to be served our drinks, and when we inquired about it we were told that the finishing touches were being put on them (a shot of vodka straight up and a glass of champagne). It then took forty five minutes after we finished our appetizer to be served our entree, and the restaurant was not even full that night. Our bread basket was snatched away from us without asking (I snatched it right back) in the middle of our meal.Finally, when I made the reservation, I mentioned that it was my husband's birthday that day. I then repeated this three times at the restaurant (to the hostess, our server, and some women wandering around checking up on things) indicating that I wanted a candle to be placed in his cake. I was assured that would be no problem.Twenty-five minutes later the cake was served without a candle. I hate to say it but the bad service really did ruin the experience.

I am extremely pleased to report that our second brunch at Sadelle's was a complete, massive success!

Seven of us shared:

One fish tower (two kinds of salmon, salmon salad, sturgeon, sablefish, and whitefish salad, plus tomato, red onion, cucumber, and capers, all sliced thinly and expertly) to accompany bagels for each of us. Comes with plain and chive cream cheese. The bagels are not huge, which is fine -- the fish is the star here. By all accounts, it compares favorably to Russ & Daughters, high praise indeed. The tower is $100 and perfect for a group of fish lovers.
Two LEOs (lox, eggs, and caramelized onions; the eggs are frittata-style, with a layer of salmon draped on top). It's $21 and great for sharing.
One French toast -- this was awesome. It's custardy (god knows how many eggs are in there) and massive. For $20 six people could each get plenty.
One chocolate babka -- excellent. A thick slice for everyone, plus three left over. $18.
Side of home-fried potatoes -- these were $12 and fabulous. Came in a big bowl. I'm pretty sure these were Yukon Golds. Crunchy on the outside and creamy on the inside, tossed with onions and red pepper. Really an unexpected treat. 
Bowl of pickles -- half sours, full sours, and garlics. Excellent.

I think that's it. Not anything close to a clunker.

Our server was up to the food -- helpful and professional.

Just an all around ridiculously good meal. 

NB: On the weekend, make a reservation or don't bother, unless you want to kill the better part of the day.

review pertains to take out only. i have not had the dine-in service. 

waaay overpriced for a tiny bagel with tuna fish. nothing special, could have gotten a better bagel at ess a bagel or any other decent bagel shop for a fraction of the price. 

take out menu is limited to bagels only with spreads

seems like it would be a much better experience for dine in.  beautiful decor, the other food looked good.
I mean, yes it's a bit in the pricier side, but you do get a definite value for the money.
Bagels hot off the press!  Lines out the door!  You know it's good in here without having to read my review.

I get it I get it - this place is trendy as all hell. I stopped in here for a bagel and lox one weekday morning. I will give them this - the salmon was fantastic. Thin, smoky, delicate, and delicious. However, the bagel that I put it on was, for lack of a better word, HARD. I ordered an everything bagel and when it came out, I immediately knew something was wrong. Inspecting more closely, I noticed a large amount of fennel, FENNEL!, on the bagel. I've eaten a lot of everything bagels in my life and know that one thing you never put on an everything bagel is fennel. Jeez louise guys, keep it simple. Overall, great ambience and yum lox, but they couldn't do the think they're known for very well, so it's a 3 star review for me!

I Went for brunch on a Friday for my birthday,it was amazing. We ordered the tower and substituted the sturgeon and sable for egg salad and extra smoked salmon. It was so delicious and the bagels were so tasty. The French toast was the best I've ever had.
Can't wait to go back!

Was very excited to try this, I made reservations weeks before to bring friends visiting from out of town. Unfortunately we had a terrible experience. I had a reservation for 1pm, we arrived about 10 minutes early. We weren't seated until after 1:30. After that, we were pretty eager to order and eat, it took a while for a waiter to get to us. We placed our order, and 45 minutes later still no food. We talked to the waiter and the manager stopped by and neither could seem to explain what was happening with our order. The table next to us sat down after us, ordered, ate and left and we were still waiting. They seemed very disorganized and not able to handle the brunch rush. 

The food was good enough, but not great. I really wanted to love this place. The manager did apologize and comp the meal, which was very nice. However, the experience was so frustrating I don't think I will go back.

Sadelles... Where do i begin? 
Surly hostess ( todays wasnt friendly at all). She must be having a bad day especially since every person trying to enter restaurant tried each of the 4 doors until you see her irritably gesturing to the furthest left door.
Bustling bus service means they will brush against your chair, where my bag fell. Dont expect a sorry. Try to ask for booth if you can. 
Very nice waiter - the only nice part of todays breakfast

Ordered the $16 custom omelette that comes with 3 add-ons - chose chives, salami & mushroom. Nice round omelette with firm, brown edges. Reminded me that i shouldve asked for lightly cooked egg. 
My best friend ordered their $26 salmon benedict which was comped after i commented that she bit down on eggshell twice to our server. Yes, i was surprised to find eggshell on a poached egg. The comp was very nice of restaurant.
Wasnt told about their bagels but later found out that its complementary with meal. Good to know for those who wanted to carb up. 

Their sticky buns and chocolate babka slice was the highlight of our meal. I would recommend their bakery items. But after todays meal, this reminds me why i dont frequent Major Food Hospitality grp restaurants. Their pricing and service isnt to my taste. I would come back for take out and bakery items only.

You'd get a 5 for the food and the server. Unfortunately a few fixable issues brought my review down to a 3. I hope to be able to increase it in the future. 

I came for breakfast this morning at about 9:30am. My first time, and my husband has previously had breakfast here. 

The bad first - lack of customer attention in several areas. 

1. First impressions? Entering a restaurant shouldn't be a freaking puzzle. If you choose to have a bunch of doors but only one opens, can't you just LABEL THEM WITH A SIGN? Making a customer feel stupid and embarrassed upon entry is something you can easily fix. 

2. You don't take cash, only credit card (and NOT debit,) but you don't mention it until the check comes. Some people the US (new flash) live on cash and debit cards, and don't have credit cards. Burdening the server and customer with this unreasonable rule is strange to say the least. 

3. You don't even attempt to acknowledge the fact that your plates, stands and other stuff don't fit on the tiny round tables. Two tables around me were dropping utensils, pepper mills, etc., off their tables due to the lack of room to maneuver. This really is ridiculous...and easily fixable. 

4. Second time my husband came here and you were out of the pumpernickel bagels. It was only 9:30am. You can plan for the expected...

The good - great food & server experience. 

1. Excellent server with great attitude, friendly, knew the menu and offered solid guidance. From what I saw on the faces of other guests, the other servers appeared to be have similarly positive effects on the customers. The manager roaming around showed attention to detail in calling for our water to be refilled, etc. 

2. The quality of my Scottish smoked salmon and my partner's order of sturgeon were impeccable. Delicious combination of the everything bagel with the cream cheese, fish and accoutrements of ripe sliced tomato, shaved onion, capers and cucumber. Best fish & bagel combo I've had in years...I nursed this meal quite a while to enjoy every bite. 

3. Best bagels I've had in a long time, even though we settled for our second choices. 

4. So many delicious sounding choices on the menu, I want to get back to try more.

Went here for brunch on a Sunday. We obvi knew our food was going to take long but 45 min??? We didnt even order that much on top of that my food came in 10 min later than everyone else's and the portions are extremely small and really PRICEY, the bagels are great however they are so tiny!! not the size of bagels I had growing up in NYC. The service however was excellent. The manager did apologize for the inconvenience for the food arriving so late. 

Overall the bagels aka mini bagels were delicious and the service was excellent -  if you are planning on spending major $$$$ for mini dishes and an hour wait for your food you will enjoy Sadelle's.
Should try the bagel and salmon!!! I love their bagel,not too dry and not too soft,and if you like sesame bagel,you must try their sesame bagel!
The inside is lovely and the fish is fantastic! I've given it a few tries and the bagels are alllwaaays tough regardless of when I go. It's disappointing.

I didn't want to like this place. After several attempts to dine here only to be turned away due to a fully packed waitlist, I wanted to give up. Unfortunately, after I finally scored a table here for brunch, I have to say the hype is justified. 

Definitely one of the best bagels I've had and the tuna melt is epic. The vibe is super fun and it's  definitely not an experience you'll want to miss. Stoked to come back and try the salads.

Brunch should always be fantastic. Although the experience and ambiance of this place is lovely inside and out- the food and everything else was average. For the price. You'd expect more elbow room and a table to enjoy your food on.
Ordered 2 cocktails (bloody Mary and a grapefruit vodka.) I originally did not like the bloody because it was over bearing with pickle juice (gross.) Super diluted and barely had any alcohol. For $15 a cocktail? It was crushed ice with a splash of juice...or whatever it was.
Got the house salmon with bagels (bagels are complimentary) and they offer free cream cheese with it (whoopty doo.) Also had a side of bacon and potatoes. The bagels were a bit burnt. Was not a fan.
This place is cool and the vibes are great but I don't think it's worth the price. You can get great lox on nonburnt bagels for $4 with a nice cup of coffee. Get a real cocktail at a real bar. 
Nice for the experience. Food and everything else..
 SUPER MEH.

This place is AMAZING!! Wow!!! From the ambiance (retro-modern) to the freshly baked bagels, everything is perfect! You order your fish (we had delicious, ultra-thin sliced house smoked salmon and whitefish salad) and then you get unlimited bagels with it!! Waitstaff was friendly and great. Food came out very quickly even though they were jammed! We also ordered blintzes which were yummy - just like grandmas. Other things looked fantastic (chocolate babka, French toast, pancakes, etc) but we just couldn't eat that much! Oh, and the coffee was piping hot and great.

Despite the other lackluster reviews for their food and service my experience was overall pleasant.  Seated promptly for a brunch res on Saturday 2pm, our service was swift and friendly.  Food was all on point and our entire party enjoyed it.  What really brought the stellar experience to a grinding halt was when their POS system was unable to process several credit cards properly.  This resulted in some of us charged 3 times,  myself included.  They use an iPhone (not an iPad like coffee shops) based POS that each server carries around and I'm sure the business was sold on what seemed like an innovative system.  I wouldn't be surprised if some of the other negative service based reviews were cause by this.   I'm all for innovation but field testing a product on live guests seems pretty risky... I think it was called Flow and Flow it did not do.

Current hours listed as opening at 7:30am on Weekdays, not open on Mondays.  

Sit-Down or Take-out Service?
If you'd like to be served at a table for a relaxing breakfast, see the hostess.  If you just want a bagel or pastry with coffee, step into the blue ropes for counter service.

Take-Out Tables:
They actually save a few cafe tables near the front for people who are taking out but want a quick cafe seat.  You'll know which ones they are because they don't have plates or silverware prepared on them.  If they aren't available- you can take your lovely packaging across Houston to one of the street-side parks or Washington Square.

Sit-Down Service:
Included with sit-down service is essentially unlimited hot bagels- similar to basic bread service.  That alone makes it worth sitting down for.  If you want a specific bagel flavor, just order that with your server since it's unpredictable what will come out of the oven next as hot bagel service- you can grab a hot bagel when it comes by even after you've ordered your meal.   At first glance you probably think the prices are steep for breakfast compared to other cafes nearby, but the secret here is that most of the portions are shareable sizes, and when you factor in unlimited bagels and bottomless coffee (even on my iced coffee).... it's actually not bad at all for a SoHo eatery.

Bagels:
You don't HAVE to order fish to get a bagel- but if you do, you'll get all the veggie fixins and cream cheese with it.  Everything Bagel 2.0 includes fennel & caraway seeds.  Everything has all the other stuff you're used to.  Cinnamon Raisin, Poppy Seed, Sesame, Pumpernickel, Plain.  Toasted or not- it's up to you.  The hot bagels certainly need no toasting.  Our bagels had a pretty thick crust to bite through after being toasted and were moderately dense on the inside.  The scallion cream cheese tasted freshly mixed- as though the scallion flavor and cream cheese hadn't fully intermingled.  They were freshly slicing salmon and other fish at the counter- but we opted out of that option.  

Eggs Any Style:
The scrambled eggs tasted like there was a touch of cheese and a sprinkle of scallion. The potatoes are thin slices then deep fried for a crunchy outside and soft inside, sprinkled with dill and a few other seasonings.

Coffee:
Iced coffee has the little crushed ice cubes, which I prefer. You can pour your own milk or cream along the side wall if you're taking out.

Sticky Bun:
More like a croissant texture on the inside and the caramel on top is almost as hard as Carmel candy- it will definitely stick to your teeth.

Babka: (updated 1/16)
Previously unavailable by the slice, but stepped in today happy to find those babka cakes sliced up in pieces and ready to sell by the slice!  Yesssss!

Went for lunch. Bagels are small but doughy, and not special at all. Chocolate bobka was average. The coffee was really good. Matzoh ball soup would've been good if not so uber-salty. Fruit flies were hovering around our table and our neighbors.

Not a great overall experience. Sat us down promptly for lunch but took forrrrreeeeeveer for a waiter to come. Didn't write it down and got order wrong, of course. All of the front of the restaurant was cold. I had to put my hat on, everyone else around me was wearing coats. Not really a relaxed experience. Matzo ball soup was very good. Salmon salad platter with bagels was quite good also.

I love the food here, but have had to walk out twice because of really poor service at the take - out counter.  They don't yet seem to have their act together there yet.  My husband has walked out as well - it is a shame because we live down the street and LOVE their bagels.  Last time I was there, there was one man behind the counter slicing salmon, and one man taking all the orders AND making the bagels.  There were only 2 people on line in front of me, and it took FOREVER!! I was never even acknowledged, so walked out.  I really hope the manager pays some attention to the take - out counter.  Local word on the street is the bagels are great, but the service is seriously lacking.

Excellent French Toast, good bagles -- also served free when hot out of the oven -- salmon, waffles, etc.  Beautiful setting.  Good service.  Not easy to get a reservation.  Expect a 2 month wait for a weekend spot.

What is the bagel rave?  On any block/corner you can find the best bagels in nyc, especially in brooklyn.  i recommend patronizing any place in nyc where the bagels are made on premise. my fave is my bk neighborhood spot, bagel delight.

i give this place 3 stars for its ambiance and the fresh slice experience.

Fantastically dumb restaurant. Go-for-broke bagel enthusiasts. Like a mattress salesman going out of business. Waitress was like, I got a thousand bagels with your name on it. Just take as many bagels as you can; take em for dinner, for breakfast tomorrow, for your stoop mate, just get these bagels off my hands. Left with like 20,000 bagel calories.

All said, the enthusiasm was so infectious, we both left with smiles on our face; made of cream cheese, however.

Kind of incongruous to have a white table cloth bagel experience, but it worked.  Of course, the price reflected the great service and lovely setting.  We ordered the salmon with bagels, sticky buns, and matzo ball soup for three.  Loved every bite of everything.  The bagels were smaller than normal but our server kept bringing more out, so there was no shortage of bagels for us.  My friend loved the everything bagel; my favorite was the salt and pepper bagel. At the end, we were given a complimentary slice of chocolate babka.  So yummy!  We're definitely coming back the next time we're in NYC!

So I called Sadelle's before walking over to see if there were any chocolate babka loaves left given they close at 4pm (it was 2:30pm) and was told yes.  I arrive at 2:45pm and the manager decides he doesn't want to sell one of the 3 loaves left and tells me slices only.  Um... where's the logic in that especially as it's towards closing and I called AND the bakery and restaurant are both closed tomorrow.  BAD CUSTOMER SERVICE.  Don't they know better bakeries exist around the corner.  Dominique Ansel doesn't parcel out cronuts and often sell out.  It's called first come first serve so that when they have a handful left they don't go breaking each one out and sell it by piece?  People it's called SELLING OUT...somehow I think Sadelle's won't last in the neighborhood as they don't know who they're catering to nor the concept good business...oh wait perhaps they misunderstood that 'selling out' meant putting customer service last.  Either way - I hope those 3 babkas are sitting stale til Tuesday.

I just don't understand the hype about this place. I went for brunch on a Sunday and the food was good but nothing extraordinary. The service, however, wasn't very good. We waited for each dish, or for drinks for ever. Our waiter didn't seem to really always understand our order. But worst of all was the temperature control. It was either freezing or boiling hot. Overall it's ok but not necessarily a place I would need to come back to.

Truly negligent & incompetent service balanced by a festive space & delightful concept. Bagels were decent but nothing to write home about - the tower is fun but nothing knocked our socks off enough to put up with service this poor.  First, they lost our reservation & after agreeing to give us a table anyway, they took another 15 minutes to seat us. We informed them we had to be out in 45 flat since we were seated late, and it still took 20 mins for a waiter to take our order. Once we finished eating, it took over 45 MINUTES & 3 asks to get our table cleared & the check dropped. It sat with empty water glasses & dishes that whole time.  Getting waiters to make eye contact here is like getting audience with the pope!!  Clean up your service guys. The place has great potential for longevity as a classic, but carry on w the service you have & it'll fall in a couple of years once the buzz dies down...

Sadelle's is a lot of fun. It's a bit of a commitment for just a bagel, so be prepared to order aggressively and leave excessively full. I went for a birthday breakfast, and by far the best part was 'HOT BAGELS'! Gave us a good laugh. The food is good, especially the salmon. Again, go hungry and be prepared to drop some dollars on multiple menu items so you can get the full experience. The only thing that I didn't enjoy was the tiny table - but that's probably because we over-ordered.

Sometimes you have to have a cheat day and indulge a little.  For this fashionplate I definitely indulged and had a decadent dinner at Sadelle's in Soho.  I decided to dress up a bit and rock our Ali polka dot romper.  Sadelle's is a Jewish appetizing shop with bagels, lox, whitefish and more during the day.  Come nighttime it's transformed into a candlelit non pretentious caviar den complete with house infused vodkas.   My dining companion and I were seated upstairs at a great table overlooking the bottom floor of the restaurant, such a fab view.  I was sticking to sparkling water since it was still Dry-unary.  However my dining companion tried the beet cocktail which was fab.  The complimentary truffle studded brioche is beyond, I need to get this for takeout and eat 4 loaves in the privacy of my apartment. We knew we were going in for it and ordered the Royal Transmontanous caviar which came complete with rye toast points, blinis, POTATO PANCAKES and all the condiments.  I would've been happy with this alone as my meal, you get a good portion for 2 people.  This caviar was extremely creamy and luxe and all the accompaniments were on point.  We didn't stop there though, we also ordered the pigs in a blanket which were amazing and a great contrast of high and low culinary excitement.  As something a little lighter we picked the scallops which were also great.  The meal from start to finish was amazing, our waiter and the whole staff at Sadelle's are beyond accommodating.  Definitely a place to splurge for downtown caviar service.

Now on to the fashion part of this fashionplate.  Most patrons were part of the fashion crowd and Soho locals, so feel free to dress to impress.  At dinnertime this spot is not as packed as during breakfast/brunch so you get to enjoy a nice leisurely dinner.
