Awful. Just AWFUL. Is this place a joke? Legit felt like an episode of MTVs "Boiling Points" given how rude and weird the waiter was. You know the saying run don't walk to "x"? Well run, run far far far away from this overpriced mini bagel shop.

KenScale: 8.0/10

There is probably no other restaurant group that is hotter in New York dining scene than Major Food Group headed by Torrisi-Carbone super chef duo. I've always been keeping tabs on what their next biggest idea is (they started with casual Italian tasting menu at Torrisi Italian Specialties until branching out to old-school Italian-American at Carbone, coastal Italian at Santina and decadent French at Dirty French). The next big project had a somewhat more modest proposal: in partnership with Melissa Weller, a former baker of Per Se and Roberta's, they decided to open a Jewish-inspired restaurant serving bagel and other food with Jewish bent. I haven't been to Russ and Daughters Café yet, so it's hard for me to clearly define what Jewish cuisine would be, but based on the description of Sadelle's I've been hearing, it seemed as simple as bagels and other pastry dishes to go along with smoked fish. At the risk of sounding too simplistic, that is really what Sadelle's offers during brunch time; sometimes, simplicity is the virtue in dining, and Sadelle's exactly shows how food that doesn't have a ton of flair can still more or less deliver.

Obviously, any meal at Sadelle's would need to start with freshly baked bagels and smoked fishes that are also accompanied by a plate of tomato, cucumber, onion and capers. I wasn't quite sold on the bagels; I was hoping for something that was baked right on the spot but the tower of bagels that came in wasn't really delivered just-in-time. Anyways, the combination with house salmon and sable still worked, especially the fresh and silky smooth sable that I kept digging. This being a brunch, Sadelle's offers a number of egg dishes. We ended up choosing salami and eggs and it turned out to be a winner. I probably saw similar omelette dishes a million times at other brunch places, but the one at Sadelle's had that addictive quality to it with very nice balance of flavor (definitely no overseasoning!). You also have to get pastry dishes at Sadelle's: sticky buns from Weller were just out of this world! I haven't really had similar bun dishes lately (watching for my sugar intake) but I really had to succumb to the sensational flavor of sticky buns (although I wish it came at the end of the meal as opposed to beginning) that were literally melting in my mouth with delicate sweetness. I would totally start every morning with one of these without any hesitation! 

The restaurant is probably the hottest brunch ticket right now (all Major Food Group restaurants are very difficult to secure reservations, but my OpenTable search constantly showed "no table" signals for the next 8 weeks whenever I was looking for weekend brunch openings). The best bet may be to show up early and take your chance for walk-in tables. Sadelle's has a number of brunch cocktails too, but if you're inclined to skip alcohol, freshly squeezed orange juice would probably enhance your brunch experience. Is Sadelle's an over-hyped brunch destination? Perhaps, and probably because I think all brunch restaurants are overrated in some way (people love brunch but the restaurant doesn't showcase its full range of skills during this time), but Sadelle's overall delivers the type of experience you're looking for: a trendy vibe with a lot of young, handsome crowd in a brightly lit and chic dining space, accompanied by solid food offerings.

ORDER THE FRENCH TOAST. Overall a really nice time, great food, and great concept. Really packed on weekends so don't go expecting a cozy, quiet brunch. My main gripe is that the coffee is horrible. Like not just bad, but really bad. And they don't have special coffee drinks like espresso, cappuccino. In my opinion, in order to be a really great brunch spot you need to pay attention to the quality of your coffee. I hope they will work on this. Again, Ill say order the french toast, and try the salami/mustard omelette - its delicious and unexpected.
Despite the plastic-coated New York welcome so common these days (Hihowarrrryou is really not a word, let alone a question), even at a whopping $5, that cinnamon roll is extraordinary!

Exceptionally beautiful space with food to compliment. The house salmon is a must have in addition to the Cobb salad. Don't know why this place isn't 5 stars all around. Wow.
Blown away!

Suberb bagels. Some of the best house made, expertly hand-sliced smoked salmon and sable in NYC.  Beautiful space. Well trained service staff. Brunch Bloody Mary is the best I've ever had. An amazing experience. Don't miss the sticky buns, amazing cobb salad and first rate omelettes and egg dishes.
Amazing meal. Beautiful atmosphere. Delicious salmon Benedict. My daughter had the crispiest pancakes. And the side of sugar charred grapefruit was the most delicious thing I've ever had!

I came here for a unique experience and that's exactly what I got, a uniquely bad experience! Everything is so expensive and and not worth what you pay for. Place is trying to benefit of yuppies with their decor and lame paintings. Everything is so slow and place isn't near functional. I went to the bathroom and had to wait in a long line because they only have 2 small bathrooms for a place that seats maybe a 100 people. While on line I noticed the kitchen which was smaller than my kitchen which makes me think that the people running this are delusional if they think that kitchen can feed a full restaurant in a timely manner. Servers try to be helpful but from how everything is set up they are doomed for failure and a stressful day regardless. Basically everything about this place is "meh" and I would not ever come back again for the long waits and mediocre bagels. Try fooling people who have money to throw away for inferior quality everything.

One of the best bagels I've had here in NY! But the real star here is the house cured salmon, to die for. Service very attentive and knowledgeable. This was simply a very nice experience. The menu is brunch and the place looks very hipster gastropub ish'....Never heard of a breakfast/bagel place that takes reservations, after going I see why. Upscale and a touch pretentious hence the 4 star not 5. The sticky bun is good not great, could have been warmer?Didn't want to dress up to have bagels lox and coffee....

I had a bad experience at Sadelle's on my birthday.  I won't go into too many details, but the management at Sadelle's did everything they could to win me back as a customer and boy did they succeed.  Given the hospitality I've received I'll definitely be back for the delicious baked goods.  

Its a cool SoHo space where you are likely to spot a few celebrities. 

Comments on some of the items. 
+Sticky bus-  Amazing.  These have been on many best dishes lists for good reason. I believe my wife's quote was "This woman is a genius" when first eating them. 
+Chocolate Babka-  Wonderful, wonderful.  I think this passes the Breads bakery Babka which I previously regarded as the best in the city
+Bagels- An excellent example of a New York Bagel.  I prefer them to Black Seed which is overly influenced by the Montreal Style
+Blueberry Pancakes- Delicious If you want to stray from the smoked fish and bagels section
+House Salmon-Fresh and delicious
+Sable-Solid
+Whitefish Salad- Best example I've had. Wisely not over pulverized
+Coleslaw- A very good vinegar based version
+Tuna melt- I didn't eat it, but I heard wonderful things
+Grapefruit-Fresh and delicious
+French Toast.  I thought it was too sweet, I'd pass on this one
+Mimosa/Screwdriver- Fresh orange juice not soo booze heavy

Overall really wonderful food.  No everyone wants to spend a lot on bagels, but if you appreciate the best of this type of food, it is really worth it. 

The takeout counter is also a good option if you can't get a reservation
Favorite bagel spot in the city hands down. Fish is always fresh, presentation is beautiful and dishes are full of flavor.

We had a fantastic dinner here the other night. Let me start with my one complaint to get it out of the way... service was very confusing.  It was not that we were neglected, but we never saw the same person twice, so we had no idea who our waiter was or who to ask when we needed something. The ambience is beautiful and the vibe is upscale and extremely trendy. I did not feel quite cool enough to be dining here.  The table was too small for all of the things on it- candles, holder for silverware, etc, so it was a bit awkward and I kept knocking into things.

The food was outstanding.  The complimentary bread is really unique and delicious.  We had the scallops and chips as our appetizer-- what a fun idea and very well executed.  The Trout Franceska was probably my favorite fish dish I have ever had the pleasure of eating.  It was perfectly cooked and the beets were an interesting and delicious topping.  I also tried the fried chicken special (not on the menu but they have it in limited quantities- so ask!) that is served with hot sauce and honey and it was just amazing.  The cocktails, although expensive at $15 a pop, were well made and very well balanced.  We also enjoyed the cinnamon roll dessert with ice cream. I am not normally a cinnamon bun fan but this was mouthwateringly good.  Overall, a wonderful meal in a gorgeous restaurant.

Went here for brunch on a really cold morning and it was perfect. Walking into spacious yet cozy space with exposed brick and all the smoked salmons and bagels was amazing.

The food did not disappoint. You get unlimited bagels with chive cream cheese along with the thinly sliced cucumbers, red onions and tomatoes, it was perfect. I would definitely come back to NYC just to visit Sadelle's

Vibe: 10
Food: 10
Design: 10

We organized a large dinner at Sadelle's, were promised a private area that we didn't get. The service was terrible it took 30 minutes to open the wine because he had to run down the street to get a second bottle...meanwhile it was double per person what we paid at another restaurant and everything was below expectations except for the bread which was the best part of the dinner. They brought out way too much food, such a waste, and they couldn't even bring everything out together timing of the whole meal was terrible.

1 star for the poor service, long wait once seated and the extremely tight space you are provided to eat a relatively overpriced meal at.  Food is probably 3 stars - basic whitefish platter and egg sandwich...many other similar better Jewish style delis that are worthwhile. Try Russ & daughters instead for a much tastier and enjoyable dining experience!

Beautiful space, delicious food, adorable and wonderful waitress, good music and outstanding wine. That pretty much sums it up. We sat at the gorgeous main table in the middle.  My only complaint is that the music was super loud when we arrived. The table is huge so we felt very far away from our friends and had a difficult time hearing at first. But, after awhile the music was lowered or we acclimated I'm not sure which. It was smooth sailing from there...

Highlights: 

Bread. Not sure what it was, but a small loaf of something unique and delicious.
Oysters
Lobster 
tuna tartare- so different. I've given up ordering it because it always tastes the same, but not here and our waitress described it just right. 
Scallops
key lime pie
pineapple cheesecake
spice cake- non of the guys wanted this, but then they tasted it and thought it was the best dessert. 
wine- we ordered a dry Riesling from Germany that everyone loved, including my husband and he doesn't drink white. 

Very romantic and sexy. Loved.

Food was 4.5 stars, service was 3 stars, and truthfully its a bit overpriced for what it is. However, I enjoyed the bright and open atmosphere, and the food was truly good.

I love the presentation of the food in their signature towers. The food was delicious and I will definitely be back. The lox was delicious. The everything bagels are out of this world. Obviously bagels and cream cheese and fish are a must here.

Breakfast sandwiches were also great, especially the classic with challah toast and yummy runny egg yolk. I highly recommend getting the breakfast potatoes - they are fantastic. The food is definitely worth the wait and the trip. 

My only complaint is that the service was sub-par. Our server kept forgetting things (like bringing a coffee cup but forgetting to give us the actual coffee), and we were largely left alone. It's one of those places where it's impossible to flag down a server if you need something, and they rarely come by your table to check on you.

The food here is very good. However, the pricing and service are outrageously bad.

Went here to get breakfast take out. I had heard great things about the sticky buns so I wanted to try them out. There were two people in front of me on the take out line and it seemed like I was waiting forever. There is not a take out menu to look at while you wait. When i was finally able to order, I asked about the sticky buns since the menu they had at the register did not have the sticky buns listed. The cashier told me they were $5 a piece?! Seriously?! $5 for one very small sticky bun less than the size of a tennis ball?! What a complete ripoff!!! (especially since on the regular dining menu you can get 3 sticky buns for $8) Since I was already there and I had already waited on line forever, I ended up getting one, although I was bitter about it. I then proceeded to "wait for them to prepare my sticky bun", which was already made but just sitting behind the counter because they were busy preparing the complicated bagel orders that the people in front of me had placed. How inefficient! I was really quite offended by my whole take out experience. Needless to say i will not be ordering take out from here again.

I have also dined at Sadelle's for brunch on the weekend. It gets ridiculously busy because it's the newest trendiest brunch in Soho. It's kind of obnoxious. When you first get there you can barely enter the restaurant because there is a mob standing around the take out area. And people always go over their reservation time so the next party to be seated just stands in the entrance way waiting for their table. Its terrible. When we had finally made our way into the restaurant and pushed through the crowd of people and were able to be seated we were so relieved. We ordered coffee immediately. But the waiters kept walking past us despite our attempts at reminding them we had ordered coffee about 3 times and still had not gotten any. When the waiters finally paid attention to us we were able to order bagels, lox, and whitefish salad. The food was very good and the fish was fresh. They never told us that with our order we could have unlimited free bagels. When we tried to order more, we were again ignored. And again, when we tried to get the check, the same thing happened. Our waiter was nowhere to be seen and no one would help us. The service was outrageously bad.

The food was good but the entire experience from getting seated, to ordering, to enjoying our meal, was just overall very unpleasant.

Sadelle's, Sadelle's. We had a reservation with you, but you made us wait for half an hour--you're a hot spot, so we'll let that one slide.

But come on--don't pretend your magical bagel tower feeds two people when it feeds one and a half; six paper-thin slices of lox do not two sandwiches make. And half an avocado for $9? Say it isn't so.

But the real offense was how EXCEEDINGLY cold it was in your establishment--you basically kept the door open to let hoards and hoards of faux-couture Soho denizens linger near the hostess's table, just to tell them it would be an hour wait. I've been freezing--and hungry--all day. 

Here are some better choices to get your nova fix:

Black seed bagel
Russ and Daughter's
Any NYC bagel shop with some good schmear and smoked salmon.

Sorry, but I need to be honest--$21 for a bagel is not Instagram worthy, it's a little shameful.
Excellent food but not always easy to get a table, esp. on the weekends. Try the bagels with chives cream cheese

We went to dinner here last night and...mixed feelings. Our reso was at 9:15 and we were seated at 10pm, with no apologies no offer to get an appetizer or anything considering we got seated so late. Our waiter never smiled once and when we apologized for being frustrated and hungry he condescendingly told us he gets hungry too at the end of shifts. 

Cons:
a) we ordered two steaks and were told the restaurant doesn't carry steak knives
b) there are 6 entrees on the menu, one of them being a burger that 3 (out of 7 of us) were looking forward to ordering. when we finally were seated, were told they were out of the burger. why didn't you tell us you were out of an entree when we were waiting for our table??
c) almost everyone commented that the steak was way too salty
d) very slow service


Pros:
a) the restaurant itself is gorgeous inside
b) veal pelmeni were amazing
c) horseradish vodka was a definite must
d) russian potatoes amazing!

Oh sadelle's... The hype for this overpriced bagel and lox is one I've never seen before in my life...

Is it good, yeah it's pretty good. The Scottish salmon was very good... But how different could a regular smoked salmon be... Bagels were good, small but they gave you as many you wanted so that's definitely not a complaint...

I think you come here for the other things on the menu...

Oh the French toast. This was absolutely delicious. Idk what they do to this French toast, maybe smother it in liquid crack but it is amazing. We were double dipping it in the syrup and the preserve. You have to try it.

Don't get the tuna fish... I can make you better tuna fish if you come to my apt, just pick up some cans of tuna fish at the supermarket first.

I wanted to order the pigs in the blanket but I wasn't allowed. The others in my party thought I already ordered food for 8 and we were only 4. Soooo, I asked the table next to me if I could try one of theirs... And since this place is filled with giving people they said ok... And they we're great! The Russian dressing type sauce they give you to dip them in is great!

Bottom line: expensive but good! Give it a try and and get the Scottish salmon and the French toast and don't let others at your table influence your orders. Get everything you want everywhere you go, including the apricot vodka which again I was not allowed to order...

I'm not quite sure what the Torrisi crew is trying to accomplish here, but this is a bizarre operation. 
Sadelle's is primarily known for it's brunch. It appears to have attempted dinner, but if you've read the reviews, dinner has not fared so well. 
It offers a selection of bagels, accompanied by a variety of fish (like house cured salmon, tuna fish, etc), and salads. 
When you walk in during brunch time, on the weekend, you will typically be advised the wait is a couple of hours. The reason for this is unclear, as usually a few tables seem to be available, and there is a communal eating area which has some space, but nevertheless, that's what they say. Some people will walk in and get seated right away in the interim, so I'm not sure what rule they follow. 
I don't usually mention what the make up of a restaurants clientele are but, let's just say, there isn't much, if any, racial diversity to be seen. In fact, the only people who bring any diversity to the establishment are the ones working the counter, cutting the fish, bringing in the fresh bagels, cleaning the tables. I found it a bit jarring. 
After returning 2 hours later, I was advised by the maitre'd, a young woman with short cut hair, that I had actually been told I would be seated an hour beyond that time. I explained to her that was incorrect. She looked again and offered me another time, which was still 30 minutes away. Although there were plenty of tables available by then, I was promptly seated after waiting exactly 30 more minutes. Strange. 
After we sat, we ordered the house cured salmon and the tuna salad. This comes with a variety of bagels, you could let them know which one you want. I asked for coffee, it came without milk. I asked for milk, but the waiter never brought it, so I had to ask the attendant to get it for me. I explained I wanted skim milk, not regular. The attendant said ok, then turned back and asked me if I wanted skim or regular milk. Something like this happened twice, where the servers forget what you asked for merely seconds after being told!

The reason for two stars and not one? The bagels themselves were quite good, as was the house cured salmon. The tuna was not bad, but you can get tuna salad of this caliber in many places. The bagels were small, and chewy, which is how I prefer them. If you are an ess-a-bagel fan, you may not like these. 

So to sum it up, the food is good, but the service is just awful. If you read the other reviews, I think you see they would concur.  I would advise you come here and order something at the counter to go. The way it's run now though, I would not come back. 

I hope the Major Food Group is trying to run this as a restaurant, not as a "scene", because the bagels are quite good, and "scenes" don't last.

so I've been meaning to try this place since it opened and was hoping the reviews werent doing it justice. we arrived and placed our order rather quickly but probably waited almost 20-30 minutes for our bagels.

Yes they now sell babka by the slice! it was still yummy and really good. comparable to breads bakery but i am still partial to breads bakery.

i got the everything bagel with chive cream cheese, salmon and tomatoes. when i finally opened my bagel i found out that they messed up my order ]: they put capers and onions in it also. sigh i ate it anyways but have to say i prefer tompkins square bagels more. the bagel was cold and wasn't as soft as i wanted. so basically pretty average. i'm not sure it was worth hefty price tag.

Loved Sadelle's! 

I don't know how I have never heard of this place before - but I saw a snapshot of it on a gluten free Instagram account I follow (nobread) - they mentioned the lox and gluten free bagels, so of course I had to check it out!

Wow. Even better than I expected! The space is gorgeous. Big and open and lots of light, exposed brick, and turquoise accents.  We split their signature tower  - which is all of the cured fish plus unlimited (I got the gluten free) bagels and cream cheese. Heaven. 

My friends are not gluten free but they loved the bagels! I have never had a gluten free everything bagel, so this was very exciting. I also tried the greyhound, which is their vodka & house made grapfruit infused cocktail = delish! 

All in all, we had a fantastic experience. The waitress was very kind, and even offered to box up our leftover lox and sent us home with some extra bagels.  

I think the next time we do this, I would try to go with 6 people instead of 4, as we had enough left over for 2 more. Would make the tower slightly more cost effective as well. 

Thank you for an amazing brunch! We loved every minute of it.

The place is beautiful, and the food is very good.  But for what you pay here, it well should be.  There's a lot of bad communication going on here, especially in low traffic times.  With only two people behind the counter.  Over a dozen people in our office have had received incorrect orders.  Quality is very high, service very low.  If you're looking for breakfast to go in Soho you're better off at Olive's.

Waited for over an hour for a table and was eventually told there is no guarantee of getting a table. At the time of putting my name on the wait list I was specifically told it would be 15/20 mins. The host kept telling us we were next for a table. After as hour's wait she said she cannot say when we would get a table. Absolutely unacceptable. The food might be good the service is not!

Came here for lunch. 

Service was great. Really loved the waiter, he was friendly and helpful. My friend dropped her bagel by accident and he brought us 2 more to replace it free of charge. 

We got the salmon benedict and sable fish on everything bagels. Everything was absolutely delicious. Words cannot accurately describe. 

Sticky buns were also amazing and moist - only thing that could have been better if they were fresh out of the oven. The glaze was good and not too sweet (I also had a black coffee to balance that out to be fair). 

Decor was on point. Very classy atmosphere with beautiful open space and bright lighting.

BEST EVER!!! EVERYTHING IS 5 STAR, SERVICE, FOOD, VENUE!!  I couldn't have been more impressed.  Coffee is strong and wonderful.  Bloody Mary's were also strong and spicy!  We ordered Bagels, with the works and it comes on a 3 tier stand with the fresh lox on top sprinkle with fresh dill, the next tier had tomatoes and capers with hot house cucumbers sliced. Our waiter said an order for one was plenty for 2, and it comes with 2 bagels, We ordered the EVERYTHING 2.0 AND THE PLAIN BAGEL.  They were crunchy and fresh with chive cream cheese! I can't say enough about the ambiance and service, very attentive except it took awhile for the bloody marys, but we were fine!

Amazing! 
We went for Sunday brunch without a reservation. We had to wait awhile, but that's to be expected.
I ordered the smoked salmon with bagels and a side of the breakfast potatoes. We also got a Munster and mushroom omelet with a side of bacon. 
Everything was truly wonderful! 
The bagels were chewy and salty-the way a true New York bagel should be! I got everything bagels and put the chive cream cheese and smoked salmon on them. Everything about it was truly delicious. 
The omelet was one of the best I've ever tasted. Moist and cheesy and loaded with the most wonderful mushrooms. 
The bacon was thick and crispy (but not overall crispy). Cooked just right! 
The potatoes were so flavorful! Really great! 
We all got the fresh squeezed orange juice as well, which was nice and refreshing. 

Can't wait to go back to Sadelles!!!

Summary: fancy deli 

Pros:
1. Unlimited bagels 
2. Great ambiance 
3. Free drinks and food because of long wait 

Cons:
1. Over 50 minute wait despite having a reservation 
2. Unapologetic hostesses for long wait 
3. Everything you can get at a regular deli, no specialties or interesting meals
4. Very busy so you have to flag down waiters multiple times 

Tips: 
1. You will get pretty full on unlimited bagels and cream cheese, so I wouldn't get more than 1-2 plates of fish (depends on people in your party). 
2. Bring a book/kindle/newspaper to accompany you on the wait. 
3. Order everything you think you might want when you have the chance- waiter might not be back for a while! 

Conclusion: I'm glad I tried it but I wouldn't return

*Recommend with caution*

What a lovely place. It's def crazy expensive for my tastes. But it was a delight to be treated there by my boss for my birthday. A tower of great bagels, really!!! And then we had a plate of salmon, and white fish, tomatoes and onions. Then a healthy egg salad sand which and fresh salad. Simple foods....all served SOOO fresh. Thanks 6 Shore Road

This is a super cute, trendy, very popular deli restaurant - of course there is going to be a wait. Its New York. Great spot to bring out of towners - it feels much more exciting and new than most brunch spots in the city. Plus with the unlimited bagels, you will be sure you are leaving very full. Enjoy sharing a lox platter with the chive cream cheese on an everything bagel. Lox is very fresh and perfectly seasoned. Everyone from the host to the busser was very helpful and accommodating. As a pair, we sat at the long communal table in the center of the room. Great for eavesdropping and sharing a laugh with your neighbor. Apart from the wait, there was a small dog in the booth behind us.... kinda odd. Also kept barking.

Sadelle's is very good. One of the better bagels and smoked fish in NYC.

That said, the size of their bagel is unacceptable for a $17 smoked fish platter. 

WARNING: it is a myth that Sadelle's serves unlimited bagels. They have recently implemented a policy where it is ONE bagel per each order of smoked fish. With their tiny bagels, this policy may be the beginning of the end of the once great new establishment. 

Tourists and first-timers will continue to go, however it would be hard to justify returning if the meal consists of only one bagel and smoked platter. Unless they significantly increase the size of the bagel, this policy effectively ends everything that was great about Sadelle's.

We went for a thursday brunch and overall everything was good. They had one of the best steak tartares I've ever had (a must!). Salmon benedict's eggs were cold but they were really nice about it. The service is really good, and they're friendly.

Wow the best meal we have had so far in NYC! We had the most delicious brunch. We had the house salmon tower, the French toast and a side of potatoes. All were amazing and bursting with flavors. Our server Austin was awesome! He was friendly, attentive, warm, welcoming and efficient!

Just had breakfast here first thing this morning. Table service starts a bit later, but that was fine for my wife and I. It's a bit of an enigma having foods typically found on the lower east side, here in the Soho district of the lower west side. It's a welcome addition to be sure, but quite unexpected in this fashion plate neighborhood. The interior space is gorgeous wide open bright and inviting. Nice architectural appointments and subtle details for a warm atmosphere. The early morning routine is to order at the counter and use the lower level seating at the front. Quite comfortable to dine on a breakfast bagel with cream cheese and lox, coffee, OJ. I would definitely return to check out the buzzing lunch hour or even a supper. Authentic Eastern European food like real New York Jewish Bagels and lox, but throw in the postmodern pastiche of a refined eatery in the heart of SOHO fashion district and you've got an unusual gem a bit rough around the edges but that's the appeal. Formal or casual, you decide, no one will judge. Rumor has it the Bobka pound cake is to die for, I was too full up to order that maybe another time. Think of it as a Deli counter from the old fashioned New York 2nd avenue deli with a fancy schmancy restaurant adorned with skylights that sprung out from it. It's quite unusual. But the food A+. If you're  in the neighborhood stop in try it, can't go wrong with a decent bagel here especially if that's your thing.

The service sucks. The food was OK, i would rather just go to a regular Deli than deal with the annoying scene there. Super cramped and I don't think I will be back. Way to much hype for this place will probably be an average restaurant in like a year.

Visited here for Sunday brunch having seen it on a blog I follow. The only booking I could get was for 4pm. When we turned up we did have a bit of a wait for a table despite many tables being empty. 

When we did get our table we quickly ordered the house salmon and Scottish and some bagels. My friend is gluten free and she said the bagels were really good and served warm. I went for a sesame seed bagel which did not disappoint. 

The Scottish salmon was slightly oilier than the house and the selection of tomatoes and onions and cucumber was good. We ordered plenty of bagels and were not charged extra! Bagels galore. 

The mimosas were large and went down a treat. Around 5 the place started to close wih all the staff heading upstairs to where we were for there food. 

I loved that you could see where the bagels were made. 

A great spot.

Went here for brunch and I liked it a lot. I got a smoked salmon bagel. It comes as a tower with different toppings and home made bagels which are great. The decor is also super nice! Prices are a little off but for a place like that in that location it is pretty much in line with every other place.

I would come back there for brunch.

Seems like this place should be in midtown or perhaps they should visit Russ and Daughters to learn how it's done. Bagels are good but service is not much different than camera store on 44th and Broadway trying to rip off tourists.

My family and I went to Sadelle's after longing to go for forever last Sunday! We couldn't get a reservation, but got a response via email that we could walk in and wait. We did just that and waited 2 hours until we were seated...if not a little longer. 

My suggestion is to stay nearby, as you don't want them to either forget you or for other's to be taken ahead of you. I noticed that other people before us were being seated (same size party) until finally the hostess caught on that I noticed her seating a party that hadn't been waiting nearly as long as we had. 

We sat upstairs, which was really nice because we were able to get our own table and not have to sit in the communal seating area next to everyone else. There were a lot of celebrities there that day, including Leonardo DiCaprio and Nikki Hilton, so I am not sure if this screwed up our service, but we didn't have the best service to be frank. 

We were seated and immediately greeted; however, our server's iPhone (they place everyone's orders via iPhone) was not working properly and he disappeared for a good 20 minutes. Following that, he returned and forgot our drink order and apologized and said he would be back with it after we placed our order. Those drinks never ended up coming until mid-way through our meal, and our server was nowhere to be found!! 

Anyway, 

You CANNOT go to Sadelle's without ordering their infamous French Toast. By far the BEST french toast i've ever had in my life. We ended up getting two!! Beyond delicious, and i would go back there just for that alone! Get extra maple syrup on the side...you will not regret it! ;) 

We ordered their Salmon Platter...little did we know it only comes with ONE bagel...so keep that in mind...i'm sure you can get more for an additional cost. Their bagels are mediocre...I've definitely had better bagels than Sadelle's...especially in NYC. 

My sister has been here multiple times, and time and time again she gets their Mediterranean Salad that was delicious (for a healthier choice). Their salad portions are quite large, so you're definitely able to share this with another person if not overly starving. 

This place is definitely a scene and experience...would I wait again? Maybe...but I am glad I tried it!

Huge space for breakfast,,lunch 
Was v surprised and disappointed that they don't serve proper cappuccino,, 
Bagels were tasty,, great salmon,, but all in all, its not a place i would return to!

First time here. And wonderfully surprised.  The food is great and the device is on point.  It is worth the extra money for the device and quality of food and environment    I would say similar to Balthazar but a much nicer space and not as noisy. A must

The brunch here is amazing. Highly recommend Sadelle's Tower, which comes with a variety of fish, tomatoes, onions, and spreads along with unlimited bagels. I went with a group of 5 and we couldn't finish all of the food, but we also ordered sides of bacon and eggs, so keep that in mind as it is a lot of food.

Overall setting of the restaurant is great for spring/summer when the door is open, lots of good lighting and seating for groups. Service was a bit slow at times because it gets really busy, but the staff is very friendly and accommodative. The staff even offered us complimentary sweet buns at the end of our meal from the bakery.

Ever walk around SoHo wondering were to eat?  Stop wondering... and eat salad!  This great spot has (giant and expensive) salads as well as salmon and bagels on a stick!  Seriously, better than it sounds.

Have been looking forward to trying this place, finally got a shot.

THE GOOD
Great schmear, soft, creamy, spreadable with lots of scallions.

The bagels were top notch. Nice crisp crust, just the right amount of chewiness, soft on inside. It's been said before, but the bagels served on the wooden post is a cool presentation. wouldn't matter if the bagels weren't good, but they were excellent. You can climb the stairs and watch them being made in the little booth, hand cut and boiled in the boiling pot right there.

Smoked Scottish salmon hand carved super thin, smoky deliciousness, tender, not stringy.

My wife got scrambled eggs which were good, but boy those accompanying potatoes were awesome. Might not be to everyone's taste, but I loved em. Sorta like potato bark, with carmelized onions, sun dried tomatoes

Really nice interior, cool art on the walls flowers etc..in an open loft.

THE BAD
I would have given them five stars but for this...

They were out of Matzoh Ball Soup! At 10:30 AM, WTF?? In a Jewish deli?? Was anticipating a nice warm bowl on a chilly, rainy morning. When I asked how long it would be before more got made, the reply was later this afternoon or probably tomorrow. Double WTF???
Best lox & cream cheese bagel I've ever had.

Let's talk about perfection for a minute. Very few times in a lifetime will you encounter perfection in food. Usually you find them in the simple pleasures of life or by someone who totally believes in their craft. The bagel and lox at Sadelles is just that...perfection. 

Despite the poor score on Yelp, this place came highly recommended to me by multiple friends in NYC so I had to make a stop. I'm trying to figure out why this place ranks so low, maybe the high price point for fish or how it's conceptually different than most bagel/lox favorites in NYC. Regardless, I thought the food was superior to any other I've had in this amazing city. 

My buddy and I ordered the two types of lox: Scottish smoked and Atlantic cured. They were both amazing in their own right and completely different in texture and flavor. The Scottish being saltier and smokey, while the Atlantic was fattier and delicate. The house made bagels were so proper it hurts. I had one of the everything bagels and made two different open faced sandwiches to properly explore both fishes. Heaven. 

Go here. Be patient. It's way better than you would think based on previous reviews. Boom.

My most favorite brunch place in NYC. They say presentation is key and Sadelles really knows how to present. I ordered the lox and bagel and the salmon was DELICIOUS. Super tasty and thinnnly cut. It was amazing. There is a super long wait if you don't have a reservation - thank god we did. 

I wish they had a place like this in LA because I would love to go weekly for brunch!

I enjoy all establishments created by the Major Food Group. I learned of Sadelle's a couple of years ago when a stand was set up at the San Gennaro festival in front of Parm on Mulberry. Anyway their baked goods are good but you have to eat them basically when you get them as they're best, like most things, when they're fresh. The space is beautiful and I was really eager to try their dinner menu. I finally made it there and loved it - so different from their morning scene and the food was better than I thought it would be. I could not have imagined I would enjoy dinner at what I classify as a bakery to be so delicious! We started with the salmon rillette which was a salmon tartare accompanied by toast and the curry lobster which is basically lobster presented in the shell (already de-shelled) with extremely subtle curry flavor) that was light and fresh tasting. For the mains we had the trout franceska and the club burger. The dishes seemed to be a nice fusion of Russian and Italian flavors. Key lime pie for dessert was not particularly memorable but that was our only option at the end of the night. Am definitely interested in trying their other seafood plates and repeat the order of the burger.

So regarding only dinner only here: the ambiance is super cool with all the candles and the brick and high ceilings and stuff, but the menu needs some work. The vodka and caviar shtick is great, but the rest feels a bit random. Nothing was bad, it just didn't feel like it belonged together. I can see it being fun for an early-stage date or a high-budget business dinner

Just had a good bagel even though it was small,
Bagels are good prices are Super High!
The most enjoying was the waiting time,
We been told 15 min ending up waiting a crazy 1 hour outside!
Hostess was not nice and was very impolite.
I don't think i will get back in there with so many nice places around!

This is an odd place.

We came here based on nymag's rave: "Best Fried Chicken in NYC!!" Then, lo and behold, there is no fried chicken on the menu. A few panicky inquiries later, we learned that they were indeed serving it that night. We breathed easier. 

But since it ain't a fried chicken place, what is it? Jewish deli comes to mind... but there's no corned beef to be found. It's kinda Eastern European, but not like Veselka. Eventually, I stopped fretting and settled down to order the fried chicken and the gravlax to start. And -- man, oh, man -- that was the right call. The gravlax was amazing, paper-thin, served with delicious buttered rye toast points that provided just the right amount of support. God, it was incredible. 

The fried chicken was very good. I appreciate the whole brining effort, and it was quite tasty, if not just a little too... messy. (I'm trying to not use the word "moist," but, OK, I said it. It was too moist!) Especially with all of its accompaniments (honey | hot sauce | even the delicious Russian dressing left over from my partner's Pigs in a Blanket), I wished that it was just a little, um, crispier.

Don't know whether or not they have dessert... we rolled our well-fed selves out of the place before finding out. But we'd go back.

Save your money and don't believe the hype. My friend and my cousin were really excited to try this place so one of them made a reservation for 3:15pm on a Sunday because it was the only time available. However, when we arrived on time, we had to wait more than 30 minutes to be seated. When we finally sat down it took about 10 minutes for a waiter to arrive. He was very charming. No problem with him. But we were told that several of the pastries on their menu - pastries we had read about and wanted to try - were gone. He said he found us the last sticky bun and we split it 3 ways. It was okay. My friend ordered the eggs and salami which the waiter recommended. She then found a long black hair in it and sent it back. SheI had also ordered a bagel, which never came, so she asked for that again. It took a while but it finally arrived.  My cousin had the matzoh ball soup and didn't seem impressed. I had the lox with a bagel, which came on a big presentation. They included the onions even though I said I didn't want them but at least I was able to separate them from the tomatoes and cucumbers. The bagel was fine (smaller than the usual NY variety and less doughy but that can be a good thing sometimes). The lox was alright, but I didn't see the big deal about this place except that it's in SoHo and they make everything look pretty. We wanted the babka for desert but THAT was all gone, too, and the nice waiter found us one remaining slice to share. All in all, if you want fancy bagels and lox go to Russ and Daughters. Or just go to Murray's and eat outside on a bench. You'll have a much better meal for a small fraction of the cost and you won't feel ripped off.

Amazing!!! My favorite brunch in NY! 

+Two options of gluten free bagels
+Chive cream cheese is bomb
+Smoked salmon among other options
+Cucumbers
+Extra thin red onions
+Cute decor and ambiance

More please!

There is absolutely nothing bad I can say about this place. The service was great and the breakfast food is outstanding. Lox and Nova are incredible and even the potatoes that come with the eggs are awesome! The Bloody Marys were also top notch.

It can get crowded so make a reservation. Enjoy!

I love Sadelle's. I know it's very sceney and the crowd is probably the worst NYC has to offer because of people who go for the instagram...but the food is just too good. I am also obsessed with the decor and old russian crystal, so huge points there. Be prepared to wait a long time if you don't have a reservation. Good thing is there is always a bagel counter.

I've been enough times to say this really is a great restaurant. Here are my recommendations:

-House salmon: it's why you came. order salt and pepper bagels, everything 2.0 bagels and chive cream cheese and you're good to go. extra capers.
-salami and eggs: great option if you're not into carbs/fish
-pigs in a blanket: so so so tasty, the sauces are great 
-white fish salad: order this with the house salmon and you'll leave feeling happy
-STICKY BUNS: DON'T BE STUPID, ORDER THESE.
-FRENCH TOAST: DON'T BE STUPID, ORDER THIS.

Best bloody mary's in the city - you must order one if you're into it!

The food is so good but the service is still lacking. No gluten free bagels during a busy Saturday brunch service... That was why I went there in the first place. Our server suggested I call ahead to reserve gluten free bagels next time. My suggestion is they make enough for their busy brunch service. My companions struggled to get served their normal unlimited non-gluten free bagels. They didn't run out but our server was too busy pouring wine and fattening his checks and was uninterested with clearing plates or checking in. In fact he was only accessible when it was time to pay. Then he really turned it on & one thing I dislike about they payment process is they stand over you while you tip them. In any case you do the right thing and give 20%. Despite horrible service and eating lox off a cucumber rather than a gluten free bagel we still had a good time. Can't let poor service ruin a beautiful afternoon.

Their gluten free bagels are the real deal! I've tried many others in NYC that were just generic bread with holes in the middle. Sadelle's actually captures the crisp outside and chewy interior that I remember from my "normal" bagel days. The flavorful everything variety is completely covered in seeds, and the house smoked salmon complements it well. 

The restaurant is more focused on stylish brunch than grab-and-go breakfast, but the bakery counter is still convenient. Staff seemed a little distracted and tended to congregate in the back - not sure if that changes as they get busier. I arrived shortly after they opened, but was told the GF bagels wouldn't be ready for another 20 minutes. 

GF bagels are kept in separate drawers away from the regular baked goods. Not sure about cutting board cross-contamination since I was the first customer of the day.

Sadelle's has delicious gluten-free bagels made fresh on the premises, in both plain and everything. But it puzzles me why they don't take a few simple steps to be friendlier to the gluten free: a dedicated cutting board and toaster for the gluten-free bagels would be very easy to add. Also, they used to store the gluten-free bagels separately, but last time I went they had changed this. WHY? 

Note: I have only ever ordered at the counter.

two words: STICKY BUNS!  Honestly, everything I ordered was amazing.  Beverly salad, smoked salmon, salami and eggs, white fish, and the sticky buns. Everything was so fresh and flavorful. The ambiance is fun and upbeat and they didn't rush you out at the end of the meal.

Actually the worst service I have ever seen. A reservation will do you absolutely no good you will still wait an hour. We spoke with the manager and it was clear she didn't care at all. In fact, they have several "managers" at all times so that no one has to take responsibility.

--------------------Edit------------------

Upon posting this review someone from the restaurant reached out to make things right. They brought me and my brother in for an experience on them. They say us right away and the service was amazing. Our server was friendly and attentive and gave us some good suggestions. In terms of food this is one of the best breakfast places I have ever been to. I usually don't like lox but they have something truly special here.

Stopped in for brunch with the family on Saturday morning.  Make a reservation, or you'll be stuck waiting for quite some time on the weekends. We arrived early (around 9:30am) and there were already people waiting.

We ordered the fish tower and some other side items. Everything was fresh and beautifully plated. While the food was delicious, it was quite pricey.

The service was en pointe and the decor is quaint. I'd suggest it for special occasions, but not a regular weekend brunch.
Pretentious ,expensive with mediocre food and service...Don't order Freddy salad: Shrimps , in mine , were laced with chlorine.

Tip: If it is nice out, and there are a million tourists lined up in front of the door to be seated, SKIP the LINE and head to the take out counter which is to the right of the restaurant when you walk in. You can order pretty much all the essentials and not have to deal with a wait...

I love their salmon salad and whitefish salad. I usually get a bagel with one of those and  tomato, cucumber, onion & capers - YUMMY. 

Their bagels are freshly made in house which gives them a great taste. 

SKIP THE LINE - GO TO THE TAKEOUT COUNTER :)

Brunching on weekdays needs to happen more often! I'm sure what would have been an hour or so plus wait on a busy weekend was only about 10 minutes for our party of 6.

This restaurant is definitely one of those places where the stars on its Yelp page don't do it justice at all. As a group we agreed that it deserved much more than the measly 3 1/2 stars it's garnered with last reviewers and honestly am a bit shocked because this place really is that good!

The restaurant itself is an open plan and with the door open the whole restaurant feels airy and cool as if you're sitting outside on a patio somewhere.

This place is known for their bagel and lox. The bakery is at the front of restaurant and you can see the staff cutting up fresh salmon into thin slivers. You can also smell the scent of fresh bagels which is amazing. 

Now let's get to the real heart of this review: the food! I ordered the "eggs any style" which comes with potatoes and your choice of bagel (I got the everything bagel). The bagel was as delicious as it smelled. Paired with the chive and garlic cream cheese, it was the perfect combination. The eggs and potatoes were prepared perfectly, which something as simple as scrambled eggs and potatoes a lot of brunch places have a hard time mastering. 

Also under their specials they have French toast. This French toast was by far the BEST I've had in the city, and yes that's a bold statement to make and I'm okay with that! We were originally planning on going to Jane which is around the corner for their French toast, but honestly this placed blew me away with theirs. The perfect combination of sweet and decadent. You don't even need to dip it in the maple syrup/ jams they bring out.

I'm so glad we were able to walk in on a random weekday. Another great NYC brunch experience to add to the list!

Yes, the bagels are very, very good. The whitefish salad is excellent. I just can't justify the absurdly high prices for what is passably good at the bagel place down the street, despite my love of both food and fancy things. If you're going to go (which means you have more cash to burn than I do, and I'm jelly) the everything 2.0 is excellent and super fennel-y, and pairs great with the whitefish salad and any smoked fish. I pay rent so will continue to indulge my love for carbs and smoked fish at La Bagel Delight.

Bagels were delicious, especially with the smoked salmon and all of the accoutrements. The
place is very cute.  The Bloody Mary was very sour and disappointing. I would not recommend it. The Rosé was quite good. Long wait time even with a 3pm reservation.

went    the  other   day  to  try  these   outstanding   bagles      hand     rooled  that     i  read   a  great  deal  about   


the  guy   at  the  counter  was   great   he  let  me  taste   a  sample   of  the  smoked   salmon  that  i  liked   so  i   asked  him  to  give   me  a  poopy   bagel  with   salomn  and  cream  chees   and   i  said  i  will   have   2  onion  and   two   poopey    bagels  plain  i  said  i  wil use  the  mens  room  and  i  will  be  right  back   


i  came   back  and   he  said  my  total   order  was   28   dollars  i  said  wow   i  asked  how  much  for  the  bagel  with  cream  cheese  and  salom  n  


he  said  18   dollars     i  said  i  do  not  want   to  pay  that  much  for  the  bagel   and  i  do  not  want  it   

   i  said  i  will  take  the  four  bagels  that   were   just  plain  with nothing  on   it  i  asked  how  much  for  each  bagel   he  said  2   dollars  each   

i  gave  him  a  20   dollar  bill  he  said  we  do  not  take  cash   on  credit  cards   


i  told  him  have   a  nice  day  and  left  with  no  bagels  

this  palace   really  over      charges  and  it  was  my  first   time  and  my  last   i  will   never  go  back  in  there  again    


they  are   a  rip  off   overpriced

So excited to come from Boston and eat at Sadelle's. Lucky my family had an 11:30 reservation. Unlucky for us we waited. Why? Because they took too many walk-ins. Not acceptable when you made a reservation. Place is fun and lively. Must admit I do not like being squished into a tiny table when ordering a lot of food. Hard to really enjoy the food when you are beyond cramped. Loved the grapefruit cocktail, a bit pricey but delicious especially when it isn't grapefruit season. I ordered the salmon salad. Beautiful presentation but beyond salty. The overpowering topping took away from the taste of the smoked salmon.  A word to the wise don't order an everything bagel with this as you will have salt with salt. Would love to go back and try some different things,not have to wait with a reservation and have a little elbow room. Maybe even tell them I am on a sodium free diet.

Came here for brunch on a Friday and made a reservation that morning on OpenTable. Charming location but probably won't be a regular. 

We both ordered tuna fish salad and shared a piece of chocolate babka 

Tuna was very good, comes with a bagel of choice, plain/scallion cream cheese, sliced cucumbers, onions, tomatoes and capers. The bagels were good but not amazing. I prefer puffier/more doughy bagels (like Murray's) and these were a bit more compact and smaller. 

The waiter was very nice and we were seated next to the room they hand roll the bagels in so that was run. Ambiance is lovely and the service and presentation is top notch but everything is a bit overpriced. I saw cinnamon buns were $14 and I'm still wondering why? 

The chocolate babka was not on the menu, fortunately I had read about it so was able to ask. It was good but the one at Bread Bakery is better.

Sadelle's
We were the oldest people there by far (except for the parents of 20 somethings who were dragged there from Long Island) this time instead of rompers everyone was wearing an off the shoulder chambray dress and a goyard bag. Why make the reservation if you need to wait for the table? We waited 10 mins. after our reservation for the table. We booked this a month out. 
Bloody Marys took 15 mins. But when it came it was the best Bloody Mary we ever had. It had just the right amount of horseradish. 
Why call an item on the menus "the tower" if everything comes on a tiered platter tower. 
Now for the food. We ordered smoked salmon, whitefish, regular and chive cream cheese, and bagels (sesame and everything). The bagels were small but tasty. I know salmon was for 1 but the portion could have been more although it tasted amazing. It made me think about how some people eat lox-smaller amounts "schmeared" into the cream cheese as opposed to piling it on top.  Salty but not too salty. Chive cream cheese was smooth in texture and easy to spread.  The capers were awesome.  The tomatoes, cucumbers and onions were well seasoned. For dessert, the babka was sweet but not too sweet and had a not too buttery taste (I will always be partial to Breads for babka sorry). The tables were small like 18" round it's hard to fit everything on it I felt like I was at a war with Gravity. 
Next time postmates will deliver it. Or we will do pick-a-bagel.

We had an excellent brunch experience at Sadelle's! 
To start with, the place is beautiful!! We were luckily seated right next to the bagel bakery that has clear Windows for you to observe the baker make the bagels, from boiling them to baking them to placing them on sticks to be delivered directly onto the tables! Excellent!! 
We were 4 of us, and I am glad my friend dissuaded me from ordering a salad. She said we came here for the tower! Our tower for 4 was a gorgeous display of lox, white fish salad, salmon salad, saddle fish, sturgeon and tomato and cucumber slices with capers and dill! A gorgeous display of delicate super brunch food!! The tower comes with whipped plain cream cheese, scallion whipped cream cheese and bagels (plain, sesame, poppy, everything, and gluten free in needed +$2 for the gluten free!). 
For dessert, if you believe we were still hungry for it... We shared a slice of the decadent chocolate bakba (covered with a chocolate sauce) and a sticky bun!! Both were amazingly sweet, salty, buttery, and fluffy! 
Our waiter was Mitchell and he was fantastic! 

Our experience was amazing from the food to the service to a beautiful time spent with friends! 

The place get really packed during the weekend, make sure you have a reservation.

A lot of hype, didn't full live up to it. Bagels and lox were tasty but bagels were a bit small. A lot of waiting in between placing order and food actually arriving. People seem very into their Instagram of the food there as opposed to eating the food itself. Would've liked to try the babka but they were out. I prefer a place where you can order a little of this and a little of that versus an entire plate of pancakes. We also waited an additional 30 minutes past our reservation time.

High end appetizing/brunch experience. Everything is fresh. It's a nice change from the typical brunch places with eggs Benedict and gluten free granola. Reviving a trip to grandma's house, with exceptional service. Sticky buns are a crime.

A few months ago, we were walking around SOHO and my daughter decided that she needed to use the bathroom.....NOW! I looked for the nearest, clean restaurant and there was Sadelle's. As I walked through the restaurant, I saw towers and towers of delicious looking smoked fish. When we came out of the bathroom, the hubby and I decided that on the first kid free day, we would come to Sadelle's.

Well that day has come! We thought we would try to come on a weekend, but that was out of the question. It is impossible to get in without a reservation and you can't make a reservation on short notice. We ended up going during the week for brunch.

When we arrived, we were quickly shown to a table near the back. The restaurant is beautiful, with skylights throughout the building. Our waiter was great and made some really terrific recommendations.

We had:

- 2 tier tower of scotch salmon, sturgeon and fresh vegetables

- salt and pepper bagel

- everything bagel

- challah bread toast

- coffee

Everything was terrific! The vegetables were super fresh and sprinkled with dill. The capers were delicious and not too salty. The cream cheese was great (regular and scallion). The bagels are made by hand in the restaurant. The jelly for the challah bread toast tasted freshly made.

All in all a great dining experience!

Came here for breakfast with a friend on Sunday at his recommendation. He mentioned this is his go-to spot to take friends from out of town (like me!) so I'm glad he suggested it, otherwise I would have never found this place on my own.

We had reservations for bright and early at 8:30 am when they opened, and I'm really glad we did, because it seemed like a pretty popular spot. There were a couple groups waiting for a table by the time we left around 9:30.

The restaurant is pretty large and feels airy and well lit. There is a small take out counter at the front for those who want to stop by quickly and grab a bagel to go as well as the fish slicing counter where you can watch the professionals expertly slice thin pieces of salmon and other fish.

My friend and I got seated immediately, and we both ordered the house salmon. Essentially they give you thin slices of the fish served in this cute little tower along with some additional toppings (onions, tomatoes, capers, and cucumbers) at the bottom. You can order as many bagels as you want to eat with the toppings (we each got two!), and once you spread some of that delicious chive cream cheese on, you're set for a delicious bagel meal! 

I'm far from a bagel connoisseur (in fact I barely eat them on my own), but I found myself enjoying each bite of this bagel more than I expected to. There was a perfect balance of fish to bagel to other toppings. 

I forgot all the different types of bagels they offer, but my friend had two plains, and I had one sesame and one everything bagel.

This place was a bit on the pricey side though. I paid $24 after tax and tip for what essentially amounted to two bagels.

Great salt and pepper bagels. We went for brunch - maybe should have ordered the Scottish smoked salmon instead of he house lox? A "healthy" egg white sandwich was unfortunately smothered in butter. Coffee was nice and strong, oj freshly squeezed.

This is my favorite brunch in the city. The Melissa's sticky buns are outrageously good- buttery with the salted caramel sauce and not dry at all. The cured fish/lox are perfectly thinly sliced and the tower with the bagel and fixings is also very well executed. Decor wise- the space is very well done. A mix of industrial with open kitchen and high ceilings with exposed brick, French Provençal touches (le creuset, flower arrangements) and the modern art- it's an all around very well executed restaurant.

Had a wonderful dinner with great friends and family. It was a hot summer night and we walked into this open air restaurant with lighted candles from top to bottom.  As we are greeted by our fantastic waitress and began sipping fantastic cocktails and beer a great evening was on its way.  Our appy's were delicious followed by a tasty meal ending with ice cream filled cinnamon buns.  Definitely a place  not to miss.
Really good food, every dish was tasty. The fried chicken and veal dumplings stood out. Cool atmosphere. A bit expensive but relatively speaking, it was a good meal and worth a visit

Stopped in here with my father visiting from out of town on a weekday afternoon. Classic Jewish fare done in a deliciously modern way. Bloody Mary is strong (I think it's a lot of olive juice) but solid. I'd say it's not for everyone. Bagels are made in-house and excellent. I had the lox -- thinly sliced and fresh. Dad had the tuna -- no complaints from him (note: he's picky). Definitely check this out. I'm sure they don't like comparisons to Russ & Daughters, but I'd say just as good. Definitely will be back.
Heavenly smoked salmon sandwich, with all the fixings, on the everything 2.0 bagel! That's all I had and I couldn't have been more satisfied.

My boyfriend and I got take out here this morning and loved it. First of all, wait was only 40 minutes which in comparison to competitors, is relatively short. However, we opted for takeout which only took 15 minutes. Our smoked salmon bagel sandwiches were awesome and they have house  baked, GF everything bagels! Unreal. Other than the price ($18) for my sandwich, everything was great.

There were no fires. No offenses. No particular conflicts. But Sadelle's simply did not justify its price. 

As a longstanding customer at Russ and Daughters' (and now its restaurant), I've gotten used to the premium price of bagels and lox. Heck, as a native New Yorker who grew up on H&H and Zabar's, I feel like I've seen it all. But unlike those places, Sadelle's lacks the history, the atmosphere, the SPIRIT; consequently they are unable to give the level of respect that should be given to the once-humble-now-trendy 'Jewish Brunch'.

The bagels were fine. Fresh, chewy, and well taken care of. The Scottish Salmon was anemic (even by Russ' miserly standards), and the whitefish was much too salty for my companions' palates. There more and more I think about it, everything we got (going up the list in price) only left the impression that it was too pricey - and that the final bill was neither justified nor even deserved.

Service? Just OK. Look, they're busy. They look busy. You can see it in the whites of their eyes. I felt sorry for them. 

This is the kind of place that makes me wonder why do we even do brunch these days. To hang out in a group? To pick up the tab in order to make the most of those 3x points credit card? There is no social bonus here, no culinary revelation, no inspiration.

Look. Invite some friends over, pick up some bagels from your favorite place, and put together a bounty that is two or three times generous for the price you pay here. This place reminds me of what is the most forgotten about food - the fact that you can take charge and do it yourself.

[Last visit: Sept. 11, 2016]

Came on a Sunday for a bagel, was told they had no salmon. What kind of spot that's known for its bagels doesn't have any type of salmon on a Sunday morning?  I just left.  Sidenote: definitely saw it right behind the counter.

Amazing place, I went here a few weeks ago and can't stop talking about it. My waitress was so nice and was willing to take pictures of me and my friend ( no matter how many times we needed re-dos). The bagels are honestly outstanding, and the lox and white fish was amazing. Even the iced coffee was good! Please don't hesitate, just go!!

This place is really beautiful but honestly I'd rather have bagels and pastries from the deli with my family - less hustle and bustle + same quality of food.

Things we ate at Saturday brunch:

1. Bagels - sesame was A-OK, though on the small side. These come complimentary with any order of smoked fish.

2. Smoked salmon - good but, as many have said, not as good as Russ & Daughters.

3. Salmon salad - I always shy away from fish salads since they end up overly mayonnaise-y, but Sadelle's got this RIGHT. This dish came with everything seasoning and a bit of hardcooked egg yolk on top and I wanted to devour the whole thing (but didn't - you're welcome, lovely dining companions).

4. Pickles - yum! Briney, and crisp rather than soggy. But also they cost $6, when I kinda feel like they should be free.

5. Chocolate babka - dry.

6. Sticky bun - THIS was sweet, dense and delicious. Recommend eating with a knife and fork to avoid sticky fingers.

Even if the concept of this restaurant were more appealing to me (Ashkenazic comfort food in fancy, airy SoHo setting - seems just incongruous somehow), Sadelle's would still deserve 3*. Our waiter seemed impatient to take our order and did a poor job of explaining the menu and making recommendations.

The bathroom situation was also a bit ridiculous - found myself waiting in line for 15 minutes when one of the coed WCs was mysteriously locked. These bathrooms are in a narrow hallway that leads to/from the kitchen, so this area was quite congested and all of us were unhappy to be there.

Great place!
Super friendly and welcoming straff.
We felt so welcome!
Beautiful interior and they make their own bagels!
Bagels are smaller than usual but wonderfully chewy! 
They only have regular coffe- I would have loved a latte with my yummy bagel:)
Will definitly make this my regular NY breakfast place!

The food here are amazing! The bagels are sooo good. We ordered the Scottish salmon, the salmon benedict, and french toast. All were delicious. My favorite was the bagel with lox of course. U get this beautiful spread to build your perfect bagel with lox to your taste! 

The place is packed so make sure you make reservations ahead of time because even with reservations we had to wait. Awesome spot for brunch!

Best to make reservations during the weekend, this is a great place for brunch if you happen to be shopping in SoHo around West Broadway, it gets really packed during the weekend so I suggest getting there around 9 am no later than 9:30 am or there will be at least a 30 min wait, if you don't want to do the sitting experience I suggest taking it to go which is best and the lines aren't as bad, you must try their gluten free bagels which are great along with their house salmon and their delicious chive cream with onions, cucumbers, capers and tomatoes! If you're into French toast that is also something that tastes great. Remember they do not accept cash only credit card.

I made a reservation on Open Table, and definitely glad I did. We were seated right away & my Bestfriend and I were so glad we came here while visiting NYC! This place is so cute! It's kinda fancy, kinda hipster, kinda casual! The food was great as well as the service! I will for sure come back here my next time in the city! 


For those that don't know their way around NYC and are visiting, this place is a quick drive to ground zero and the World Trade Center, so it's a good place to eat & then go sight see.

Yum! I have been here for lunch or brunch a few times. It is a great more formal bagel experience than the typical on the go deli bagel and well worth the difference in price. Ordering is a little confusing because you do not order bagels more so what you want in it and then assemble them at your table. 
They will serve bagels as they are ready and walk around and shout HOT BAGELS. This can be super overwhelming and exciting. I like to share the Scottish salmon platter (comes with fixings like cream cheese (scallion + plain), tomatoes, onions, capers) and a side of avocado and share with one other person. 
If you have a non bagel eater they have really good salads and eggs as well. Make a reservation and leave room for babka or take one to go!!

I came here on Pete Wells' recommendation of the sticky buns, so I can only review those.

The bun costs $5.00, and is a fairly standard sticky bun. I'm not 100% sure that the bun is worth $5.00, as it essentially comes to $5.00 for a sticky roll, but the bun is definitely not bad.

Place is fine, food is tasty enough, but the "Roumanian Steak," at $39, is the most overpriced piece of meat I've ever come across.  To be clear, it's a skirt steak - that's it.  Just the skirt steak, sitting on your plate, eliciting confusion and questions like "sir, is this the 'Roumanian Steak?'"

Pretty f'ing ridiculous.  Felt robbed, even for NYC.
The only reason I can figure why there is a wait for this place is that they are all tourists. No NYer would go here for lousy service, high prices and average food.

Delicious, fresh fish platters, unlimited bagels.  Pastries are also spot on.

--Salmon: house salmon is more of a gravlax, lighter than the smoked Scottish.  Both are good.
--Whitefish salad: yum
--Latke royale: so good we ordered a second one (it's small)
--Bagels: not the best bagel in the city, but pretty good and fresh and not overwhelmingly large.  I always get everything bagels wherever I go, and Sadelle's has an Everything 2.0 bagel, which is a normal everything bagel + fennel and caraway seeds
--French toast: best French toast every, probably because it's deep fried; crispy on the outside, chewy and gooey on the inside
--Babka: fluffy and chocolatey, and topped with more chocolate
--Sticky bun: as good as everyone says; even better when slightly heated
--Steak tartare: mediocre
--Curry lobster: good, but not that special or worth the price
--Matzoh ball soup: a bit salty

After I had written the review Kate, one of the managers reached out and asked that we return to see if she could fix things. I just got around to going again last night for dinner, and as last time the food was excellent. We had the veal pelmeni and salmon salad topped with roe - these were both delicious, the toast accompanying the salad was buttered and crisp, the pelmeni meat was tender and seasoned perfectly, the only thing I would say was that there was perhaps a tad too much dough around them. 
For our mains we had fried chicken and branzino, and again very tasty. What was really nice aside from Kate contacting me was how great the service was this time around. I had just been to Dirty French on Tuesday, one of the sister restaurants, and they were excellent there as well, so perhaps this is how it will be from now on (hopefully!) because the food here really is delicious.

I visited Sadelles for a late Saturday brunch (this place is notoriously difficult to get reservations) and the atmosphere is great. 

Tucked away in Soho the marble tables, brass lighting, turquoise Le crusset pepper grinders, and bagel kitchen in the middle of the restaurant make for a quaint vibe. 

Really the bagels and bloody Mary's are the only thing worthwhile for breakfast (and caviar if you're so inclined). It's in SoHo and the location is priced accordingly for brunch. That being said, I enjoyed our leisurely brunch and think it's a great place for a lazy Saturday afternoon. 

We had the following:
Salmon, tuna and tomato tower with bagels 

You have unlimited bagels - they are delicious and I definitely ate too many 

Pigs in a blanket - we did not need these and they were not good. 

Waldorf salad - this salad is delicious but massive portion 

Blintzes - delicious but not the best I've had. 

Overall, if you want an authentic bagel, you don't need to pay this much. However, it's an enjoyable brunch.

I did not anticipate liking this place as much as I did. Trendy/sceney, West Broadway location, lines outside, difficult reservations. I feared that they would be trampling on smoked fish, my cultural patrimony.

So when we showed up for our 3:15 reservation (the only thing available a few days in advance) I was actually dreading it.

The beginning was not auspicious. At about 3:20 our party of 4 was offered two tiny bar tables right at the entrance. No way one of these would suffer the Tower. We demurred, and about fifteen minutes later were seated in one of the booths on the right, just past the bar and fish case.

Once we were seated, things proceeded nicely. Our waiter, Mickey, processed our drink order quickly. My wife's glass of Riesling was on point. The rest of us plumped for Bloody Marys, one regular and two with the house horseradish vodka (a $2.00 supplement). The special Bloody Mary was one of the best, with flavor notes and aromas more reminiscent of fresh ground horseradish than the jar variety. The remarkable thing was the balance, so that despite the horseradish infusion, the drink tasted like a well balanced cocktail,  not cocktail sauce. Have one. If you're not driving, have another.

With four people, the Sadelle's Tower is the way to go.  Three tiers, the top comprising Scottish salmon, the house salmon, sable and sturgeon. The mid-rise, a salmon salad on the rare side - more like a tartare than Russ and Daughters. And in the basement, a light whitefish salad. This is accompanied by perfectly sliced tomatoes, mandolined cucumbers, dill and capers. The delicate shredded purple onions are just about perfect. 

For spreads, whipped cream cheese plain and chive. Our first round of bagels came in a bread basket and not on their special paper towel holder thang. The bagels are small, nicely textured and super fresh. Fairly similar to Black Seed, if less sweet. To me, more Philly than Montreal or New York. The Ess-A-Bagel/H &H style bagel is not an ideal vessel for smoked fish, Sadelle's  are perfect.

As far as the fish, it was as good as you would get at R and D's, Murray's Sturgeon Shop  or Barney Greengrass, moist, perfectly sliced. The sturgeon gets high marks, lately sturgeon in the shops has been dry or over-smoked. One thing that I appreciate from this visit, is that smoked fish tastes better when you eat it immediately after slicing, before it starts to dry out. My only complaint here is that both the sable and the sturgeon came as three slices - I realize that these are luxury ingredients, but the platter is otherwise portioned generously for four. Charge $10 more and throw in four slices of sable/sturgeon, please. You may think that at $110 the Tower is already pricey, but it's not. Buy this product retail in an appetizing store and you will realize that the Tower is actually something of a bargain. Not that much markup.

We did not need the blintzes we were going to order and went with two slices of babka for dessert. 

And here was Sadelle's Achilles heel - the babka was dry and not as lusciously chocolaty as the better versions available.  On the other hand, our second shift waiter, Austin, was pretty cool, so we didn't fret.

Come here, get the Tower, don't think twice. These people know their fish.

Tip: make a reservation. There seems to always be a line to get a table. Probably because the lox and bagels are so good. Props to the Major Food Group for making it possible to enjoy your bagels and lox at a posh restaurant in the middle of Soho. 

It's a bit of a show here, and I kinda like it. Someone slices fish at the entrance bar, which also houses expensive caviar and baked goods. The fish is served in towers like afternoon tea, and they shout when fresh bagels are out of the oven. The interior of the restaurant is gorgeous, especially with the skylight. The people are beautiful. 

Now, the food: I tried the smoked scottish, which is almost transparent the slices are so thin - it's a good thing, it makes it melt-in-your-mouth. The bagels are served fresh, and are about the size of the palm of your hand - no guilt finishing the whole thing. The everything bagel 2.0 is really good. The french toast was a surprising show-stopper, maybe the best I've ever had. Thickly sliced with an extra crunchy exterior giving way to a custardy soft interior (I suspect some deep-frying magic); served simply with raspberry jam and syrup. 

I wish the service was better. Even with a reservation, we waited 15 min to get seated. Our waiter was nice but unattentive. I also wish the tables had more space, I was aware how close my bum was to our food when I got up to use the restroom. There are areas to improve on, but bottom line is that I cannot wait to come back to eat. Sometimes you want a bagel to go, and sometimes you want the luxury of slowly enjoying it. Also be aware that they do not accept cash.

Adorable place with delicious bagels, omelettes and crispy potatoes- great breakfast! Only minus is the very slow service, everything took quite a while to bring out and we had to ask different servers for more coffee etc. since our server was not attentive.

This place can't get any better!

First of let me tell you that I do NOT like lox or anything smoked but damn I think I just changed my mind.

There is always a line, which is a good sign.  You should always make a reservation or prepare to wait outside.  But for some odd reason, this one Saturday (or maybe it was Sunday I forgot) my bf wanted to come here so bad so I said okayyyy let's go.
