He got ready first so he was there before me and kept on texting me that we should be seated by time I get there.  Sure enough I got there and we were seated within 5 minutes.  We ordered a salmon omelette - amazing!!! He also put an order for the house salmon and sturgeon.  I don't eat bagels but I said if I'm going to dance, I need to do the Sadelle's dance.  I ate that damn cinnamon raisin bagel with salmon and sturgeon, some tomatoes, capers and a wipe of cream cheese.  Damn you Sadelle's damn you!

Not one thing was left on our plates but crumbs.  Just crumbs..

We visited Sadelle's for dinner and enjoyed it immensely.  The food and service were both excellent and the restaurant is comfortable and relaxing.  The dinner menu had excellent choices and everything was delicious.
What an amazing amazing breakfast experience... Make sure you go there on a weekday. No issues with waiting... Just excellent food and vodka.
I went to this place with my mom and it was delicious. We got the tower with everything bagel and the chive cream cheese. My mom got the blueberry pancakes.
black caviare are sooooooo good , the vodka they serve goes well with it the smoked salmon also good ... one thing need to be change is the plastic flowers all over the place . its UGLY

I was graciously invited to give Sadelle's another chance. Initially I was a little on the fence but am very glad I went again as everything was perfect. I had a true 5 star experience here the second time around. 

Firstly, the food was impeccable as it usually is. We had the smoked Scottish salmon, whitefish, eggs and caviar, and French toast. The Scottish salmon was delicious as always. I actually think that I preferred the sable to the whitefish though. The eggs and caviar were light and buttery with the caviar giving it a nice salty kick. But the real star of the meal was the French toast - airy and sweet. It tasted like melty bread pudding in the middle which is one of my favorite things in the world. I actually don't really like French toast but Sadelle's is beyond that. A must order!

Also topped off the meal with a piece of their babka - almost more chocolate than bread, and just how I like it. 

Our server was very pleasant this time around and the food came out promptly. I think it helped coming at a later time in the day when the restaurant is less crowded. Overall, I was very impressed with how delicious everything is, and would definitely recommend trying this place at least once. Thank you Sadelle's!

Dined here for a late brunch on a Sunday for a friends birthday. We had a 3pm reservation for 3 and sat around 345pm. Strike one, sadelles. Finally sat and quickly placed an order for iced coffee and a smoked salmon tower. Coffee and food never came after another 45 min. Strike 2. Finally someone told us they lost our ticket. We got complimentary cinnamon buns, which were tasty but anything would have tasted half way decent at that point. When the everything bagels and smoked salmon as well as tomato, onion, and cucumbers finally arrived on the tower, we were pretty content. Bagels were of good quality but on the leaner side. Salmon was great as were the condiments. Unclear if I will be back from the poor poor service. They didn't get a 3rd strike so there's a chance I'll dine her in due time.
Nice lunch spot for good old lox and bagels. Fascinating to see them make the bagels right in the middle of the restaurant. Best to book in advance as there can be a long wait for walk-ins.

Am very happy to report that at the courtesy of an incredibly nice Sadelle's manager (Kate) I was invited back, encouraged to get the tower and was completely comp'd on the meal. Splitting the tower between two people was quite a challenge but it did fully live up to the hype which in my book is an almost unprecedented occurrence. Salmon was splendid although marginally worse than the best Nova day at Russ's, while sturgeon was better than a typical Russ or Barneys visit. Most notably, sable for the 2nd time in a row was unequivocally outstanding and we may have to officially declare it a current front-runner in the NYC sable wars.  

Other comments - I typically don't care much for salmon salad, but a touch of a mysterious crunch coupled with a curious spice forced my wife and I into the debate on the recipient of the last bite. And yes, we had a perfectly comfortable table in the corner with plenty of room for beverages, plates and tower artifacts. My advice for any groups of two still stands - avoid the small round tables in the front if planning on a medium-large brunch. But otherwise - coming hungry and getting the tower is the move very worth making, and I plan on following my own advice soon enough.

4 stars. I really like Sadelle's.  My boyfriend and I probably go once every other month since they have gluten free bagels (though note these cost extra).  Recently, I feel like they're becoming stingy with their bagels.  The first couple of times we went they would bring out free fresh bagels and scream "hot bagels" while going around from table to table offering bagels to you.  Now, they only give you 1 free bagel with your order instead of unlimited bagels.  Not a huge deal, but seems like a shift in the feel of the restaurant and their generosity.  In any event, we've gotten a couple of the egg dishes which are always good, the scrambled eggs are super fluffy.  The side potatoes are deliciously crispy and seasoned very well.  The highlight for us is the smoked Scottish salmon platter, though the cheaper house salmon is also quite delicious (a bit more fatty/flavorful).  We normally each get one so that we don't fight about who gets the last piece of fish!  The scallion cream cheese is my favorite flavor.  I hear the sticky buns are supposed to be delicious, but since I always go with my boyfriend we haven't ordered them since they're obviously not gluten free.  As far as drinks go, I don't love the Bloody Mary's here for some reason, so I normally stick to mimosas.  Overall a solid place for bagels and brunch, though even if you have a reservation you'll likely be made to wait at least 15-30 minutes before you can get seated.

Sadelle's is a SoHo'd up Jewish deli experience for glamorous ladies, the well-heeled, and your parents. Although I only acquired bagels and coffee on my one and only visit this past weekend, I was impressed with the beautiful decor and the lab-coat-wearing staff tenderly slicing first-grade lox on the slab that greets guests at the very entrace. Everyone is so fabulous that you might forget for a moment that this place traffics mainly in schmaltzy Jewish food from the turn of the 19th century.

Carry-away service was pretty good. A bit of a wait if you're just getting a simple bagel (especially if there are cured-fish eaters enqueued ahead of you), but the bagel, smaller than the NYC standard, was still very good, as was the chive cream cheese. Coffee, at $4 a cup, was pretty eggregious even for this place -- it was to-go self-serve drip, after all. I also would have liked a larger selection of bagels (nothing even close to whole wheat available). Still, I will bump this to a 4-star review for lofty ambitions and goregeous design.

Worth a special occasion visit for an obscenely expensive bagel with lox at some point. I'll start saving now.

I came in early on a Saturday morning to beat the crowds, which let me appreciate just how beautiful the space is. The long communal table and petite round marble tables are topped by elegant turquoise tableware. And I can report that the wait staff is polished and attentive. 

I chose the salami and eggs with mustard, which attracted me for  it's peculiarity. Sadly, this experiment came up short. Billed as "hard", the meat didn't have the texture or spice you'd expect; essentially I got soggy ham. This was a shame, cause I bet that the tasty mustard would have played off a protein with more snap. 

I wound up using the (included) bagel to 'structure' the meal, and it nearly saved the day. It's odd to wax poetic about a bagel, but wow! I got the everything bagel, which I think also had leeks thrown on top of all the other goodness. This last ingredient may have been a daily special, as I didn't notice it when I checked back over the menu. Warm and soft dough, crusted over with sharp and salty herbs!

I finished with a sticky bun with a salted caramel glaze (yeah, I really like salt). This thing didn't look any better than a day-old Cinnabon. Even the first bite underwhelmed, as the glaze (never) materialized. But as soon as I worked my way in, I enjoyed the moist and buttery flavor notes.

To sum up, I kinda went out on a ledge for a weird main dish, so I put that one on me. But I would definitely return; as the classic egg sandwich, challah French Toast, and the "Leo" are all highly recommended by others.
From the Bloody Mary's to the bagels and the salmon and the salads everything is amazing! Our waiter was so much fun. The food is delicious. Such a fun brunch!

The food was good. Some russian style dishes were exellent. Great lax. The best part was bartender and waiter Oleg. He made us order twice as much but no regrets!! He provided exellent service and made our visit a blast!

DON'T come for bagels to go. The staff was totally incapable of completing orders. The one guy kept taking orders while the other two argued with each other and got nothing done. The manager would come by occasionally to correct one thing and then leave this utter dysfunction to continue.

YUMMMMMY. What a fun scene. It's filled with obnoxious New Yorkers who made reservations months in advance. Usually these sceney restaurants have bad food but sadelles is great! 
Scottish salmon - comes with bagels and the everything bagel is so good and warm and delicious. 
Scrambled eggs - very tasty 
French toast - I normally don't even like French toast but this was next level
Greek salad - really great. I am obsessed with the dressing 
Babka- kind of dry. You could do without 

Love this spot and the warm, fresh, melt in your mouth bagels.

I've been wanting to go here for a long time. Finally made it today and it exceeded my expectations. We ordered the smoked Scottish salmon, tuna salad and the omelette. Everything was great!! The Bloody Mary however tasted like pickle juice so we sent it back. I would definitely come back !

UM. The bagels at this place were PHENOMENAL. Honestly it's the best bagel I've ever had. 

I didn't sit down and enjoy the dine-in experience. Honestly the whole place is frankly a little out of my price range. 

I came here with an out of towner and was excited as this was listed as one of the top bagel places in the city. But when I heard the total from the cashier I almost had a heart attack. Luckily, when we dug into our bagels it was clear that they were QUALITY bagels. 

It's a four step choice process:
1 kind of bagel
2 kind of fish 
3 kind of cream cheese 
4 toppings 

I got an onion bagel with egg salad and hive cream cheese. Honestly It was mouth watering and I dream of another one. But FIFTEEN DOLLARS for a bagel knocks this place up to "special occasion dining". And when does one get a special occasion bagel? 

I recommend it highly just once. And if you've got the budget that 15 dollars for a bagel doesn't make you flinch, then please take me with you next time!

I like this place, but I can't really argue with those who are critical. It is very expensive for what it is, and while the food is very good, I can't say I find it to be best in class. Better than Russ & Daughters? Better than Black Seed? I honestly don't think so.

We tried both the scottish salmon, and the house salmon (we both preferred the latter, even though it's slightly cheaper), along with the matzo ball soup and the breakfast potatoes. The soup was very good -- it's fairly herby/earthy, and if that's the kind of matzo ball soup you like, this is about as good as it gets. I personally prefer a softer, bigger matzo ball with noodles instead of veggies, but that's just my own taste. The potatoes were good as well, but nothing overly special, in my opinion. 

The bagels themselves were very good (they are small, but I don't really have an issue with that), and the other toppings that came with the salmon (tomatoes, cucumbers, capers, onions) were very good as well. Again, I liked it all a lot, I just don't think they're best in class, which is what the prices indicate they should be.

On the way out, I got a black and white cookie to go, which was also very good, but, again (you might be sensing a theme), not among the very best that I've had.

First time was today and it will be the last. Not worth talking about the food, which was only average, because the service at brunch was horrible. We spent about an hour just waiting for our food to arrive; 15 minutes for the starters, 30 minutes for the main courses after the starters were finished and then about 10 minutes for dessert. No coffee, tea or water was offered during the wait. Getting the attention of our server or any other personnel to inquire about our order was a Herculean task and didn't do any good once we asked. The 2 hour experience which doesn't include the 20 minute wait after our reservation time was just plain neglectful and embarrassing for the members of my party.

Great salmon in a beautiful space, but that's about it. They seated half our party when they arrived early (huge plus). The bagel and schmear tower is cute but a little too kitschy for me. I'd rather go to Essa, Murray's, or any of the other fantastic bagel options in the city. These bagels were so tiny, like the size of my fist. The service was totally pleasant and they refilled the coffees and waters frequently. Eh I don't know, maybe I'm just picky, it was ok on the whole, but not worth the price to return.

I went to Sadelle's yesterday for lunch with my sister and a friend around 1:30 PM, at my friend's suggestion. It was decently busy, but manageable given that it was a holiday weekend. We tried to request a table, but were told by the hostess that they were only accepting parties with reservations. That was a little annoying, but we weren't ready to give up completely. Luckily, I was able to book us right away on OpenTable for 2:15 PM. Not sure why they choose to fill their tables this way, but I was just happy we were going to be able to sit down and eat. It was pretty funny though to walk out and then literally walk back in a few minutes later suddenly with a reservation. 

We checked in at about 2:00 PM and waited and waited. At one point the hostess said that our table was ready, but had to take it back because she forgot that we were a party of three people, not two. It wasn't really a big deal, we were just pretty hungry since it was already about 2:30, one hour after we had hoped to be seated in the first place. I probably should have ordered a drink from the bar near the entrance to bide the time. 

The wait was pretty much worth it though. We got seated at a nice half-booth corner table and were approached by a waiter quickly. We got coffee, which was nice and strong. My friend really enjoyed all of the different cute blue dishes in the restaurant. It took us a little bit of time to decide what to order. We didn't really want to pay $110 for the bagel tower situation, but we knew we wanted lox. We ended up ordering one Smoked Scottish platter, one House Cured salmon platter, and one tuna salad platter to share, each of which comes with veggies, cream cheese, and bagels. We were able to select the type of bagels we wanted. They didn't have sesame, which is my favorite, so we went for everything. This ended up being a really good choice when paired with the fish.

The food was absolutely delicious! The bagels were warm and perfect. They had the definite bite you want from a bagel, but were also extremely soft. You could tell they were much fresher than the average bagel you find in neighborhood stores. The fish was also fresh, soft, and flavorful. I did not eat the tuna, mostly because I have a thing about cooked fish, but also the way they plated it in a circular shape reminded me of cat food unfortunately. Maybe they can rethink that. Literally any other shape would be more palatable. My friend and sister assured me the tuna was very good, but not sure I would choose that over the lox. Combining the bagel, fish, cream cheese, cucumbers, onion, capers, dill, and tomato into any ratio you desire is really something. Definitely among the top bagels that I have eaten. 

We ended up with a lot more toppings than we could possibly fit on our bagels. I'm not sure if they do this on purpose or if we just didn't stack ours quite as high as the average person. We ended up asking for two more bagels with extra cream cheese to split. We were expecting to be charged extra for these, but we happily weren't! That was a really pleasant surprise. Our wonderful waiter also brought us some sticky buns to take home with us at the end of our meal. I just ate mine this morning and it was awesome. It tasted like toffee, crack-caramel goodness. The restaurant was really emptying out by the time that we finished eating, so maybe they were in the process of switching to the dinner menu and wanted to get rid of some of the baked goods? Either way, it was so nice and unexpected!

Overall, the meal lived up to my expectations. It was exactly what I would have anticipated out of a sit-down bagel-centric meal. I would have easily given 5 stars (especially with the complimentary dessert factor) had it not been for the unusual waiting process we went through.

This is literally the best restaurant in the whole world. LOX GALORE.  BAGEL HEAVEN
Only caveat is when we received all the food, we realized that our waiter didn't give us any utensils. But service was quick and the waiter was attentive and got us everything we needed. Grapefruit juice is prime and freshly squeezed. STRONG WORK.

So the name Sadelles only came across my radar, as I don't live in nyc, because this annoying tv cook had mentioned it as being one of her favorite brunch spots as I flipped through the channels. I figured she knew food, so I booked a new years eve brunch for a friend and myself. I am so very glad I did. It was probably the best brunch of my life. We started with a mimosa. Can't go wrong with those. Now the coffee is quality but didn't have the kick i like. None of that mattered when the food started to arrive. We began with the sticky Buns.  There was only 3 small Buns, but oh the Buns they were. My mouth has never tasted anything so delicious. I told friends that they could literally be my last meal. If you only order one thing from Sadelles, these should be it. They're indescribably good. We split the egg sandwich. Again I don't know how it's done. It's simply egg, cheese and bacon but I've never had one so delicious. We also split the house salmon. It came in a beautiful tower with tomatoes, capers, onion, cream cheese and choice of house made bagel. Bagels are made in house and I've heard they're the best in town. I couldn't argue that. Sadelles gets quite busy, but the wait isn't long for food. Any place that'll serve you a carafe of vodka with breakfast is obviously amazing. I'll order that on my next visit  service is great.  It does get warm inside though so dress accordingly. Credit card only. If I lived in nyc, I'd be at breakfast every weekend. Of course you'd also need to be independently wealthy. Ha. Tonnes of food and mimosas and coffee for 2 cost around $100. Treat yourself.

I got hurt at Sadelle's last weekend. The legs of the chair and the seat of the chair separated when I was moving the chair and my finger got caught in between it. I was bleeding really badly and in a lot of pain. NO ONE FROM THE RESTAURANT SEEMED TO CARE! One kind waitress saw me by the bathroom bleeding and was nice enough to give me some bandaids - but that was IT! The manager took AN HOUR (literally) to come over and ask if I was okay. And he honestly didn't really care about my well-being at all - the opposite of genuine. Furthermore, NOT ONE THING was taken off the bill ("comped") for the inconvenience. I am happy to pay for what I eat, however, it would have been a really nice gesture to remove something from the bill since (even a week later) I am still in pain and being inconvenienced by the REALLY bad cut on my finger. Only after we called the manager over, after rolling his eyes, did he remove some of the drinks from the bill. I am shocked and absolutely disgusted by the behavior and lack of professionalism at this restaurant.

If you love smoked fish and cavier....!!!
Sticky bun is very fine..outstanding coffee. Great service.

Sadelle's is fun and the food is not just terrific but beautifully plated as well! .We started with the grapefruit cocktail that is topped with lemon zest, mint and a little sugar. It was delicious! We ordered house salmon that comes with cucumbers, onions, capers and tomatoes and delicious hot bagels fresh out of the oven. The Freddy salad could not have been better. Best of all the servers are attentive and kind and eager to please. Enjoyable way to start the day and plan on doing it again soon!

Where typically you'd buy your bagel and lox over the counter at a loud, bustling deli, Sadelle's is all about classy vibes, refined service, and a mouthwatering menu. We ordered the scottish salmon (lox lovers - this is the saltier of the smoked salmon options) which was charmingly plated on a brass tower, everything bagels stacked on a whimsical wooden pole, and blueberry pancakes which were the most scrumptious, delicate way to close out the meal. Sadelle's feels like a throwback - a place where Eloise and her pug Weenie may happily find themselves after wandering downtown from the Plaza. Things to savor: the clean white service coats, the jewel box room where they make the bagels, the blue ceramic coffee cups and pepper shakers.

I was initially so excited to hear that a bagel restaurant was opening in soho where casual restaurants are few. However this place is overpriced and pretentious. Yes the lox is thinly sliced and nicely garnished with fresh dill and chives but that's about the only positive. My salmon Benedict was served cold, and with no side salad or potatoes, seemed like a tiny portion. Another disappointment is there is no cappuccino or espresso, only regular coffee, though they are not too pretentious to serve artificial sweeteners thankfully. My daughter disliked her french toast, saying it was too moist in the middle. We found the service was fine, but slow.  Not rushing back. The bagels are great, but at $2 a pop, are quite small.

Yes, this might be the most expensive bagel you'll ever purchase, but honestly worth the experience. Step one, make a reservation. Sadelle's is insta-famous so expect the brunch wait to be ridiculous. Step two, order a spicy bloody, any kind of fish, the salt and pepper bagel, plus a side of home fries. Side note: you don't have to pay $100+ for the deluxe tower to actually get a "tower." Any of the fish options will come on a picture-perfect tower so you can build your own breakfast. Our waiter was helpful with the menu plus he kept things light and funny. Take your trendy friends here when they visit for the atmosphere and experience - it's almost sure to impress. One star off for prices, but hey it's New York.

Sadelle's manager of the night - Belleza - showed the true colors of the restaurant after making us wait unnecessarily for 20'minutes while there where SEVERAL empty tables. She insisted we had drinks at the bar - after looking at my 6 month pregnant belly. With thousands of restaurants in town you would think on an empty winter night the service will be a little more welcoming.

Whenever I'm in NYC I can't not go to sadelles for brunch at least one day. And I wish I could eat here every day. 

What more can one want than piping hot double everything (yes... double everything is a thing here) bagels served with delicious lox, fresh crunch fixings (tomato onion capers)  and chivey spread? Oh yeah... add their decadent breakfast sandwich. And their matzo ball soup. And another bagel???

It's really perfection for lox and bagels and sets a standard for brunch overall.

Reservations are pretty necessary or else you wait forever. Come here asap for brunch

Disappointing.
Hugely popular...judging by the queue...which left me even more perplexed once I'd eaten.

How good can bagels be? $100 worth? I think not.

If you accept it's a venue to post your visit on Instagram, then yep, mission achieved...as a culinary experience...I've had better bagels for $5 from a local deli.
Why it's so busy is a mystery. Three times, someone at the table next to us had to get up to track down a server. Way overhyped.

Honor a reservation to the minute . Knowledgeable pleasant waiter helpful suggestions 
Scotch Salmon / Sturgeon perfectly toasted bagel with the usual fixings plus ? Avocado
Weird suggestion I thought but ended up turning above average into a perfect bite 
Tables close together limited space on the table yet seemed to add to the experience 
Bloody Mary worth skipping in my opinion ? Pickle juice overwhelming
Salami and eggs omelette interesting - usually a dish I love but their version with mustard cooked in just not my thing 
Grapefruit Brûlée a must have 
Overall fun brunch experience I would stick to the appetizing if I went back
Definitely no complaints about the food! Delicious lox and tuna salad. Loved the pigs in a blanket. Good service once we were seated. Would definitely go back!

I didn't know what to expect when coming to Sadelle's. I'd just read it had great bagels. We were hosting a friend in from out of town who really digs bagels so we went for it. I thought at first it was silly to make a reservation for a Friday morning bagel breakfast but I'm so glad I did because the place was 2/3's full at 10am. 

I think everyone should have a decadent bagel meal once in their lives and Sadelle's really elevates this iconic NYC food. The bagel I had was good, the whitefish salad I ordered with it was okay, the salmon salad my husband ordered was excellent but the best part was the presentation, the ambience and service. 

I'd only go back really for that salmon salad...to go.
The waiting time for a table is about 30-45 mins on Sunday 11 am for us which is totally ok. We ordered house salmon, egg salami, tuna salad with 4 different bagels from lunch.  The service is good !

I loved Sadelles, food was tasty we got the house salmon and the Scottish salmon with everything bagels and an omelette, all three tasted amazing. However, the service needs a lot of help. My server was a complete jerk and I have no idea why? We asked him for suggestions and he looked at us like we were stupid. I would have given him the crappy tip he deserved but he took out an iPad and charged me for my meal then HOVERED over me when I was filing out the tip portion (awkward) so I left him 18% since he was standing there. My bill was $90 bucks for breakfast this place isn't cheap the service should be better. He deserved a 10% tip for how rude and unattentive he was!

Mentally I hate everything Sadelles represents.  Corporation takes traditional breakfast food of generations and makes it trendy.  It's not even close to some of the best appetizing that I've had.....and yet....I love this place. 

From the clean crisp airy decor, to the waiters in white jackets, the branding on everything from plates to aforementioned jackets, the beautiful people dining in and taking out ---this is a definite step up from the old days of eating lox on Sunday with Aunt Ruth and Uncle Morty.

Order a tiered platter with some of their cream cheese and a couple of their cute bagels and just take the experience in.  Sadelles make me feel like a Jewish Eloise.

Great endive salad, the trout was really good and the best was the salmon appetizer!

The front manager as well as the server were really nice and friendly. They helped us with our choices for the evening. Great place for groups and yummy dinners!

Amazing Lox! Certainly the best I have ever had. Must make reservations.
Tables are super tiny, which makes findibg room for plates, drinks, utensils somewhat of a puzzle. The vibe is fun and energetic and at the same time relaxing and quaint.
The service was wonderfully attentive and the seating (with reservations) was with in minutes of our arrival. 
I can't say the bagels are the best I've had, but with everything else they were good enough for a very enjoyable breakfast.

YES. YES. YES. 

Most beautiful and yummy brunch spot in all of NYC. 

The service is excellent, also weirdly CREDIT CARD ONLY first time I've ever seen that in my life lmao. But hey get those dining points. Ambience 10/10 and they make the bagels right there!

Got the smoked Scottish tower with a friend, and was able to get an extra bagel to split the tower. But we were still hungry after so we ordered a 2nd and DAMN then we got full. Absolutely delicious and worth every penny 

Also, don't u dare leave without ordering those sticky buns!!!!!! HEAVEN ON EARTH. It's like if a baklava and a cinnamon bun had a baby and made the world a much sweeter place.

Will come again, new fave brunch spot. Also it's pricey, it's worth the overall dining experience

It was just ok.  went for lunch.  had the tuna melt and waldorf salad.  it was ok but $26 for a salad is steep.  cool design with bakery in the middle. but not a good value for the $$ and very small lunch menu.

Great from start to finish. What a wonderful experience, we ordered to Scottish salmon, which was delicious, but the presentation, ambience and service make this place so special. Highly recommended!!!

Let me preface this by saying, the staff was very nice and friendly. That's why I gave it 3 stars. 

So first, I was advised against this place by a coworker, but a couple friends from DC really wanted to go so I was fine w/ it. One friend tells me that he made reservations last week b/c it's "so difficult to get in". Oh boy, we all heard this before in NY... So typical. Anyways, we're there at 2:30p waiting on our 2:45p reservations. We got seated close to 3:30pm! See what I mean, you go though hoops trying to get a reserved table, but turns out, that's not how it works here. Needless to say, after waiting about 45mins, our table to become available. We were starving...

We sat and ordered right away. We have multiple waiters, all friendly, but some are vapid. It is now close to 5pm, 4:40p to be exact. Two parties next to us, order the exact same thing we did, got their meal, ate it and paid; yet we are still sitting there with cold coffee and watered down drinks. I asked one waiter to refill our coffee cups and gets drinks for our guest. He never did. Was observed just randomly walking around as if he was clocking out. So another waiter came to our table and I requested the same thing, but more in a assertive tone. We started eating the food closer to 5pm. 5PM!!!!

The food itself, well...u know what they say, "Everything that glitters isn't gold." And in NY's case, all too often things are priced out the ass with very little substance, and this was my concern in going in the first place. It did not disappoint, I definitely will NOT be back. It's NY! There are better brunch places that are less pretentious. #BrunchMatters

Very disappointing. We stopped there just after noon on a Saturday and made a reservation, initially at 1:30, but then was changed to 2:30 by the hostess. When we returned at 2:20, we were then told that we had been placed on the "wait list" and that a table would be available in 30-45 minutes. Hostess was rude when we asked why they had changed our reservation. Couldn't tell you anything about the food, as we left, never to return again.
This was probably the best bagels I've had! It was not too heavy, and went great with the fish spreads and cream cheese. A place that I'll definitely go back again!

I love the food but the service is awful. We split two house salmons between three girls and were snubbed by the waiters for sharing. Our coffee was never refilled even though every table around us had their coffees refilled. We were also charged extra for 2nd bagels even though we were told bagels were "unlimited within reason" when we first sat down & on previous visits, getting a second bagel per order was not charged extra. The cost would have been fine but mixed messages front the staff and general treatment was terrible. We could also hear the waiters talking about us. Server was listed as Sam. Unfortunate that the service was so bad because the food was pretty good, won't be returning.

In general, smoked salmon and salt & pepper bagels are good but it is definitely not worth the price tag. I went with my sisters and we were treated like second class citizens for sharing two meals. We literally have eaten out hundreds of times together and often share meals and have never been treated as poorly as we were here. It was extremely unprofessional and made our experience very disappointing. We sat in the back elevated part of the restaurant where there were different servers. It might have just been them because as we left, we walked by all of them and none of them thanked or even acknowledged us whereas the servers on the lower level were very friendly and thanked us on our way out. We left an 18% tip despite the abhorrent service so it couldn't have been that. All three of us have also waited tables for years so it's not like we aren't aware of proper etiquette. Save your money and go elsewhere!

Wow, love this place! Such a yummy brunch spot in NYC. I came here first when I landed in New York. We ordered the salmon tower (comes with cream cheese, bagels, tomatoes, onions, cucumbers and of course salmon. It was sooo good! The salmons was cut super thin and bagels were delicious and fresh! 

The french toast is an ABSOLUTE MUST!!!!! Best french toast I have ever had. It is so delicious!!!! 

They only accept credit cards FYI.

I love everything about this place. The decor, the ambiance and the staff are lush. The steak tartare flawless and you MUST try the Brussels sprouts! All the produce very fresh. Only thing I will say is it will be very hard to get a place on weekend brunches without a long wait.

Wow!  Ignore the bad reviews. Not sure how they can hate on this place!  Absolutely adorable place in Soho for brunch. Must have reservation otherwise hard to get in. Also reservation needs to be made via email. Depending on where you sit you can watch the staff hand rolling the bagels from scratch which was pretty cool to watch. I ordered a Bloody Mary to drink which knocked my socks off - had pickle juice in it and was so good!  My husband, daughter and I decided on the tower so that we could sample different fishes. Not cheap, but worth the splurge. You get unlimited bagels, they're a little small so you can eat more than one!  Comes with delicious homemade plain cream cheese and chive cream cheese. Bagels come out warm. I had a salt and pepper one which was seasoned perfect. The tower includes two kinds of smoked salmon, sturgeon, sable, whitefish salad and salmon salad along with tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion and capers. The three of us did some major damage and everything was fresh and delicious. Haven't had sturgeon or sable in so long so it was really a nice treat. Place decorated so cute. Nice blue touches with the mugs and menus. Service was great. Our server took the time to explain menu to us and gave his recommendations. Definitely would come back again!

Recommended: Making a trip to Sadelle's
Highly Recommended: Making a reservation at Sadelle's

There's a perpetual line to get into this edenic bagel paradise, home to some of the best lox in Manhattan. It's a chic restaurant hosting a trendy crowd in one of New York's hottest neighborhoods. If you don't have a reservation, put your name down and take a stroll through the nearby art galleries where you can gaze upon $25,000 pieces of metal that someone decided was art.

Sadelle's is not just a place where food is served. It is a place where you witness a performance, a show, a marriage of food, beverage, and mediocre service that tickles the palette and leaves it wanting more.

You can check out the pictures of towers piled high with a variety of fish and stacks of fresh bagels. To be honest, the bagels are not much better than some local shops or Ess-a-bagel. But everything that comes with the bagels is absolutely top-notch.

We loved every single thing we ate. Options for your tower include:

- House Salmon
- Smoked Scottish
- Sable
- Sturgeon
- Whitefish Salad
- Salmon Salad

Each item was better than the one before it. The House Salmon is sliced paper-thin so you can have total control over how much you want to outfit your bagel with. I promise you, it literally melts in your mouth like nothing you've experienced.

As I alluded to, the service is only okay, perhaps even sub-par. You will wait for you table, wait for your water, wait for your orange juice, and wait for your bagels. It's well worth it though.

There are some other items that looked awesome but we just didn't have room for:

- A variety of salads
- Tuna Melt
- French Toast

If you can come with 4-6 people and share a bunch of dishes, that would be ideal.

I went here for dinner on a Friday night with 3 other people. The atmosphere was intriguing and different than a lot of the nearby places. There were cafe tables and booths with candelabras everywhere. Their wine list is good but expensive even by the glass. We shared a few appetizers and then split the spicy fried chicken with a huge bowl of potatoes which was excellent. The potatoes had dill, sour cream and caviar. The chicken had truffle honey for drizzling which pushed it over the edge (good!) Come later in the evening for a more full house, and be prepared to spend more than the average, but for a unique atmosphere.

Food is good. Prices are high but that's par for the course. What isn't so great is the constant attempt to up-sell... every single time the waiter came to the table, he tried, rather forcefully, to get us to purchase more food than we wanted. It was unseemly.

You really have to plan your visit - as in weeks ahead if you even a chance to get a reservation. But i always try because it never disappoints! Egg salad here is so good - on the bagel with a little lox on top! But the real dreamer here is the matzo ball soup!!

Came here for breakfast and I felt like it was my birthday (it wasn't). Super fun atmosphere and it is a great place for out of town guests visiting New York. We had the house salmon, sturgeon and egg salad with a variety of bagels as well as the breakfast potatoes. All were delicious.

Our attentive server, Maxwell, went above and beyond to make our experience amazing!

Although we ordered waaaaaay too much food, it was all quite tasty.  The mushroom barley soup was plentiful, thick and comforting.  A little on the salty side but still yummy.  The Freddy salad was beautifully composed but $38 is a little steep for a salad with shrimp.  The French toast was huge and decadent.  The sticky bun was a sweet gem just large enough for sharing.

I'm not a big bagel lover and I have to say, even the plain bagel was delicious!

Contrary to many reviews on this site, the service was excellent and our overall experience was a good one.

I would definitely recommend Sadelle's for brunch or lunch.

Mixed feelings about Sadelles today. I love the house lox, it's superb. The presentation of everything is beautiful. The service is usually just ok and today it was worse than ever. Thankfully Austin, one of the managers was there to pinch hit. He made up for the waiter who was completely out of it. I will be back, but my expectations regarding service are managed.
For me this is a must! It is a new classic! Breakfast & Brunch here is amaZing! This is a place for tourists and non tourist! Pancakes are the best I've ever tried for real! Please go!

I finally came back for full brunch because I had to do the "tower" - three tiers of smoked fish and all the bagels you can eat. The tower for $110 was perfect for 4 people. The bagels were excellent and the smoked fish and salads were delectable. Out only quibble was that the cream cheese had too much air in it - we are rather exacting when it comes to cream cheese. But overall Sadelle's is worth it and the real deal.

This review is for counter service. I've been here twice now, and it's easy to grab a bagel and go at their counter. Both times i've gotten an everything bagel, which has been delicious! The cream cheese with chives is amazing, and I would totally recommend that. I got it the second time with salmon, but I think it would have paired better with plain cream cheese. Overall, though, the bagels are amazing and you have to try the cream cheese with chives!
The food here is amazing. Love how they slice the lox super thin and they serveA he beat French toast I've ever had. Definitely one of my favorite brunch spots in NYC

Came here on a busy day. Extremely rude and pretentious hostess who seemed to judge us the moment we walked in. The food was mediocre and in my opinion overpriced. There are better places that serve bagels in LES. Disappointed since I anticipated coming here and regretful that I did. Do yourself a favor.

Very nice experience at this business! Food was delicious and service was great. Had the Scottish Smoked Salmon platter, Lox Benedict and the Grapefruit appetizer. Platter was so nicely displayed - only gripe was that the bagel is a mini bagel size. Had leftover lox and veggies at the end. Benedict was awesome but the Grapefruit was the STAR! It had mint and lemon and caramelized sugar on top. Not something that I would usually order but my friend got it and I ended up devouring it. A must order!!

Went back yesterday afternoon (I think this was our 4th time here) and so glad we did.  We had a couple drinks and some apps.  Gazpacho soup was outstanding!  We love the pigs in a blanket and the kids had some bagels and cream cheese.  Everything was excellent and the service was terrific even as we caught them in a shift change.

Love it and hate it! Food is very good but extremely pricy as well. 

House Salmon- 3 tiers tray is very nice way of serving. The salmon was amazing. But $21, worth it or not?
Salami & Egg- I think it's very delicious and flavorful  but again, an egg dish at $21..... uhmmm
Waldorf Salad- flavor was good but uhmmmm.... a salad at $23?

Make reservation ahead! We waited 50 min for sat brunch without reservation ....
Hands down the best brunch I've had in NYC. Everything we ate was amazing and the service was pretty good considering our waiter was slammed. We will be back very soon

Have been here a few times. It's fantastic!  Unreal bagels, delicious breakfast sandwich, great sticky buns and pigs in a blanket. It's just so so good. I don't understand why it only has 3 1/2 stars. Worth the wait and the staff is so accommodating and nice.

Sadelle's has been on my list of places to cross off my list for a while now. I came here thinking it offered unlimited bagels with the choice of tower. It did not. (That was the reasoning for knocking off a star.) we had read in a few places they offered bagel towers that were unlimited. That disappointment/misunderstanding aside, the overall experience was good. 

We came here with our 9 month old baby at 1pm on a Saturday expecting long waits. We got there and were told 25 min so we got a slice of chocolate babka and an iced coffee to hold us over. The wait was accurate and we were sat towards the front entrance overlooking the take out counter. It was perfect and we were able to keep our baby in the stroller. 

Upon being seated, we got water right away, but It took longer than expected to take our order. With an infant, you notice these things right away! When we were finally greeted by our waiter, we ordered the eggs Benedict and the Scottish salmon which came with 2 bagels. 

The eggs Benedict was awesome. It came on fluffy English muffins that just melt in your mouth. The eggs were perfectly poached and the hollandaise was perfection. 

The salmon tower was great. Perfect amount of salmon for 2 bagels. The tower also comes with really sweet, ripe tomatoes and cucumbers, capers, and dill. We also got one scallion cream cheese and one plain in the tower. The bagels are smaller than your average oversized ny bagel, but they are really good. Perfectly doughy and tasty like a proper NY bagel. We got the normal everything bagel instead of the 2.0 which had fennel and caraway seeds. Again, we thought bagels were unlimited so when we asked if we could try the everything 2.0 bagel we were told we could get it for $2 and that they already threw in an extra bagel into the tower for us. Umm really? That would have been so pathetic to get just one small bagel with that tower. And TWO DOLLARS!? For a teeny tiny bagel after we already devoured a large slice of chocolate babka, a salmon tower and a full Benedict meal? No thanks. 

Anyway, while that didn't ruin our pleasant afternoon meal, it did leave a slightly negative experience at the end. Still not sure how we got confused about the unlimited bagels, but perhaps that's something they should institute since their bagels are so tiny.... I'm still slightly sad I didn't get to try the everything 2.0.

The ultimate brunch experience, for any occasion you can think of (or just for no good reason at all!) Service: incredible. Food: not only instagram worthy, but it tastes amazing as well. Experience: authentic and fun. Be sure to get the lox tower for your group; the unlimited bagels would be reason enough for any Jew.

I really wanted to love this place. Who doesn't want to spend their Sunday morning with a great cup of coffee in a cheery le creuset mug?

However, there were just a ton of miscues and when you spend close to $100 on brunch for 2 (sans alcohol even though I tried to order a mimosa), you expect better.

We were seated by the bakery in the back half of the restaurant. I'm not a clean freak but it was gross looking at the glass next to us (picture attached). I ordered coffee and a mimosa to drink. The mimosa never came. I got my coffee fairly quickly but it got cold while I waited to ask for some form of milk. I then opened the sugar container and there was only Splenda. I got a waiter's attention and asked for sugar. He pointed to the sugar container and said "in there" and walked off. So I had to wait a few more minutes before I could track someone else down to actually get sugar. 

I ordered my bagel with butter, but it came wth cream cheese. Again by the time I could get the waiter's attention to ask for butter, it was cold and a room temp bagel with ice cold butter isn't overly delicious. 

Lastly, we had ordered sticky buns as dessert after our entrees. I never thought they were going to come (like the mimosa) so when a second waiter brought the check, I just pulled out my card and didn't say anything. Then the first waiter brought the sticky buns and asked who had brought the check? When I just said another waiter, he persisted and asked "which one?" It was rather awkward as I'm not trying to get in the middle of an employee spat. 

Lastly, when another waiter came to swipe our card, he complained about the big party next to us. Yes, they were ridiculous. Everyone in the restaurant could tell they were a very difficult party, but it was incredibly unprofessional for a waiter to complain to us about other customers. 

The food was pretty good, but not great for $90 and definitely not good enough to put up with this hassle.
Gluten free everything bagel and lox. Best gluten free bagel ever!! The tower was fresh and wonderful.. definitely a new favorite.

The only reason I'm writing this review is because the website gives me no opportunity to tell the owners privately about my experience.  We got there on a Monday morning and it was packed...we had a 30 minute wait.  We were dying of thirst from walking around waiting for a table so sitting at the table and seeing two servers look at us and not stop by hit me wrong.  I'm in the restaurant business and I understand when a place is busy, but from what I could see the food runners/bussers outnumbered the servers so there was no reason two servers should stop and look at us and not come over.  Who I assume to be the manager on duty finally came over and took our order.  One of the servers that looked at us came over and she shoo'd him away and said, "I got it."  I ordered the blueberry pancakes and my partner ordered scrambled eggs with potatoes and a bagel.  When it arrived I had no butter for my pancakes which I found odd, but they were OK with just the syrup so maybe they don't serve it that way.  My partner's eggs were cooked earlier and held and the potatoes were basically fingerlings that were boiled, smashed and fried.  The manager came back over and asked how everything was to which we replied, "fine."  She then got a quizzical face and repeated "Fine??"  OK, let it go because now I'm going to tell you.  I told her the eggs were "sad" and that it was disappointing that they weren't cooked to order. She told me they were cooked to order, but they were too yellow and rubbery to have been.  My partner also didn't get her bagel and had to hunt down someone to get it.

For the price it just wasn't worth it...everything was just phoned it in.  The people next to us ordered the salmon and perhaps this is what should be ordered here.  Skip the basic breakfast fare as very little care is given to this.

The egg dish was taken off our check, which wasn't requested and didn't need to happen.  I dine often and I know going to a new place is a risk and I'm willing to pay regardless.

I've been wanting to try Sadelle's for a while so took the holiday weekend as a chance to go without a crowd. (Meaning the space, which is super cool, wasnt noisy, but I can see it getting very loud).

There are a TON of waitstaff, but the wait to place our order and to get our food was over 20 minutes for each...and the place wasnt even half full. The hostess sensed my annoyance and kindly came over to say sorry (after avoiding my eye for about 10 minutes) and gave us some drinks/desserts on the house. This was a saving grace for my experience. 

The food itself is good - we had amazing lox that were thinly sliced and the bagels were okay too (made in house) but really not sure it was worth $20+ for a bagel and lox.  The egg dish we ordered was also tasty, but again, for eggs and a bagel it made me a little sick to pay that much.  

Overall, I wouldnt go back to dine - I'd likely just order some lox to go and make something equally as good for a fraction of the price at home.

Nice atmosphere. Service was good and prompt.
Food was average nothing memorable. For tourists I find it to expensive. Be sure to have a credit card because they don't accept cash!!!

Skip this place.  

Very rude manager, way over priced.  

This was my new neighborhood spot but after this experience I won't be coming back.  

Head past this place to Prince street where you can find a million other great restaurants.

I'll start off with the fact that the staff is very kind and amazing. The brunch menu here is to die for. They serve really good food for brunch. The restaurant looks vintage and prettt cool as well. Loved it

My girlfriend took me here for brunch because she knows that I love salmon. I think this place had one of the best salmon benedicts that I've had. We also ordered the salmon bagels and the presentation was amazing. Each part (salmon, bagel, tomatoes/capers/cucumbers/onions) came out on a separate plate in a triple decker which was nice. 

The only reason for the 4 star is that we I found the waiter a bit rude. He seemed to roll his eye when we would ask for a coffee refill. The menu also didn't mark the price for coffee and other drinks so I was a but shocked when I was charged 7 dollars for the sparkling water. The waiter made it seem like sparkling water was of no charge when  he asked if I wanted tap or sparkling. 

Anyway, thus is a great brunch spot and the food was great!

This place was very interesting, the place itself was packed for Saturday brunch so you HAVE to make a reservation ahead of time. We ordered the omelet (with mushrooms, tomatoes, and cheddar-with arugula on the side) the breakfast potatoes, everything bagels with the salmon tray and the French toast. The food came out really quickly BUT our table was so small that we literally couldn't fit all the food on it, something they should rethink because it was a little unpleasant to sit with my plate basically in my lap until we could eat and clear some things out of the way. The omelet was an omelet, good but nothing extraordinary. The bagels were great and with the salmon was super yummy. The potatoes looked way better than they tasted, they were really dry and needed more flavor. However the French toast was amazing, one of the best I've ever had! It was crunchy on the outside and gooey in the inside and with the jam-incredible! We split the bill 4 ways and each ended up spending about $25 so not nearly as expensive as I was expecting but overall this is a pretty pricey place! Would go back tho!

Awesome bagel and great cured fish! Their food is so well made that I immediately want to go for the second time after I went for the first time. Highly recommend! The food is a little bit salty though.
What a disappointment.  The most overrated, over priced brunch I've ever had.  To top it off, rude, slow service.  I went running out of that place!

This is not just a bagel place. This is a bagel lox and cream cheese experience. It's indulgent but I could go there every morning. Great food. Incredible food as a matter fact. Best French toast I've ever had. And the best bagel lox and cream cheese in the world.

House salmon was very thinly sliced and tasty but a little more would have been nice. Steak tartar was not bad but had too many other ingredients in it. The bagels (comes with the salmon)  and buttered toast ( with tartar) were wonderful!!!  The seating space felt a bit crowded.

Don't bother. Go to Russ and Daughters!!! The service is beyond awful. They could care less are RUDE and apathetic. The food is fine. FINE. Not worth the $ and not that great. Portions are SMALL. Why is this placed always packed? The bagels? Please-ur kidding with The Best Bagel in NYC, right? Omg.
A P.S.- my boyfriend just went to Think Coffee and had a bagel with CC and lox for $8 and said it was 100% better than  Sadelles.

I LOVE THIS PLACE.

As a girl who loves salmon and smoked salmon, this place is heaven. Their salmon benedict is to die for. The bread isn't the typical English muffin, it is a beautifully buttered and served under soft, fresh salmon and a perfectly poached egg. While the hollandaise was bit too vinegary for my taste, every bite is heaven in my mouth.

The salmon bagels are also delicious - plated on triple deckers ! The fish is so fresh and delicious. The plating and decor are also adorable and everything is color-coordinated. The Type A freak in me is so pleased and satiated by similar shade of blue that lines the walls and adorns the cups. 

The four stars is because the service can be a little rude and uppity but aside from that, love this place and will come every time I visit NY!

They say the sticky buns are life changing and I'd have to agree. They're THAT good! If you go to Sadelle's these are a must try. 
Apart from that I shared the house salmon dish with a friend and an order of that + the sticky buns were enough to satisfy us with leftovers to take home! Overall although it is a little tight on space it's definitely worth a visit to. Also as a side note - this place is very instagrammable. Like, their food is just downright photogenic. So if you need some cute brunchy IG pics this would be a safe bet.

I've been here for both brunch and dinner, and personally I'm a bigger fan of the dinner menu. The brunch scene is crazy; think super long lines, over and hour long wait. The food is good but not really worth such a long wait. The brunch is famous for smoked salmon and bagels, and the way they serve the smoked salmon with tons of dips and spreads on a three tiered party tray is pretty nice. However, it's way overpriced for brunch! I don't need to eat a lox cream cheese bagel for over $25!

The dinner is another story. I enjoyed my meal thoroughly. The place is not too crowded and easy to get a res on a saturday night. My drink, the salty dog, was delicious, containing pamplemousse vodka and grapefruit juice. The vodka was pretty masked and it tasted like fresh grapefruit juice. We started with the veal dumplings which came in a delicious rich onion gravy that we later mopped up with buttery slices of bread. For my main I had the salmon with mustard sauce and my husband had the spicy fried chicken. Both were cooked so well. The salmon had a crispy exterior and was cooked just right so it wasn't overdone. The spicy fried chicken came with a truffle honey dip that was to die for. 

Overall, really delicious dinner, skip the brunch!

I'll start by saying this - the inability to make a reservation and the inevitable 1.5 hour + wait is not ideal by any means, for anything. With that being said however, the food was A+. My advice: go there expecting to eat 2 hours later and use that time to walk around Soho and kill some time. Plenty of nice areas in the hood.

Anyway, when we were finally seated (note: it is very tight in there, especially at the communal table) our server was excellent and very attentive, considering how busy it was. We ordered the now-famous tower with the complimentary bagel (one complimentary, rest extra but they're cheap), pickled onions, cucumbers capers and tomatoes and then added on an order of the egg salad. Additionally, we got an order of the coleslaw and the pickles. Everything was DELICIOUS. This is a trendy, hopping spot - great to take visiting family and friends or for enjoying a day in Soho.

For dinner! We went with dear friends for dinner, and our waiter Max was AWESOME. The food was soooo good, and  while you can order dinner items, we enjoyed brunch for dinner! The restaurant staff was so generous with portions, extras, and all around amazing service. The homemade bagels were so good - loved the s/p one! From the lox, pickles, whitefish salad, Freddy and Beverly salads to the most delicious cinnamon sticky bun ice-cream sandwiches to the french toast we've ever had, this place is a MUST. For brunch or dinner!  Thanks Sadelle's - see you next time!

INCREDIBLE experience!  The ambience, food and most of all, the SERVICE was above and beyond.  Everyone that we encountered wanted to make sure we had the most amazing experience and truly catered to our needs!  Can't wait to go back!

Overpriced for mediocre (at most) breakfast/brunch. Bagels are small, not even soft. The extent of food "presentation" is in the form of an expensive "tower" which, as seen in accompanying photos, is not all that impressive. If you opt to not pay an arm for the tower, and order just a plain bagel or sandwich, it will be delivered to you in no different manner than at a diner. Along the same lines, boozy cocktails are in the $15-$20 each range, served in standard sized glassware, and you're only kidding yourself if you think they put more alcohol in them for the higher price point. 

In summary, this is the first brunch place I would actually go out of my way to DETER others from going to. I actually felt guilty being the one to insist that my party dine here. Frankly, I am surprised by the number of high positive reviews here; my guess is that people mentally tend to associate a better overall experience with paying a higher fare, in order to make themselves feel less shafted. 

Sure, the restaurant's interior decor is lovely, but I can confidently say that if I had time to whip up and sell average-tasting and average-looking brunch at the same prices charged by Sadelle's, my apartment would look just as swanky on the inside.

unbelievable ! this is not your typical deli spot, I was so blown away - like how often can you get little hot dogs on a menu ! we loved them you could tell there was high quality meat.  We did have a reservation and sat at the long communal table which was ideal you are right in the middle of all the action. There is amazing ice coffee/ pure black cold brew from La Colombe ! 

Their potatoes that came with the eggs are the best I think I've ever let into my mouth.  The bagels come on a stick and are stacked up which looks very visually cool ! and they taste pretty good too! 

the matzoball soup was herbalicious and had a lot of flavor, I really enjoyed it as well.

Will definitely plan to go back next time in NYC!

This place is amazing ! Although the front end tables are small, they are cozy and allows for an intimate dining experience that's casual yet chic. The smoked salmon in there was one of the best I've ever had.  The eggs Benedict was cooked to perfection. The service is attentive and I'll definitely be back.

Sadelle's is a fun spot for tourists, or those looking to get back in touch with their Jewish roots. 

They have a great selection of bagels and fish, but the hype, wait times and price are just not worth it. The fish I had were all delicious (lox and tuna) but the bagels were hard - you can walk into any bagel store in NYC for a better quality bagel. 

The prices are also a bit insane. I don't typically complain about prices, but I think you can walk into any bagel store in NYC and grab similar ingredients for a quarter of the price, but enjoy the taste more. 

The presentation of the food and interior was lovely and I'm glad I went, but don't need to go again.

What seemed like a promising venue for a delicious combination of bagels and 'bits' in the classic New York tradition fell woefully short. Certainly the venue is 'cool', but the bagels. One word: pathetic. The bagels are the size of the very small donut; in New York City this just doesn't cut it. Go to H&H, buy a bag of bagels and start again. Oh, and stay clear of the wine list unless you can stomach battery acid.

An absolute must for a great NYC brunch experience whether you're a local or tourist. I love absolutely love salmon so this was a no brainer.

Their lox towers ($21) are great to split if you just order an extra bagel. We got the house salmon, an extra bagel, side of potatoes, and a side of bacon. It was the perfect amount of food for 2 people. 

Salmon was fresh and paired well with the chives cream cheese. Loved being able to make your own lox bagel and the aesthetic of the restaurant. The brunch potatoes are awesome! Huge chunks of potatoes, but still has some crispy edges.

Reserve on OpenTable ahead of time and you won't have to wait!

The French Toast was to die for! 

My husband and I went on Friday we were able to make reservations which was ideal because we heard that it gets busy on the weekends. But, I would wait in line for the French Toast any day.  They were crispy on the outside and warm and gooey on the inside and tasted amazing.  I'm still thinking about them!  

In addition to the French Toast we got some bacon and potatoes(which could feed a family of 4).  I know its pricey for breakfast items, but its New York and food was so good that it made it worth it.  I can't wait to go back! Yums:P

I have lived in New York for five years and have never left a review before. I ordered a salad to go last night from Sadelle's and became violently ill an hour after eating it. I would expect a $38 salad to have the freshest ingredients and am horrified by this. I have eaten here before without getting sick, but this was a horrible experience.
Food was great.  Service (waiter) was great.  VERY pricey for what it is ($7 half cup of iced coffee).  Be prepared to wait out even with a reservation.

Fairly expensive, but great for the quality that you get.  My friend and I stopped in for brunch/lunch on a weekday because she raved about the babka cake. And she was right. It was dense, but moist and chocolatey, and very amazing! We also got bagels and lox, which were great and came in a tower, which definitely made me feel special.

(P.S. casually saw Jake Gyllenhaal on the way out, nbd. Typical day in NYC, right?)

Severe food poisoning from a Waldorf Salad.  My own fault since when I took my first bite of the chicken, I knew something wasn't right.  But couldn't get the waiter's attention so decided to roll the dice.  Bad move.  Never again.
Amazing! Sticky buns are DELICIOUS! Service was excellent! Our brunch waitress was Ilana and she was so attentive and accommodating! Great experience, food and atmosphere is fabulous!

We stumbled upon Sadelle's for breakfast and are so happy we did!  Neat atmosphere, great food and great service!  A little pricey but they do have options that cover reasonable range.  Overall great experience!

I ordered a $100 tower with all different types of smoked fishes and bagels. Incredible. It was enough for 4 people. But since only two of us were eating from it, we had to take most of it home. I eat a lot and there was plenty left over. The third person at our table ordered an omelette and said it was the best omelette he had ever eaten. Service was excellent. I highly recommend this place.

We made sure we were on time, for you are charged 30$ per person if late on reservation. However we waited for more than 30 minutes passed our reservation time, so we waited 45 min outside for being a respectful 15 min prior.  We ended coming in rushing hostess for a 3rd time after it started raining. 
The place is nice, the staff was professional, our waiter was tall blond guy who I forgot the name was attentive and he gave us a good service. The salmon was great. Pass on the omelette. The coffee is only regular, there is no espresso, cappuccino, macchiato, only regular black coffee and it is 4$ a cup. Hey at least the cups were nice.  The highlight was the sausage, the salmon, and the Benedict. The choice of white, turquoise and wood for decor is lovely.

Been trying to come here for a while but could never get a reservation but then walking past mid week randomly we noticed it didn't look full and managed to get sat right away. We had the blueberry pancakes- really light and fluffy so I'd recommend these, and the salmon bagel tower which tasted great, but the bagel itself was tiny and so loads of toppings were left. For $21 for the tower a second or more normal sized large bagel would have been nice! Table was also tiny and it couldn't all fit on very well so things were always in danger of falling off! Great decor in the place though but not enough bathrooms, both of us stood in line on separate occasions for a while and both times restaurant staff were in there taking ages! Perhaps have separate bathrooms for the kitchen staff? Probably wouldn't return to eat in but I'd maybe grab a takeaway bagel from here.

Everything was great, service was excellent taste of the food exceptional especially egg benedict. I love the sauce of egg benedict. We ordered bacon as side and the crispiness was as perfect as I expect. Unfortunately I have to admit that blueberry pancakes were not the best but still good to eat. I strongly advise you to have mimosa as first drink with your brunch and have some salmon.
Understaffed. Poor management and service. Lack of attention to customers. Great good.

Sadelles is SO tasty. Came here with my husband and we sat down for an awesome brunch. We shared a matzah ball soup to start - a little fatty but tasty. Then we shared two bagels, the house salmon and the scottish salmon - both excellent. The tower is such a beautiful presentation. Is it overpriced? Yes. But the salmon was not salty and it was perfectly sliced. I would love to come back for the ambiance and the delicious bagel and lox. Make sure to make a reservation though!

Sadelles definitely lives up to the hype. Came here for brunch today for the second time and was not disappointed. I would've given it 5 stars if it wasn't for the wait, even with a reservation and the price. It is a pricey brunch but so worth it every once in a while. My friends and I got bagels, lox, whitefish, and egg salad all of which could not be more perfect. We also got a Cobb salad to split which was huge and amazing as well. Overall we all left very full and happy, will be back again!

Is this New York's best bagel spot? No.
Does Sadelle's have the best lox in New York? No. 
Is it the place to see and be seen? Yes. 

I have a theory Sadelle's exists solely for the insta. For real though, those towers...so photogenic. And when you're dining there you feel super posh and *elite.*

Yes, the food is good and it's expensive for what you get, but it's certainly a cool place to spend your Sunday brunch. They also have the best Bloody Mary I've ever tasted (with house-infused horseradish vodka, a must). The omelets are good too, and very fresh.

The service, however, is lacking. When we got the food, they didn't bring us plates until we asked. It also took a while for it to come out. When it did, they messed up and didn't bring us one of the bagels we had ordered. When we told them, they said it would be right out. In a span of 20 minutes, we asked twice about the missing bagel and they said it would be right out (it takes time because bagels get toasted and apparently they stand in line for the toaster). Then, almost a half hour later, they said they were out so we had to switch from our original salt and pepper bagel to a cinnamon raisin one. And behold, another bagel wait. Then, as we were finishing up, but not finished yet, a waiter came and TOOK OUR TOWER WITHOUT ASKING. Sir, did I say we were finished? When we gave him the look of death he left the plates on the table but took the tower to a neighboring table. I guess they were out of towers? But seriously, in a place that's famous for them, YOU CANNOT RUN OUT OF YOUR #1 INSTAGRAMMED PIECE!

Now for the bagels...they're small and almost Montreal-style when it comes to size and taste. They're good, but my biggest pet peeve is a toasted bagel. A proper bagel should never have to be toasted. In fact, legit NYC bagel institutions don't even have toasters because they know that's the worst thing you can do with these round little delightful carb-bombs. But I digress...the bagels are fine. Order two. Shoutout to the cream cheese, it's so perfectly whipped and delicious, they even give you chive as well as plain.

Yes the bagels are more expensive then other bagel shops, but the food is really good, and the tuna melt is exceptional. The service was impeccable and our waitress made our experience wonderful. Highly recommend for breakfast.

Such a fantastic breakfast, lunch, and dinner spot!
For lunch and brunch, think high ceilings with lots of natural light, a delicious spread of lox, bagels, and all necessary accoutrements (2 different kinds of cream cheese, tomatoes, red onions, capers, etc.), 
It's strange to have steak tartare for lunch, but the one on their lunch menu is one of the best I've ever had. 
The pastries are some of the best in the city. Known mostly for their sticky bun, which is to die for... really to live for. 

For dinner, think high ceilings with excessively tall candlesticks burning bright, standing in candelabras around the room. The food has a Russian theme. The potatoes with sour cream, chives, and ikura (salmon roe) is seemingly simple but filled with such diverse flavor. 
We tried several appetizers and several mains and everything was fantastic! Everything is quite filling, so we had quite a few leftovers afterward. However, we still had room for the famous sticky bun that is served warm, sliced in half, with a scoop of vanilla ice cream sandwiched in-between. 

The food and ambiance are both fantastic, but the service is something to be noted as well. Not just the kindness of the servers, which is something to certainly be noted alone, but the small details of the service is exceptional. From the small elegant tray of utensils that is placed on the table, to the at-table check processing.

Everything about this places screams what NYC once was and should always be.

I absolutely loved this place. We had made reservations for Saturday morning brunch and just fell in love. We knew we had some major Soho shopping to do afterwards so we wanted to have a nice brunch and get all our delish food in before we walk it off. We ordered the lox platter which come one is very photo worthy and couldn't wait to receive it. We also ordered a side order of white fish salad as well. But to start fresh squeezed orange juice which is a must order to pair with the lox.

The platter came and their bagels, we had the salt and pepper ones were absolutely divine. Some of the best lox I've ever had as well as beautiful presentation. I will definitely come back to this place on my next NY trip. The white fish salad was also tasty but I wouldn't get it again and I would just get extra lox next time. The cream cheeses were also very good I must add.

I didn't get their much talked about french toast just because we were more in a savory over sweet mood and it was enough food for us. Our server was also very sweet and on top of everything. Out of all the places, this was one of my fave on this last trip, plus the atmosphere was just adorable, makes you want to sit here for hours at a time. I will definitely be back someday! Sadelle's you're a winner!

Tonight was wonderful to break fast at Sadelles. The food, ambiance and the wait staff were wonderful especially Max. There were a few rude customers who came in with an attitude. There were four courses to be served and it was a special arranged night but they continued to be rude till they didn't finish their meal and got up and left so nasty. The staff said it was a busy night it was very crowded but they weren't having it. The wait staff tried to help them they just weren't having it. Anyway it's a wonderful place and very delicious!!

This has been on my foodie list for a very long time now and I was so happy to finally come here on Saturday. Got here early in fears of losing our spot but ended up waiting 15 min anyways. This place gets busy!! It was Yom Kippur and it was still busy. It was SO worth the wait. We got two types of smoked lox, everything bagels, and caviar (mmmmm). Oh and let me tell you the Bloody Mary was one of the best I've ever HADDD!!!! My favorite Bloody Mary is actually from the W Hotel bar in Barcelona sooo definitely hard to top;)

Very rude waiter named MAX. I ordered and he left brought coffee after 10 minutes.  Ok whatever.  He later came back and told me that they had no gluten free bagels. I told him I could not eat regular bagels. And then he looks at me like he wanted me to leave. He said nothing more and walked away. So I left.

I had also asked him to turn down the music a little bit, he seemed quite offended by that so perhaps he just wanted me to leave-- regardless of food. Hostess was very upset that I left and thought it was about the music.  She was very nice too bad she has to work with Max

Ok you win. I left and Max --you are still a Jerk.

Food is great. Sampled a lot, including the breakfast potatoes, bacon, pigs in a blanket, omelette, breakfast sandwich, coffee, drinks and of course the famous bagels. Our waiter had a bit of an attitude, and the hostess didn't acknowledge at all that it was a special occasion (my birthday) which was noted on the reservation, so that put a slight damper on things. We ended up having to ask to be moved to a nicer seat because they placed us all the way up front originally almost as if we just walked in without a reservation.  But after we moved it was generally a pleasant experience. Surprised  that there is no acknowledgment for special occasions especially when you're spending over $130 for what is essentially a good breakfast. Don't want to read into the why we weren't treated the nicest but I saw a marked difference with others serviced around us ...

This is a review for a most simple take out order. I just ordered their Everyting Bagel with chive cream cheese. I wish I ordered half a dozen of these for myself because I could have had these all day. These bagels were fresh, perfectly made and delicious. 
I would love to come back to this place for a legit sandwich and enjoy a meal here

Sadelles is a "Disneyland" type restaurant. Completely on theme with the upscale Jewish deli vibe; all waiters wear the white coats butchers wear. Its located on a busy street in Soho and is expensive. People come here decked to the nines in designer clothes as well.

My sister and I both got the classic Sadelles House Salmon which comes with deliciously seasoned cucumbers, tomatoes and capers. For $23 for a bagel, the bagels were pretty small and the salmon was sliced VERY THIN. They offer everything, everything plus, poppy, sesame, cinnamon raisin and plain bagels. 

Nonetheless, it was absolutely delicious. Would return with a friend from out of town, but a little expensive to be a regular spot.

Wow. Epic French toast. I went there after seeing a review about the best French toast in town. Even it can be too oily for some, it's perfect for my crave! Heard the bagel was good but only tried a sesame one and was not too impressed.

At Sadelle's, bagels are probably the most popular item, whether it's breakfast, lunch or dinner and there's a good reason why - they are absolutely delicious! They are on the small side, but size here is in no way a predictor for quality. The salt & pepper bagel I had was the perfect amount of chewy, and the salt and pepper flecks (apparently Icelandic fleur de sel is used here) on the exterior packed a lot of flavor but not in an overpowering way, and managed to impart a great contrast in texture from the bagel itself. I'm not sure whether the selection differs from day to day, but when I came here for an early Saturday brunch a couple of weeks ago, they were offering plain, sesame, onion, salt & pepper (what I opted for) and everything bagels. The much-lauded pumpernickel bagel was nowhere in sight, unfortunately. Only two types of cream cheese though, plain and chive, though it didn't matter to me because chive is one of my go-to's and the chive cream cheese here is the bomb. 

In terms of other brunch items, they serve up some delicious fried eggs here, and a decent omelette. I was not impressed with their potatoes though, which lacked consistent flavor despite being aggressively seasoned on the exterior. I hear that their French toast is also amazing but did not get a chance to try last time. The bagels alone will lure me back here so I'm sure I'll come back soon enough.

Very expensive. Mediocre service.  Staff inattentive. Nice atmosphere.   
Our sugar bowl was only stocked with sweet-n-low or Equal.   No natural sugar.  Asked our waitress , she said she will try to find some! What! Or you serious? No real sugar?!  She returned five minutes later with only two packets of sugar for two generous size mugs of coffee. We had to ask for milk for our coffee (it was not offered) for which she returned with a creamer that had about 4 tablespoons worth of milk. Not enough!
Bagels are very small and not soft.
