We had an aerial view of the bagel making station and saw that the bakers would cut a piece of dough from a large plastic wrapped piece and weigh each piece before they  rolled and formed into a bagel. We observed them trimming the smallest amount of dough off as I suppose it was over the weight limit. Funny that the cream cheese amount offered was generous for a tiny bagel, but we couldn't 
get enough sugar and milk for our coffee.
Breakfast potatoes had good flavor but were mostly fingerling potatoes that were much too hard to eat.   
Would not visit again.

This place gets 4-5 stars for the food but 1 star for the consistently horrendous service. I have been here about 5 times - 3 for takeout and twice for sit down. The service is terrible for both! Takeout line takes a very long time (as they only staff one person.) for reference, with 3 people ahead of me getting bagels, I waited for 30 minutes!! Once I got a salmon cream cheese bagel and when I got home discovered that they didn't actually put the cream cheese on the bagel. Another time I got a bagel and chocolate babka but again upon getting home discovered that they forgot to give me the cookie! I went back and they didn't apologize or anything, just made me wait in line to get a cookie. When dining here, the service was awful as well. Came with my husband on a Sunday morning - granted it was a busy time but they are a breakfast place so they should have figured out how to run the operation. Ordered two towers with salmon and tuna as well as tea to drink. The bagels came first toasted, with only one plate for two people. I had to ask for a second plate and wait for 5 min. The towers came later at which point the toasted bagels had cooled. Also no tea...I had to ask three times for tea (different waiters/service staff each time) and finally got it after 15 minutes at which point I was almost done with my bagel. I then discovered that they brought the wrong tea even after I asked to confirm that it was earl grey and they did. It was green tea. Overall it's clear that this place does not care about customer service at all - literally the worst service I have ever experienced  on each visit!

Went to Sadelle's on a Monday brunch after hearing high praise from veterans of the restaurant. We were expecting to be "wowed" but were anything but. Soon after being seated we realized we had no identified server. As wait staff passed by we politely asked for coffee. One cup arrived at a time and we had to ask each time for another. We were wrong to assume that this would cue service for a waiter to take our order. We snagged someone walking by and asked her to explain the concept of "towers," a feature unique to the restaurant. In a barely audible tone she half heartedly explained the tower and walked away. Her explanation offered no clarity and inspired no appetite. Then our search continued for our true server. We finally found someone to take our order. Food came out promptly and tasted good which was fortunate as no one checked in the entire meal. It seemed that no was in charge and employees all looked less than enthusiastic. We had to ask multiple times to pay while a line built to the door. This place seemed to rely on their status at the expense of service. Will not be going back here!

Last week I bought the most expensive bagel I ever ate. $16 bagel with lox and chive cream cheese. It was absolutely worth it. Lox was fresh as could be and the bagel was excellent, I'm coming here again. I can't stand $8 deli bagels with 2 week old lox... it's not natural.

Do you want to be seated at an undersized table, cramped between strangers too busy taking pictures for the 'gram?

Do you want to taste *authentic* New York bagels that give bricks a run for their money at breaking your teeth?

Do you want to be shamed by your waiter and subsequently ignored for not wanting to spend $100 on brunch?

If you answered yes to any of the above, step right up because Sadelle's the place for you!

Honestly though, I wouldn't even want my worst enemy to come here. No one deserves this. I've had bagels from supermarkets that tasted better than this crap.
Best French Toast ever!   No celebrity sighting, but the great food and service made up for that.

I try not to go to the same place when I come to a Cory not my own but every time I come to NYC I have to come here at least once!!!! If you dine in they set a beautiful casual table. They're known for their lox (smoked/cured and hand sliced onsite) which is served in a tower with all the accompaniments (onion, tomato, capers, cucumbers...) and homemade bagels but everything here is spot on!

Need a bagel and coffee/juice to go, they have you covered too. 

Service is amazing and food comes out perfect. 

This is a spot not to be missed!

4+ stars food, particularly the the classic egg sandwich and the lox plates. Love the different  flavors they offer along with all the fixins! 

On my first visit I didn't have good service (see my earlier review for more details) but I have to give management credit because when I complained about the service, management took it seriously and contacted me to express concern about my experience and invited me back to try eating there again. I had a stellar experience on this visit and I hope that is more typical that my first trip there.
Overrated! We waited almost an hour to be seated! Staff were rude,the salmon wasn't anything special, save your time and money and go somewhere else!

As usual the lox tower with warm bagels, succulent tomatoes sprinkled with olive oil and sea salt and fluffy cream cheese doesn't disappoint. Eggs Benedict were wonderful as well. Service was great even though we felt that they wanted us to finish quickly I order to serve more people

I always love a Sunday-brunch stop at the uber-trendy, slightly-more-upscale deli!  Sadelle's is the perfect spot to cure a hangover, or if you're having a hair-of-the-dog kinda morning, or simply desire classic deli food with a fresh and fun vibe!  From the Salmon tower to the Egg Sandwich, Sadelle's delivers good-to-the-last-bite food!  The staff is friendly and efficient, and the playlist isn't so bad either. Who doesn't love to hear Steely Dan or Hall & Oates as you nosh on a homemade everything bagel?  And if you are coming off of a late-night bender, try the Bloody Mary...if that doesn't bring you back to life, I don't know what will!

Meh. We walked here from Katz's because the line was so long. Should have waited. The matzo ball in my soup had such a weird texture. It was grainy. Yuck. And you better like cilantro and parsley because it drowning in it. A bowl is 12$  On a better note the lox tower was tasty. And fancy feeling. But that will run you 23$. We asked for an extra bagel to go with, cause we were feeling cheap. The vibe in the restaurant is really cute. A bit of old school fancy but the music didn't match the vibe which is a missed opportunity in my opinion. I won't be back but mostly because of the price.
Prepaid $190 for 2.  Horrific, non existent service. Left b4 last 2 courses. Restaurant maybe 60% occupied.  Happy New

Excellent brunch place, be prepared to wait a while. Also, you better like fish. I highly recommend coming with a bigger group so you can get the smoked and cured fish platters. I thought bagels were a bit overrated but they're worth a try. The bacon egg and cheese was also very good. I recommend it if you're ordering for yourself and sharing with a group. Overall, very good brunch spot.

5pm reservation for a late-late Sunday brunch (early dinner?). I inform my hostess that 2 members of the party are stuck in traffic in an uber... and then she tells us that the kitchen closes soon.

I mean... why even take that reservation then???

Manager told us there wouldn't be an issue which calmed me down. And then waiter was excellent and very accomodating.

No issues whatsoever rest of the way. 

Bagels were solid (albeit mildly on the smaller Montreal-ish side). I got the burger, which was good... but nothing to write home about (a bit too much slaw for my taste).

Maybe akin to Russ & Daughters in terms of pricing (with a fancier address/location).

I got a bagel at Sadelle's recently with lox, cream cheese & all the toppings (capers, tomatoes, etc) and I have to say I was pretty underwhelmed. The lox was perfection, but the plain bagel tasted like one I could buy at the supermarket. For the price I paid (I think like $15, but I could be wrong), I would expect better. 

I would definitely go back and dine in, as I only got my bagel to go. Looking around at the tables eating around me, I would bet the food they serve is much better than the below average bagels they have. My advice is to just buy the fish or to go for brunch and skip the bagel.

I have been dying for a really good bagel spot near my office. Sadelle's being a few blocks away fit the bill. I ordered an everything 2.0 bagel, with regular cream cheese, house salmon, tomatoes, onions, and capers. This came out to $16. The bagel is certainly delicious, that is without question. The crusty outside and the level of resistance in the bite is just right. The flavor is all there. The addition of fennel and caraway seeds really kicks this everything 2.0 bagel up a notch. The bagels are a bit smaller and thinner than a typical bagel so I was a bit disappointed about that, however I am willing to overlook that because the house salmon was decadent and certainly better than average. I'm curious to try the other fish options they have. After having the everything 2.0 bagel I don't know how I will ever go back to regular everything bagels. A regular everything bagel just seems too boring now.
The Everything #2 with fennel and caraway seeds is my favorite NYC bagel, but holy crap the price difference between to go and to stay is way too extreme.  Just get it to go and save your money!

Sadelle's is awesome for the experience. When else will you ever be presented with a fish and bagel tower? Everything was delicious - the lox and sable, the bagels, the matzoh ball soup, the pickles, etc.
Only downside is the hefty price tag, making this a one-time kind of place.

Sadelle's is a bakery and restaurant located between W Broadway and W Houston in the heart of SoHo.

The obvious draws are the presentation of food and the beautiful interior. 

They are mainly known for its salmon tower. On my first visit, my friends and I ordered the salmon tower accompanied by several side dishes. It comes with two kinds of smoked salmon, cream cheese, dill, capers, cucumbers, tomatoes, etc. The dish is large enough to be shared among two or three people (if you order an extra bagel and some side dishes). 

The restaurant's interior is punctuated by the soothing color scheme with hints of sky blue and white (i.e. blue ceramic cups, dishes, and some wall arts). 

Once you walk into the restaurant you will see the bakery, where you can see the staff cutting up fresh salmon. 

The staff is friendly and attentive. Overall great experience.

Overpriced for a brunch place. If you're looking to have just a solid bagel sandwich, I'd head on over to Brooklyn and step inside your local deli shop. But wow oh wow is that bagel tower a sight for sore eyes. Beautifully crafted tower filled with many o' toppings and a generous, eclectic variety of spreads! Definitely worth a visit for that 10 second Insta story.
Food was just ok. Bagels were mediocre. Sticky buns overly sweet and cold. Tuna melt was small. Food took a very long time. Ambience was good. Tables were too small.

Amazing food!!!! Amazing ambience.

The salmon Benedict was incredible.
Mushroom barley soup was rich and delicious.
The house salmon stand....yum.
Bagels. No words to describe.
Watching the bagels being made. Priceless. 
Must go.

Wow! What a great breakfast experience! The service was excellent. The "tower" is perfect for two+ people. We had the salmon(s) and egg salad with all of the trimmings. If you've never tried it, go for the salt and pepper bagel. Pretty cool. The Columbe coffee is very good. Our daughter really enjoyed the iced coffee with almond milk.

Definitely overpriced for the quality, but all tasted delicious. Nothing different than a glorified Jewish brunch place. We got the smoked salmon which is really not enough for more than one person. The salmon is very thinly sliced. The bagels were delicious. I think I would have been happiest just eating bagels for my meal! We were told to order the chocolate babka which isn't on the menu. It was ok...slightly dry but not bad. The tables are so tiny so it's hard to maneuver but the food was good.

Everything was perfect. My boyfriend and I were able to try a selection of fish before we ordered. We eventually ended up getting the smoked salmon and bagels and then we tried the French toast which was amazing. Loved the vibe there, the staff was so friendly. I'd definitely come back with a bigger group so we can order the tower.

Sadelle's is not in the same league as Russ and Daughters. Their salmon is very good as are the omellet's but, the bagels are tiny. They do not serve chopped chicken liver, blintzes, latkes or herring which are all staples of any good Jewish deli. The place is very crowded and noisy but they do take reservations and the service is good. Do not waste your money on the "sticky buns". They came to the table cold and they are very, very small. Overall, Sadelle's is way overpriced for what you get.

After having Sunday brunch here with family I understand the reviews, even the negative ones. This is a unique experience and definitely a bucket list experience. It is the stratosphere of smoked salmon and whitefish salad as well as the tuna fish and bagels. Yes it's crowded, yes the tables are pure NYC sardine cans, but the food is awesome. The French toast was incredible. Our server was on point, helpful and friendly. It's very expensive but as I said, it's an experience that if your're a fan of the aforementioned foods you will remember. One tiny detail, pass on the babka. It's disappointing, I've had much better in Jersey.

The bagels were a serious disappointment. They are nothing like the classic NY bagel that people come to the city for - they are small and not dense at all. So depressing. 

The bright side - The NY Times names their sticky bun as the best in the city, and boy does it live up to it!!! Would highly recommend getting one of those...but for bagels, go to Ess-a-Bagel!

I had been wanting to try Sadelle's for the longest time and was a bit underwhelmed by the experience. Don't get me wrong the location is great, the restaurant itself has a great vibe and ambience, but with all the hype (and long wait times) I was expecting more.

The food was good. I had the smoked salmon tower and my friend had the LEO eggs (eggs with smoked salmon on top). The smoked salmon was phenomenal- so fresh! but the rest of the food was just ok. As mentioned above, I was expecting more - especially when both breakfast entrees were over $20.

The service was also just ok. Our waiter looked at us blankly when we asked for recommendations. Had to ask for the check 3 times and when I got it I was charged for an orange juice I never had! Good thing I checked the bill. Also the OJ was $8 which gives you another indication of how the pricing is high. Probably won't go back , but happy I tried it.
The food was super yummy - handmade bagels fresh fish, and amazing salads. Atmosphere is casual chic. Be sure to reserve in advance, or you'll wait around for a good long while for a table.

Went here for breakfast around 8am on a Saturday morning. The hostess at the front was a little rude saying that they opened at 8:30 and seemed as if she expected us to wait elsewhere. I ordered the fried egg sandwich while my boyfriend ordered the salmon benedict. The sandwich was more on the bread-y side. Salmon benedict was amazing though! I am usually not a salmon person, but the hollandaise sauce with the biscuit made each bite perfect! Would definitely recommend the salmon benedict. A bit pricey, but it's definitely a "treat yourself" kind of meal. You can also order caviar on the side. Service was just fine.

My friend had recommended this place because of their amazing bagels and lox. As an avid lover of lox I had high expectations, and boy were they met. The salmon was seasoned well and had a great flavor to them. The bagels were in my opinion ok. The reason for the three stars is mostly due to the fact that this place is way overpriced for its purpose. For a tower (lox, cucumbers, tomatoes, capers, cream cheese), two bagels, a scrambled egg and coffee our bill totaled around $60+. It's definitely one of those places that you try once mostly for the ambience and aesthetic instagram pic.
Love having brunch here! Typical menu but serve excellent dishes! The bakery is on point, especially the sticky  bun. Russian salad dressing, classic egg sandwich and Waldorf salad are my favorite.
I didn't have the bagel, but I've had the Sticky bun twice! It is hands down the best Sticky bun I've ever had. The customer service however, is horrible. I don't think I will be back because of it.

Came here for their famous lox tower as it is hyped up everywhere! It was quite easy to make a reservation online.

I love their decor and the ambiance of having Sunday brunch. Their lox was good, but quite oily as it is covered in oil. I enjoyed their housemade bagels, although I wish they were a bit larger. We also had a side of pickles which were delicious, but on the pricy side. The tables are pretty close together and it's pretty cramped overall in the restaurant. The service was quite slow and our server was not very attentive. A party that got there after us, got their food before us, and left before us! I am not sure that my experience and food justified the price.

They make a delicious bagel and I enjoyed the chive  cream with capers and cucumber! I opted for takeaway as there was a line otherwise. The staff is friendly and over all it was a good experience!

They are known for their various fishes but im a vegetarian so oh well
What's everyone complaining about? Make a damn reservation and go eat a freakin' delicious lox sandwich (also, the tuna melt is TDF).

Best tuna melt I have ever had. Bagel is inside out and toasted to perfection and the tuna is mixed perfectly.No celery in the melt which is key and an important detail. Matzo ball soup just ok and overalla little pricey for Jewish deli food, but hey it is Soho and quality is superior.

This will forever be my go to brunch spot in NY. I love the interior and the atmosphere. 

Service was spectacular, he helped us find the right items to share. You MUST, I mean MUST try the French Toast. This earned a 110% on our taste-bud meter. Its perfectly crunchy on the outside and soft and warm on the inside, forget all other food items. Although the rest of the items were pretty darn good too!

Amazing brunch. I came here today with a few of my friends and we ordered bagels and lox, blueberry pancakes, and bacon. It was all so delicious. It seemed a little expensive, but definitely worth it. I'd love to go back! The inside is also cutely decorated and feels very cozy - nice ambience.

Love love love the interior and style of this place. It's like a fancy deli style place with some Jewish and Russian influence. Presentation is what makes the place great. Order a tower of seafood and bagels. I had the white fish salad which was great and house salmon which was good but they kind of skimp on the portion and cut it very thin. Oysters are served beautifully but not the best oysters. Can't wait to come back when I am in New York.

The best breakfast I had in a long time! Very casual place with delicious food. French toast is a must, the best I've had. The salmon & white fish platters served with bagels and cream cheese are delicious. Also the vegetable platters go hand in hand with the fish platters. I will definitely return when in NY City.

I ate at Sadelle's approximately two days after I ate at Russ & Daughters. I think this is what I did wrong because for me it did not measure up. I ordered the Sable tower with a Salt & Pepper bagel and a cup of hot tea. The tower came with 3 very small slices of sable and what I thought was an insanely huge amount of sliced tomato and cucumber, neither of which I like. It was filler. I did eat the capers and sprigs of fresh dill. The sable was delicious I just felt like the fish portion was sparse and the bagel was tiny by New York standards. Nothing was bad but it just wasn't Russ & Daughters which is probably one of the best places in the world to eat this type of food.

The French toast is OMG yummy!! I highly recommend it! Definitely a diet breaker though, so don't expect anything less. 

We asked the waitress what else they are known for which we should order and they said the Breakfast sandwich and the Leo Omelette. I HIGHLY recommend the sandwich but not so much the Leo. I personally think it lacked flavor even though there is a large slab on house salmon on it. 

I am giving it 4/5 because the prices are a bit crazy for what you get. $22 for two half pieces of french toast seems a bit excessive, no matter how yummy it is.

I was really excited about this place, as it was highly recommended by friends.

I got breakfast to go - so I know I shouldn't judge the whole place based on this one experience but I was really unhappy.

I got an everything (although they don't call it that) with smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, and onion. It came to $21. WHAT? They charge you for condiments such as onions and tomatoes. Absolutely nuts. 

The bagel was tiny and I would argue that I got about 2 slice of salmon. There was actually more tomato then there was salmon. I'm sorry but it truly was robbery. I can get MUCH better bagels with MUCH more smoked salmon for MUCH cheaper in other places. Total let down. I will not be coming back.

This place was so darn cute inside. I went on a Monday so thankfully it was crowded but I hear it gets insanely busy on the weekends. I also hear it hosts a ton of famous people, none of whom I saw sadly. The decor is comfortable, relaxed, and just made me feel all around invited. The staff were super nice and polite. The prices are on the pricier side but then again it's New York so I guess everything is. 

The food is good. The only downfall is that the bagel or whitefish salad I ordered were a little too salty. I love a good whitefish salad but I couldn't tell which was the salty culprit but something was. The bagels are also on the small side. The lox was fresh and delicious. Coffee was warm so that wasn't ideal but it wasn't a meal ruiner. Overall I really enjoyed my time and would deff go again!!!
Had a lovely family gathering here- we didn't want to leave. The food and service were lovely and the coffee was great. Hope to come back next time I'm in the city.

YUM, all I can say is do yourself a favor a go here for brunch. There is definitely a wait so do expect that. The inside of Sadelle's is also very cute you can see where they make the bagels which is fun. Once we sat down we ordered some coffee, the tower with smoked salmon, everything bagel and all the extras and also ordered the French toast. 

The bagel tower was delicious, I mean I've had a lot of bagels with lox cream, cheese, capers, onions and tomatoes and this was VERY good. You can tell that the bagels are homemade which is always appreciated. Then I shared the French toast and let me tell you this dish is AMAZING absolutely delicious. The downside of it is that I could only eat about 4 bites it is so incredibly sweet that I don't think my stomach could have handled much more. I wish that it was less sweet, would have been more enjoyable.

We went to Sadelle's for brunch today. We liked the food and the atmosphere, but - like many reviewers - had misgivings about the pricing:

Tomato soup: was $11, should have been $9
Custom omelette with bagel: was $19, should have been $13-$15
Three cheese blintzes: was $15, should have been $10-$12
Coffee: was $5, should have been $3

Total before tax: was $50, should have been $35-$39

In summary, we would recommend that Sadelle's drop their prices by 20-30% to be competitive with similar places. When accompanied by a savvy media campaign, this could make the restaurant reach 50-80% capacity instead of the ~30% that we observed today. The way it was, we won't be back.

P.S. The blintzes were outstanding. The omelette was a little too salty. The tomato soup was much too salty.
Overpriced food and bad service. Seems like a tourist trap that is on auto pilot. The maître d' spent more time looking at her phone then engaging customers.

what really made our experience so amazing was our waiter maxwell! he was so kind accommodating when a few things got messed up he made them right and offered free shots! he was so professional the entire time we felt like princesses. 

obviously the ambiance is amazing cute deli style with tons of seating and a fast loud pace. the food is amazing known for their smoked salmon cut and cured in house with their hand made bagels as well. love how their bagels are small and thin and not really massive and doughy. if that makes sense lol. 

house infused vodkas are amazing. especially the olive. drinks are expensive but the food is so well priced it makes sense. bloody mary's come with tons of garnish peppers which was so cute!

Really enjoyed the House Salmon ($24) w/salt & pepper bagel, and mushroom barley soup ($14).All were very flavorful- especially the salmon, tomato and bagel combination. The place has a very cool vibe and was really busy during brunch. 

I was thinking it seemed way overpriced when I first saw the menu but after seeing the presentation and tasting the first bite, quickly forgot about that.

Would definitely try if you are in the area; the wait wasn't terrible with only two people. Also, when you do get the bill take yourself back to that first bite it will be less painful handing over your card.

First off, this place is ADORABLE. High class, great decor and the energy is amazing. Not only are the staff all extremely friendly, they are also very knowledgeable about the menu and the area! The food is AMAZING! No joke everything is so fresh. I'm pretty sure their cream cheese was the best I've ever had. You have to get the famous salmon tower--it's definitely enough for two people and you can get extra bagels if needed. When I'm back in NY I will always make this on my to do list!
A bit pricy and the portions are not large but really delicious, lots of unique items, Russian/Jewish style tasty food items. I had breakfast and cheese blintzes and challah toast were excellent.

Where to begin? This place came highly recommended by a coworker as a "typical Jewish brunch" joint. We were in the city for a sisters weekend. Let me tell you. It was everything and then some. We made reservations which also was recommended. We were lucky to snag a 10:45 on a Sunday. SO. LUCKY. The wait was long without reservations. 

With large light fixtures, high ceilings, candlesticks, and waiters walking around with traditional hats on; you are immediately taken back and feel as though you're in this gatsby-esque room. At the front a chef is there slicing fresh lox. It was right, don't get me wrong. We were seated upstairs in a corner booth practically on top of other people. But that doesn't matter. Everything made up for it. There were 4 of us. Here's what we ordered:

First, the bloody Mary's. Holy Jesus. We made it with the horseradish infused vodka. Hands down the best blood mary I've ever had. Accompanied with a green olive, red pepper, celery, green tomato, and yellow pepper. It was the best thing ever. 

Food (heads up the waiter said we ordered like champs):

Tower with house lox, 2 egg salads, side of pickles, side of bacon. The tower comes with a plate of tomato, cucumbers, and capers as well as 2 scallion cream cheeses and a regular cream cheese. The bagels are also made IN HOUSE TO ORDER. They came piping hot. We got the everything. (The everything 2.0 is different. Those bagels have caraway seeds and fennel). I totally appreciated that they had bagels without those seeds because I hate them. 

And then. For dessert. We had an order of their famous French toast. Each order comes with 2 THICK slices of challah. How do they make it? Let me tell you: they soak challah over night in milk and vanilla bean. Then, in the morning, they PUMP it with CUSTARD! WHAT!!?? It was crispy on top, super soft and moist inside. It was incredible. Comes with syrup and delicious raspberry jam. It was EVERYTHING. You really are doing yourself an injustice if you don't order it. 

And then, of course, we had to get a chocolate babka to go and bring Home for tonight. At $20 a loaf, I hear it's absolutely worth it. 

Was it pricey? Hell yes. Was it worth it? Hell yes. It was such an enjoyable experience. I would easily do  the same thing over again.

A Jewish girls dream. Any girls dream. Any boys dream. A dream. 

I'll expand. The entire Sadelle's experience was a pleasure from start to finish. Whoever is in charge of their reservations should be awarded. I have been involved in an email chain with a woman regarding a reservation for this morning for almost a week. She was so sweet, helpful, and human. Yes, human. Not some automated message thanking you for your "patronage". She really helped get us a prime reservation for a Sunday morning with a weeks notice! Which, if you're familiar with Sadelle's, you'll know is quite the feat. 

Upon walking in you're greeted with the scent of freshly made (yes, FRESH) bagels. Not to mention the man behind the counter who is slicing fresh lox for table service. High ceilings, stunning light fixtures, all with the bagel-making area at the center. The ambiance of the restaurant truly takes your breath away. 

And then, the food. 
We began with horseradish vodka Bloody Mary's. The best I've ever had- no question. I've never seen my fiancé order one, let alone down one so fast! 

We ordered a tower with lox, and two orders of egg salad. Everything bagels, again, freshly made. A side of pickles and a side of bacon. Oh, the tower also came with seasoned cucumbers and tomatoes, cream cheese and scallion cream cheese- yes!!! Everything was amazing. But then, the kicker. We ordered their famous French toast. Soaked overnight in a vanilla bean milk, pumped full of custard upon service and grilled to perfection. I will dream of this until the next time we go to Sadelle's. Served with a homemade jam and syrup- my mouth is watering just talking about it. 

To finish the meal we ordered their chocolate babka loaves to go because, why not? 

The entire brunch was incredible. Pricy, without a doubt. But worth every penny. I was ready to walk out the door, pivot and turn, and renter for round 2 immediately after. Sadelle's, well done. I cannot wait to come back.
Sadelle's was great! I started off my birthday here and it was a great start to my morning. Everything from the food to the atmosphere to the service was great! Our waiter Max W. was exceptional!!

Well, again... this is a brunch dream. Let's make it known that the Major Food Group has never done anything wrong. 

For people watching, this place is a 5/5. For service, 4/5. For food and FRESHNESS, 5/5. I mean you watch your lox get delicately cut and carefully served to you. 

This place murders the brunch basics. Lox, cream cheese, bagels, eggs... perhaps, all in one? Either way, this is not your hungover brunch spot(although it can be). You'd rather come to this place perfectly prepared like Sadelle's prepared for you.

Caviar? Check.
Bagel towers? Check.
White coats? Check. 
Expensive? Checkkkkkkk, but worth it.

This is an amazing breakfast spot. Great prices and great food. Ambience and Staff are super nice and helpful. 

I ordered the salmon loc plate, which is filling enough for 2 people (although they say it's for 1). I would add a side of avocados, they give you a good amount and they're so tasty.

Also, the breakfast potatoes are amazing. Highly recommend those as well.

Sadelle's has amazing food & service, period. I made a reservation and we got seated right on time. I specifically came for the tiered smoked salmon presentation and I was not disappointed. Everything tasted amazing -- the cream cheese was fluffy and creamy and the smoked salmon was incredibly fresh and thinly sliced. I'll definitely be back.

We came at 12:09 and it was somewhat busy, so we put down our names and they told us to come back in 30-45 minutes but be back in 30 just in case. We walked around for half an hour and got back to the restaurant at 12:41. When we checked in again, they told us another 20 minutes. So we waited. At 1, we checked again, and they told us 10 more minutes. After 10 minutes, they just told us "soon".

By 1:20, we checked in again, since it was more than double the original wait time they had told us originally. One of the hostesses/manager? told us they would buy us drinks at the bar, which was a nice gesture. We ordered our drinks and finally after almost an hour and a half, we were seated.

We sat down and the first thing the waitress said to us was "Did you pay for your drinks already?" instead of greeting us.

The meal was good. We ordered the house salmon and Scottish smoked with the everything bagels and it was good. Bagels were a little salty but it was soft and toasted perfectly. When we were paying, they failed to mention that they didn't take cash, only after my friends and I sorted out our payments. 

Overall, good food, but unfortunately, the service didn't match up.

Excellent food, but the service is a bit slow and uncoordinated. The wait times in between waiting for someone to take our order, receiving our order, and then having my coffee order forgotten was a bit odd.. since the restaurant was not packed/hectic in the first place. 

The "Leo" is a delicious, rich, massive plate of eggs, caramelized onions, green onion, and salmon. Definitely big enough to share among two people -- and obviously get the bagels with fish/eggs. This is a great place for a nice brunch/lunch, but be wary of the slow service!

Let's face it, don't come here on a Saturday or Sunday at 11am even if you have a reservation because you won't enjoy yourself. This place is so popular there is always a crush of people on the weekends. 

However, if you go early or on a different day, it is a great place. You do get great service. I have had great wait staff who give me tips on what to order outside of my usual. I am also gluten free and they have THE BEST gluten free everything bagels on earth! Last time I was in, I got an inside-out grilled cheese on a GF everything bagel with tomato soup (no croutons). DO NOT MISS THE GRILLED CHEESE! You will thank me later. Their scrambled eggs are amazing because they make them with cream cheese in them! The salmon towers are excellent too, the egg dishes, the salads. What's not to recommend? And you can get bagels to go!

Be smart about it, go at an off time and make a reservation! You will have an enjoyable experience and great food.

Grabbed a bagel to-go and this was literally the best bagel i've ever had in my life. I'd give it 5 stars except it cost me $18 for a bagel with salmon and cream cheese spread. Salmon is hugely overpriced, but it's SoHo i guess.

The wait time for if we were to sit down for three people would have been 45 minutes and the restaurant was pretty crowded around 1pm on a Saturday.

The hype is real. Everything is outstanding - an awesome place for brunch with friends. The fish is to-die-for and the line out the door is for to-go orders. We waited about 45 minutes. They're operations are supreme and I loved watching them make the bagels through the clear glass window!

Very over rated, came for brunch. It's kosher style so I think people like it. I think the food is very mediocre. The only good thing is the locks are fresh. Aside from that the tables are extremely small, not many options aside from bagels. I won't be coming back to me this place is really nothing special the food looks better than it tastes.

Really like Sadelle's  but this time we went and they had "Grade Pending" sign. If a restaurant has a 'Grade Pending' sign, it had enough violations to earn a 'B' or a 'C' and it is contesting the low grade (New York Times). Left without eating.

What a disappointment. I really was looking forward to meeting friends there on March 3 for brunch. The reservation can only be made by email. They made a reservation for a different restaurant in the group and I only caught the mistake the day before. The appetizer we ordered to share came after the entrees. We had to ask them to hold the entrees. Then the food got cold. (They did remake it after complaining) The food was good- but Tal's Bagels on the UES makes a better bagel and lox for a fraction of the cost. It was really loud, super tight in table placement, and not really fabulously delicious for the price. Service was slow and not attentive. We had to flag down a waiter for coffee refill and just about everything else. This is a lot of hype for not a lot of value. But obviously a place to be seen. And... there were open tables while people were packed at the front of the restaurant waiting to be seated creating the appearance of being overflowing. But wait! The Bloody Mary was really tasty! Good thing we had the alcohol first.

Make a reservation for a weekend brunch as there are long waits. Great presentation of their food items. I love the way Sadelle's presents their food but it also tastes just as good as it looks!! The bagels are so fresh and tasty. I truly think they may be my favorite New York bagels. Also, they will bring you extra bagels to go along with your salmon if you request. The everything bagel is awesome!! I love that the salmon is topped with dill as it adds to the freshness of the nova. The nova also pairs great with the chive cream cheese. Definitely worth a visit when in the Soho area!

Super crowded around brunch time on Saturday- we stopped at the counter where you can get bagels to go. I ordered the everything bagel with everything but the fish and it was ~4$. Honestly, was not impressed - bread wasn't very toasty and cream cheese wasn't anything special. Would definitely rather go to a mom n pop type of bagel shop in NY.

If you're excited about bagels and stuffing yourself with cured fish, this is the place to be. 

Sadelle's Tower was more than plenty for 4 people, and we absolutely loved the addition of the tuna salad. I'm not a Bloody Mary person, but my brunch companions loved theirs (get the olive-infused vodka). 

You probably won't have room for dessert in the end, but force it down; the French toast was unbelievable.

Had brunch at Sadelle's a few weeks ago and it was excellent! The decor is beautiful and I layout of the restaurant was interesting. I loved the attention to detail throughout the space. I made a reservation on opentable 3 weeks prior, as I saw there was availability at a normal brunch time (1pm). Upon arrival the hostess was very welcoming and sat us shortly after. We started off with the pigs in a blanket, which were delicious. I ordered the Cobb salad and my friend ordered the tuna platter. We both really enjoyed everything! It definitely is on the pricier side, but it's a great spot for an occasional brunch!

Great food, especially trout and burger. Good track selection out from speakers. 
Recommend for dinner, because of the light, candles and wine selection.

Sometimes it takes me a while to review places, so I forgot the name of this place. I googled "fancy delicious bagels in NY" and Sadelles was the first place- and that was the place I went to. I am glad to see that the internet agrees with my assessment. What i hope the internet agrees with is that the service is amazing.
We ordered to go because it was a 45m wait- and when the wait for our bagels was 10m long. the cashier/bagel maker gave us a free brioche thing. So nice!

I really enjoyed the atmosphere in the restaurant. The tables are close so be prepared to hear other people's conversations. I made reservations but it wasn't busy when it first opened. The service was great and the food was good. It's really the experience more than anything. If I came with others, I would have tried the tower but I went with the Salmon Benedict instead with the house salmon.

The atmosphere itself was nice but the menu
is totally over priced !
I ordered the house salmon, side of eggs and chamomile tea. Including tip I payed 53$.
Eventually  it was a bagel with salmon, cream cheese and veggies. The price was 24$ for the plate of the bagel and 12$ for a side of eggs.

Holy shit, I just spent 20 bucks on a bagel. I started feeling an undeniably heavy feeling of remorse, but then I got my bagel and it was the most delicious thing I have eaten all year. Will be back on my future NYC visits. That cream cheese... I don't know what they put in it but I want to inject it into my veins. Truly scrumptious.

Prices are 50% higher than Russ and Daughters, portions are smaller and food is on par. So why would anyone go here when that alternative is only a few blocks away?  Hard to not feel like you're being fleeced when even the coffee on the menu is $8 and a side of pickles is $10.

Given the location, I expect it to be overpriced so this review is somewhat forgiving in that respect.  

The Sadelle's tower is nice and enough food for 4 people without questions.  That said, the bulk of it was salmon/whitefish salad which, although very good, do not justify the $125 price tag.  The amount of sliced smoked fish was rather paltry, although what was there was good.  

The wait staff was pleasant enough but I was surprised that, after making an announcement that the bagels were "unlimited" when we ordered, that when we in fact sought a second order that we were told that they would check what was available, if anything.  At $100 per couple for bagels and a drink each, I expected slightly better. 

All in all, quality is good and if you enjoy a "scene" this is the place.  My advice, splurge $100 at a proper appetizing store and go bonkers on the good stuff instead.
Holy wow. Just wow. The salami. Tower was everythinggg. I want this 10000099 times over. I need more. I can't stop thinking about this bagel. Need more coffee. But wow this bagel

Let me start by saying the food was very good, but it wasn't worth the price for breakfast. If you want to pay for the ambiance and a place to enjoy your food, then it is a good spot. We made reservations because it was recommended; on this chilly rainy weekday,​ we did not need them. I was glad there was no rush to leave as it allowed me to make every one of my bites perfect with a little bit of each ingredient​. 

The ordering technology was impressive. Each server has an iPhone​ that they put the order in on so it is immediately given to the bartender and kitchen. 

I had a Salty Dog with some lovely vanilla​ salt on it​ but only had one because it was $15. My hubby​ and I shared the house salmon tower. I love the presentation of the tower. The tower is three levels. The top one has the salmon with dill and the second was very fresh tomatoes, capers, ​and cucumbers. The third plate of the tower has the bagel and cream cheese. If there are two people eating breakfast, then you can add a bagel for $2. We got the salt and pepper and​ everything 2.0 bagels. I LOVED the everything 2.0 bagel. It is 2.0 because on top​ of the everything ingredients it had fennel and caraway. Personally,​ I think the tower should come with two bagels since it is $25, as I don't see one person eating a tower on their own, but maybe it happens. 

We did enjoy our time here, and the server was attentive​ but didn't smother; I didn't like​ the NYC prices.  ​
Definitely worth the prices. Salmon was best I've had and service was great. Good coffee too!

Food is delicious, beautiful plating, nice ambiance, amazing pancakes!!! A little on the pricey side though. They do need to incorporate espresso as part of their menu as the coffee is awful for my liking (they only serve American coffee which for me is basically coffee-flavored water ‍).  Other than that, great restaurant and will definitely go back whenever visit NYC.

Ok I really really wanted to like this place because I am rooting for places that are bringing back appetizing. As a Russian jew I know my appetizing and this doesn't live up to my hometown place. I paid $70 for ok overpriced teenie tiny portions of not great salads. We waited for our reservation for 20 mins. When we sat down they were out of the kind of bagel I wanted, all the desserts, and the food we got was less than ok. It just doesn't make me want to get out of my sweatpants on a Sunday when I can just go to my hometown place and get triple the stuff that's phenomenal and way less expensive. 

My advice to this group. Redo your recipes immediately! Especially the whitefish which was sacrilegious! Make more freaking babka, don't be famous for it and then run out by noon on a Sunday!  You can do better! Also if my hometown place can cut an order of a half a pound of lox in less then 2 mins you can do it in less then 20 which is how long we waited for our food. We canceled our second order which never came because we were waiting to long for an extra bagel which we had to pay for and more smoked salmon. 


Please do better sadelle's

I've been here twice. Both patronages I had problems with my order and found the staffmembers' response rude in an uppity, annoying way. I am excessively polite, which is why it further angers me that I was accused of being rude.

Yes, you have to make reservations (30 Days in advance for Sunday brunch). Yes, it's crowded. Yes, they don't seat you when your reservation time is. Yes, the teeny tiny tables can barely hold the food you order. But damn, it's worth every bloody penny. Terrific house smoked salmon and bagels should absolutely be on your order list. Same goes for the hash browns and bacon. Delightful!

This isn't my first time at Sadelles but it may be the last. I typically love coming here but the service was not up to par. It took so long to get our drinks (coffee and tea) that our food came first and then my eggs got cold because I had to wait 10 more minutes for a fork. Not to mention that the front door was open the whole time so we had to wear our coats while eating.

Love Major Food Groups restaurants and have been wanting to try this one for a while. Everything was good just not great. Everything bagel was too salty. Breakfast potatoes were perfect. Fresh squeezed orange juice was okay. Great coffee and iced coffee. I do not recommend ordering the matzo ball soup here, definitely not my favorite. All in all this place is worth trying. I liked how they used iPhones to take your order.

Completely overpriced! Now...I know NYC, I am from there but really? It is like a kitchy NYC overpriced bagel place.  Was the lox good? Absolutely! Was it worth $24.00 for a SKINNY bagel, tomatoes, capers, cucumbers and lox? No way! 

When we walked in at 8:30am on a Thursday morning I was asked if we had reservations.  I told them that I did not know I needed reservations for breakfast( there were 4 people in the place). We sat and ordered 1 coffee, 1 hot tea and SHARED the lox tower. After we were done the bill was $56.00 before tip. I do have to say that by the time we left and went on our way we were hungry again. ( dirty dog and knish did the trick!) $6.00 for a cup of coffee? $6.00 for a cup of tea?  Crazy!

We went there because my friend works at the Bellagio in Las Vegas and they are opening up a site there.  To be honest... not worth it.

Sadelle's had been on my list for a while and I was excited to try it out --while the wait for a table was long, the food did not disappoint.  I had a bagel with lox and my friend had a salad, with a side of pickles. Have to give it a 3 star because my waiter was less than attentive and unfortunately, it is really overpriced.

This review is not for the restaurant, but for the take out counter.

I had the opportunity to 'grab' a bagel at Sadelles on a weekend morning...and everyone had the same idea....it was so busy!

It is a little chaotic when you walk in.  As a first timer, there was definitely a learning curve.  There was a long wait for a table, and the wife and I didn't have the time.  So I was told that you can wait at the deli counter to order.  But there is no organized line for the counter....and barely space for a line.  Inside the restaurant, there are people waiting for tables, there are people waiting to order from the deli, and there are people waiting to receive their order from the deli....yeah..definitely feels like New York.

At some point, I was able to stand behind some regulars and get my order in.  They have a pretty good selection of homemade bagels and smoked fish, which was impressive.  I ordered the everything bagel 2.0 and the house smoked salmon.  

It took a while, but when I finally got my bagel, it was delicious.  The key was really the bagel.  All of the 'seeds and salt' on the outside of that bagel really gave me an aromatic mouthful, bite after bite.  Having said that, I think this was the most expensive bagel sandwich I have ever had.

I would like to come back and dine at this restaurant when I have more time.  Being this busy, I'm sure it wont disappoint!

I had an 8:30 am reservation, and it was so empty. I had heard their sticky buns were incredible, and came here to try them. I was told by my waiter that the sticky buns were not yet ready, and would not be for at least another hour. That seemed so odd to me. A signature item not ready when you open? Not cool with me. The French Toast is what I ordered, and it was fine-- custardy in the center, crispy on the outside. The raspberry jam is a must with it, as it cuts through the sweet of the maple syrup, and gives a great bite. But, they are nothing special. At about 10:30, when I was finished, the sticky buns were JUST ready, and we ordered an order to go. Sadly, they were more like a cronut-- flaky and not soft at all. When I think sticky bun, I think cinnamon and soft center, cream cheese frosting. Don't expect that. Expect a circular flaky pastry that was so underwhelming. The order comes with 3, and for the price, you're being ripped off. The ambiance has the makings to be exceptional. Cool brass candles with wax drippings, Le Crueset everything in blue. It's one part medieval chic, one part modern, one part barnyard chic... Identity crisis, and you're seated at a small round table that pray you get the booth side, or your seated on a wooden chair without a cushion-- the making of a bad back, or the exacerbation of one. Expect to talk to your neighbors, as you are so close to them, it's almost uncomfortable, and almost rude not to. So, make this a cafeteria type of seating, or all booths. Bummer. My waiter was perfectly nice, but not attentive enough. Oh, and I am no coffee snob. Literally, anything will do for coffee. This was awful. The table next to me, a couple from England was gobsmacked by this. And, the coffee was about $12/cup. I mean, What the BLEEP.... So so dissappointed, as this is promising and in such a nice neighborhood. If coming on Sundays, nothing opens until 12pm, so sleep in, and come here with a reservation at 10:30/11. The sticky buns will just be out of the oven, and you can decide for yourself.

We went for breakfast at around 9:30am, on a Saturday. We were seated right away & got our coffee quickly. We loved the decor and the neighborhood vibe. We felt lucky to get in because only a few minutes later the place had a wait. My Eggs Benedict was superb - loved the salmon! My hubs had a traditional breakfast that included one of there homemade bagels & crunchy breakfast potatoes. A neighborhood gem!

We ordered the everything bagel and house salmon, sticky buns, and an aperol spritz. The aperol spritz was delightful and the sticky buns (with just the right amount of salt) were to die for. The salmon was good, bagel ok, but I'll stick to Russ and daughters for that craving. Will definitely return for the beautiful space, a classic cocktail, and those sinfully delicious buns.

It's not that I object to paying $24 for a rather basic Salmon Benedict or $10 for a side of pickles. It's not that I am surprised that a SoHo restaurant sits four people at a table that is better suited to two at the very most. But when you have a restaurant this size you should not have two small unisex bathrooms, one of which was out of service for part of the time I was there. This resulted in long uncomfortable lines which included staff. Why have what is in many ways a rather nice restaurant then spoil it with inadequate facilities?  It was like eating in an internment camp.

I was in New York for NYFW and was craving a bagel and lox after my red eye. I dropped off my bags and was searching Yelp for a bagel place in SoHo when I stumbled across Sadelle's. I promptly made a reservation on OpenTable at the suggestion of other Yelpers.

When I arrived I was seated fairly quickly. However, the tables were placed very close together which made it a little difficult to get in and out.

I ordered the smoked salmon tower, as well as the horseradish Bloody Mary. The tower was beautiful but I wish the lox were sliced a little thicker. The Bloody Mary was pretty bland which was surprising after the waitress had told me the horseradish vodka really gives it a great kick. Considering the price point I was definitely underwhelmed with my meal. You really are paying for the kitschiness of the tower.

Overall the food wasn't bad and service was good. It definitely would not be my go to bagel spot next time I am in New York but it served its purpose after a long 6 hour flight.

While food was good and a neat atmosphere. Extremely tight seating and Service was horrible! Obviously figured we were not from Soho and therefore did not feel the need to refill our drinks and check on us. 
If not from NY do not go as you can find a similar Brunch location for under the cost of Sadelle's

My husband and I came in for breakfast at 9.30am on a Sunday. We had a reservation and were seated relatively quickly. The restaurant looks beautiful and the food is just good enough (according to my husband is is mediocre at best), but the service was simply a joke. It seemed like the server didn't want to be there or maybe he was too hung-over to care. It took 5 minutes for him to come over and say hello. Another 10 minutes to get a glass of tap water (!!!). I had to ask for a piece of lemon twice. My husband ordered coffee, but I guess at Sadelle's you shouldn't expect spoons... just use your finger to stir. A simple platter of smoked salmon, tuna fish, and 2 bagels took more than 30 minutes to serve and when it finally arrived we had no plates to eat on. We finished eating but nobody bothered to clear dirty dishes until we asked for the check. So if you like an over hyped bagel place with bad service, Sadelle's is the place to go!

I've never been so impressed and so happy I waited 45 minutes for this bagel place! I was shocked that even at 9am, this two story restaurant was packed with people who look liked they also dressed up early. While the front take out section may appear to be a salmon lox specialty deli of sort, don't be fooled! This magical, exquisite place completely overtook me. Once we were finally seated, I was famished and excited to order. Being my first time, I thought I'd begin with the classic House Salmon order with toasted everything bagel. They even took my order of Russian potatoes (which includes creme fresh and caviar) which were to die for. I had remaining fish and cream cheese at the end of our amazing breakfast experience, so we asked for another everything bagel (I believe two per person are free with your lox order) to split. We were so overwhelmed by the combination of delightful service, all the ingredients provided, classic presentation, and most of all, the taste to perfection. Still now -- the chive cream cheese and caviar were my favorite memories.

I made a reservation a month out, but it was well worth it. They made delicious gluten free bagels in house that were a treat. We also shared the smoked salmon, white fish salad, and egg and potatoes breakfast. Everything was delicious.

The restaurant itself was super cute. It was special for a brunch out, yet still casual. Our waiter was very friendly and the food came out quickly. 

I had heard Sadelle's was overrated but I have to disagree. Fun place to bring out of town visitors or to celebrate something!
This place is so beautiful, staff is super friendly and kind, and bagels are amazing!! The everything was my favorite and Salt and pepper was really good too. Will definitely be back
Over hyped! There is amazing fish all over NYC and the bagels here are not the best. Russ and daughters cafe or deli is a better move.

There are so many reasons to love Sadelle's.. their interpretation of classic Jewish/Lower-East-Side fare is truly scrumptious, the staff are warm and funny, the location is fantastic..
I particularly loved the smoked salmon.. and their fried chicken is spectacular.. as for the Greek Salad, it was better than that of most Greek restaurants in NYC!

Sadelle's is a must for locals and tourists alike. 

KRD NY

Love this place!!! Bagels and eggs anytime!!! Service is excellent and very caring! Rachel was taking care of us and she was very professional and truly caring. I would love to visit this place again.
Trendy over priced menu. Service was okay, food was acceptable, but there are better options. Sorry.

Went here with a friend a couple of weeks ago for lunch. Yes, the food was good, not incredible. The service good. But, I really don't see what the draw is. They only have brunch items and everything is way over priced. I won't be back.

I'm not the brunch person I could be in Manhattan. I have a deeply held belief the best breakfast is a bagel or pastry in Manhattan (other boroughs are different concerning brunch), most brunch places are adequate and outrageously overpriced. 

Sadelle's is a breakfast/brunch I happily pay for. All of the food is so fresh and delicious, the service is excellent and the atmosphere is so chic. It's a beautiful restaurant in a darling part of Soho. 

My husband ordered the lox, which comes with the beautiful 3 tier tower of salmon, bagels, smear and vegetables (tomatoes, cucumbers & capers), and I ordered the eggs any style (scrambled soft) which comes with potatoes and a bagel (the everything, which was recommended). It's hard to find a restaurant that prepares scrambled eggs well, and admittedly I'm a bit fussy about my eggs, and the scrambled eggs at Sadelle's are the best I've had at a restaurant since the Wolesley in London. And the potatoes! I ordered them thinking I wouldn't really touch the potatoes, and I couldn't help myself. They are so delicious!

I've had better bagels, and my husband has had better lox, but if you just want to sit down and have a nice breakfast in Soho with Jewish deli food, this is your place. If you just want to grab a bagel, go to Ess-A-Bagel or Barney Greengrass. If you want Lox for take away: Russ & Daughters, Zabars and Barney Greengrass. 

When we're in the mood for a sit down breakfast, chances are you will find us here. We had a great experience and will definitely be back.
Love this place for brunch! Definitely try the bagels and the different types of lox

Lovely room, great music,happy service and every bite was perfect.   My guy and I  started with a shared sticky bun (comped by the waiter when I expressed indecisiveness between said buns and the french toast), bubbly for me and a cider for him.  We had the sturgeon, tuna salad (not to be missed) wafer thin Scottish smoked salmon AND the religious experience that was their French toast. Excessive? Maybe. But we were in it for the experience.  Complete with bagels and their lovely accouterments (ripest most delicious tomatoes ever) -- this will be the meal I think about again and again.  On the expensive side for what it is, but the fellas from Major Food Group are great at interpreting the classics (Parm, Dirty French, Carbone, etc.) and taking them up that extra delicious notch. I shall return.

We tried breakfast here (I guess you can call it brunch) because we wanted to get some bagels and lox and some whitefish salad.  This place did not disappoint.  The bagels may not be as a big as some other places, but they are fresh and delicious.  We were a party of four and we each had a bagel with Smoked Scottish (Lox), Whitefish Salad, Tuna Salad and Egg Salad.  It came on a three tiered tower with sliced tomatoes, cucumbers and cream cheese.  It was all fantastic.  The service was great as well.  I can't wait to return and try out the pancakes and eggs benedict.

My son and I had the best lunch at Sadelle's. Everything was exceptional from the food, to the waitstaff to the atmosphere. The lox melted in our mouth and the blintzes were so light and delicious. It was truly a treat we will remember.

Great service and solid bagels. I ordered the everything bagel with lox and cream cheese. The side of potatoes were perfectly seasoned. If you want a sit down breakfast/brunch, Sadelle's is a nice place to relax before you do your shopping in SoHo.

A real treat. It's nearly impossible to get in but they do take walk ins- try not to do that at "prime" brunch time on a Saturday or Sunday. I love the decor; simple and clean with pretty blue Le Creuset cups and dishes. Try the whitefish salad and the salmon (nova) for sure! One can even see them making perfect bagels in the see through glass cage center stage. Their appetizing tower is superb! (They cater to the gluten free crowd as well).  Service is excellent.

Perfect for lunch. There are so many toppings to offer. The ambiance is great. The gluten free options were amaing. The hostess was kind and seated us right away. The waiters are outstanding. We really enjoyed it.

My son heard about this restaurant from a collaboration with his favorite store, Kith. We sat at the top level over looking the fresh bagels coming out of the oven. Absolutely delicious bagels and cream cheese. We ordered 2 different kinds of salmon which comes out in a tray which was a very nice presentation. My other son loves potato's and the smashed potatoes with his eggs was right up his alley. On a non-food note I really appreciated the nice linen napkins, the Le Creuset dishware and the silver serving tray.

I have been wanting to try Sadelle's for a long time now, and was thrilled to finally get a reservation on a Sunday afternoon. The restaurant is light and airy with an open mezzanine above a small glass chamber where you can watch the bagels being rolled. The bagels are delicious - a bit smaller than an average bagel, but very flavorful. The smoked Scottish salmon is ethereally thin and beautifully silky and tasty. The grilled cheese is a gooey mess of salty bagel and melted cheese, the Cobb salad a veritable acre of lettuce and goodies, and the eggs Benedict a fluffy cloud of Hollandaise, salmon and poached egg atop a circle of Challah. Service is friendly, and the wait was worth it.

Sadelle's is a charming + popular breakfast spot in SoHo, specializing in freshly made bagels and accoutrements. It can get busy, so it's best to make a reservation. There is some seating available on the first floor, as well as on the second floor, but tables are small and I wouldn't recommend going with a party of more than 4. Everything is adorable with the hues of blues, and it's so fun being able to see the bagels being freshly made in front of your eyes. 

Our waitress recommended one fish tower per person, but instead we decided to get one to share (you can add a bagel on for $2), and then another dish to share. Both dishes were simple and delicious, with quality ingredients doing the talking without any bells and whistles. 

HOUSE SALMON // The house salmon comes on a three-tiered tower that adds to the charm of this breakfast spot. The house salmon is cured, and sliced into paper thin slices. It's not overly fishy and pulls apart easily. The addition of fresh dill adds a pop of earthy freshness. This is probably the best salmon I've had on a bagel ever! The tower also comes with slices of bright red juicy tomatoes, thin slivers of cucumber, and some capers, as well as a bagel of your choice + 2 cream cheeses (plain + seasoned). You can add on a second bagel for $2. I'm no bagel expert, but this is one of the best dang bagels I've ver had. I had the plain bagel, and it came perfectly toasted, where it was chewy inside, with a crispness on the outside. It wasn't too cakey or too bready or too thick or thin or crunchy. It was just perfect. 

LEO // The LEO is served differently than your traditional lox, eggs, and onions dish. The base is a dense circular omelette with caramelized onions, which is then topped with those super thin slices of the house salmon, drizzles of creme fraiche, and fresh dill + chives. 

The only complaint I can see with the place is the price. For breakfast, I definitely would not be able to shell this out on a regular basis, but for a treat for delicious bagels, it was worth it. Also, the drip coffee was $6! That was way too overpriced if you ask me. This place is perfect for a Saturday or Sunday brunch.
The tuna melt was one of the best I've ever had! And the rosé flight, just perfect :)

Guys! These bagels are really good. I am currently craving a bagel right now and the bagel iteration I am imagining is the poppy seed bagel from Sadelle's.

The rest of the menu is very tasty too.  However, they are somewhat pricey. 

The decor is pretty cool too. High ceilings, exposed brick. Feels really homey. 

If you're looking for a sit-down breakfast, Sadelle's is a great spot.

For real though, I am craving their bagels.

Sadelle's breakfast was awesome, however the prices are a bit steep. I feel that $6 for a regular coffee is a bit excessive. We had three coffees for $18.00 but then again it is NYC. We ordered two house salmons for three of us and it was plenty. We LOVED the salmon and the bagels, and our waiter Maxwell was extremely attentive and friendly.
Our waiter, Maxwell,was fantastic! He is the reason we will make this our spot when we come back to visit New York!

If you're looking to spend $40 for a small bagel and a burnt coffee, this is the place for you. Coffee is $6 ($8 for iced), price not listed on the menu. The coffee was almost undrinkable- mentioned to a very rude wait staff that it was burnt and they offered more from the same bad pot after rolling their eyes and having me wait 10 mins. The food is good enough but the bagels are very small and we left hungry. The set up is cute, but not worth it at all- overpriced and overrated.
I'm not sure why this place doesn't have at least 4 Stars. It's off the charts. They spare no ingredient. Everything was great. Go here. Eat bagels and eat salmon. The egg dish was also exceptional.

Wow. Simply breathtaking. I've spent 2 weeks roaming the cafe/restaurant scene in New York, and this has been my favourite restaurant by far. The salmon bagels were mouth-watering and the French toast is the best I've eaten in my life (not an exaggeration). Superb hospitality. Beautiful decoration. I couldn't recommend this place enough! 10 stars if I could!

One. Of. The. Best. Restaurants I've ever been to. From the aesthetics,  to the emaculate customer service to the extremely delicious food. These people know what they are doing and really give you the "Sadelles" experience. I was in on the day of the pride parade doing some food photography of their pancakes, which were so yummy and filling. They were patient with me and were very accommodating for the photo shoot.  If you are in manhatten and are looking for a great place to dine for breakfast/brunch you HAVE to go here or you haven't lived.

Great gluten free bagels, make sure to try the smoked salmon tower - so delicious. Friendly service and good mimosas too. 
Only problem is you can't just have one lol

Food 3/5
Service 5/5
Ambiance 5/5
I wouldn't recommend and don't plan on returning. The food is good but nothing stands out and it's definitely not worth the price. 
I went with two friends and made reservations for Sunday 12:30pm. We got seated right away- they won't seat you until your whole party arrives. I definitely recommend a reservation for weekend breakfast/brunch times because it was packed. 
We got eggs any style, classic egg sandwich, tomato soup, sticky buns, orange juice, grapefruit juice, and coffee. Bill was $100. 
Each juice was $7 and is less than 8 oz. The only plate that came with a bagel (+cream cheese) was the 'eggs any style'. I asked for mushroom barley soup but they were all out by 12:30pm so I got tomato. 
The service was amazing. Our waiter was very attentive, super kind, and informative. 
The decor is 5/5. Super cute and charming inside. Space is a little tight but not too bad. 
I just won't be returning because the food wasn't anything better than 'good.'
Horrible host.  Rude and disrespectful. Made us feel like we were a burden rather than making us feel welcomed.

The salmon bagel is everything. 

25$ for a bagel is crazy, but totally worth the try!!

*update* they lost a star from me because they don't accept cash!!! Only card! Which is like so weird to me haha.

Pros: Tasty breakfast food all day. More restaurants need this concept.

Cons: $22 for French Toast. That is an insane price even for Manhattan.

While I liked the food, i cant get past $22 French Toast.

Smoked salmon here is absolutely amazing, probably the best I've ever had. Extremely fresh fish/veggies/herbs/bagels. Very open, airy, (large) cafe-like setting. Some of the seating is a little tight, but definitely worth it for such high quality food.
I bring all of my out of towners and visitors here. I'm is absolutely amazing. Best bagels, salmon and the French toast is to die for!

Best decision I made during my trip to NY was listening to my friend and going to Sadelle's....twice.

So THANKFULLY, my friend had made a reservation for brunch here a month before my visit, so even though we had to wait kind of a bit to sit, we were able to get a table that morning. And honestly, the wait (even though long...about 45-1 hour), it goes by quickly because you get to watch this guy finely slice pieces of lox. [PRO TIP: if he catches you drooling over the lox he is slicing, he will offer you a couple of pieces to eat while you wait.]

So we were three people, and ordered kind of a lot, but it's all so good nothing gets left behind.  We ordered bagels, a lot of lox, eggs, tuna, avocado, iced coffee and omg the french toast for dessert. Everything I just listed is a MUST ORDER. The lox will melt in your mouth. The tuna is literally to die for.

Sadelle's was so good, that on my last day in NY, I went back and got a bagel with tuna for the road and just sat outside on a stoop next door downing my bagel.  

Kind of pricey, but honestly so worth it. And if you're in NYC, you already know everything is going to be expensive so to be expected.

The worst bagel I've ever ordered on trycaviar. And it cost $20 a lox bagel!!! The first time we ordered they sent us two salmonless bagels and still charged us $20 per.  Took an hour to fix it and even then they tasted like crap.  Never again...

HIGH quality salmon lox here. Delicious and addicting. Id go for the everything bagel + smoked scottish....pigs in the blanket....and pancakes. Awesome place for lunch and a must go to if you are in the area looking for a great meal

The theme of this restaurant is, "Our food ranges from medium to excellent and our service will be medium if we are hitting on all cylinders.  We are just good enough to keep the place packed".  

Inside: The tables are not uncomfortable.  The booths looked like the best bet but the hostess gave off a don't you dare tell me your preference vibe.  There are 2 single use unisex wash rooms.  Bring hand sanitizer if you want to wash your hands before you eat or be prepared to wait in a dark hallway for 10 minutes with 5 other people until you all have the opportunity to jeer at the poor soul that will embarrassingly run past you ashamed of what everyone knows was just happening on the other side of that door.  The bagel making station in the center of the restaurant is pretty cool.

Food:  It's good.  The hand sliced fish is high quality.  The portions are a little stingy but that is to be expected at this type of place.  Soup was great.  Bagels are excellent.  Sticky buns are delectable.

Service:  We had a very nice waiter.  She introduced herself and then returned 25 minutes later.  She was nice but probably covered more tables than were conducive to providing good service.  As alluded to earlier the hostess was acting like the Queen of Hearts from Alice in wonderland.  I wanted to keep my head so I waited outside until called upon.

Summary:  Would I go back?  Yes.  Would I bring hand sanitizer?  Yes.   Would I order everything I want the second I sit down?  Yes.   Will I expect bad service?  Yes.  Would I recommend?  Depends on who I'm talking to.

they don't accept cash wtf??!!!  so not cool!!!

and you can't get butter on the side!!

too many rules!!!

would never go back here!!

This quiet, hot Labor Day morning, we find ourselves sitting in Washington Square Park guessing who's a tourist and who's a townie, while googling best bagels in NYC.  Sadelle's comes up, as it does on several NYC food lists.  Best Brunch, Best Bagel, Best Buns.  You likely won't find it on a Best Bargain NYC list, as the sticker shock is not for the faint of heart.  But, bellies before bank, we took a stroll down to West Broadway below Houston.

Kos ordered the Healthy Egg Sandwich comprised of eggs whites, a mound of dressed arugula, and green chilies.  Knowing the week to come was promised to diet and exercise, Kos asked our kind and attentive waiter if the kitchen could add Muenster and serve it on an everything bagel.  He so obliged.  It may be $18 but this is no deli egg and cheese.... When served it was hot, the bagel buttery and toasted, the arugula peppery with a touch of oil and vinegar, the chili's add a baby bit of heat, and the eggs and cheese generously continued from the bread onto the plate.  Not an easy pick-up-and-eat but the sandwich deserves an unashamed appetite.  Just go for it.  

Tello ordered Eggs Any Way. Two fried eggs, potatoes, and an Everything Bagel side.  Eggs perfectly done, beautiful color.  Potatoes were crunchy, possibly cooked then fried, great seasoning, and colored with a nice amount of bright peppers and parsley.  The bagel delivered on the craving that began some steps ago in the park.  Served toasted with chives cream cheese on the side, it is small, but that's a good thing.  The woman to our right ate two and she was teeny tiny.  She had ordered the Salmon Tower, which allows you to build your own bagel from a healthy serving of salmon, tomato, cucumber, onions & cappers.  I was 

This place has a following, so make a reservation.  

Looking back on the menu they have something called an Everything 2.0.  If you get one, or have had it, PLEASE let us know what it is!  Sensing another craving to come...
spacious - rustic vibe - great service. this place gets pretty busy, has a great vibe/energy! the french toast was very good a little undercooked and soft but i loved it. great food presentation!

The table setting, atmosphere and overall design of the restaurant is the perfect combination of trendy and traditional. The sticky buns, grilled cheese and bagels are amongst my menu favorites. However, the line is always always EXTREMELY long - not worth the 1-2 hour wait to be honest. I would only go back if the wait time is exponentially decreased.

Sadelle's is one of those places that you see a million times on Instagram before you actually go (or it least it was for me.) After seeing all those photos of beautifully arranged smoked salmon tower things, I was excited to see if Sadelle's lived up to the hype. And honestly, I would say that it did. First of all, the restaurant itself is beautiful. There was a super cool piece of artwork hanging above our table and the whole atmosphere was serene. 
While I didn't get the instaworthy salmon platter thing, I had the salmon Benedict and it was absolutely delicious and beautifully plated. The hollandaise was creamy and flavorful and the sprig of dill on top was a nice touch. I also liked that their portion sizes weren't huge--it was the perfect amount of food. My iced coffee was also very good. 
The bagel wasn't exactly what I expected. It had a lighter texture and wasn't as dense and chewy as a typical New York City bagel. The flavor was top notch, though, and the everything seasonings on top were plentiful and tasty.  Overall I would definitely recommend Sadelle's. I'll definitely be back for brunch at some point. I probably wouldn't come here for just a bagel because of the prices, but if you're in the market for a pricey but delicious bagel then I'd say go for it.
My first time in New York, and an googled Best French Toast in Newyork and boy was it good. The breakfast potatoes are incredibly delicious as well. Will definitely be back!

We heard so much about this place and therefore was willing to wait about 45 minutes to have a table. 
But then 45 minutes turned to 90 minutes and as we were about to leave they had a table. 
The food was okay but nothing special that will justify the wait or the prices.

Loved the concept and food, but pretty over-priced for what it is! Ordered the smoked Scottish and whitefish salad, which was served on tiered plates and came with a selection of bagels (everything bagel is on point!). Also ordered the salami and eggs which was different (in a good way) - never had mustard on an omelette before! Between the food and coffee, our bill was about $100 for breakfast. Overall, tasty but way too expensive for bagels and coffee. We also had to wait ~30 min to get seated despite making a reservation.

I was shocked at how not worth coming here this place is. Loud, terrible service, small portions, very expensive, food is okay but not wow (like Russ & Daughters). 

We were recommended to come here from a couple who lives in NYC and also by The Infatuation (pretty reliable restaurant review app). 

The food itself is good, BUT not at all as good as Russ and Daughters. The ingredients were fresh and overall smaller size portions. 

Almost every item was about $5 overpriced for the size and what you get (hint, it adds up).

The only thing I liked and would maybe pop in for in the future is the Matzah Ball Soup, it hit the spot and was the only healthy portion. 

That's if the service improves or am seated so I don't have to see how unprofessional they behave. We were seated near the entrance where we were continually exposed to the management members hovering over their laptop and phone, as they had taken over the front two tables right next to us and other guests. 

They had bags and backpacks shoved near the nicely designed restaurant fixtures. They would speak loudly, lounge around, make gestures to servers who would come and circle around them from time to time and laugh loudly.
