Our server completely disappeared after we ordered. Then we noticed she came back and was sitting next to us talking to the management group. She never looked at us again or come back... totally messed up service lacking professionalism.

This is my experience with Sadelle's after scoping out 30+ bagel shops in the city:

"The Gourmet Bagel"

Order: Dry cinnamon raisin bagel
Bagel cost: $2.18
Wait time: No wait at 10:50am Thursday

This was a classic 2 oz Jewish bagel. It was neither crunchy nor chewy, just the kind that needs to be toasted. Despite its petite size, there was a strong cinnamon flavor and many raisins sprinkled into the bagel.

The place is not your typical bagel haunt. It's kind of ritzy like a gastropub, with prices to match. They don't take cash.

Waited an hour. After
Back surgery walked upstairs
 Worst Table location at top of stairs. Nothing fit. Would not move us. Blueberry pancake dripping out butter. Disgusting.  So overpriced and snobby. Server never refilled coffee. Never again.

Sadelle's is a family tradition for my family. Every time we are in NYC we try to head to Sadelle's for brunch and this time we brought some friends. Honestly considered giving them four stars because they are a pain in the ass about letting you sit down if your entire party is not there and it's nearly impossible to get a reservation but I let that slide because the food is so good.

Service is hit or miss and if you can't stand a loud restaurant, don't bother coming here. But if you can handle a little noise, a 30 min wait at minimum and not the best service it is totally worth it for the excellent food.

Most recently ordered the bagels, house salmon, smoked scottish, whitefish, greek salad, pancakes, and blintzes. But we have been here plenty of times and I'm pretty sure we have ordered everything on the menu. The chocolate babka is amazing, the blintzes are phenomenal, the greek salad is picture-esque and oh so tasty.

I could go on and on about how much I love their food but I'll post some pictures so you can see for yourself. If you're in Soho looking for some amazing Jewish food, do not miss Sadelle's.

I got an everything 2.0 bagel ($2) with house salmon ($13), chive cream cheese ($1), tomatoes and onions, plus an iced coffee to go. The total? $25. I'm honestly embarrassed I spent that much on a lox bagel and an iced coffee. Coffee prices aren't listed, but while I was waiting for my order I heard the guy at the counter charge someone $7 for a to-go cup of hot coffee. Uhhh, what? The sandwich was fine but I don't think any salmon bagel is worth that much. I found this place to be overhyped and overpriced. Also, despite some reviews, there are no "cafe" seats (at least on weekends?) for take-out customers to sit.

The place is awesome. Great music. Great food. My only thing to say is that I wasn't allowed to pay with cash and I wasn't even notified at when I arrived nor there is any sign to explicitly state it.

Simply not worth going to this place.  The food is ok but nothing really overall to write home about.  I do have to say the pigs in a blanket were super delicious however that doesn't make up for the poor service.  Our waiter appeared to be more interested in flipping our table rather than giving us a good breakfast experience.  We barely saw him throughout our experience and spent time tracking down other staff members for a fork and napkin and a second drink etc.  It was just a hassle.  Ad when we did see him it was always to try and clear a plate that was clearly not ready to be taken away just yet. Additionally, I don't mind spending $ on great food but the food overall just wasn't that great.  Better off going to classic NY establishments like Clinton Street Baking Co. or Russ & Daughters.  At least they value their patrons.
Excellent!  Whitefish a bit too salty but lox unbelievably good.  Love the GF bagels.

Amazing lunch/brunch spot on a quite street in Soho. The decor is industrial classic and I love the teal Sur la Table pepper mills on each table. Almost all the dishes are served seafood tower style, which can't help but make you feel like you ordered the best thing on the menu. I had the tuna tartar, while my friend had the house salmon and bagel. Both were delicious! And don't forget the rose, it compliments the dishes in looks and taste.

I remember when Sadelle's first opened. My coworker and I lined up on their first day to get a bagel. We back again the week after. It was expensive for a lox bagel, but it was a damned good bagel.

I took a break from Sadelle's for a bit and returned on a Friday morning to treat myself to a house lox bagel with chive cream cheese. To be honest, it wasn't as good as I remembered. The bagels are teeny tiny! They're so small! There's definitely a lot less lox than there used to be.

I'm not sure if Sadelle's will be my go-to in the area for lox bagels. I'm 100% sure I can find better if I looked.

When is it appropriate to call a place "bullshit" in NY? Can't just be when it's overpriced -- that's naïve. NY is overpriced. So it goes. But there is a particular brand of NY retail bullshit (and being overpriced is part of it) that involves taking a thing, NewYorkifying it without actually making it better, and then selling it with 3x the fanfare for 3x the $$, as if New York invented it. Oh, is fried chicken good? Are there 10,000 unsung little joints feeding people good-to-great fried chicken all across the American South? Well now we've opened a boutique "shack" in SoHo, with sawdust on the floor and quilts for tablecloths. $16 gets you a leg and a thigh on a square of butcher paper. It's called Hen, or maybe Roost. The chicken's decent, but is it really the Best in the Country? New York Magazine says it is, so....   Sadelle's is a funny variant on the theme, because the bullshit they're selling really does come from New York. Somehow, though, they've managed to take real NY Jewish food, build a 1920s Lower East Side drag show around it, and magically create something that's historically rooted and embarrassingly fake at the same time. Three stars because I can't deny my bagel and the salmon on top tasted great, and my waitress was a pro. Two stars off because I felt like a sucker, surrounded by dupes, eating my $24 bagel and sipping my $6 coffee, serviced by about 35 staff dressed in kitschy white pharmacist's coats like the chorus of a Broadway musical about bagels. The coffee, by the way, was terrible.

A short trip to NY calls for New York bagels. I came here for a late brunch with a friend and we knew we were somewhere special because we were surrounded by all of these towers of lox, tomatoes and other toppings.

Definitely a more luxurious bagel experience, we ordered everything bagels with egg salad, lox, tomatoes and cucumbers. The cream cheese was exceptional but I found the bagel rather salty with the lox together. The tomatoes were a tad soggy, but tasty nonetheless. Combined everything was delicious and made for a great meal. It was about $40US a person for coffee and bagels, so be prepared to spend. 

The service was efficient and it was very packed for brunch mid-week, which is a great sign. I would definitely return - but would just stick to plain bagels!

New favorite brunch spot in NYC. Love everything about this place. Great location. Fun atmosphere. The gluten-free bagels were delicious. We came for a bachelorette weekend brunch and had the best time. I will definitely be back again.

Very very overpriced. We ordered an iced coffee which was charged $8 and a hot one cost $6. Not to mentioned the 90 mins wait. The food was fine but not amazing. Overall, it's an overpriced place and I won't recommend to my friends.
Really good bagels and salads--Highly recommend. Make a reservation beforehand though because the wait can get long.

One of my favorite Bagel spots in NYC. Excellent service and delicious bagels as well as other breakfast offerings. I had the Eggs Benedict and all was great along with the bagel and tea service. Recommend making a reservation for either weekday or weekend service.

My family and I had sunday brunch at Sadelles and absolutely loved it. We met Adam who was just fantastic, and Eli was our server who was also so kind and amazing. We got all different breakfast foods.. but the bagels and french toast really stood out. I can't explain how good the french toast was. Highly recommend !

Stopped in for a bagel, but given the cold weather I opted for some soup. I'm surprised by how good their tomato soup was. And continually craving it from Los Angeles! Recommend stopping her for a proper sit down brunch or a bagel to go. They offer platters where you pick your own lox. The coffee is served in the cutest Le crueset mugs. Ambiance is fantastic!

My lovely bride enjoyed an early breakfast at Sadelle's on Saturday morning. The food was excellent, especially the sticky buns, the house salmon with everything bagels, and the grapefruit cocktail. Service was prompt and professional. My only complaint is the way the two-tops are squeezed together tightly in a row along the wall. Otherwise, a stellar meal.

I waited almost 2 weeks before posting this review but upon reflection and deep thought about my experience here I really felt the need to make this post. I had a dear friend visiting me from Florida. We were shopping in Soho and decided we would stop somewhere and grab some lunch and a nice glass of wine. Random guy on the street saw was looking at the menu of this restaurant and said that he highly suggested it. When a real New Yorker gives you a thumbs up it's highly suggest you take them up on their recommendation.

We decided to go in and eat. This restaurant is absolutely chic and lovely inside. Apparently they are known for their smoked salmon and they also have some great baked goods such as their sticky buns. My friend and I ordered grilled cheese and tomato basil soup. We each got a glass of wine. Our waiter was there to take the order. He brought out our wine and some water for the table. Then he disappeared. We looked around for about 15 minutes trying to flag someone down to find our server. After almost 30 minutes went by we stopped a woman who appeared to be a server as well. She said  'I am your server now so-and-so left for the day'. We were like 'WTF', why didn't either of these servers introduce themselves OR say they had our table??  They brought our soup out and we kept asking for sandwiches. This waitress was extremely snobby and seemed annoyed anytime we asked for anything. She finally brought our food out. She then walked away. We flagged her down and said we would like to get one more glass of wine and we are going to split it. So she came out and split a glass of wine for us. Then without anything else she simply brought the check out and set it on the table. Never said can I bring you coffee? Would you like to try our sticky buns? Can I bring you anything else? Not even a thank you.

Upon review of the bill she had charged us for four glasses of wine and we could not find her to have her correct it. At this point I'll be honest we were just simply frustrated by the whole experience. I won't name this person but her first name began with an 'I', restaurant management will know who I am referencing. She then became very defensive with my out-of-town guest at the table. My guest spoke to the manager and the manager was lovely. She apologized profusely and offered to adjust the bill but we had already paid and needed to go. So she brought out a box of sticky buns as a kind gesture to right the wrong of our server.The chef also came out to the table to tell us about the sticky buns.  Now that is excellent customer service. I will say the food in this place was fabulous. The management was very attentive and very concerned that we not have a bad experience so I can thank them for that.

As stated in many of my previous reviews though all it takes is that one person in the service industry to ruin your experience and or your day. I rarely see this friend of mine from Florida and we were really looking forward to a fun little time in the city that day. By the time we left we just felt beaten down, ignored and kind of had an attitude like why us?!  I would love to have given a better rating to this restaurant overall because of the beautiful decor, the management support at the end of our experience in the food but those things all seem to fly out the window when you have a bad experience overall. Let me just end this by saying I do recommend that you go try the food here because it is good and it's a snappy little place. But heed my warning of 'Buyer Beware' because the servers seemed to be way off their game, we had two people not just one who created a negative experience for us. We spent probably close to $150 for lunch for two people including the tip so no small change here.

You shouldn't have to go to management to get good customer service.  I work in an industry where if we fail at customer service our clients 'Vote With their Feet', if you know what I mean.

If you want amazing brunch experience look no further. 

We were heading into the city with some family from out of town and this was one of their must have destinations while we were in town. We made reservations which I highly recommend because on a Friday morning this place was packed! The restaurant has a nice chic vibe. While we waited to be seated we were able to watch them prepping the locks. If you've never seen it before it will be a really intriguing experience and the staff is friendly and will chat with you and answer questions. 

We ended up with the best table in the entire place on their upper level seating area and had an amazing view of them making bagels and sticky buns. Our server was friendly, knowledgeable and helpful. They're known for the smoked salmon and so most of us in the group got the Smoked Scottish. It was amazing, they serve you a plate of fish, sliced tomatoes and cucumbers, cream cheese and your choice of bagel. Plus they have other breakfast options which include French Toast which was out of this world and a large portion. They also have different styles of eggs and side options you can add. Everything was fantastic and very fresh. Their Bloody Mary was so good I loved it and I don't even like tomatoes. 

Be prepared to pay 40-50 per person but you won't be disappointed.

My husband and I had an awesome first experience at Sadelle's! We had made reservations, luckily and still waited a few minutes for a table to be ready. For those that did not have a reservation, I heard the host tell them it could be hours before they were seated . While waiting to be seated, my husband and I thoroughly enjoyed watching fresh salmon being thinly sliced. Now, that's fresh! 
We were then seated and my husband and I ordered mimosas. The mimosas are large and they're pretty strong! Also note that, like anywhere else in Manhattan, the seating was very tight. 
My husband ordered the tower of house salmon which came with a bagel, chive cream cheese, capers, onions, tomatoes, cucumbers, etc. Beautiful display and absolutely delicious!!! I ordered the salmon eggs Benedict. Also very delicious!! We split an order of the pickles. The pickles were very good and included some pickles green beans, which I thought was pretty neat. 
Our waitress was super friendly, she picked up on our accents immediately and told us she was from Alabama. She was a total sweetheart. My husband and I were there to celebrate my birthday, so she brought me a bagel with a birthday candle on the plate! Such a great touch. Highly recommend this restaurant! I can certainly see why they stay so busy and why it's so popular! 
My husband and I look forward to returning to Sadelle's the next time we are in Manhattan!

We booked last minute a reservation for my niece's birthday.  They couldn't have been nicer accommodating us.  Immediately they sent over a slice of babka with a candle.  We had the bagel tower, grilled cheese and tuna tartare.  Everything was presented beautifully and tasted just as great.  Our waitress was attentive but not obtrusive.  This place as a total experience was amazing.  I highly recommend it
The everything bagel is phenomenal.  I would definitely recommend.  Didn't try the bagel with fish but it looked great.

Food was amazing & had an awesome experience with out of town friends. 

I work in the catering/hospitality industry & I was very upset with the customer service after my visit to the restaurant. 

Two days later I received my bank statement I saw that I was double charged. I tried to call the restaurant but they have no line so I emailed the reservations box and received no response. 

I showed up to the restaurant and spoke with the AGM in regards to being double charged who said she will be in touch with an update. I sent a follow up email and no response, sent another follow up email a week later and received a response asking for detail questions again. I gave all information that day. I never received any response & again followed up as still nothing reimbursed. Here we are an entire month later and they have not solved the problem & there is now a claim with my bank on this restaurant.

While visiting the fantastic city of New York we came to Sadelle's because we had heard so much about it.
My husband and I just couldn't help ourselves and ended up ordering more than our stomachs can hold. We wanted to try everything and anything that looked yummy.
 We ordered two orders of Lox platter with everything bagels, the french toast, egg bagel sandwich and fried chicken. I ate one order of the Lox , most of the French toast and half of the egg bagel sandwich....How did I manage to eat all that you ask? Let me tell you how:
- The bagel itself is absolutely scrumptious! Not dense or chewy. 
- Once I put cream cheese, slices of Lox, cucumbers, and capers on the bagel my world changed. I honestly wished to be alone, at home to simply enjoy the bagel creation without people judging me on the mmm sounds I was making. 
- The French toast is another story! It does not taste like any French toast I've ever had! I ate it without adding syrup because it was magnificent on its own. 
I could eat that French toast everyday, it was just on a whole other level.
- The egg sandwich was really cheesy and delicious! What made it was, again, the bagel itself. 
Conclusion, you give me the best bagel and the best French toast I've had in my life and I will eat like there's no tomorrow. 
If you're in New York, go to Sadelle's!!! I must warn you, it is not cheap but it is worth every penny.

WHOA! This place is so good! I've been there for a quick bagel before, but finally went and had a sit-down breakfast. We had the smoked Scottish (comes with bagels, cream cheese, cucumbers, tomatoes, and capers) and it was soooo good. You definitely need to get one of the fish towers when you're here. The people working there were very nice, and fast. The decor was beautiful and made you feel like you were having a really special meal. Definitely will be returning.
YUM! Great atmosphere, beautiful dining room, fun people watching - and thinly sliced lox! Great brunch, on the pricey side, but quality can't be beat!

By far the longest I have ever had to wait for a bagel. We paid $40 for 2 bagels with cream cheese and smoked salmon, fine it's New York so that's not too unusual. But then it took the guy 30 mins to make the bagels. There was only 1 guy who ordered before us. Granted he had a big order, but this guy making the bagels was so slow it was excruciating to watch. He made bagels 1 at a time, he had to recheck the order screen every 5 seconds. Then they made me the wrong bagel, so we had to wait longer to get the right one. 2 stars is only because the bagels were good. I wouldn't say they were any better then any other bagel place I've been to here. We should have taken the train to russ and daughter, we would have been served and have eaten our bagels in the same amount of time.

We went here on a Sunday morning for a quick breakfast and I couldn't be happier. Probably the best lox bagel I've ever had in my life. The place is so cute inside and you can just see how fresh everything is!!! Will absolutely come back here again

My roommate and I went back to Sadelle's to celebrate her birthday (and after I had been reached out to by management regarding my review) and had a much more pleasant experience. We were seated upstairs and had Austin as our waiter, who was so friendly and personable. I still believe the food is overpriced and serving such large trays on such small bistro tables does not make a lot of sense, but Austin created a great restaurant experience for us, and even brought over a tray of complimentary cinnamon buns to celebrate her birthday. Overall, I probably wouldn't go back but I was grateful for the kind service following my previously negative experience.
Horrible customer service. At the table and at the bagel counter. A gf bagel took 10 min for them to prepare and was cold and hard by the time they gave it to me. The guy clearly was being a jerk.

Staff are not the most helpful. When we arrived and asked for a three top, they neglected to tell us we had to wait to be seated until our full party was there, which caused confusion later. 

Beautiful space, bagels were great! The rest of the menu was expensive. I ordered a side of sausage and it was way too much sausage for one person to consume.

Seemed like a place tourists go. There were about 15 suitcases at the front of the restaurant. 

Our actual server was incredibly nice and attentive. This is a great spot to go if you want fancy high-tea food and pastries on a three-tiered platter. But not if you just want a meal. 

Not the best spot for intimate conversations. 

Bonus: gluten free bagels!
Great brunch place. The salmon was excellent so was the bagels  I absolutely loved this place. Highly recommend it.

Came for Christmas day brunch. Thank goodness we had a reservation, it was packed! Between three people we shared the Sadelle's fish tower which was actually better than I expected it to be. Plenty of food (can comfortably feed four people) with plates of different smoked salmons, sable, white fish salad, salmon salad, and more! I loved the variety, everything tasted good, and even the bagels were great (on the smaller side so you can load up on even more ;)). Only complaint is service was slow and they ran out of iced coffee.

Great ambiance for a fun brunch, would love to come back again.
Great breakfast spot that makes their bagels fresh every day. If you are going with a big group of people, I highly recommend sharing one of the salmon towers!

Sadelle's was good but for what you got it was over priced. You could find any other breakfast place that serves the same thing for half the price and it would be just as good. The atmosphere itself was cool! We got a tower with tuna and everything bagels. We also got sticky buns which were hard.

I usually don't post. I wish I could give this negative stars. If you are colored or have any pigmentation in your skin please don't go here. They won't seat you. Correction Rachel won't seat you. She told 45 mins which is okay. And hour and 10 mins later no seat. We were the only Indian (colored people) everyone else got seated. If you are financial able to afford this place don't waste your time. They still believe in segregation...

This restaurant is 80% attitude (bad), 10% good food and 10% highway robbery for way overcharging for good food. There are 10 places with better brunches within 2 blocks. Everything was significantly over priced. But there is one highlight: if you want entertainment, this is the place. You can see guys in 'finance' (most likely nocturnal debt collection) in their track suits with their much younger dates who were 'models' at the beginning of last evening and transformed into a more traditional profession by the end of the night (see "Melania")

If you're visiting New York or you're just a big planner, Sadelle's is definitely the place for you. Sadelle's has arguably one of the best bagels in NYC. The only issue is if you don't have a reservation, you have a long wait in store. If you go you are more than likely to order the bagels with loxs that comes on a fancy tower and makes you feel like you could be an influencer on Instagram when you take pictures of it. The bagel is delicious and you should absolutely get it. One of the best kept secrets of Sadelle's is the tuna melt, do yourself a favor and order it (even if you don't like tuna). Great restaurant with a great atmosphere.

A tad disappointed! My boyfriend and I had looked up "the most beautiful restaurants in NYC" hoping for an uber romantic Saturday date night.  We found images of a candle lit Sadelle's and fell in love.  Upon arriving we were immediately disappointed.  Rather then a sexy, pretty restaurant we had hoped for we walked into a very bright over priced cafeteria.  The waiter was very nice, the food OK.  Will not be coming back

Came here with my family for a special brunch and have to say I left somewhat dissatisfied. I have heard a great deal about Sadelle's so was truly looking forward to the meal.

Placement of our table was great because we were able to watch the bagels being made. Unfortunately the restaurant ran out of matzah ball soup which we were looking forward to enjoying. Additionally prices are high and I couldn't say I would definitely return.

The saddle tower comes with unlimited freshly toasted bagels and many different kinds of toppings in a tiered tray (smoked fish, fish moose, vegetables) . It is meant to be shared amongst 5 people and it is 125 dollars for the whole set up (so 25 per person). It is not touristy, and the space is very tastefully decorated with beautiful paintings and bakers pulling bagels in a glass pod in the center of the room. A top New York breakfast, don't miss it. Their reservations run out months in advance so be wary of that and plan accordingly.

We came here because it was a must-try list for New York. I am a bagels fanatic and we came here for a quick bite. Unfortunately for a table for 2 wihtout a reservation, the wait was 1 hr. So we decided to go for the quick grab-and-go. Over rated bagels that are the size of your fist. Coffee was good but not worth the $6. Took about 15 min to get our 2 bagels and coffee.
Three small desiccated slices of sable with an ok bagel for $25. Really? As to the ambiance, if you want a drafty room with half hearted service then you're in good hands. Avoid at all cost.

Unfortunately, I didn't have the most amazing experience at Sadelle's. A few college friends and I decided to meet and catch up over brunch. I was really excited and looking forward to eating here. I must say the service wasn't so great. It seemed like the waitress was attentive with every table accept ours! I noticed she was chatty and pleasant with the tables nearby. With our table we got a strange cold vibe from her and felt ignored. First, when we were ready to place our orders she walked away from our table. Also, I asked for a cup of coffee and didn't get one until we finished our meals and were ready to pay for the check. She gave me an empty cup and neglected to tell me they were making a fresh pot of coffee. Overall, the food was good but the service could use improvement.

Sadelle's has everything you could hope or want from an upscale breakfast and brunch restaurant in New York City. They make the bagels fresh in there open kitchen in the back. The lox is incredibly fresh. The coffee and cocktails are exceptionally fantastic as well. From the moment you walk in, the energy is positive. The staff makes you feel unbelievably welcome and comfortable. It's icertainly not cheap here but you get what you pay for, especially in Manhattan, and it's worth every penny. If you're looking for an amazing breakfast or brunch dining experience (they do serve dinner until 8:30PM on the weekends), Sadelle's couldn't be more perfect.

Note: they had a KITH x Versace event this weekend to launch the brand collaboration during fashion week. This should give you an idea of what to expect. High-end, top notch quality delivered by the best.

To their credit, our group was seated within 2 or 3 minutes of our arrival. The service was fine up to a particular point (which I'll get to in a minute) the waiter was helpful with our order and made some good suggestions. The food arrived quickly enough, along with our cocktails, and I must say it was very good. Bagels, which I understand they make on site, lox and whitefish all very tasty. I had the tuna melt, which was delicious and my daughters fiancé loved his friend chicken. The bagels and appetizing were the domain of my wife and daughter. It was after the table was bussed that things completely disintegrated. It took 10 minutes for a waiter, and not the same one who took our order, to come for our dessert order. We all ordered coffee, and my wife was anxious to try their famous bobka. We were told by the waiter that they had sold out for the day. Disappointed, we agreed that coffee without bobka would not be as good, and I said "thanks anyway, just bring us a check.  Now it's about 4-4:30 and the place is 80% empty mind you, and over 10 minutes later we have no check. The four of us are fine, and enjoying each other's company, but as we are talking, my wife is scanning the room trying to make eye contact with anyone who works there and it was as if we were invisible. My blood is now boiling as I stand up to get someone's attention! Another wait staff member comes over and we request the check again. He brings it over a few minutes later and while my wife was begging me to leave a bad tip, it's just not in my DNA. That said adding only 20% to a $260 brunch that fell apart in the home stretch felt lousy. 20% is as low as I'm ever going to go because I do appreciate what these people try to do, and that tips are very important to them. When my wife went over to the manager, who was sitting in a booth 2 tables over and told her what a letdown it was, she looked up from whatever she was doing and said "sorry", so that happened. Worst of all? As I was going through my emails from Open Table to leave feedback there, I came across my actual reservation where I requested a little something sweet with a candle as it was my wife's birthday, which of course never happened! What should have been a fun and special meal was just another overpriced SH#T Show thanks to a staff that fell down on the job and an indifferent manager.
An email to the restaurant group that owns this as well as some other quite good places went unanswered. It's a shame, because things were going so well...until they weren't. Anyway, go, don't go, it's all the same to me. Next time I want a bagel, whitefish and lox I'll go to Zabars or Russ and Daughters.

I ordered a gluten free everything bagel with cream cheese, bacon on the side, and the grapefruit cocktail. The bagel & cream cheese were great. The bacon was burned and dry. The grapefruit cocktail is a great idea but the grapefruit itself was not ripe and had very little flavor which was really disappointing because I love grapefruit. Service was slow but friendly. Overall seems like they pay no attention to detail and have very low standards for the food they serve.

Solid brunch experience 

Service was on point, from the start to sit down to exit , 
Constantly greeted and welcomed to the establishment

Bagels B+
Lox A
Tuna salad D (nothing special)

Overall it was something worth trying 
Expensive but ok
Not for something to be done on a regular..

I live in NYC and brunch is a weekend staple for me. Sadelle's def didn't live up to the hype. The service is terrible. We would have ordered another round or 2 of drinks, but the server never checked on us. Food is good, but nothing special. Leo's and Brooklyn Bagels are just as good and a lot cheaper.

Promptly seated us with a reservation and the food was SO good. It's the ideal place for a Saturday Brunch in NYC. The food is a bit on a pricey side ($22 for French Toast) but when you take your first bite, you understand why. The people, the energy, the atmosphere were delightful and I was so glad to have come here

SOO good wow !! You will need reservations to get in. A little on the pricey side but damn it's worth it. The French toast is likely the best I've ever had and it's huge you would have to share it. We also had a smoked salmon which is delicious. They didn't charge us for the extra bagel which was nice. The service was great. A must go to when you visit New York.

BEST BREAKFAST BAGEL EVER! Great brunch experience and love the teal plates, cups etc. The lox was so fresh and the bagels were on point. you can actually see the guy cutting the lox. Def make a res for this place. We got the tower so we were able to try different fishes. Also, its unlimited bagels.

Nothing but amazing experiences here at Sadelle's. If I am being honest I wanted to come here at first because I had seen the bagel towers all over Instagram. But when we walked in and tried basically everything on the menu, we knew we'd found a gem. Brunch for four consisted of a lox tower, healthy egg white sandwiches, French toast, cinnamon rolls, gravlax omelette, and more. This is also a good celebrity sighting spot too:) Every time my family comes into town this is the first place we go when they come from an airport!

Major Food Group's Brunch Mecca demonstrates that their expertise and culinary flair is not limited to Dinner.  If you want the best thick French Toast you will ever have which has been soaked in egg and vanilla and then grilled to perfection this is your place. If you want smoked salmon and breakfast smoked fishes that redefine the genre, this is the place to be as they bring out huge towers holding the smoked fish, capers, cucumbers and dill. Add on to this fabulous home made bagels, sticky buns, omelettes, pancakes, matzo ball soup and you will quickly realize why this is a very hard reservation to get for breakfast. I wish I could give it more than 5 stars.

This place was rated for the best French toast in NYC.  I cannot disagree more.  The toast was greasy and the bacon wasn't done.  I didn't eat the bacon and only half the French toast.  Very nice atmosphere but not impressed with the food nor the service.

Sadelle's is a beautiful restaurant and well that's about it. The service at least initially was a little indifferent and confused.
The menu is great at least on paper, however in execution simple items fail. How do you ruin franks in a blanket? Not sure but Sadelle's manages it. New York is not the bagel city it once was and I thought I might get great bagels here but these are simply average bagels. Same for the lackluster lox and the whitefish. The watery matzah ball soup was also uninspired. Sadelle's is not the 2nd Ave. Deli or Zabar's and I understand that, but I expected better food. Nothing even touched average.
Presentation is what Sadelle's does best and the towers are beautiful, the room is beautiful and even the waiters outfits are spiffy. Too bad the attention to detail and care did not go into the food.

Just went for the sticky buns. Would have been much better heated up. Very buttery but nice and flaky. Nice place/atmosphere. You can watch them make the dough for the bagels, etc. looked like there was a very nice bagel/lox tower. Be prepared for high prices. The sticky buns are pretty small, plate of 3 was 18 bucks. French toast was 22, we passed on that.

Hester Pepperfield here with another ice review... can I just start off my saving how ravishing Sadelle's perfect cube shaped ice were... they held figure and did not melt in an untimely fashion; in addition, they kept me and my chilled drink comfortable throughout the process (note the before and after photo of ice with drink filled vs. Empty) . However, there was one complaint. When they served their water the ice was missing; given their room temperature was around 62 degrees to keep their salmon fresh it still would have been nice to have at least some ice of the shaved variety.

Gotta say, these bagels and smoked salmons are absolutely phenomenal.

But for an hour wait (or longer, on the weekends) and extreme prices ($20ish for platter = 1 bagel, cream cheese, and the lox), I would recommend any other bagel shop

On the other hand, the custom omelette was actually wonderful.. especially with carmelized onions and and choice of other fillings (lox, meat, cheese, or more veggies)!!!

So good... what's surprisingly super good here (other than their famous fish/bagel tower which was delicious) is their french toast. It was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft (almost like bread pudding) on the inside. It's extremely rich so I recommend sharing but boy was it a treat. Tables are a little small but the decor is gorgeous. Glad we checked them out. Service is also super friendly (friend was late to our reservation but they were super cool about it).

Sadelles is a bit of a love hate for me. 

They really excel on absolutely lovely presentation and vibe. Reservations are really very annoying to get and don't try walking in because they'll quote you 2 hour waits for weekends and you'll probably end up waiting even longer than that if you stick around. Also it's incredibly over priced. 

That being said, when you do finally get the bagel tower, it's pretty tasty and really beautiful - definitely an instagram dream. There are several places in the city that are significantly better for lox and bagels, but if you're looking for a pretty classic soho brunch experience, this is on brand. 

Try going on off hours - slightly less frustration will ensue.

Really airy and beautiful space. I would say perfect for a group brunch however slightly overpriced. Their bagels are to die for, baked on premises, taste like heaven. 
Service is very attentive. Myself and my friend went there mid week for a brunch and it was busy! I ordered cream cheese bagel with salmon(super overpriced!)and my friend scrambled egg whites with a cucumber. Food presentation is very pretty on tiers although a bit silly...waiter should have advised that 2 people don't need to order 2 tiers of cucumber....That was just unnecessary and a total waste of food. Also they don't offer specialty coffees just simple black and forget about asking for warm milk!!! Worth visiting but be mindful of a price tag!

Got a great table for two second floor in the back, food was great and reasonably priced considering the lox and great presentation of a tower for two people without having to spend $125 for the big tower. Service could have definitely been better, very slow to bring coffee and simple drinks but otherwise fine - will be back and a great place to bring visitors!

Went here to try their famous sticky bun. I have to say that initially I was a bit underwhelmed by the size, but after tasting its richness, I understood why.

The pastry is done perfectly, but what separates this sticky bun from others is its glaze. Upon first bite there is a little bit of sweetness, but then it takes a more salty/savory tone.

For someone who really likes sweet pastries, this was a bit disappointing, but it was still a well done pastry nonetheless.

Come here to get a good instagram but pass if you're looking for good smoked fish, bagels, or service. I knew what I was getting into when I came here for brunch - the food was just ok, really nothing special in terms of taste, but looked cute stacked on plates in a tower formation. That's all there is to it. This is frankly just an overhyped, overpriced Major Food Group spot. Russ and Daughters or even Tompkins Square Bagels are much better if good lox bagels is what you're looking for.

Each of the incidences described below, on a standalone basis, aren't enough to form a negative option, but the culmination of these less-than-ideal experiences led me to give Sadelle's a solid 3 star rating.

I walked in to check in for my reservation, and was greeted by a hostess who looked like she hasn't smiled in years. She looked annoyed during our entire (thankfully brief) interaction. She also assumed she knew which reservation was mine before asking for my name...she said my last name aloud and asked if that was me. Good guess that one of the few asian last names on your list belonged to an asian woman, but it would've been less presumptuous to just ask.

Also, side note- why do you have to email to get a reservation? It's frankly inconveniencing more than anything, especially in the day and age of Resy/OpenTable/Yelp Reservations at your fingertips. 

Next, we had to wait a while before we had water but he did ultimately apologize for the wait. Given we had plenty of time to review the menu, we had questions for our server by the time he came to fill our waters. We wanted to ask him questions but he seemed annoyed and replied, "let me do the waters then I'll come back to answer your questions." When he returned he asked what we wanted without offering to answer our questions so we were confused. All in all I understand it's a busy place during peak brunch hours, and this guy is probably busting his butt trying to handle all of his tables, but if you're going to charge $24 for some thinly sliced fish and a small bagel, I'd imagine that you would strive for your service to be a key differentiator.

Bagels here are pretty small. When they first brought out our bagels, they mixed up our order. We asked for 3 "everything 2.0s" and 1 everything bagel. They gave us the reverse, and one of the bagels was actually 80% the size of the other. They fixed this quickly after we asked about it. Also, the "famous" sticky buns were flaky and buttery but kind of hard/tough. Glad we tried it but wouldn't necessarily recommend.

Bagels here are good but not amazing. I'm sure everyone has said this already but PLEASE BE WARNED!! A plain bagel for take out (not delivered) with cream cheese was $3.60 and is about half the size of a regular bagel. LOX WAS $15 !!! ON ONE MINI BAGEL!!!! So ridiculous. I was fuming when I handed over my card because it was too late. The lox was delicious- super fresh, but nothing can justify $15 for two thin slices of lox on top of a $3.60 mini bagel lol. Total $19- and yes, I was still hungry after! Be careful!

This place is a scam. You pay double prices for tiny portions. I ordered 3 items and nothing came as we ordered it. It cost $10 to substitute sausage for potatoes! $8 for 3 oz of orange juice!! Are the oranges made of gold??? Plus the waiters at Carbone won't shut up about the place. We get it, it's the same owner, who cares they're both overpriced and corny. Anybody who eats here is a schmuck...

Since I moved from London to NYC, I have been a regular at Sadelle's. It is my absolute favorite place to brunch for the following reasons; 
- The staff are the warmest people you'll ever meet. They've all been working there for years which says a lot, they remember you and really make you feel as though they care.
- The food is delicious. I recommend the house salmon, bagel, avocado, roast potatoes, tuna melt and the babka. The house salmon is incredible and they bring it on a tower so don't feel as though you need to order the Sadelle's Tower. 
- Yes you have to wait a little, but it is so worth it and despite being a more upscale brunch spot, there's something about the decor and atmosphere of Sadelle's that makes you feel so at home and comfortable. You almost don't want to leave but the groups of people waiting for a table reminds you that everyone deserves to enjoy brunch at Sadelle's. 
- It is just an iconic NYC restaurant. So if you're someone like me who loves NYC, go support. Or don't - they're never short of a customer anyway.

The service was abysmal. It took us an hour and a quarter for our food to arrive. The two tables next to us, arrived later than we did, & we're finished and gone by the time we were served. No apology from our server. It took 1/2 an hour to get the alcoholic beverages & another 10 minutes to get coffee. The waiter claimed it took 10 minutes to make a fresh pot of coffee. It tasted like it came from the bottom of the pot. Cost of brunch was definitely not worth it.

Bright, airy space and not nearly so loud as one might expect. Yes, bagels are good and it's fascinating to watch as they're made in the glassed-in central kitchen but it is the french toast that you MUST order. I've never had better -- thick (at least 2") slices of challah bread with the perfect amount of char and just the perfect amount of sweetness. 
Sweet roll, another acclaimed menu item, didn't live up to its reputation. It has an interesting sweet/salty flavor but it was dried out 
Good service. Prompt, correct and gracious.

Great Brunch place. Perfect house cured salmon, perfectly sliced. The bagels are made made in house too. The matzo ball soup tastes home made. The waitstaff is lovely but overwhelmed and harried., bringing all the food at once and forgetting important utensils like the soup spoons and having to be reminded. Unfortunately the had to actually go downstairs to get them by the time we got them the soup was cold and so were other hot times by the time we could make room at the table to eat them. The quality of the food is amazing unfortunatelyI suppose when you don't have to cater to patrons needs because there is such a demand for reservations and seating the attention to detail falters.
Also be careful making your reservation because trying to correct it is impossible!

Crazy to think my fiancé and I had to wait 2 weeks before we could even get a reservation at Sadelle's! However, once we stepped foot, we soon realized why that is the case. Sadelle's beautifully intertwines a modern and rustic look into its atmosphere. Business is definitely booming, as there is already a line both by the door as well as to the side of Sadelle's. People eagerly waiting an extra 15 minutes to get to their tables - but what's 15 minutes extra to the 2 weeks of waiting for a reservation? Sadelle's is loud, but more so in a lively and bright manner versus the cacophony that screeches across a less classy restaurant. 

Our waiter was so helpful and answered any questions we had with a smile on his face. He even told us about ordering one sticky bun, as opposed to the three that the menu offered. Loving this compromise, we ordered the famous sticky bun as well as the Salmon Benedict and famous french toast. 

The sticky bun came out first as if it were the appetizer to the breakfast main course. To our surprise, it was much smaller than anticipated. It was indeed sticky, and we enjoyed how it resonated of caramel flavoring. As the waiter explained, it was like eating a mini pecan bun, but without the nuts. Although glad I tried it out, I don't think I would get it again. 

Next up: the french toast. Very thick and fluffy, it looked like a french toast dream come true! One bite in, and I was pleasantly surprised to both feel softness and crispy textures! I am still puzzled at how the chefs could cook up such a texture juxtaposition. Eating this french toast reminded me of eating a funnel cake at a fair - lovely and nostalgic. 

Seeing as Sadelle's specializes in a lot of fish dishes such as salmon, I decided to try out a more savory option - the Salmon Benedict. Albeit small, this entree definitely packed in a lot of flavor! The salmon tasted so fresh, and the hollandaise flavor bursted with flavor! The eggs were also perfectly poached, and the bread was quite soft too. I am surprised the Salmon Benedict doesn't have as much recognition as other dishes such as the bagel tower, because the Salmon Benedict definitely deserves it! 

The Salmon Benedict was a small entree, but that was a good thing in our case because the french toast was huge, so split between two people, this would be a perfect meal for both people! Overall, we loved our experience at Sadelle's! We would come back just to order the same entrees!

Although small, the bagels are high quality classic New York bagels. I went with chive cream cheese and a tomato (perfect meaty and ripe). It seemed like a bagin at $3. They also have great looking fish options. The only negative is it took a bit longer to make them I would have expected, but once I took a bite it was worth it. I'll come back for sit down service soon!
This place was wonderful. Best breakfast I've had in a while. Perfect ending to a great trip to nyc!

Came here with a group of friends on a weekday for a late brunch at 11:30. We made a reservation a few weeks in advance so there was no wait, but it was decently busy at the time. Three of us ordered the House Salmon platter, and one of my friends ordered the Whitefish Salad platter. All the platters were served with a choice of bagel, tomato, onion, capers, and cream cheese. We also ordered sticky buns and breakfast potatoes for the table. The sticky buns were great and I highly recommend them. The smoked salmon was also fresh and delicious. We left extremely full and satisfied!

The Restaurant is situated in the high- rent district of West Broadway in Soho.  

We had lox and Sturgeon on a bagel.  Both fishes were fresh, good quality, but expensive.  The service was fine.  They boast the "best bagel in New York" but they were not.  While they were homemade, they were no better than Tompkins, Bagel Bob's or Ess a Bagel.  They had a limited selection - (no pumpernickel, rye or whole wheat) and the bagels were  smaller (distinctly smaller) than a normal sized bagel and you only get one bagel with a $24 bagel and lox.  If you wanted an additional bagel that would cost another 4 or 5$.   I ordered a grapefruit juice, and I got no more than 1/3 of a wine glass of juice for 7$ or 8 $ .  If I hadn't been with other people, I would have returned it.  

This restaurant is overpriced.  They will not accept cash - only debit or credit cards.  This practice is not only annoying, but discriminatory against those who don't use, or are unable to use credit cards.  The tables are tiny and everyone is crowded together.   I would not recommend it.

I'll start by saying the meal was delicious. The three stars are because of the service. Our waiter was charming when he was with us. The problem started after the entrees were delivered. He never popped by to check that all was well, so we were unable to alert him about a mistake in the order. This annoyance was followed by our $6 mugs of house brewed joe remaining empty until we resorted to waving our arms. Call me crazy, but I don't feel I should have to beg for basic service or coffee refills when I'm spending over $100 on breakfast for three.

Despite being quoted for an hour wait, my best friend and I only waited 30 minutes earlier today around 1130am. It was definitely busy and obviously trendy, but I actually was impressed by the food. We split the French toast (MUST GET) and the house salmon tower. The tower only comes with one bagel but the rest of the fish, etc could be shared by two. I ordered a side of sesame bagel with cream cheese. 

The winner though, was the French toast hands down. It was gigantic and could feed 2-3 people. Crispy outside, fluffy inside. Just perfection.

Over-rated. People rave about Sadelle's but I found it noisy, over-priced and below the quality I was expecting given all the hype. Ordered expensive fish plate and expected enough slices to share among four people. It arrived with two measly slices which my party had divvy up. Never again.

I can't speak for the dine-in experience, since I've only come to Sadelle's to pick up a quintessential salmon bagel to start the day back when I used to work in the Soho area. Although on the pricier end, Sadelle's truly does have some of the best bagels in the city! (Then again, it's pretty hard to find truly horrible bagels in NYC, and I've had comparable quality bagels for less.) The bagel counter does get somewhat crowded though, so be prepared for a bit of a wait.

My usual order is the house salmon on a salt & pepper bagel with plain cream cheese, tomatoes, and onions. The salt & pepper bagel balances out the creaminess and acidity of the tomatoes and onions, and the texture of the salmon is delectable when taken as a whole with the rest of the ingredients! Too bad I'm back on a low carb kick, since otherwise I'd definitely be making more trips here!
Amazing Tuna melt and House salmon bagel! The restaurant is spacious. Definitely make a resi before going (the walk-ins usually have a crazy wait even at 2PM)

Wow, just wow.  We ordered up a storm and everything I put in my mouth was delicious.  Even the Bacon, Egg, Cheese sandwich was unbelievable.  The blueberry pancakes rival the Clinton Street Baking Company.

Obviously don't miss the salmon.  And don't, don't miss the blintzes.  They were the best I ever had.

Service was very good.  Place is handsome.  Prices were high but worth the quality.

Only giving 1 star because the waiter was ok.

The OJ was $7.  It came in a wine glass and filled about 25% of the wine glass.  It was likely the absolute worst OJ I've ever tasted.  A nasty aftertaste.  Please avoid it or you'll regret it! Thank me later. 

I had the French toast for $22.  Cool concept - essentially making French toast using 1/2 a loaf of bread - presliced.  However, terribly executed.  The inside was so soggy (hadn't poured the syrup on it.  Could not finish it. 

Came with my bosses and coworker.  I was embarrassed that I was unable to finish my food.  I refused to take it with me - that's how soggy the inside was... it was not even worth it.   I wanted to take a picture- but again, I was with my bosses.  

Save your money and go somewhere else.  That's just my 2 cents. Wish I had actual breakfast before this.

I've been to many, many restaurants in NYC, most the time I'm not very impressed. Sadelle's is truly a gem. Consistently delicious, great atmosphere, wonderful service, 10/10. Make sure to make a reservation because they are always busy, but so worth it! Highly recommend.

Sadelle's falls into the category of overrated NYC brunch spots. It's similar to Russ and Daughters because it's known for smoked salmon and bagels, and always has a long line, but I was disappointed with the food. I got the smoked salmon eggs Benedict and it was mediocre at best. The eggs were overcooked and the yolks had no runny effect whatsoever. The smoked salmon was good, but there was a very thin slice given considering the dish was $24 and did not come with any sides. The dish was quite measly. The highlight of the meal were the breakfast potatoes. They were perfectly cooked, super crispy, and had a ton of flavor with peppers, onions, and seasoning. The bagels were fine but not the best when compared to Ess-a-Bagel or most local bagel stores in Queens. However, the restaurant itself is pretty cute and they use lovely Le Creuset products which is nice. Overall I could not recommend Sadelle's for brunch because there are so many other great places in Soho.

Sadelle's is adorable inside. 

I went on Saturday with a friend for brunch. We were squeezed into a table that was not near any other tables and was behind the waitstaff station. Service was spotty. 

Service aside, the food was really great. I loved the salmon platter. The salt and pepper bagel was perfect with the salmon and accompaniments. We also ordered the french toast to share. This was hands down the best french toast I've ever had. The inside was the consistency of bread pudding and the outside was delightfully crisp. Amazing! We both ordered a pineapple cocktail that I would not order again. 

Towards the end of the meal something must have happened with the A/C. It got so warm I was sweating and started to feel faint - we couldn't get out of there fast enough. I'd still go back for that french toast though!

I love sadelles. Everything is delicious and they are child friendly which i love. Bloody marys are delicious! Expensive yes, but Sadelles give you a true NYC brunch experience. Weve had the egg salad, french toast, bagels and eggs.. everything was delicious. The only thing that was disappointing was the price of sticky buns.. tiny but expensive..

If your going to Sadelle's don't forget to make a reservation for this place because it seriously gets super busy even on the weekdays!  My first time coming here and a friend had told us about this spot so we decided to come and enjoy a nice brunch. The inside of this place is super gorgeous and the lighting looks so pretty. 

We ordered a smoke salmon Sadelle's tower for the three of us and got everything bagels. You can put as much as you want in your make it yourself bagel. 

Overall we had a great time here and I would say everything tasted nice and fresh! Loved smoke salmon and definitely enjoyed the bagels on top of it. This order is for sure shareable between friends and it was a fun experience. 

The tower also is very picture worthy!
Love this place! The food is delicious! Definitely make a reservation because it gets busy! This is a great brunch spot and worth checking out if you're in the area!!

Pricing is hilarious. "Yeah I'll have miniature speck-of-sand bagel atom for $25.99" said no human ever... It's a cute, high ceilinged, white girl, exposed brick palace of pretentiousness, but honestly who in the Wild Wild West Broadway set the prices at this place? Going here is like the time grandma accidentally slipped you a $100 bill instead of a $10 but in reverse. I mean jesus, this is the gold buckle of the NYC "bagel belt" that's made of the kind of gold you find in a Ritz Carlton faucet lever. Kitschy, costly, dripping with self-acclaim.

Arriving at the restaurant with two friends, there was a lot of people waiting out front with an obvious wait. I'm not the type to wait around for a table, I'd rather not eat than wait. As I walked up to the hostess (Rachael) I asked her if there was room for a party of 3, she said it's about an hour. In response I asked if there was "anything that could be done to speed it up", her response was " there's always something that can be done;)". I walked over to the ATM and took out $20, went back to the hostess and showed her discreetly and she accepted the bill. Asked me my name and told us to wait out front. The weather was nice so we sat outside, literally for AN HOUR AND FIVE MINUTES!!! As for the food, it was completely overrated and took another 30 minutes to arrive; definitely not worth waiting for. Had I know we would have just went elsewhere. If you like Dos Caminos happy hour a couple doors down, you'll love this bridge and tunnel restaurant as well.
I absolutely love this place... The service here was amazing the bagels are like no other it's a little pricey but it's worth every penny.

This is probably the most over rated place in NY :
Yes , bagels are great ! But service is horrible!!!
The most not welcoming host at the entrance of the restaurant who creates a not necessary queues !
No espresso machine in a way way way over priced breakfast!
That's what happens when they enjoy a massive wait of guests.
Buy their bagels for takeaway...much smartest
Great bagels. I loved it when they had the unlimited bagels! We got to try tons of bagels! Bring it back please!

Overpriced but delicious food for brunch. Excellent Bloody Marys. I had the Scottish salmon on a bagel with the standard accoutrements (sliced onion, capers, tomato). It was presented in a tower which was nice but certainly not worth the $22-24. The Scottish salmon was delicious. The bagel was also very good. My friend had an egg white omelette, which she said was very good. My husband had the blueberry pancakes, which he said were the BEST blueberry pancakes he'd ever had. We also ordered the signature sticky bun, which was a buttery bite of cinnamon sticky goodness.  Whenever there is a "signature" dish, I have to try it. It WAS very good and very tiny. I've had better sticky buns. 

If you are seeking a fun place to have brunch, you really can't go wrong with Sadelle's. Just be prepared for the hefty bill at the end.

Made a reservation for 2:15. Got seated at 2:40 and got menus 10 mins after that. We ordered the salmon eggs Benedict, the Greek salad, the honey friend chicken with pickles, and an omelette with potatoes. For having to wait for a while, the waiter also brought out pigs in a blanket and grapefruit cocktail. Everything was amazing! The "spicy" chicken was not spicy at all but was amazing with the truffle honey on top! The salmon eggs Benedict were incredible and were on a soft spongey biscuit. This place is a Jews dream come true! Everything was amazing and I would definitely recommend.

Totally overrated. Spent $70 for 2 bagels and lox and cream cheese. Got the salt and pepper bagel which was a total pepper bomb. Asked for an everything instead and they charged us another $3! There's way better bagels and lox in the city that won't cost an arm and leg. Not going back. *ps the bagels are like mini bagels.

Ok, the food was completely fine. But if you look up over priced in the dictionary, you'll find a picture of Sadelles. Tiny, infant sized bagel for 24 dollars - now that's basically theft. An omelette with NO SIDES for $20. It's TRULY not worth the hype. I suggest going to essa bagel or absolute bagels if you want your fix.
This place was great.  We went all out and ordered the three tier fish assortment with unlimited bagels.  All the fish was great and the four of us almost finished it!
A bagel lox and cream cheese $25 and really nothing special and the French toast is fried and mushy ..... horrible

I came here for one thing and one thing only... French toast. I've read that this was the best French toast in the city. All of my previous go tos: Carnegie deli, Stage deli and Ben Ash Deli have all closed down. I had high expectations coming into the establishment and those expectations were definitely met. Yes, the prices are high but the quality was just as high.

This is my absolute favorite lunch time spot. The food is fresh delicious on point. My favorite item on the menu is their tomato soup! It's the most delicious tomato soup I've ever had in my life. It's big enough for 2 people to share. Everything I've had here is super delicious. Couple other favorites are the club sandwich which is big enough for 3 people to share. And the basic tuna sandwich on a gluten free everything bagel, onion, tomato, scallion cream cheese is everything. The prices are a bit on the higher side but the quality and the portions I believe match it. I highly recommend here!

Came here for breakfast on a recent trip to NYC. Was about half hour walk from our hotel in Midtown. We were able to make a reservation for 9 at 9am. Most people ordered the everything bagel with fish (house salmon, smoked Scottish, sturgeon) while others chose other breakfast dishes (healthy egg sandwich, salmon Benedict, French toast). 
The consensus was that the smoked Scottish was the favorite with the sturgeon being the least liked. I had the healthy egg sandwich and it was a large portion. An aunt ordered the French toast and was impressed with the thickness of the bread and was satisfied.
We also ordered a serving of the sticky buns to share. They were standard sticky buns. 
Service was fantastic with our dishes coming out shortly after ordering, coffee being asked for refills, etc. A good experience overall.

Took forever to get my overpriced tiny bagel.
It's the worst take away experience I've ever had in my life.

Sadelles, located in the lush flower conservatory - Wow.  There is only One Breakfast you should order:
Their Signature dish, the Salmon Eggs Benedict.

Never before have I experienced the Eggs Benedict of this caliber.  A work of art.  

While slicing thru the perfectly cooked Egg, I marveled watching the yolk explode - flowing onto the plate.

Gently pushing my fork into that velvety smoked Scottish salmon, egg, covered with chives & perfectly cooked sauce, I couldn't help but to slow down and taste every morsel of this meal - I think this is...perfection.

Sadelle's is definitely the go to spot for bagels and traditional NYC brunch fare in Soho. Unless you make a reservation weeks in advance, you are out of luck if you want to have brunch there on Saturday or Sunday. The advantage of living up the street is the Sadelle's takeout counter. The same great bagels and lox (cured salmon) you have in the restaurant. While you won't see all the Celebs, you still get all the great taste. Dinner at Sadelle's is also terrific.

Second brunch I have been to in New York! It was very busy when we arrived. So we put our name in and it was an hour and a half wait. Luckily the area around it super cute and so we kept busy during the wait time. Seating was very tight. We sat in the chair and booth area and you were literally almost shoulder to shoulder with the person next to you. The food was pretty good. I ordered the salmon Benedict and got a side of bacon. I was going to order a mimosa but it was not worth $15. Our waiter did a good job of refilling our water. My friend got a coffee that was $6. A little pricey for just normal coffee that mediocre. Overall the food was good but the atmosphere could have been better. I would give this place 3.5 stars if that was an option.

The best French toast anywhere. The fishes are so fresh and good. Better to be a pary of at least four so when you over order there's more to taste and less to take home. Been there three times with a reservation (a must) and had to sit upstairs each time. Not the best spot.

Reservations must be booked far in advance. We didn't have one, but you can put your name down and shop around soho while you wait, which is what we did. Came here with a friend on a Saturday around noon. We ended up having to wait about an hour to get seated, but it wasn't bad since there's a lot of places to browse nearby and they give you a decent estimate of time to leave and come back. The place is very cute and two floors. We were seated upstairs which we enjoyed because it felt less crowded. We started with the cheese blintzes which were tasty, but we were surprised they were sweet rather than savory. For my meal I got the Leo which is basically a frittata with salmon on top. It was super tasty! My friend got the eggs any style, which came with a bagel and cream cheese which was a large portion and their bagels are very tasty. Service was good for how crowded they are. Overall definitely worth a try but not trying to go back every weekend because of the crowd! It is also a bit pricey for brunch.

Pro:
Very popular brunch, service is Ok.

Smoked salmon is very good, chewy and savory.

Con: 
Everything is too salty, including the bagel.

Can't say enough about this place!! It's a MUST! Went on a Sunday morning and they are already filling up, however, the entire staff works hard to give you a great experience. There's a worker behind the counter slicing the smoked salmon and it's mesmerizing (and also makes your starving) to watch before being seated! 
The service of your choice of fish comes with bagels, smear, fresh tomato, cucumber, and chives. Incredible- we could have eaten this over and over! Also ordered an omelette on the side which went perfectly with our meal. They have other egg options such  as Benedict, egg sandwiches, etc. and plenty of breakfast sides. Coffee is great, they only serve iced or hot drip though. 
We had a wonderful breakfast and would absolutely love to come back soon!

Overpriced breakfast/brunch items thats got the stuff to leave you warm and fuzzy. The atmosphere is elegant yet rough with the exposed brick interior. 

You can't go wrong ordering any of their fish. It comes with a couple and some bagel fixings like capers and tomatoes. Their bagels aren't huge, which was good for me since I ordered a fairly big meal. The smoked Scottish salmon was everything I had hoped for.  Buttery, Smokey, and a great fish taste. They have an amazing distributor, cause it tasted quite fresh. The bagel is amazing as most New York bagels are. The cream offer is damn good too. The capers were just the right amount of tart without being too much. 

The bacon sausage egg and Muenster sandwich is like eating a tasty cloud. The egg and challah bread feel like they become one and the same in this beautiful marriage of spongy bread and egg white. The bacon and sausage further enhanced the grease profile, but neither were too greasy.  Both had an elegant pork taste while being distinguished from each other. They add just the lightest touch of mayonnaise, which I didn't think was necessary, but I was ok with.

We had a wonderful experience at Sadelle's. The environment seems swanky and upscale for brunch. If is perfect for celebrating a special event or if you want to get a little fancy for brunch!

We tried the classic breakfast, it was absolutely delicious. The eggs were soft and fluffy and flavorful. The bagels were some of the best I've ever tried. My sister had the lox and she loved it. Yes, it is pricey, but worth it for a special occasion!

Found!
Sadelle's serves an excellent brunch.  The salmon is expertly sourced, smoked, and sliced to go with the bagel and smear. Plenty else on the menu to round out your meal like latkes, salads, matzoh ball soup, etc. The place is quite lively and not easy to get a table, so book early!
For more great reviews visit TheLoupe!

It's a great bagel and a cool restaurant but it just isn't the worth the price. I got a bagel with Lox and cream cheese and it ended up costing $20 with tax and tip. Overrated and not worth the wait or price. So many spots to try in the city, explore a little

Food is always great. Here's the problem: after ordered a very expensive brunch delivery via Caviar, my food came and there was NO BAGEL with my $24 Scottish smoked salmon. And guess what? You CANNOT get in touch with this restaurant if you have a problem. There is no phone number, no email, nothing. I'm now hungry and angry. And if a business has no way for you to get in touch if you have a complaint, something is seriously wrong.

The food is way too expensive, the tables are way too small, I didn't get the impression the wait staff really knows the food on the culture, they serve soda in little bottles so it's warm and non-refillable. The long wait of over an hour was definitely not worth it. Some of the food is very good but the matzo ball soup was a bowl of dill weed. Over seasoned with dill weed. The Russian dressing was way too pickle tasting

The pigs in the blanket the lox and the egg salad we're all good once you scrape the dill off the top of them. Overall I felt like they were trying too hard to reinvent Jewish food. Junior's has much better matzo ball soup. Katz's Deli much better everything

The salmon eggs benedict is excellent...high quality salmon, light hollandaise and delicious! The french toast is the best french toast in the city...crispy on the outside and super soft on the inside and not too sweet, just the perfect level of sweetness! The bagels are okay, they are smaller and the tower is definitely overpriced.

Super cute and fun spot for breakfast/brunch! My cousin raves about Sadelle's and was able to snag a reservation for us here on short notice. I highly recommend reservations here because Sadelle's will be packed no matter when you go. 

The space is slightly loud, open and welcoming; perfect for a group or a date. We started with coffee which was tad pricey at $6, but our cups were never empty and it was delicious! We then ordered the House Salmon with everything bagels and the Blueberry Pancakes. I loved the size of the bagel, it was filling without being too much. The salmon was a perfect balance of smoky and salty. The pancakes were amazing!! They were thin and slightly crispy on the outside, just perfect. We were treated to the Grapefruit Cocktail which was unlike anything I've ever tried. It had crystallized sugar along the top and the mint complimented it nicely. Our server was so wonderful and sweet, he made sure we were taken care of the entire time. I will definitely be back!

My friend told me that Sadelle's had authentic bagels, schmear and lox and I had to try it. We came for brunch on a weekday and it wasn't too crowded thank goodness. The tables are very close together so you're almost sitting elbow to elbow. 

We shared Scottish smoked salmon bagels and their French toast. The smoked salmon came with tomato, cucumber, onion & capers and we ordered the sesame bagels. The bagels were nice and chewy and the smoked salmon was perfect. The French toast was quite big and was so good slightly crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. I'm not normally a French toast person but I really liked the French toast here!

Near the back of the restaurant is a glass enclosure where the bagel makers were making bagels. I thought it was so neat that you could see them making tray after tray of yummy bagels.

Service was efficient so no complaints there. Sadelle's is a great place to eat...have to load up on carbs before a marathon shopping jaunt :)

Had brunch here on a Friday... the staff is friendly, seated within a few minutes at the upper level. I ordered a Bellini and the salmon salad with the cinnamon raisin bagel. No complaints... didn't think I was going to enjoy it but glad I gave it a try

Fantastic food including the salmon and best French toast ever! Don't miss it!
Very expensive and medium to small portions...

Sadelle's is definitely one of the most popular spots in NY for breakfast/lunch so make sure to make a reservation or come early or expect a wait. Obviously had to have the bagels with their house salmon, it was delicious. Get a tower with whatever you'd like on your salmon and don't forget to snap a classic picture. My friend got the french toast which is a huge portion, great for sharing between 4 people for a little bit of sweet after your savory bite. Atmosphere is so nice, great service and overall a very nice experience. It is pricey but it is NYC prime real estate and a trendy spot so expect to overpay for a side of avocado and your mimosa.

What an amazing place for brunch! We went for my daughter's 29th birthday and it was a gem. First, do make sure you make reservations the correct way if you want a specific day or time - that means using email 30 days TO THE DAY before your chosen date! Look on their website for complete directions. 
I would've given them 5 stars if it weren't for the complicated reservation system and the fact that they made a mistake TWICE with my reservation. 

But back to the food! We got a fantastic lesson on all the different types of salmon - smoked lox, sable, etc. it was an excellent service to provide and she was spot on! We tried two different kinds and the blintzes - I'm a nut for good blintzes and these were wonderful although a bit pricey for the amount. But the flavor was...MMmmm! 

The space is so adorable and my daughter was thrilled which was the whole point, right? We even topped off our morning with mimosas, so it was a fabulous way to start her last year of her 20's! Everyone should start their day at Sadelle's if they can!

I love Sadelle's, the food is good and the atmosphere is really cute. The only reason I did 4 vs 5 stars is its a little pricey, but I like it enough to spend on breakfast when o normally wouldn't at other locations. they have these little cinnamon buns that are so good and something they are "famous" for. The servers are always very nice and get your food to you pretty quickly. However one
thing you MUST get are the pigs in a blanket - i'm really
sad that I didn't get two orders cause I want moreee !!

If you are planning to get a quick brunch go somewhere else. When I ate here with friends for brunch it took around 1.5 hours to get our food and 2.5 hours until we left. In that time, I could have flown to Scotland, caught a salmon, smoked the salmon, and then served it in the restaurant. The waiters were inattentive and we had to keep asking for coffee, water, or our food. One of my friends got shoved by a rude waiter who did not apologize but instead laughed. The food was good but the service severely impacted the experience of eating at this restaurant. I WILL NEVER EAT AT THIS ESTABLISHMENT AGAIN!

Wish I could say I loved this place, but unfortunately, I didn't.

I was staying over in the city and looked up a nearby bagel place. This restaurant popped up. I've honestly never heard of this place before but seeing the great reviews and the amount of reviews, my boyfriend and I decided to try this place to-go.

Upon entering, I noticed how crowded it was so that was a plus. We maneuvered our way over to the to-go section and I ordered a plain bagel lightly toasted with bacon on the side and apple juice.

Two problems: they don't serve bacon or apple juice to-go. What? Why not? That was a bummer so I settled for a plain bagel with grapefruit juice. I had to question if these were full sized bagels or mini bagels because they were EXTREMELY TINY!

The juice was way too strong so I didn't finish it and the bagel was super dry. My boyfriend ordered a toasted bagel with cream cheese and wasn't impressed.

For two bagels and juice it came out to a whopping $13!!!!! We were so shocked at how expensive this place was.

Yeah, never coming again!

Great breakfast/lunch place.  Huge salads. Beautifully displayed bagel items. Lox, cucumbers, tomatoes, avocado and capers
The staff is friendly. 
Got to see Neil Patrick Harris with his family. 
Good time.

Went last Sunday. Reservation was taken and guaranteed via OpenTable the week before. When we arrived no wait. We were seated at 5 Pm. Ordered shortly after being seated. I ordered DeCaf coffee. The waiter told me they were out and they were not making any more. And if I wanted hot coffee they had a bit of regular left. 
Before the order came out I asked to order an additional order of Nova.  I was told the kitchen closes at 515pm.  After that we were told they were out of the bagels we ordered. The waiter even told us that they believe they should not take a reservation or seat anyone so late. It was the most absurd did Inc experience I have ever had. Order did not come out correctly and could not be fixed because the kitchen was closed. Now tell me what kind of sense does that make? Should have been called the twilight zone cafe. Not a good experience very disappointed. And we felt totally ripped off...
Very long wait.  Paying $21 for a  bagel cream cheese and lox is too much even for New York.   Would not eat there again.
Best tuna in the business! It even beats subway's tuna!! Fun place with good veggies as well. Two thumbs up.
My favorite place in New York! I wish you guys would open one up in Los Angeles!! Best gluten free bagel I've ever had and best lox I've ever had!

Your definition of a fluffy New York bagel, with good flavor and a good bite to it. The egg salad is a safe choice, and made not too overly salty so as to accompany an everything bagel well. The salmon is cut super thick, with attention made to cut out the middle so that you're not reaching for a toothpick to remove the sinews with every bite.

I went to the deli, so I cannot comment much on service or other meals. The cashier was friendly and happy to answer questions.

My only complaint is that they're tiny and what other bagel shops would label a "mini bagel." The prices are also incredibly steep, especially when you add smoked salmon (which goes for about $15, I believe).
