Sadelle's is good for one or two visits a year, but I couldn't afford to make this my regular spot.
I've tried their pancakes  it was good, you will be lucky if you got a bigger table than mine, and yes I'm adding it to my collection to recommend people to try it.

Delicious, overpriced, trendy, Instagram-ready, great service, would come again. But so expensive. Not special enough for the $$$. Would give it 3.5 stars if I could, which I think is the current average Yelp rating anyway.

Had a delightful brunch here with my friend. She ordered an egg white omelette, and I ordered an everything bagel with smoked Scottish salmon and cream cheese. We also got a side of crispy potatoes. I loved the open kitchen, where you can see the staff rolling and baking the bagels. The presentation was also beautiful; I wasn't expecting the three tiered plates for just a single serving of bagel + fixings. Our server was also attentive, and the food came quickly. Everything was delicious.

But $24 for one bagel and some lox? That's basically 2x what it would be anywhere else. And for a little ambiance? I'd rather do Murray's, Brooklyn Bagel, or Ess-A-Bagel and have some money left over for drinks. Yikes. No regrets though, I got my pics and my views.

The food is high quality, and the service chill and attentive especially considering how packed it is.  They were very kind and helpful over email when trying to make a reservation at the last minute.

One cold brew costs 8 US Dollars.

Today's brunch would be my very first time finally dinning here after 2 failed attempts. Last 2 attempts were without reservation and it was a 3+ hours wait... So should I just come back for dinner?! LoL 

So this time, with reservation, we were seated right away. Great service, cozy ambiance, casual setting. 

Pros:
Latke Royale: really really fresh salmon. I'd say it's sushi grade fresh salmon with just enough fat. I don't think they were smoked it. If any, just a tad bit and it was not overly salty. And the caviar on top. Oh my, so fresh! I inhaled it in like 2 min and still feeling hungry. 

French toast: oh man, so good. Crispy on the outside, creamy on the inside. Come with side of jam and syrup. There were a lot of silence moment with our heads shaking because we enjoyed the food so much lol 

Fried chicken: not quite full yet, so we ordered fried chicken. Juicy, flavourful, quite good. 
"Quite good" was elevated to amazing when they asked if we would like to some TRUFFLE HONEY with it. Oh my my, so heavenly delicious. 

Cons: grapefruit cocktail is NOT a cocktail. It's really just a cut up bowl of grapefruit with bits of caramelized honey on top. Um OK so $14/bowl is NOT worth it. Feeling disappointed with no booze for Sunday brunch...

So I'm definitely coming back to try other items on the menu... With the TRUFFLE HONEY lol
Food is great but service is terrible. The heavy set woman at the entrance should get a lesson in customer service!

Yum! sadelles is a soho institution- also has a location in Las Vegas! The bagels are legendary, they are tiny and absolutely filling and delicious. The avocado was unlike any I've ever had, with the chives / and olive oil on top- delicious touches. The service was speedy and non intrusive and we were seated pretty soon after we came into the restaurant. It's all exposed brick and cool melted candlesticks for the decor. Make a reservation in advance, they book up for breakfast/ brunch on the weekends quickly!

Probably the most famous Jewish brunch place in the city. Reservations are only made through an online system and it's impossible to talk to anybody over the phone. But once you make a reservation through the online system, any modifications or questions can be emailed to their email and they answer right away. It's actually not that bad.

The interior is very pretty with a ground floor, half raised ground floor and a second floor that are all filled with tables and some communion tables. In the front, they also have a take out section where an employee prepares their famous salmon. The bagle with salmon and cream cheese with variations can be taken out here. For the diners, a lot of people enjoy 3-tier spreads/salmons with bagles. I tried their famous sticky buns but was pretty disappointed as I was imagining cinnabon looking buns but they were tiny and flat and they were $6 each.. However, their salmon egg benedict melted in the mouth and was amazing. French toast was fantastic as well, really moist inside and crispy outside. But it's lightly deep fried so it's a bit heavy but still really good. 

Service is amazing, everyone here is really friendly. I'd like to try their 3-tier salmon and spreads with bagles next time I visit. It's definitely pricey so for that, I'm taking one star off. But the location and atmosphere is amazing. They are not open for dinner!

Finding something great to eat around soho has always been a headace. Other then chains there is only few mentions thats worth the walk. Sadelles is one worthy of a great lunch. Major food group never fails to satisify the tummy. Prices of course is high like all MFG establishments. But as always worth the trip. Try the smoked salmon tower~a must. Add some sides. Have a bloodymary, also excellent. Then finish off with their famous expensive french toast...YUM. now keep on shopping.

I can see why there was a line for this place. Had a plain bagel with cream cheese, lox, onion and capers. It was excellent! Miss having real NY bagels. We don't get this kind of quality in California!
Such a tasty bagel, friendly staff and a very cool vibe in here but it's extremely expensive- paid $24+ for a takeaway smoked salmon and cream cheese everything bagel.

Loved everything about this place! You get the true New York experience and ambience. Staff is super friendly and helpful, and don't make you feel rushed to leave especially when there are many others waiting to be seated (btw, making reservations are super easy and apparently you can make them a month in advance?!). Best bagels n lox by far with large portions if you order the tower situation (we didn't but saw many around us order it). Sliced-to-order salmon and sturgeon...so fresh you can tell these people know what their doing and take pride in their food. Bloody Mary's are great. I would also recommend the healthy egg sandwich. Will 100% be back to try the French toast next time!!

Went here for "brunch" on a Sunday at 430 pm and it. Was. Amazing!!! A reservation here may be tough to get and very popular but it is absolutely worth it. The place has s beautiful interior and the staff is extremely attentive. Great spot for a date as well. Here's what to order:
- the potatoes side dish- these are the best potatoes I've ever had. They're fingerling potatoes semi mashed and cooked super crispy. So much flavor!
- Matzo ball soup: could easily feed two as an app- delicious broth and the matzo ball was awesome.
- Salmon Benedict- there's something different about salmon here- it's absolute fire and anything you order needs salmon on it. This Benedict was perfect, the hollandaise sauce was amazing, and the bread was toasted perfect.

What a great experience and I would def go back.

Order the salmon Benedict, matzo ball soup, and most of all the potatoes side dish.

Food was amazing. The service is sooo good. The workers check up on you and make sure to apologize for any mistake they made- ( if they even make one). Such a great place but make sure to make a reservation! Highly recommend.

Simple an Slique - "Sadelle's" review 
SoHo, a very trendy, chic area in New York City where you will find some of New York's busiest eateries. Sadelle's is one such place. It's very reminiscent of a Jewish eatery except for this institution serves what I believe is "pork" bacon. Upon arriving, I noticed a few people standing and sitting outside.  I walk in and felt like I traveled back in time to an old-fashioned ice cream shop. The small tables and chairs, the waiters, and the openness just took me back in time. I was excited. It was crowded and quite busy, but the waiters were artfully dodging each other and the customers, while holding large platters of food in the air. I could not help but love the atmosphere of this place...the exposed brick, high ceilings, tasteful art pieces, and sky lights that ran the length of the restaurant were lovely. As per usual my server pours my water, and coffee immediately, while I dissect the menu. I ordered two medium fried eggs with a side of white fish salad, and per the menu their "famous sticky buns". When my meal arrived, it was presented beautifully. The tower of food was visually pleasing. However, the eggs were not "medium", but instead quite runny, more so than I like.  As for the "famous sticky buns", they were tiny, and tasted store bought with butter melted on top. The whitefish salad was very tasty and when paired with the homemade bagel, superb!
The service, and the atmosphere was very nice. And honestly the experience, was not that bad, but the BEST part... the music I dined to was "Sara Smile" by Hall and Oates!  I would give the meal a 6 out of 10.

Probably the best brunch you will have!  The smoked fish is perfect, the tuna salad delicious and the grilled cheese and French toast off the charts!  Everything is so fresh.  Tough to get in but worth it!

Hands down best french toast in the city. It was literally dripping when I cut into it-- so moist and incredibly delicious. Also tried the "famous sticky buns" which were good, but not even near the caliber of the French toast. The ambience is lively and colorful, although it does get quite busy, so I'd say go as early in the morning as possible for breakfast. And definitely for the French toast
I just had the best tuna melt in my entire life. The bagels are hand rolled every day and the service is amazing. Would recommend for anyone who is looking for a great meal in soho!

This was such a fun brunch experience! The ambiance and decor in the space invited you in and envied all of the finishing touches. We did the platter and honestly would recommend it if you have at-least 3-4 guests. Only thing I wish we would've skipped on was the whitefish (extremely fishy). Perhaps they could bring out small samples of each to try before you settle on your selection of 6 fishes/salads. Bagels were amazing and they have gluten free as well.

French Toast is the best i ever had! 
White Fish incredible

lox and bagels are small but good. Russ and Daughters and barney green grass lox are better.
Quality equal to Russ & Daughters.  May possibly be better.  Tried the house and the Scottish.  House was better tasting. Bagels were sort of on the small side.

Really disappointed. Came here for brunch with my friend who is celiac and cannot eat anything containing gluten at all. The menu posted online AND in person has gluten free bagels. When my friend ordered a gluten free bagel our server told us they no longer have gluten free bagels. Not sure why the haven't updated any menus or posted that information anywhere, as gluten in a very common allergy.

I just love Sadelle's and I'm so happy to see them open again after closing during the first 6 months of Covid. I'd love to venture into trying more of the menu If I can stop myself from ordering the bagels and lox platter- which is so good that it's difficult to take that chance.

First time coming to sadelles and we will definitely be back! 
Nyc coquito for the holidays was amazing! French toast for me and everything bagel with chive cream cheese and Salmon for my husband! Plenty of space and very clean with great service! We loved the food!
great bagels and smoked salmon. it was difficult to make a reservation. always busy. their seating was comfortable and warm enough

Even though Sadelle's review on Yelp isn't a four and above, I wanted to give Sadelle a try as it's an iconic brunch location. It's also by Major Food Group, so I was even more excited. It did not disappont! The smoked fish is a must try and the setup is instagram-worthy, which is another bonus. It was so flavorful and we wish we got more. We also got the egg sandwich, which was also very good. 

Reservations were difficult to get, but we did walk-in and waited around 45 minutes. The covid setting is ok as the seating in the patio was a little crowded.
Overpriced overall brunch for a salty everything bagel, regular fried eggs and $8 for half an avocado. Cocktails and blueberry pancakes were alright - nothing special.

Went for Saturday brunch. Their outdoor setting is just okay, both the sidewalk and patio are a bit crowded. The food is good. I went for the house salmon and it came on a tower with tomatoes, cucumbers and a bagel of choice. The bagel is for sure smaller than most New York bagel shops but nevertheless tasty and imo quite filling given the other items that it came with. The side order of breakfast potatoes was surprisingly good. They are smashed and roasted to crispy with caramelized onions. 

Our waiter strongly recommended the french toast, which is fried and is crispy on the outside with a bread pudding like interior. The first few bites were really good coz I've never had anything like that before. But several bites in I felt a little overwhelmed: too rich, too much butter, too big. Two of us weren't able to finish it.

Sadelles is a very fun brunch spot! I ordered the scottish salmon platter and adored it! The salmons is very thinly sliced and was a wonderful flavor! The server recommended the french toast but unfortunately I didn't like it at all. Compared to the photos I've seen of the french toast on yelp, mine was burned. Regardless, I think the scottish salmon is worth it and will be coming back my next time i'm in New York!

Even during COVID, this place is absolutely magical and the experience was phenomenal. Everything from the coffee to the service and recommendations from the team were spot on. We went with the top specials which were the Leo omelette and spicy chicken sandwich. The pictures speak for itself. What is most phenomenal about this place was the French toast, perfect to share as the last bite. It was made to perfection, I can't wait to go back.

Despite the freezing cold weather, my friend and I sat in the winter patio at 9am. The waitstaff were extremely friendly, and immediately offered hot water, which was just what was needed. 

We ordered the house salmon, two bagels and the soho omelette. When the omelette was served, the smell wafted around so fast and it was so hard not to dig in right away. Though a bit overpriced for bagels, I'd say it's worth a try at least once because it is still a delicious bagel with all that it comes with! 

The omelette was definitely my favorite, and I would recommend eating it quick before it gets cold.
I ordered delivery and this place is insanely good, as are all the MFG restaurants. Highly recommend the Greek salad, tuna melt, and smoked salmon bagel.
From the minute you walk into Sadelle's you feel a warm welcoming environment. The bagel tower is fantastic and the salmon is so fresh. I will be coming back!

Sadelle's is one of those spots that you see all over social media, try to make a reservation soo many times and fail, and think maybe you should just give up. I'm here to tell you not to - it really is that good and completely lives up to expectations. The lox is on another level from any that I have ever had. Their bagels are pretty standard New York bagels, but I love that they have gluten-free options (that were just as good!). I didn't try the salads but they also get a lot of praise; I'll definitely try them next time I can manage to grab a res!

Asked for a table and the bald host dude nudged his minion only to tell me that they were closing. Didn't have the courtesy to tell me himself. 

Then a pregnant lady asked to go inside to use the bathroom and the same big bald dude said no, patrons only. Dude, she's clearly pregnant and just wanted to use your facilities. It's not a big deal. Humanity at its worst. 

Place is terrible. Never would dine here and if you had some decency and respect, you won't either.
one of my fav brunch spots in the city! order the lox tower and the pancakes... so so good!

Ate brunch here over the holiday weekend. For a more "upscale" restaurant you would think they'd put a little effort into their outdoor seating set up besides just tables plopped on the sidewalk but that was fine. Once we sat down, it took us about 30 minutes to get our waiters attention to order drinks then another 20 to order food. Our food came before our drinks which was a little annoying but the worst part was that there was a hair in our smoked salmon! We showed the waiter who didn't really react. He brought us a new one but did not comp it from our bill, which was rather disappointing. They also charge $2 extra per (TINY) gluten free bagel which should have been told to us before ordering. The food itself was delicious (minus the hair) but for the amount they're charging, I was expecting better.

Incredibly overpriced and underwhelming food. Had the healthy egg sandwich which was super small, on burnt toast, and probably the greasiest thing I have ever eaten. My friend had the avocado toast which was a VERY small piece of toast with just an avocado and some chili's on top - nothing special. Somehow all this came to $60. Not only that but the service was very slow and lackluster. I would definitely avoid.

The staff at this restaurant is amazing. We were a walk in and were able to get in right away. We started with the pig in the blanket and it was soooo delicious. For my breakfast, I had the eggs and potatoes. Everything was super fresh and flavorful. I love the food, staff and the overal decor! We will be back!

Finally Sadelle's offers delivery! I am such a huge brunch person and Sadelle's really is the best. The omelette's are exceptional. Even the bagel and lox is just perfect which is impressive for a place that does not specialize in bagels. Every experience dining in (less the crowd) and take out is consistently fresh and delicious. If you haven't tried I highly recommend but be prepared to get hooked. Every out of town guest I bring raves about it. It truly is the quintessential New York breakfast/brunch experience.

Sadelle's is very posh to say the least. It's almost a prerequisite to arrive in your best (leisurely) outfit, hang out at an outside table and have your phone ready like a gun at the OK corral showdown to make sure you snap the best looking pics of your salmon seafood tower (without actually eating it). The food is solid, terribly overpriced (it is SoHo after all), service is fine, but it's really about saying you ate at Sadelle's and proving it by posting your photos on IG than anything else. Ah the life of a Manhattanite. It never goes out of style.

My friend and I went here today for our 2:45 reservation. I got there at 2:40 and the hostess was so incredibly rude and told me I had to know exactly what my friend and I were ordering before we sit down because the kitchen was about to close. I told her I was going to wait the 5 minutes for my friend to get there (we weren't even seated yet). Then we sit down and we get handed a menu with 5 items on it. I ask to see the actual menu and the waiter told me they're kitchen is closing so this is their limited menu and we missed the actual menu by 30 minutes. When I told him no where on their website does it say this he said "yea, I know, we're going through some changes". The table next to us was seated 5 minutes prior to us and they were given the actual menu.

Because of every part of how this whole situation went down I will not be going back.

Bummed, planned to bring my fam here for a special occasion only to find that they do not have a full (or even realistic) menu after 3pm! This information is not included on Resy and we were totally bummed.

Was bot aware of the fact that they don't serve bagels and salmon and other bagel menus,

I ordered 
-pig in a blanket
-salmon
-their burger 
-drinks
=$100. Something 

It was overall overpriced and just normal,
Nothing special about their taste in food

The employees are okay, not friendly nor rude

Delicious food - healthy servings and fun decor. The Everything Bagel was "everything" you would a bagel to be - baked to perfection. You will want to add this spot to your list of places to visit while in New York.

Absolutely loved this place! The service was phenomenal - our waiter was so nice and sweet. He was very attentive and always checked in on us. He recommended great drinks - the Tommy pineapple & salty dog grapefruit drink! I loved both of them. We weren't that hungry since we had eaten a couple hours before but we got a salmon lox and an onion bagel. The salmon lox was so fresh and tasted amazing! The onion bagel was perfect too. I will definitely be coming back here.
Also make sure to make reservations! We made reservations for Friday 4 days in advance!

I don't even know where to begin with this review. It was one of the worst experiences I had with a hostess in my life as a born and raised New Yorker. I had come to Sadelle's with my husband to treat my friend from out of town to lunch. We arrived at Sadelles and asked for an outdoors table at 11:30.  I was told I had to wait 1 hour for a table. There were SIX 2 tops available outdoors during the time I was waiting. Knowing that my friend came all the way from San Francisco to eat at Sadelles - I thought I would take my chances because there were so many tables available. 

**These tables remained open for an hour** past any time a reservation would hold the seats- and the woman hostess would not seat me. I was the only patron waiting. 

Even the waiter asked if I wanted a seat and wondered why I was waiting. He even approached the woman and she said "I told her 1 hour." She didn't even ask if I wanted to be sat indoors. I explained that I was hoping to be seated because I was a new mom and had to rush back ASAP to nurse my infant daughter. This did not phase her at all. She snuffed at me. She didn't even give a reason for the 1 hour wait. I just had to wait it. 

She proceeded to seat other walk ins as they came in - indoors/outdoors wherever. As I was the ONLY PERSON waiting at the door. That's when I realized what was going on. The treatment I was getting was specifically for me. When she realized I saw what was happening - she then told me to please move over away from the restaurant and not wait by the door and please wait away from the restaurant. She literally used a hand motion to shoo me away, like I was some fly or gnat. Mind you, the restaurant was still pretty open and my husband and friend were down the block by the antiques store. I was the only person waiting at the restaurant during that time and by the banister, where (because I was eventually seated there and did not leave the restaurant for 3:45) EVERYONE HAD WAITED AT THE RESTAURANT FOR A TABLE NO PROBLEMS FROM HER. ONLY ME DID SHE SHOO AWAY. 

During my 1 hour wait, when other white patrons came in she sat walk ins immediately and gave them the option to sit indoors. She never offered me an option for indoors. I was kept waiting. The sun was oppressively hot but I waited - by the area where they kept empty tables and chairs outdoors.

After I waited my arbitrary 1 hour as I watched empty tables stay empty, she basically points at the table and rolled her eyes - acted pretty immature.  My husband, friend and I were aghast at her behavior. 

About 50 minutes later - a white woman came in and asked for a party of 6. They moved all the empty tables I was watching, and allowed her to comfortably wait at her table even though her party had not arrived yet. I watched as she sat there  treated much differently than my party was. Generally, parties are not seated until everyone has arrived. There is a reason for this. So that people like me aren't waiting. However, maybe it's different because I'm Asian. Who knows. 

Then and only then - were my friends and I able to be seated. I was seated AFTER ONE HOUR. (To add insult to injury) Even though there were empty tables outside for the entire duration of my wait, another woman was able to languish and I was basically the only person to have to wait ONE HOUR because of some axe the hostess had to grind the moment I walked in. I watched as that woman sat at her 6 top table comfortably. Her entire party only arrived around 1:30-1:45. 

How do I know this? 

I sat at the four top directly in front of the hostess station, and it was hard not to notice how she treated people differently than me.

We were not able to done with our meal at the restaurant until 3:45, that's four hours!!!!!! Our lunch cost $350. I wouldn't have waited if my friend from San Fran didn't want to stay. In fact, having been a loyal customer of the restaurant from the beginning - I am never going back to Sadelles again. Their food (and clearly service) has also gone downhill since prior to the pandemic. They made mistakes with our order. They also do not serve 2.0 bagels anymore. The fish and everything was overly salty. 

I have never encountered a more rude hostess in my life. Who treated me as if I didn't deserve to have a seat at this restaurant. Even when other waiters tried to seat me. They also looked confused as to why I wasn't offered a seat. I had never seen/met/talked to this woman in my life - but I felt it was because I was Asian. 

I will say the waiters were great. The server that tried to seat me at 11:50- but the hostess wouldn't let him - is an angel. Our eventual server was great. The food was not as good as it used to be and the hostess, quite frankly, should be fired. 

I tried to call someone at Major Foods to tell them about this - but its nearly impossible to get anyone on the phone if you have ever tried to do so.

Everything I ordered was amazing. I'd say that I over did it with the latkes and they were closer to hash browns versus latkes. When I do revisit, I'll be sure to just stick with the side of potatoes that comes with the breakfast which were divine. The service was also quick and efficient, our waiter was kind and attentive. The interior was inviting and clean, they could use a dusting but nonetheless, everything was perfect.

food is good, service is good. some items on the menu are better than others. 

we ordered:
-cold brew w oat milk
-french toast
-omelette (made my own)
-side of avocado
-everything bagels (toasted, of course)
-smoked salmon
-cream cheese and scallion (chive) cream cheese

our favorites were the bagels and the toppings of course, my friends enjoyed the smoked salmon and i had my everything bagel with chive cream cheese, avocado, and tomato. we would agree that the bagels, although good, were not the best bagels in new york or anything spectacular. the omelette was fine, not good but not bad. we did really like the french toast, but we were pretty full and unable to finish it- it is a great dish for the table to share. the inside of the french toast is soft, kind of like a flan texture, and crispy on the outside, with peach spread and syrup. 
we would also highly recommend the cold brew. 

we reserved the AMEX patio and sat outdoors. pretty hot out, even with the umbrellas over us. service was prompt, friendly, our waiter knew what he was talking about. may come back!

What a charming place! We came on a recommendation of a family member. I saw the poor reviews and was concerned. 
We did have a reservation through Resy, we were seated promptly outside and the service was quick and thoughtful. Never an empty cup. 
The food was simply delicious! Everything we ordered was warm and fresh. 
We were very comfortable and saw zero issues.

Ok so this place gets ALL the hype. The bagels are OK at best. Coffee is below average for NYC standards. We ordered the typical lox tower and the salmon was EXTREMELY fishy. To the point where we were worried to eat it. The bacon gets it up to two stars. The potatoes were bland and overall we were extremely underwhelmed. If your looking for an NYC staple bagel this isn't the place with so many options. Don't believe the hype.

Thanks for making my 78 year old mother stand outside in the raging heat because you wouldn't seat her five minutes or less before the remaining group arrived.... On time.... With room for an elderly women to sit. Then proceeded to give major eye roll and attitude after we got there.  We gave no attitude and my mother is the nicest. With a table reserved there was no reason to make her stand outside and to her off to the side of the restaurant like a beggar. ( This hostess is clearly aggressive and rude. ) Get a new hostess, sadelle's.  It's 2021. The hostess attitude era of manhattan is way past.  Your front door staff are grumpy and clearly hate their job.

Loved it! We had the smoke Scottish salmon tower and ingredients were really fresh. The bagels are made in house so they were awesome.
The waiter recommended pigs in a blanket which they were like croissant wrapped sausage like. Really really good.
And for dessert we had shared French toasts. Honestly they were the BEST French toast I've ever eaten. Everything was perfect and on point. I just added a little syrup and that's it.

This place blew my face off. Was visiting from San Francisco and came here early on a Saturday morning, which was great as we avoided any lines and wait times. Staff was very friendly and attentive throughout our brunch.

As a long time doubter of lox bagels in general, this place completely 180'ed my view of what a lox bagel can be. We ordered the house salmon with an "everything" bagel and also shared the latke royale. Bottom line, I'll be dreaming of this breakfast for a very long time. Definitely recommend giving this place a try. Read through some of the lower ratings and most seemed to discuss long wait times. If this is something that bothers you, do yourself a favor and come early - it worked out for me and I only have positive things to say about this dining experience. 

Look forward to coming back again (hopefully) soon!

After telling our kids that we thought Sadelle's was just OK for egg white omelettes and that $75 was ridiculously expensive for 2 omelettes and 2 regular coffees, they laughed. It seems people go to Sadelles for the bagels not omelettes. I guess we ordered the wrong thing. In any case their prices were over the top for omelettes. If we ever go back, we will have the bagel with nova platter.

Literally just walked out of Sadelle's. We live in a tough time and everyplace is short-staffed, but when they charge you $180 for a meal where your omelettes are cold, your orange juice is warm, your coffee is luke warm, it takes an hour to get your food, and they don't even ask how things are, you feel fully ripped off. We wanted to splurge a little and get the caviar - $80 and it was ABSURDLY small and the latke it came on was crazy greasy. They also charge an extra 3% to cover Covid expenses (even though their prices are absurd for what you get). it's horrible to walk out of a meal you were excited for and feel like you were taken advantage of. Also the host was not friendly AT ALL. In fact he seemed angry to have to show us our table.
The everything bagel with chive cream cheese was the BEST bagel I have EVER had!!! We had to wait 30 minutes but just walked around and it was definitely worth it!!

Stopped in to grab a bagel and a coffee... being that I was the only one in line I was hoping for a quick visit. I was instructed to wait by the high chair and.. (some mumbling). After waiting for about five minutes, and confirming that I can longer fit in a high chair, I interpreted the delay as the universe telling me that I've had enough bagels, and upon some reflection, maybe that's what the hostess mumbled. 

3 stars because they were busy with dine in, the hostess was pleasant, and the universe and her are both probably right. 

I'll be back
Terrible host, terrible hospitality.. food is so so. highly unrecommended. You want a great brunch few blocks down the road? Balthazar.. classic with amazing service.

Sadelle's is definitely one of the most popular brunch spots in NYC and the wait is always so bad. Luckily, we only wait 30 mins for a table for two on a rainy Sunday noon. 

The decor is elegant, authentic and good for Instagram photos. The ambiance was chill, their service was friendly and it's overall a cozy place for brunch. 

The options on menu weren't various and we had their signature Bagel Tower & French Toast from friend's recommendation. The Bagels were decent but not the best bagel in NYC. 

Our favorite was the French Toast and it's one of the best we have ever had. It was extremely satisfying since it melted in our mouth immediately with soft texture. It really made our day!
Overpriced bagels and lox. The ONLY reason you should be going here is for the incredible French toast. Everything else can be found better elsewhere in NYC

Sadelle's is an adorable little bakery with the cutest ambiance! I was not a fan of the Bellini drink I ordered as it had too much lemon and was looking for more of a peach flavor. The food itself was wonderful, I am a big fan of lox and they had a tower set up with our choice of bagel and toppings. We also ordered latkes to share and these may be some of the best latkes I've had - we topped it off with apple sauce and sour cream. I would highly recommend stopping by here on your next trip to New York!

We were visiting our daughter from out of town.
She did good job of finding this great place.
Everything was great! Food presentation was great, food tasted great, the server was awesome and helpful.
Only thing put "bad taste" in our mouth was the hostess. She had some "attitude".
We don't know what her deal was.
The hostess should be friendly, inviting, welcoming...with a smile! 
That's her job.
She needs to REALLY think about her role and what kind of impression she gives to the customers coming through the door!!
Someone in management should do some coaching about tuber attitude.

Was lucky to snag a table for 2 on a beautiful
Sunday during prime time!  We had the house salmon and whitefish with onion bagel and gluten free bagel. My whitefish salad had chunks of fish if you like that, I prefer more chopped whitefish in my salad and alittle bit on the salty side.  The house salmon was very fresh and delicious.  We are used to a little larger bagel but the bagels served here are good for
Portion control.  Service is main reason I would come back, friendly and personally staff all around.  Definitely recommend.

Good service; everything indoor was spaced out pretty well which made us feel comfortable. There was a slight 15 minute wait despite us having reservations, but that didn't bother us. 

Indoor ambiance is nice. Given how the outdoor seating was so close to pedestrians walking by, we decided to sit indoors. They have large open doors which was pretty reassuring. 

We ordered the smoked scottish salmon and the salmon benedict. The bagels were a bit burnt on the ends for our taste. The egg with our benedict was also a bit too well-done, so I would recommend requesting for it to be a bit runnier if that's something you'd prefer. 

We had a good experience that was ultimately held back by portion sizes that did not justify the price tag. But why should I be surprised, we're in SoHo after all.

Best bagels, cream cheese, and fine fish. I wondered how it would go. But it exceeded my expectations. The fish is delicate and delicious. By the way, the French toast is from another universe: bread soaked in custard overnight; then dredged in sugar; the deep fried. Yep.

After a 30 mile sunrise bike ride we decided to come here. It was a beautiful Saturday, group of 5, brunch time and it was crowded. Apparently they're a staple in soho and we found out why. First thing that catches my eye is the guy preparing the fresh salmon of the day at this little nook when you walk in. The ambience is a modern rustic type vibe, which was cool and inviting. Now to the food...

Our server Jeff was top tier. Efficient, knowledgeable and friendly. 

I decided to get the Salmon Benedict with a side of bacon. The Benedict was a winner. It was filling and the bread was melt in your mouth satisfying. Bacon was MEHHHH nothing to brag about. However, my friend did get the sausage and it was AMAZING. So sausage over the bacon for sure (and if I'm not mistaken he said they make the sausage there). Also wasn't a big fan of the breakfast potatoes. With that being said I was able to fork a little of my friends hash brown side served with a sweet sauce (could of been apple) nonetheless it was amazing. Overall, it was pretty good...would I go back hmmmm maybe.

If you love bagels, you have come to the right place!! The bagels are really good and the fish was really fresh too. Overall it's an amazing brunch spot, a little pricy for bagels but we thought everything was really good!! Definitely coming back for more.
Food is good, but only go if you are willing to pay ton of money for what you get.   For example,  a single toasted everything bagel with cream cheese to go is $23 with tax and tip.

I would concur that this place is not worth the hype. I can for a mid afternoon reservation with a friend and split an order of the house salmon and a cup of tea. A nice presentation, but an average tasting bagel with lox. The most ridiculous part of my meal though was getting the bill and seeing that our single cup of tea (just bagged tea) was $7! That's robbery even in new york!!
the house salmon with everything bagel was amazing! the cream cheese is super light and whipped! Very cheap for the quality and taste:)

The food and service are good but we were left outside by the hostess for 20 minutes because we did not have a complete table. When we went inside the restaurant, there were many empty tables. Given I am nearly 60 and my wife is also, I think this is very unreasonable and the restaurant needs to change its policy on this to allow guests to come in when there is plenty of space and it's very cold outside

Food is always excellent but service has gone down dramatically. We could never get the attention of our waiter, even though we were dining at 9am with only one other table being served by her. Took forever to order and she was always just chatting with her other coworkers not doing anything at all and drinking their own coffee while we were waiting. Very poor service and will likely not return for a while

Sadelle's has one of the best lox bagels I've ever tried. We ordered the house salmon that came with an everything bagel base, tangy cream cheese, fresh cucumber, tomatoes, dill and capers! Their housemate bagels are nicely flavored and baked to a chewy crackle. Besides the house salmon, we also got the blueberry pancakes, one of their specialties. The big stack of fluffy pancakes are butter-soaked and served with warm syrup on the side. Though it's a basic dish, Sadelle's manage to make them so well

After our dining experience, I finally understand the long wait time and will most definitely come back when we visit New York again!

I hate that I loved Sadelle's soooooo much!!! Your bill can make your eyes pop out of your head (as other Yelpers have said) but it's worth a visit!! 

Space: The space is beautiful!! There are beautiful chandeliers that hang from the ceilings, not something you see everyday when you go out to brunch! Seating arrangements vary, from booths on the side to a whole dinner table that could seat 8 people right in the middle of the floor, to smaller tables for 2-4 people. There's a section in the back that's elevated with a couple of stairs. There's another floor that's actually considered the "UPSTAIRS", although I couldn't see how much seating they had. 

Atmosphere: MAKE RESERVATIONS. We came at 12:15 on a Monday and the place was PACKED. I was a little annoyed at first because our server tucked us away in a back corner RIGHT next to another table, even though the rest of the row was empty! It's like the equivalent of sitting next to someone on the train when the rest of the train is empty! BUT within 10 minutes of sitting down, all the seats around us were filled... so, make reservations!! 

The food: We didn't get the salmon tower that everyone has pictures of but warning: it's way smaller than the pictures actually show on yelp! In fact, the bagels are like mini bagels, the size of my palm, and I have pretty small hands to begin with! No wonder why they gave 3 bagels per serving! 

I ordered a salmon benedict and my friend got the french toast with bacon on the side. Both dishes were immaculate. The french toast was the biggest french toast I've ever seen! It's perfectly crispy on the outside and perfectly fluffy on the inside! Syrup and blueberry jam is served in a tiny cute metal cup. The salmon benedict did end up filling me up even though the bagels were tiny. They ran out of the bread they originally use for benedicts (challah? I couldn't really hear her) so I opted for an onion bagel. It was still delicious! The salmon just melts in your mouth! I will say though, if you order the same thing, be ready for it to be super small lol 

Our server was attentive and kept refilling our water without us asking. I also loved that they didn't clear our tables right away or rush us. There's pictures on Yelp of workers cutting the salmon but when we went the counter was empty :( not sure if they stopped because of COVID or if they just open the counter on certain days??

A must go to if you're visiting NYC or a local!
beautiful place had reservations, but server was not very fast to greet us And finally took order not very friendly, and 45 minutes waiting for food.   after lunch too at 2pm.

I met a friend of mine for brunch at Sadelle's before we headed to the Brooklyn Museum for the Christian Dior exhibit (go see it!!).  You definitely need to make reservations as the restaurant was packed at 10:30 am on a Thursday.  We ordered the cheese blintzes, salmon benedict, Greek salad and my friend also got an everything bagel.  The Greek salad is huge.  Probably enough for 4 people! Everything was delicious!

The best lox bagel I have EVER had. The drinks were also really delicious and the service was great. It's expensive but worth it in my opinion. MFG consistently serves up tasty food and good vibes. Check it out for a fun brunch experience with friends

Went for brunch and the bagels and all spreads are so good. But we had to wait when we had a reservation which was a little annoying and the spacing between tables is very close making it a little uncomfortable. But besides that service and food are very good. Highly recommend and if you can get a reservation please go.

Not the best bagels I've had and also very pricey but if you're looking for a place with good ambiance and a cool vibe - this is a place to go. Def a good spot to bring friends or family who are visiting for brunch. I was able to walk-in and be seated within 35 mins on a late Saturday afternoon, but I'd definitely recommend making reservations as it's always pretty busy. 

There is a gluten free bagel option which I was very happy about, but it was really small and kinda hard. I got the Smoked Scottish tower which was yummy and the Salmon Benedict was *chef's kiss*! I'd also recommend getting the breakfast potatoes. All in all, I'm happy I checked this off my NY food list and you should to!

OVERHYPED. The french toast was definitely a highlight but this place is way too expensive for the portions. You can find better bagels in NYC elsewhere, but I would say the ambiance is great. I would say the atmosphere is perfect to bring your family or girlfriends. Service was good and the staff greeted us really nicely!

This has it all: the ambience is old world. You can watch masters carve beautiful smoked salmon. You can watch the bakers make bagels from scratch. All the while you're feasting on a tower of impeccable fresh smoked salmon varieties, cucumber, tomatoes, capers, onion, and of course amazing bagels. A must visit.

I wasn't sure about going here because of the menu & the popular dishes, but omg the food here was absolutely AMAZING! We didn't have any reservations so we walked-in but luckily the hostess was able to seat us at a table if we finished within 1 hour.

The French toast is absolutely HUGE, but it was super crispy on the outside and soft in the inside. My friend and I were both surprised at how delicious the French toast was and wondering how they had it crispy on the outside but eggy on the inside. The eggs benedict seems like any normal benedict, but the bread that they use was phenomenal! You can tell it's housemade (they make their bagels in house too!). Finally, the latkes reminded me of a hash brown and it was very crispy. I like the sauce that comes with it too.

I would definitely come back here again if I'm ever in the area. My friend even said this is a place she would bring her parents to when they visit New York! It was THAT good!

one of my favorite restaurants in the city! i came here for brunch the other day with a friend and we split the avocado benedict, french toast, and house salmon. everything was soooo delicious!
avocado benedict - the eggs were perfectly poached and the flavor was incredible!
french toast - i usually don't love french toast but i would eat this all day every day if i could! the toast is so thick, perfectly crunchy on the outside, and soft and fluffy on the inside. it was the perfect amount for 2!
house salmon - this comes as a little salmon tower. the salmon is on the top and was unbelievably delicious! the next plate is tomato, cucumber, and capers which were all perfect. 
then the bottom plate is the bagel - we got two everything bagels so we could each have one! the bagels are amazing and so fresh. 
highly highly recommend all of the above! cant wait to go back and try more!!
If you're looking for a nicer breakfast/brunch place to spend a while at, this is definitely the place to go! The smoked salmon and the bloody mary were definitely the stars of the show.
Over priced and over rated. I had the house salmon tower and it was honestly the worst bagel I've ever had. Save you're money go some where else

honestly was skeptical because I had heard so many mixed reviews but sadelle's was fantastic! 

The service was so attentive and the food was honestly so good. I got the smoke scottish salmon on the everything bagel and everything on the plates were fresh and so tasty. The only complaint I had was the coffee - it tasted just like water, but they gave me a great tea instead.

The food is very expensive and does not worth the payment even tho the dishes are very big. we actually could share those because every one of us eat barely half of the dish. Although the expensive prices they not give change for cash and doesn't have even paper for receipt. Eventually we really not recommend.

Upon arrival, no one acknowledged our presence. I literally waited for the hostess to stop joking with their co worker to get her attention. The hostess is the most unprofessional person I have ever encountered in a restaurant. I honestly wish you guys would step up with the customer service. How do you tell a customer "just because I said it's an hour and a half, doesn't mean it's going to be an hour and a half.. it could be more than that. We didn't know all the reservations were going to show up."
Delicious food , very good service. Would def come back again . I recommend this place.

Dear Sadelles,
I love you, I love you, I love you. The salad doesn't disappoint, but don't even get me started on the egg salad...Pure perfection. I wish I could love my husband as much as I love Sadelles.

I completely understand the hype now. This spot lives up to all that you've heard and then some. The food is outstanding, the service is just attentive enough and I can't think of a better place to get brunch than Sadelle's -- especially if you have a deep love for lox and bagels.

My friend secured the reservation awhile back, and we attempted to be seated earlier (we were in the area, 30 mins prior to our resy), but they told us it'll be close to our original reservation time. We window shopped and it was just 15 mins later that we got a text saying our table was ready. 

We ordered the house salmon, tuna melt and the french toast. The house salmon and everything bagel was INSANELY DELICIOUS. The tuna melt? Best thing I've ever eaten in a really long time. As for the french toast -- yes, it's good, but I think the other two dishes were far more outstanding. Oh, and we also had mimosa's, because you know, brunch.

The bagels are also slightly different here. You're not getting that super dense NY-style bagel. Instead, the everything bagel was pillowy and thinner, but it works. Trust me. 

Must. Return. ASAP.

I am so thrilled we were able to get out door seating for my friends birthday brunch last minute! The staff was so kind and welcoming! The food was beyond delicious, I honestly can't remember the price but I don't care that's how good the experience was! I would definitely recommend checking this place out and booking reservations in advance so you can enjoy the inside of the restaurant!
Poor service and awful attitude from the staff. 100% do not recommend. Waited over an hour for a table to be told it wasn't ready and had to wait longer.

Omg amazing  the omelette w salmon n etc is great. It's very much replicable though. I literally made the same dish at home and it tasted the same. Very pricey, great taste, but their value solely rides on brand equity.

In the city with the entire family on spring break from Florida, including two kids, and this was recommended by some locals. Amazing. First the area is great to explore for something different and adventurous and can walk to wtc and other  tourist spots (Harry Potter store included). The restaurant itself is a great build, very cool spot. Service was wonderful, attentive, nailed the reservation time at greeting. Our server was very friendly and helpful considering we had kids, are Floridians, and walked us through the menu. We understand and expect nyc is more "business" but it was refreshing to get some southern kindness from a local. She gave us some pro tips on activities and very appreciative. The food- right on time and excellent. Wife had salmon and bagel set up and as their specialty the salmon was superb. Kids had French toast, devoured it and the other one had a basically big breakfast as did I. We ate as much as we could and raved. There are reasons people all over the world come to nyc for good food and this is one of them. Cannot get this experience at home.

Our waiter left the restaurant about halfway through our meal. I had to inform the maitre d' that our waiter had left, twice, because she had forgotten. They then started to avoid me, no effort was made. I had to beg for the bottle of champagne we ordered for the rest of the meal as no one was reassigned to our table. Sadelle's is walking distance from Russ & Daughters, so clearly I'm paying for the service, not the fish. There is no reason for me to return. 

P.S. You call those latkes?

Sadelle's is a super poppin brunch spot that gains a lot of fame from tiktok and insta. We got brunch reservations for 3 at 3p on a Sunday afternoon. 

What we ordered: we each just got a salmon and cream cheese bagel spread. The presentation is lovely and our server was so nice. It did take us forever to get drinks. We were done eating by the time we got them. (Not our server's fault. He was great!) The salmon + cream cheese + bagel was around $24. And was it worth that?.....I have had bagels that compared to this one for $6. 

Overall: it's a fun atmosphere and a good place to post for socials, but not worth the price imo.

Yes this place is worth the hype- we grabbed a resi a few weeks ago for brunch at 2pm on a Saturday. Place was packed as expected but service was really great! We ordered Paloma's/Mimosas to start - then ordered house salmon, tuna melt and the French toast. Prob the best 3 things - each of them really nailed it. Loved the salmon presentation, the tomato's/cucumber/caper/dill tower just makes it more fun. The tuna was delish and perfect to share and the French toast was really good! It's more like a bread pudding? It came with syrup and this delish jam, SO good. I'm so glad we went- service was so kind and they didn't rush us out at all. I'd love to go back and try the salads! Thanks for a great brunch!!!

I went here with my husband on a Sunday around 1p. We were able to be seated immediately without a reservation-- not sure if that was luck or not. 

We ordered a coffee, Tommy pineapple drink, latkes, house salmon and whitefish. Coffee tasted great but could have been hotter. My husband really enjoyed the Tommy pineapple drink. 

The latkes weren't too oily which I appreciated and everything came out in a timely fashion. They came with sour cream and applesauce. 

We both got the everything bagels-- they weren't the best bagels I've had in NY by any means, but you come here for the fish. Both the salmon and whitefish salad were delicious and fresh. 

The server was kind and attentive as well. We weren't rushed at all.
Loved brunch at Sadelle's!! You definitely need to get the bagel tower and also don't sleep on the latkes!!

What a terrible rip off. Over priced Mediocre food. Restaurant took a 4:45 reservation and kitchen closes at 5. Sitting eating your meal while restaurant is cleaning up to close. Really outrageous. Definitely would avoid this restaurant They re are many places to eat brunch in the city that are far superior
Omggg hands down the best pina coloda, burger and tuna melt. Never disappointed when we come here.

Excellent brunch spot that you have to try, if you're ever in the city. Food was impeccable and came out rather quick. Customer service was great and very attentive. It's usually packed, so I highly suggest always making a reservation. They have a lot of great menu items to choose from. I personally loved the tuna melt. Not something I get everyday, and it definitely lived up to its expectations.
Overpriced!!! Over $150 for 4 bagels with lox, the tiniest blinis you ever did see, and equally small latkes. An insult to the cuisine and to NYC tradition. Go to a real corner deli and skip this.

I don't understand the hype about this place. I arrived with a party of 4 for lunch on a Wednesday and was surprised at how crowded it was. We were seated promptly and the server took our order fairly quickly as well.

We then proceeded to wait 45 minutes for our appetizer and another 15 minutes for our entrees to come out, which was the salmon tower and 2 salads. I'm actually shocked as to why this tower was $125. Don't get me wrong, the smoked Scottish was good, but the slices are paper thin, and definitely was not enough for 4 people. They recommended us to get 2 towers but this pricing is absurd. The bagels were small, but flavorful.

Truthfully, I'd be much happier and more fulfilled getting a lox bagel from a bagel shop.

Going to Vegas is all about having a unique experience that you can only find in Vegas. But so much of that experience hinges on great service and attention to detail. Sadelle's delivers in spades - Cindy our server was attentive and polished. The good met all our expectations for a nice breakfast after a few too many cocktails the night before. Highly recommend and will come back as our go-to in Vegas for breakfast.

Sadelles is always shown on social media,..and since I was in SoHo for the weekend why not give it a try? Here is my review.

Food: 5/5
Got the sampler tower ( $125)  which has all the fish types: smoked salmon , sturgeon , white fish.. substituted lobster salad and egg salad. White fish salad was savory smoky ..lobster salad was the table favorite. 

Bagels came fresh n hot stacked on a stick. I noticed there is a bagel making station onsite. Probably the best bagels I had in NY so far..from oven to table.

Potato Latkas were crispy and savory addition . Highly recommend.

Drinks: 1/5
Mimosa : was not fresh orange juice and the champagne was non existent. Very bland drink. Was not served in champagne flutes. Not festive and was a strange missed detail considering every else at sadelles is top notch.
Vodka pineapple mandarin: also fell flat ..see my pic. Juices tastes like canned. Lackluster drink . 

Salad : TBD
Waldorf salad. Was not able to eat it..was very large portions ( enough for 2-3) and took it home instead. 

Interior : 5/5
Indoor seating wait was 1.5 hours .. outdoor seating - 2 hours. Cute exposed brick interior  Floral arrangements scattered around the space makes for perfect IG shots .

Covid : 3/5
Servers wear masks. Tables are really close but they blast the AC to get some air flow.  Opt for outdoor if you are playing it safe .
 
Tip: Expect to pay $$$ but this is Soho and well worth it if you're visiting or just wanna know what all the hype is about.

It was disappointing that their cups smell like eggs. It was grotesque to drink water here and worse that even when we got the cups replaced they smelled worse. Are they washing their dishes here? Yes of course. Are they using enough detergent or cleaning their washing machine periodically? Probably not. I expect more from a place that charges as much as they do. While the food is delicious it's a disappointing outcome to not enjoy the experience here.

Absolutely delicious. Their regular coffee was very tasty. We enjoyed their cocktails. The bloody Mary was especially good. We went for breakfast and had bagels with the smoked lox. Request scallion cream cheese, it's the best. The potato latkes were also really crisp. The staff is kind and knowledgeable too!

GET A RESERVATION. I knew they were going to be busy so I came at 8:45am (they open at 9am). Was told we need to wait for 20 minutes for a table.

Anyways, love how the fish comes with tomato, cucumber and bagels in a tower. Absolutely love the presentation - afternoon tea for breakfast! Haha

I got the house salmon and it was very good. The tomatoes and cucumbers were so fresh, and the bagels were perfect. 

You can also watch them make their bagels fresh. Very nice experience!

An adorable breakfast / brunch place in Soho. Most famous for their house made bagels and salmon, Sadelle's offered a good taste of the New York bagel and lox combo. I got the smoked salmon with an everything bagel to pair it with. The bagel was light, the fish was fresh, and the tomatoes, cucumbers, and capers were all fresh. Overall, will come again.

Taking a staycation in the big Apple and found Sadelle's for an absolutely scrumptious breakfast.  Unbelievably great food, selection and service.  

We will be back to sample the rest of this incredible menu.

Adorable, great food at a price you can stomach in SoHo! Sat outside in the nyc heat and humidity and it took our server over 20 minutes to come over and that was after we flagged someone down but it was great!
Love the vibes here. Perfect place for a quick breakfast in the morning. Got the omelette with mushrooms, onions, and bacon

I'd you're still coming here for the bagel tower, grow up - it's not 2015 anymore and the girlies aren't tossing back $23 mimosas at a major food group hospitality restaurant. However, just get a bagel to go it's pretty comparable to like a black seed I guess. If you sit down their egg options are great and so are the donuts. The service is also pretty good. The bathrooms are disgusting, don't bother using them because that hallway will make you feel sick when you're hungover. Other than that, they are pretty much just seating carbone outside to capitalize off girls coming in from Miami and LA wanting to spend $32 on spicy rigatoni, so things are just weird.

Consistently good fish spot and overall great breakfast.  
French toast and the salmon tower were great

Sadelle's located in Soho is definitely a bit of a "treat-yourself" brunch moment for me. I went with my friend to celebrate an upcoming birthday; he told me had to make the reservation quite a while in advance! We ordered the French Toast and the Smoked Scottish with Poppy and Everything bagels. Starting with the Bagel Sandwich, I love the presentation of the ingredients with everything on the stacked plate tower. I had so much fun putting all the ingredients on my bagel. I found the bagels to be delicious but nothing special. It tasted like it was supposed to taste and was nothing that surprised me. I remember really enjoying the chive cream cheese, the capers, and the everything bagel in particular! Then the French toast... this was so yummy! It was more like bread pudding with two massive slices of toast that were deep fried. It was slightly unappetizing to see the oil coming out of the toast but it was very delicious. The toast had a crunchy hard exterior but upon biting/cutting into the dish, it was very soft and pudding like. I really like the contrast of the textures. It was also served with a very fresh raspberry jelly and syrup. It was a very sweet and heavy dish but also not bad to have once in a while! I would come back to Sadelle's as a treat again!

My group and I had a wonderful time at Sadelles! We got a last minute reservation and we're so happy to finally be able to try it. We were seated promptly and served very quickly. The tower is a must have !! It came with house salmon, smoked salmon, sable, sturgeon, whitefish salad, and smoked salmon salad as well as many tomatoes and cucumbers to add to the endless bagel supply! Everything tasted so fresh and delicious. They truly use quality fish. This was more than enough for 4 people and we even took some home. I highly recommend going with a large group to share all the high quality fish!
Yes to towers of food! Really great brunch here at Sadelle's. Friendly service and high towers!

I finally bought a pound of their house salmon, salt and pepper bagels and cream cheese.  I asked for chive cream cheese but came home with plain.

But I love their house salmon which is really like gravlax.  I used to make it but now I just buy it from them.  They cut them super thin.  Beautiful slices!

I miss their cinnamon buns.  Wish they still have them.

I have been back every week to get the house salmon.

Our group lucked out with a last minute reservation and we're so excited to start our day here. The bagel tower is a must and comes with your choice of a bagel and fish and also cucumber tomato and capers. We also ordered the famous French toast which is about 3 inches thick and worth every calorie! I highly recommend and will definitely be back!

The Highlights- trendy brunch, strong cocktails

Reservations Highly Recommended. Sadelle's Soho is that girl and she knows it. Brunch is always booked weeks in advance and a lengthy wait for walk-in's. 

Mimosa's were an 80/20 mix (iykyk) - solid start. I ordered the Soho Omelette (4/5) and a side of sausage (5/5), both were great. Breakfast potatoes were a miss but the Crispy Latkes were such a hit they didn't get a photo op- would recommend. 

Overall Experience- Positive. Sadelle's has locations in other major cities throughout the country that I'll definitely visit going forward.

We received outstanding service today. We went to Sadelle's for our anniversary had a lovely cozy booth. We had the coffee cocktail which had lovely hints of coconut along with their signature breakfasts (fish breakfast and leo breakfast). You won't leave hungry, as the portions are deceivingly large. 

Thank you to Luc and Cindy for creating a warm and welcoming experience. We will be back again soon!

The only disappointment was the fact they aren't selling their coffee cups atm due to a shortage, but otherwise everything else was top notch.

Ambiance is nice. Would not recommend the French toast unless you're okay with eating soggy bread. The middle is soaked with the mixture and doesn't get cooked. When I told the wait staff, they said that it's because of the batter and it's meant to stay soft, mushy was more like it. I can't comment on the other food but presentation looked nice.

Really loved it here. Great atmosphere and cute location- definitely worth the hype. Had the lox tower, Cobb salad, French toast, drinks, & potatoes. We went for four people and had the perfect Amt of food- for the tower we did 2 spreads and gas 3 small sides. There lox and drinks were delicious- really enjoy this place

First of all, you know this place is great when you see celebrities walk in... so definitely get a reservation! 

The food was amazing, my favorites were the everything bagel, lobster salad, and the latkes. You can smell them making fresh bagels when you walk in - it's glorious. The drinks are delicious and strong and all the ingredients taste super fresh. 

We would definitely come back, my only issue is when our server suddenly disappeared for about an hour. We never got our side of pickles and we put emphasis on how we really wanted to try them when we ordered them. We had to flag down other servers during that time and still never got our pickles. Womp womp :/ Food and drinks were still too delicious for me to knock off any more stars despite that mishap.
Great service. Delicious salmon and bagels. Salad was bomb. Great ambience too. Will go again with friends and fam
Biggest portion sizes ever! Reservations recommended. Great service! World class food! Great brunch menu. Dog friendly outside! Strongly recommend

my server was AMAZING !! 
He was so helpful, attentive & sweet!

love the Lox, the French toast & the pigs in a blanket ..

Lox is served w yr choice of bagel, tomatoes cucumbers & capers.. i always ask for No Olive Oil as it usually comes doused & drenched in it..  

The French Toast was some of best I've Evr !! Had.
So toasted & crispy on the outside and the inside was soft & soaked up the delicious maple syrup ..

Pigs in A Blanket were so so Delicous !! 
The sausage was so flavorful & juicy 
& the bread was perfect & buttery and so Yum!!

definitely recommend ordering 

while you can def pass on the pickles .. v mediocre !!

Okay definitely overhyped and overpriced. 
A bagel with smoked Scottish, cream cheese, tomatoes and cucumbers was $24. Everything tasted good but I cannot say this was worth the money. You can get this for like half the price and it'll still be good. The pigs in a blanket were good but literally nothing special. The French toast is apparently famous but it was too sweet for my taste and very mushy in the middle. 
The service was good and the restaurant was pretty but, honestly, save your money and the headache of getting a table.
Sadelles is such a great brunch location. Reservations are highly encouraged. The location is clean and the staff is friendly. The food was delicious.

Love this place! The French toast was so light and airy( a bit greasy though,  but delicious nonetheless) I can not wait to return to order it again. The Jam they serve on the side  is amazing too. We also ordered the tuna which was luscious and the egg sandwich, fabulous! I need to try the blintzes and pancakes... why would anyone order the salads! Lol. I'm sure they're  great.

We are visiting New York and we were looking for a place to eat breakfast, this place is awesome the service was great, food was delicious and the place is packed so get your reservation before you come.

Best French toast!!! It's thick, crispy on the outside but also soft and moist on the inside. Love it. 

Their egg salad is perfect for kids since it's not too salty and goes well with the bagels. 

What was surprising for me was the grapefruit cocktail. The top was brulee'ed and the mix of sweet and sour was perfect. 

Although weekends are hard to book but week days are much easier.

If you are looking for great Lox this should be the first place you go! The quality of the smoked salmon here is by far the best I have had I absolutely love how thin they slice it! I recommend their towers with Lox and white fish by far superb! I can't get enough Chef's kiss

*** you neeed to make a reservation on resy if you don't want to wait hours to get a table here! even if there are empty tables it is usually super understaffed at peak times so it can take really long to get seated.

i came here on a weekday for lunch and saw the incredible bagel towers on social media --have been wanting to come here ever since. even though it was a cloudy, grey day, the ambiance was still incredible. i also kind of liked how the waitstaff wore white doctor-like coats even though that was probably more to simulate the clothing that people in delis wear to pay homage to sadelle's roots in bagels and spreadables. 

we got the house salmon, matzoh ball soup, eggs benedict, and greek salad. although expensive for a salad, the portions were really big. would've loved the option to add different proteins to the salad(?). the bagel tower is literally the best part and the presentation is so nice and unique -- like an english breakfast type -- tiered plate setup except it's with BAGELs. heavenly. i wish teh bagel itself was more fluffy and fuller (i asked for it toasted tho, so maybe that contributed to some shrinkage). The chive cream cheese that came with it was so airy and whipped well. The dill and capers (as well as thinly sliced cucumbers and tomatos) that accompanied the salmon were perfect garnishes. The salmon wasn't too salty either; which allowed me to focus on the texture of it. 

the soup itself was pretty lacking --not flavorful and the matzoh ball was kind of dry (even though it was submerged in soup)! I would rather go to bens and get a soup for less $$$ and better taste! 

lastly the eggs benedict was really good --nice juxtaposition between the toast at the bottom's crunchiness and the runny eggs at the top. 

Would definitely come again!   

PS they also serve cocktails all day. use that information at your discretion.

Always a scene, always good. You can't go wrong with bagels and lox and you gotta get the French Toast to split as a table. My favorite bagel is the salt and pepper and then the everything 2.0. You are going to want to order more bagels than what come with the lox's. Just saying.

I can't figure out the obsession that most ny'ers have with Sadelles, and with their bagels.  We had a reservation on a Friday for lunch/brunch, and when we arrived the hostess led us up two flights of stairs to the nosebleed level claiming that we were only a party of three, and the tables downstairs were designated for larger parties.  My wife preferred to be seated on the main level despite the hostess being rude and insisting that we be seated on the uppermost level.   Another hostess intervened and we were eventually seated at a table for four on the main level.  As far as the food is concerned, there's literally nothing to write home about. It was mediocre, at best.  The coffee was also mediocre.  When you order coffee here one cup arrives, not a carafe. We were surprised by that as at Sadelles in Las Vegas at the Bellagio, when you order coffee, a carafe arrives at the table.  The waitstaff is also far more professional and accommodating. The restaurant is elegant in LV, not so in SoHo. Despite being born and raised in NYC, I don't miss the attitude. It is legendary, but as soon as you can find a gentler place to live, with great weather, less traffic, and happy people, start packing.   NYC nowadays is reminiscent of the 70's-'80's when Bernard Goetz was a hero, and movies like Death Wish were sold out.

MEAN!   Mean people.   The food is great.  The service is very good.  The management stinks. I had a nine AM reservation for six. I'm 76 years old and handicapped.  I got there at 840.  They made me sit outside in the coke til nine.   There was no reason I couldn't sit inside.  They were just nasty.  "I only work here" said one employee.  Why are people like this?  I was very cold.  They saw me sitting there. They wouldn't let me in.  I doubt that ill go back.
One of the best brunch spots in NYC so you if you have a hard time getting reservation it's because the food is that good.

Sadelle's was so worth the hype. To be honest, I didn't think it would be, but I will never go to NYC and not visit Sadelle's again.

We made reservations about a few weeks in advance, which is definitely recommended. The place was packed. Even with reservations, we waited quite a while to be seated, but it was well worth the wait. We were seated at a cute table with a nice view of the restaurant.

For once, we skipped on cocktails and just went for the food. We ordered a few things to share; the pigs in a blanket, the french toast, and bagels with smoked salmon. If you're coming with 2 people, you won't regret copying this exact order. The pigs in a blanket were absolutely to die for. We almost skipped them because it felt a bit basic, but believe me when I say that you need them.

The french toast was the best I've ever had. I don't typically like French Toast, but I ate every single bite and fell in love more and more. Lastly, the bagels. Served on a super cute little tower with all the fixins. Wonderful presentation and delicious NY bagel.

I'll be back and I will be trying their famous bagel tower and caviar next time!

I was so excited to come here for the NYC Bagel experience. I am gluten free so it is always tough for me to find bagels anywhere. Finding a sit down restaurant that serves gluten free bagels is always one in a million. And I found a place in the heart of soho! 

My review is solely on my gluten free bagel experience. I loved that they brought them out (warm) on a separate plate. They were light and fluffy, but still somewhat dense! These are hard traits to replicate in non-gluten baked goods but they found out how to make the perfect bagel. I loved the cream cheese along with the Sadelle's Tower that we ordered. The salmon is definitely the best on the menu. I don't think I would order it again, but rather instead get trays of salmon- personal preference we didn't like the white fish as much!

On a side note, make sure you have a reservation. They stopped seating walk ins because Kendall & Kylie Jenner showed up for brunch and booked out the top portion of the restaurant!

Edited: spelling

Everyone's got a favorite brunch place and bagel place in New York - Sadelle's so happens to my choice for both. The House Salmon was fantastic, adding a silky texture to a well toasted bagel smothered with very whipped creamy scallion cream cheese. Tomato and cuumbers excellent are refreshing flavor-neutralizers, cutting the richness of the oils and cream by adding a faint sweet tang to the bite. Would recommend you try adding everything on the bagel (even if you're not the biggest fan of tomatoes). French Toast is also delicious, wonderfully crispy on the outside, soft and rich at the center. To  brighten the meal, order the grapefruit cocktail (Palomar?) - super refreshing. Everything is as good as it looks .

One of my favorite brunch spots in New York, they have a salmon platter that allows you to make your own bagels and a great selection of other breakfast items. The interior is so cute and posh, and the salmon is so fresh!

Booked a Wedding Eve family Brunch reception at Sadelle's with approximately 35 people attending. We got the private loft, 3rd floor to ourselves. An event menu package was planned with alcoholic breakfast drinks available by the glass. 

Pros: 
Food was amazing! The French Toast-OMG, like no other! 


Presentation was on point

Service was responsive, helpful, attentive, service-driven

Ambiance the perfect New York brunch vibe one can experience

The ease of coordinating was done majority online thru email, contract & payment online, final walk through of venue a few days prior to event to discuss layout

Accommodated outside dessert brought in due to their lack of dessert options 
3 hour event timeframe was allotted 

Location in NY was walkable from subway 

Cons: 
Expensive!  I considered deducting a star for the price but do feel every dollar was worth the experience so no deduction. This was a unique NYC experience, there's no price on that.

The layout configuration recommended by the Event Coordinator was not the best and the day of the event it was changed to accommodate flow and enough seating for the space. Space is tight on the 3rd floor, utilizing the booth space for seating was the correct thing to do and that changed last minute. 

Event Coordinator was ok, adequate, got the job done, not great. The quality of communication was deducted one star for this reason; there was unnecessary stress due to what seemed to be a lack of experience, delays in emails, (but when it came to $, she was on it!). The apathy in serving us was evident and did not match our enthusiasm for the occasion. 

Their contract specifies anything with their name,  including your invitations must be approved by Sadelle's. We had to get approval on our Evite. Never heard of that before on any invitations. 

Long lines for the restrooms 

Lack of a non-alcoholic beverage package for event-adding more expense

Overall, we were pleased with the event, everyone had a great time.we would recommend if you want and can afford this New York bourgeois experience.
The food was not the best, too over priced, service was great, coffee was not good. Too hyped, I was expecting more but not worth it

Delicious!!! The ambience is very nice, and a great unique experience. As someone who isn't from New York, I had a blast dining here. Service is a little hectic but that's to be expected. The servers and front of house do their best with how packed it always is!!

Cool breakfast spot in soho. Made a reservation ahead of time which I recommend. Wife has the salmon bagel and I had the tuna sandwich. Both were really good but nothing extremely special. Not worth the hype imo. So much more to try in NYC.

Super long wait on a random weekday morning. Full of themselves. Staff spotty. 

Not impressed.

Still one of my favorite places in the city. Never disappointed by the food or service.  The last time I visited they had taken a drink I love off the menu but the waiter was able to get it for me anyway - love to see it.
Nice place for breakfast, cozy and charming inside the restaurant, everything tasted good but maybe a little bit pricy for breakfast
Best bagel place we went to in NY by far! Highly recommend this place to anyone visiting
Everything is incredible. We had omelette, French toast, blueberry pancakes, smoked salmon bagel towers ! Get it alllllll

Didn't understand the hype with this place at all. The food was bland at best. I've had better white fish from other places. One of the bagels was decently smaller than the other one. They had cold area blowing through the whole top area when it was snowing out. Their green tea was amazing! Overall not worth the value when there's other better bagel places in NYC
But the French toast!!!! Don't walk run. Everything was exceptional. The French toast was extremely moist and the salmon tower was perfect for 2.

I was so underwhelmed by my experience at Sadelle's. I made a reservation for indoor dining but was told that they had accidentally over-booked the interior and was placed in the outdoor area, which would have been fine if not for the continuous draft passing between the half-open curtains and the loud mariachi band that the table next to us had hired for a birthday surprise.
