The bagels and smoked fishes were just okay; they certainly did not live up to the hype, and the meal was not filling at all. If you're looking for an amazing New York bagel, this is not the place.

The second best smoked salmon in the city. 
Amazing bunch. 
Wish the coffee was better, but everything else is amazing.

First and foremost our waiter was displeased that we didn't want an alcoholic beverage to begin our meal.  This was just rude. The special cheeseburger wasn't particularly special. The waiter wasn't sure of what was on the burger beside cheese, and recited a few things. I said ok to the extras, except no Russian dressing.  I received a plain cheeseburger with no extras.  It was far from delicious.  The side salad I ordered was basic and fresh. The dressing was delicious.  I sat indoors and the ambience was lovely.  Attention from our server and others was very good.
Perfect breakfast spot for a New York experience. A bit on the expensive side, but worth the experience.
Best breakfast food and bagels I've ever had. Can't believe how many people haven't left 5 star reviews this place. Hands down the most delicious smoked salmon I've ever had .

Wonderful experience on so many levels. Went here for a special birthday and it was so nice. I'd been looking forward to a meal here for a long time and wasn't disappointed. Ambience is fantastic..pretty decor, high ceilings and best of all...not super noisy. Where to start... bloody Mary's looked delicious with right amount of horseradish and I had a wonderful tequila cocktail w cucumbers. Yum. We ordered the tower : an orgy of sturgeon, Scottish salmon with of course bagels and lox. Salmon was exquisite ...buttery and smooth. Only disappointment were the bagels...not terrible but adequate. Surprise hit of apps was the exquisite French toast ...one of the best things I've ever had. We were sharing but I wanted a whole plate for myself. Next time !! The pigs in a blanket were also delightful. Service for most part was terrific. Would I go back? You betcha !!

The food, ambiance and service were all amazing. I highly recommend coming here for brunch on any day. If you have a chance request for Jeff - an amazing server, witty and a great conversationalist. 

If it's your first time I would try the tower to find what you may or may not like. So for the next time that you go, you already know. Definitely have the French toast - one it's big second the outside is crispy while the inside is warm and soft and third it may be big but it's so good you could go for another. This place is worth coming back regularly.

This place is trendy and popular. AND SO WORTH IT! The French toast was the best...the green chili sauce that we asked for as an extra went great on egg dishes. Oh and the Pigs in a Blanket were so good!! The service was GREAT! The atmosphere is spacious and airy. This was...as my picky 13yr old said...a 10/10!!
My favorite brunch in New York. Everything is delicious. If you have the opportunity to go, you won't regret it.

Summary - if you like food more than vibes, please go elsewhere. There are so many actual bagel place that's worth the money and time to come here. 
 
Food - at best they are edible. Consider this actually bagel, I don't know. Bagel is small and more like a flat bread. At most you can get like 4 bites and for $25, I don't know what to say. Bagel shouldn't be that expensive. Moving to Brussels sprout, they are actually decent. Also the wait for the food is sooooo long. 

Ambiance - this place is crowded and long wait without reservation. 

Service is very good. But seriously took 30 minutes to get a few bagels. 

Overall - not worth the hype.
Beautiful aesthetic, great service and ambiance. Excellent dishes. I will be back to try some more dishes and see if they remain as perfectly executed.

Love this place. Went to the Vegas location and knew wanted to try New York. Had the salmon tower and my party had the tuna sandwich and Benedict. We also had a bottle of champagne (celebrating a birthday) which was delicious and didn't cost an arm and a leg. I would definitely go again! Try to make reservations if possible as it gets super busy.

Great friendly, accommodating, and timely service with a solid ambiance indoors. Got the tower in which all the options from the smoked salmon to the whitefish salad tasted amazing. In addition, the bagels, especially when freshly warmed up, were perfectly soft with a crust. The surprise of it all though was the French toast. Honestly was expecting the fish to be the highlight, but it was overshadowed as soon as I bit into the French toast. Super thick cut slices with an almost brûlée-like toasted crust and a custardy interior. Took me a while to figure it all out as I thought it was stuffed but no, it was just that good. Prices were reasonable for what it was but definitely on the higher end. Would highly recommend.

The service was nice and i got a little candle for my birthday. When it comes to the food though, the saw along bagel i ordered was the absolute opposite of flavor. However the tomato soup and grilled cheese was so good. It was nice inside and cozy. Great for taking pictures.

My daughter was so excited and looking forward to having brunch here but was quite disappointed in the end.  

Having reservations, we were seated timely at 8:45 am on a Sunday.  My daughter had the salmon bagels which she claimed were just okay.  My husband had the French toast but didn't care for it as it was too oily.  The outside was crispy and the inside was fluffy but it seemed to be deep fried and was very oily.  I had the blueberry pancakes which came with 3 large pancakes.  The blueberries, which were cooked in the pancakes, were a bit tart for me.  

Although service lacked a bit, we didn't mind as the shops nearby didn't open until 11:00 and we didn't have anywhere else to go.

I totally agree with the other yelper ... if you're going for only the food, you may be disappointed.
A must try in NYC. Great blueberry pancakes, although the portions were a bit excessive. The service is amazing and I became friends with one of the waiters.

My favourite brunch in the city.
My must order: Sadelle Tower and Freddy Salad.

Four stars bc, long line ups and very intimate in the restaurant.

Extremely rude hostesses. Used to be a regular customer but I will never come back.

Food is decent.

Strolling along in SoHo - NYC -  I was asking - Where is the best brunch , a great bagel(gluten free to be exact) and 8 out of 10 New Yorkers said #sadelles so do the math 80% of 8.8. Million that's a loyal following .  Anyway - I went and I can see why. This cute cafe with fantastic friendly staff --- and my Salmon Beni - awesome !!! I am coming back !!  Cheers
Best French toast and best new place to have breakfast for myself.
Pretty cute nice atmosphere. I wasnt a fan of the table size and location. But the food was delicious and its the perfect spot to have brunch with my long time friend

I got Sadelle's to go so that we could eat in a friend's hotel room before their flight left. 

I have always heard such amazing things about Sadelle's and their bagels and fish, but I think my expectations were too high going into the takeout version of their food.

The fish was extremely good. Some of the best lox and Sable I've had. Would've loved to try their whitefish salad.

Next time, I'll definitely eat at the restaurant. I think it would be a 5/5 experience then. Although, I did think the bagels we received were on the small side. Maybe that was a fluke though
Service was fantastic; food was solid; iffy on value...will try one more time - hard to judge anything on just one visit.

These people are thieves. I made a reservation for breakfast but my
husband got sick right before we were going to go and the restaurant
had the nerve to charge me a 100.00 cancellation fee. I will never go
there and will tell everyone I know about this fraud. BEWARE of thieves.

Sadelles might not have the best bagels in NYC, but it's still aesthetically pleasing & a great place to grab breakfast with some friends. We ordered their seafood tower which comes with a wide array of fishes, salads, toppings, & endless bagels. It was a little too big for three people, but we made a decent dent & it was nice to try a variety of things! Really loved their salmon salad and lox. We also ordered a side of their latkes which were just okay & would opt to skip next time.

Although the food was expensive, the whole experience of eating breakfast here is a must for people visiting NYC. The food was delicious and we discovered we love matzah ball doup. It gets very busy here for breakfast but the servers will still be able to take care of you in a timely manner. Festive ambiance which feels like a perpetual Sunday brunch atmosphere.

It was amazing... Luckily the wait was only 45 minutes lol but it was worth it. Loved the grapefruit cocktail - basically a scooped out grapefruit with a hard sugar crust on top. The house salmon with bagel was delicious - salmon was great and tomato perfect with fresh olive oil. The LEO or salmon omelette was the best salmon omelette I've ever had.
Ordered delivery. Am a regular customer. Found a long strand of hair in the order. Disgusting.

Crooks. Fraudulent charge of $100.  Tried to cancel reservation.  They do not answer their phone, direct you to email, then nobody ever responds with multiple attempts.  No way to contact the restaurant at all.  Crooks

Always love this place! Great service, great atmosphere, refreshing drinks, and fabulous food. So happy we have a Sadelles in Dallas! It gets busy here! Sadelles is a great people watching place where you will hear laughs and conversations amongst a busy crowd of carefully orchestrated staff that make sure you are taken care of. A reservation is needed and make sure to arrive early to find parking or simply valet for free and enjoy a unique experience.

Waited 20 minutes for a table -45 minutes to get our order -Avocado Toast with egg over easy ..instead I got BURNT toast with OVER COOKED eggs! The server was great -very apologetic-My husband's omelette was over salted & his bagel was just like ok -could have been a bit fresher. I'm just not sure why this place is always so packed since the food is just so so! With so many options -look elsewhere.

Pigs in a blanket are so flaky & yummy! The salmon bagel tower was amazing for its low price. The scallion cream cheese was a great addition to the bagel. Definitely make a resy, service was good & very aesthetic inside!

Overall, great restaurant for brunch but a little bit on the pricey side for what kind of food you're getting. 

Food: Ordered the House Salmon and Scottish Salmon. I preferred the Scottish salmon. Thought it was unique that you could choose the type of lox you wanted, which is not necessarily always possible at other restaurants. But it was a little pricey for the amount of food you got. 

Service: Great service! Servers and Waiters were very attentive. Did a walk in on a weekday for brunch and was seated immediately.

Ambiance: Really cute. Had outdoor seating and indoor seating. Great little place for brunch!

This place can get crowded, make a reservation if you can. A friend and I waited  about 30 minutes  for a table but that's not too bad because you can look at the shops close by. You have 15 minutes to get back to the restaurant. This place is so cute if you want a higher end brunch and bagels. We got the smoked salmon tower and it was fun to eat with a friend. The service was nice. I enjoyed my drinks as well. They have other locations too so when I travel I can check it out.

The best salmon and best gluten free bagel I have ever had. It's unbelievably good, if your gluten free you need to go and get the everything bagel! *coming from someone with a gluten intolerance, not celiac*

We pulled up to Sadelle's on a Sunday around 1pm and they had no space for a party of 6, so we got on the list for 3:30 and just meandered around SoHo. When we came back, we were seated immediately. Good service so far!

We ordered everything on the menu (LOL!) & nothing let us down. My friends chastise me for ordering French toast everywhere I go, but Sadelle's was BY FAR, the best FT I've ever had. I made everyone at the table try it.  Sadelle's lives up to the hype.

This place is overrated in my opinion. Prices are high and food was average. We came in on a Thursday at 12:15 with reservations and were seated right away. The atmosphere is beautiful and the place was packed. We ordered the following:

French toasts: the toast was fluffy and extremely oily. It was good my table shared this otherwise it would've been too filling for one person. It came with syrup and a compote which were yummy. 3/5

Healthy egg sandwich: this was a regular sandwich which a daily sized omelet and veggies. It was good but also nothing spectacular. Wish us could have some kind of sauce added to make it more flavorful. 3/5

Bagel: we ordered the house salmon and Scottish salmon. Again, nothing spectacular about either. Bagels are homemade which is nice but you can definitely find a better priced bagel with salmon elsewhere in New York.

Overall this place is overhyped. We spent $120 on the dishes and weren't very full after.

I mean this place is a hot spot for a reason. Vibes, incredible. Service, on top it. Food, AMAZING!  i've been thinking about the pigs in a blanket and tuna melt sandwich since they day I had it. 10/10 recommend this place if you can get a resy.

I had a reservation for 3:45 pm on a Saturday. It was such an odd time to eat, but the only options were 8 am and 3:45 pm. 

I got a Cobb salad and my friend got blueberry pancakes. The Cobb salad was super filling and the perfect amount of food. My friend liked her pancakes but didn't finish it because it was a lot of food and again, 3:45 pm is a weird time to eat. 

Despite it being 3:45 pm, the entire restaurant was packed! I would come again for a proper brunch and try one of the towers and French toast'
Service and food are great I recommend cucumber margarita, oysters, and the sturgeon bagel tower

I ordered the house salmon and it was really good! However, the bagel was not my favorite. It could've been fluffier and more tasteful in general. That being said, I am giving a 5 star rating because of how good the other food was. The lox was delicious, and the tomatoes tasted very fresh. The ambiance was nice- great brunch spot. The service was also good.
Highly priced. High brow low value. Tables close together. If all you want is breakfast go elsewhere

Came here on my last day in NYC and was able to get an early reservation on a Sunday right at opening  Easily the best french toast I've ever had and that's coming from someone who usually doesn't care for french toast. Salmon eggs benedict was perfect as well. Good service. A must try if you're in NYC!

This place is beautiful. I love my experience there. Server is very helpful and give me a good advice about order. They found a table for me quick while they are very busy and packed. I like the food and presentation. So delicious. Best bagel with salmon in the world. Definitely will be back and recommend this place to my friends!

My husband and I came here for breakfast last weekend and this was probably my 4th or 5th time and his first time. I've always had a pretty good experience and the food has been really good even though it is overpriced. This time something was just off. Our sever was not very helpful and she seemed annoyed to be working. I think she maybe came by our table twice the entire meal so we ended up having to ask other servers for help. While I love the ambiance of the restaurant, they seem to be putting the tables way too close to each other. This was particularly problematic for us as we had a screaming child to the left of us and then when they left, they were replaced by two women playing TikTok videos on full volume. I understand it's not the restaurants fault for how people dining there act but when they choose to put the tables on top of each other, I feel that they should still hold some blame. The one other odd thing that I had never experienced there before was that there was a loud ringing sound that was on and off the whole time we were there (we also heard other people complaining about t. In terms of the food, the bagels are really good and I particularly love their whitefish spread which they give you a very generous portion of. The smoked salmon is also very good but you can't say the same about the portion. We also tried their puff pastry pigs in a blanket and they were just ok.

While I was in NYC, my friend took me to Sadelle's! I appreciated that they had gluten free bagels and it didn't taste like cardboard. 
My friend made a reservation for us here and we got seated quickly. The team here was always checking on us and made sure we got what we needed. 
The spread was decent and good for your basic bagel sandwich. 
My only feedback is make sure you mark off on resy when people check-in. We got charged a no show fee, even though we ate at the establishment. We also had a really hard time getting ahold of anyone via phone and email, after we saw the charge the next day.
We had go out of our way to go to the restaurant to tell them what happened. At first, they didn't believe us until we showed them the email and the charges along with our receipt of eating there. 
Eventually, it got taken care off and it should have been an easier process to get the $150 no show fee taken off the card.

Service is decent, food is good. It's not worth really a wait to eat there though. Got the eggs Benedict and everything bagel and cream cheese. Liked all of them but there are other places that are easier to get a reservation at and are at least as good as this place

Next Level Bagel & Lox here at Sadelle'!

Happy Jeff recommended it. Very attentive service despite how busy it was.

TikTok brought us to Sadelle's, it was a must-do on our trip to New York. We made a reservation prior to our our trip and had no issues. On the day of our reservation (7/22/2023), we arrived a bit early and there were already people waiting. They opened on time and we were sat immediately. Our waitress greeted us quickly and we started off with (the overpriced) mimosas, they were good. For our meals, we got the French toast and a salmon tower. The French toast was perfection, literally touched by an angel. Both my husband and I are not generally people who like sweet food, but this French toast was unnaturally good. However, the salmon tower was mediocre and that's me being giving. The salmon had a smell and did not taste good, in addition the cream cheese was also not good. I am going against the grain as everyone loves the salmon tower, we were excited about the tower, however we do not recommend...at all. The reason this is a 4 out of 5 (I debated on a 3) is because the French toast and service were superior, we recommend the restaurant and we also look forward to going back, however skip the salmon tower!

Sadelle's is my top brunch place (thank you to my bffff for taking here for my birthday way back in May, and now my fiance for enjoying as much as I do lol). Like. Yes. This place is worth the hype. The bagels are itty bitty, but the fish, tomato/onion/caper helpings, and set up makes all the difference. The soft scrambled eggs with caviar (the splurge on the baeri royale IS. IT.) wowowowoow. And finish off with that super fluffy french toast. 

Ambience wise.. it's always full. Unless you're one of the few last customers still sitting around at 3pm. It's that good. Grab that reservation DAYS ahead.

I recently visited Sadelle's in New York. While the ambiance was pleasant, I found the service to be slow and often confused. The food was average at best, and the bagels weren't as flavorful as I expected. Considering the price, I've had tastier bagels at more affordable places. Unfortunately, I found Sadelle's to be overrated and overpriced. It's not a place I would choose to revisit.
I wish so badly There was a Sadelle's closer to me. Everything on the menu is exquisite and cannot wait for my next trip to Vegas.!!
Loveeee sadelles. The most perfect brunch spot! All dishes were delicious. Get the tomato soup and pigs in the blanket as an app!! The bagel and cream cheese was fantastic!
I enjoy the food here . The waiter was very nice I went for brunch to celebrate my birthday .

This is definitely a trendy social media spot. But I'll admit, it was fun just for the experience. 

Bagel tower. Just do it. I preferred the Smoked Scottish over the House Salmon. I also asked for extra cucumbers during our brunch (I love the crunch). My friend didn't love her Benedict for brunch. 

French toast was also a perfect sweet bite. We split this as our brunch dessert. 

One star knocked because I do think it's overhyped and why is it so difficult to get a reservation??
Checks all the boxes! Busy all the time so make a Rez! Great spot for both locals and tourists.

I landed a last minute reservation to Sadelle's. We opted for the French Toast and house salmon bagel. I'm usually not a fan of french toast but the one here made me reconsider. The servers were very attentive despite being busy.
Cute spot for breakfast or brunch. Service was friendly and fast. Dining available inside or outside. Food was fresh and flavorful.

This restaurant did not disappoint. Beautiful rustic environment and excellent service. The food was amazing, literally everything we ate was just *chef's kiss*. We had the caviar eggs, house salmon tower, pigs in a blanket, and French toast (amazing).
Delicious food and excellent service. A great start to a New York morning. Would return again

Fancy place for bagels and lox - you are paying for the ambience and pretty dishes etc.  who doesn't love their bagels on a pole and lox on a layered tray- fancy fancy

The bagels are on the small side but tasty.  Lox sliced super thin and my favorite was the house salmon (whichever is the first on the list-lol)

I had an espresso martini but my girlfriend wanted a cortado but they didn't have any espresso drinks-so I'm guessing no real espresso in my martini- shocking - only regular coffee!?!  For a NYC breakfast/brunch place?!?

I went because it was recommended online. I made reservations and service was great. The food was average though; I am not sure it's worth the hype if you are expecting great food. The salmon was average, the chicken sandwich was dry, and the omelet was average as well. The space is very big, but there's a lot of tables close to each other.

Unbelievable. Came here on a Sunday morning and it wasn't too busy (but of course make a reservation)! We were pretty hungry, so we got the House Salmon and Scottish Salmon for our bagels and the French toast - heard it was great from a rec and it didn't disappoint. Everything was amazing and the fish was refreshing. The house salmon was a bit fishy, so if you don't enjoy that try the smoked Scottish. We were dying to try another fish after finishing everything so we ordered the Sable afterwards. Not the biggest fans of the sable, but it was nice to try a fish that was more soft and oily.

Next time I'll be back with a bigger group so we can order the Sadelle's Tower!!

Came to Sadelle's with super high expectations after hearing/seeing all the good reviews. The food was good but definitely overrated and overpriced. My friend and I split both the French toasts and the salmon eggs benefit. The eggs benny was good but a bit too salty for me (ironically I think it was the salmon that was too salty, which is what they're known for). And the French toasts was sooo oily - like not to be dramatic but I almost felt like I could squeeze the oil out if I tried. 

Service was decent (nothing spectacular) and the restaurant itself is quite cute, but it is a bit on the louder side if you're looking for a quieter place to talk!

Went there for a quick breakfast and it was really great. They didn't have some of the drinks but the server was very friendly and tried his best to offer other options. They had a great French toast and while I wasn't a fan of the cheese blintzes, my partner really enjoyed them. Would def return! When I return, I'd like to try the pancakes next. Really good ambiance as well.

My sister and I love Sadelle's! Generous portions and delicious smoked salmon dishes :) the restaurant gets quite busy and loud but this is a plus if you are enjoying NYC as a visitor and want a fun Saturday or Sunday brunch :)
Foods out of this world for not just another breakfast joint. French toast is a must have! Service is exceptional.

Can a brunch place be any better than Sadelle's? The answer is no!!!

LOVED it! 
Will move to NY only for this place!

Yes you need reservation if not you should expect 1:30 hour to get in. But the neighborhood has so much to explore so of you are not starving, you ll be fine!

The fish and bagel bring life back to your mouth! 
Fish tower is a must! 

We got house salmon and sturgeon! Ah was melting in my mouth! The bagel itself need another review! 

Make sure to order side of bacon too. You have not had anything like that before. It cooked perfect amount crispy but still juicy! 

Who does brunch without mimosa? So order couple glass of mimosa so fulfill your experience. 

Again loved everything about this place.

Food 5/10
I can't believe I paid 20 bucks for a bagel. We went here when Popup Bagels was an unsuccessful venture, but it really just wasn't worth the amount of money we paid. Definitely a place for the vibes. Our bagels were fine but they weren't mindblowing. 

Atmosphere 7/10
Sat outside, good for people watching, but because it was the middle of summer, I was still sweating profusely.

Service 7/10
Not bad, not great.

Overall: Pretty, vibey, and mostly tasty food and cocktails. 

Tastiness: I understand this place prides itself with their fish selection, however my experience with the Sable fish was too salty. The bagel, cream cheese, cucumbers, tomatoes and blintzes was excellent, so I can forgive the very salty fish. I was also disappointed that they did not make espresso based drinks, serving only freshly brewed coffee and cold brew. My friend's custom omelette was tasty and almost put her in a food coma. Cocktails are nice.

Service: Decently attentive before 10, a bit unaware of queues after 10, when it gets busier. Courteous and effective at all times. 

Ambiance: This is a cute, spacious, and bright brunch spot, with well curated music at the right volume. 

Cleanliness: Pretty clean. 

Price: Decently priced for SoHo.

Excellent brunch with very good quality ingredients and presentation.
I recommend the terrace if the weather permits.

The smoked salmon is truly delicious and pure artistry!

Anything you eat here is 5-star+!

Fantastic staff and a true gift for your palate

From the time you taste the smoked salmon, you immediately want more and more.

Sadelles was one of the restaurants I was looking forward to the most as a foodie visiting from Los Angeles. I booked the reservation as early as they take their reservations because I was so excited. Their reputation and popularity really created high expectations, that unfortunately, were not met. Our server seemed unhappy to serve us, and didn't seem like he wanted to answer any questions, which really put a damper on the experience. I felt he just wasn't helpful. We ordered a couple cocktails, the Saddelle's tower, pigs in a blanket, French toast, scrambled eggs, sausage, and the Freddy salad. The food was okay. I felt it had potential, but missed the mark for us. The French toast seemed undercooked? It was quite mushy inside (maybe that's the way it is supposed to be? I'm unsure), however, the outer crispy portion was delicious. I really enjoyed their sausage, and the tower had great presentation, and was really good. Pigs in a blanket is hard to mess up I feel, and was really good here too.
The ambience inside was great, super cute restaurant with great vibes. I would definitely want to go back and give it another try one day to see if the experience could be different.

I left our server either a 18% or 19% tip, when usually, my minimum tip starts at 20% because I was so disappointed.
Loved the french toast, it was the perfect consistency of toasty and soft. Would recommend.
Food was amazing at Sadelle's!  I ordered French toast, eggs, potatoes, and a bagel.    Everything was fresh and delicious.    Service was friendly and helpful.

We had heard rave reviews about Sadelle's, so we were not surprised that every table was booked.  We walked in and were seated on the second floor at a lovely table (we had 0945 reservations on a Monday).  We ordered cold brew coffees, and they were excellent!  Our server was Charley, and she and the staff treated us like celebrities.  The food was outstanding!!!  I have never in my life had such creamy, fluffy scrambled eggs.  They make the bagels ten feet from where we were sitting!  The salt and pepper are baked in the bagels, topped with sea salt and served with plenty of cream cheese.  The breakfast potatoes were smashed and seasoned perfectly, the potato latkes were fluffy and crisp and served with applesauce, the bacon........ (I've dreamt of bacon like this), the FRENCH TOAST, OMG!  It was like french toast and funnel cakes had a baby.  They served it with delicious maple syrup and strawberry preserves.  Avocado toast, the tomatoes/cucumbers, cold brew coffee.....

I am going to NYC again at Christmas, and this will be my first stop!  Thank you for the amazing food and the amazing service!  Every employee there was very friendly and they boxed up our leftovers.  I wish I could give Sadelle's more than 5 stars!!

Setting, service, food all top notch.
And the French toast is unlike anything I've ever seen served for breakfast. 
If you could handle deep fried angel food cake out of a bundle pan? Go for it.

Always wanted to try Sadelle's and I am so happy I finally got to try it. Made reservations for a Sunday afternoon. The chicken walfdorf salad was so colorful, fresh, delightful, and refreshing. The bagel and salmon tower is an IG moment and super fresh. The highlight would have to be the club sandwich, I mean that size and the sauce. It was filling and delicious.
Amazing brunch place with a super friendly staff. The food was flavorful and the place was very aesthetic.

Fun experience! Ordered a salmon tower and bagels. The bagels were pretty bad especially considering they make them on site! The salmon was good- but I've had better. Coffee was weak. Got the omelette and it was overly cheesy and so greasy - by far the worst thing we ordered - did not enjoy it or finish it. Service was good - waitress was friendly and helpful. This spot is sceney which I enjoyed and I liked interior. Good vibes- very subpar food.

Sadelle's doesn't quite live up to their hype.

The ambiance is rowdy, plain and not suited for special occasions.

The salmon eggs benedict lacked flavor, texture, and was small in portion size, especially considering the price.

The french toast was overly sweet and too dense.

Overall, the quality here is lackluster.

We had a 9AM reservation and were promptly seated at a great table. Our server immediately appeared to take our drink order. This was right at opening, so I attributed the prompt service to the lack of patrons, as our time there progressed, the service remained top notch. My coffee cup was watched like it owed them money, empty plates taken away with a sleight of hand, and sparkling water refilled before I realized the goblet was low. 
It's a small space but somehow not overwhelming with chatter. 
The food was beautifully presented and delicious. We had the smoked salmon and the eggs with potatoes and bagel. The salmon was a delicate balance of smoke and fresh salmon flavor, the veggies served chilled and the everything bagel had great chew. The eggs were seasoned and delicious. I really enjoyed the smashed  and griddle crisp potatoes along with my sesame bagel and cream cheese. The portions were more than sufficient and the coffee was superb. A very enjoyable visit.

I love lox I love bagels and I love caviar. Nothing not to love about this place. For us Californians who don't get to experience super fresh bagels and hand cut lox this was something out of a dream. You will not regret coming.

Thrilled by the great customer service, I had an issue with my order & the team reached out to me right away to ensure there was a resolution. 

Thank you, excited for my order for my event next week!

First time here.  Great atmosphere! Great vibe! Fast service and food is excellent! Everything we ordered is delicious and fresh! I like the size of the bagels too just enough for 1 person even though I did not partake on the bagels. Omelettes are perfect! !

We did walk-in on a weekday for brunch and waited around 20 minutes to get called back for a seat. We ordered the french toast and salmon omelette! French toast was so fluffy but too sweet for me, so we didn't end up finishing all of it. My favorite was the salmon omelette since I love salmon and the sauce tasted so good with it.

MMMmMM this socal girl has never had bagels like this before. 
We got the tower with a side of potatoes and eggs benedict salmon bagels, which was perfect. The meat, veggies, condiments, water, bagels, and service were all delicious and top-notch. 

I absolutely loved the atmosphere inside. It's a 1.5-floor restaurant with high ceilings, so it feels grand and luxurious. You can see workers making the bagels in one glass room and butchers(?) busily catering fish orders, which all adds to this restaurant's glamorous industrial brick-and-mortar core New York feel. 

It gets really busy and crowded, so always reserve ahead of time! The effort is worth the food & experience.

One of the best brunch I've ever had!! At first, I thought it was meh, since it looks like a regular American brunch, nothing special.. BUT!! This is my favourite brunch so far in NYC! 
The smoked salmon is really good served with poppy seed bagels and the soft scrambled egg with fish roe is A MUST ORDER!!! We had 3 orders for only 2 of us hahaha and we devoured all of it!
Love the ambiance and it is located in the heart of SOHO.
The service is phenomenal as well, food came pretty quick.
All in all, Sadelle's NYC is a must try

Amazing, delicious, cute brunch spot in New York. Always crowded but worth the wait and quick service once seated. By far my favorite place in the city. The bagel toppings and sweet selections are unmatched. Everything on the menu is a must order--your table will be filled but it's all worth it!

I've been wanting to try Sadelle's for awhile and thought it was totally worth the hype! The bagel towers are such a fun presentation, and definitely come with great fish and bagels for New York standards. We also got the pancakes which had the right balance of fluffiness and richness with a bit of crispiness on the outside!

I came here wondering if this place was overhyped as most popular social media spots are, but I was pleasantly surprised. We came in for brunch, and the place was packed. Reservations are definitely recommended if you want to avoid waiting for a long time for a table. This place has a cool rustic industrial look. I enjoyed seeing the sliced fish on display and the area where they make the bagels. They also had Russian nesting dolls on display.  There are 2 different levels. We got a spot on the upper level, and the corner booth seating was very comfortable. The menu has a variety of Jewish deli staples such as sliced fish and bagels, along with your more typical brunch items like French toast and omelets. Our server was Enriquetta. She was awesome and gave us great recommendations! Despite how busy it was, she was very attentive and checked on us throughout the meal. We ordered a variety of items, including the fish tower with house salmon, smoked salted salmon, sturgeon, bagels, pigs in a blanket, French toast, grapefruit, and pickles. The quality of the fish was impressive. The fish was fresh and so flavorful, the house salmon and sturgeon practically melted in my mouth. The fish tower is popular not just because it looks good in pictures but is absolutely delicious and a must try if you come to this place. The French toast is probably the best I've had, and I'm not typical a fan of French toast, but this was crispy on the outside and soft and delicious on the inside. A surprising favorite was the grapefruit. They added some brown sugar, and this enhanced the flavor really nicely. For drinks, we had the Sadelle's spritz and raspberry smash both fruity and refreshing. The espresso martinis were so good! I can not say enough about the quality of the food. Everything we had was on point. This place is pricey, but that's expected considering the location and quality.

Ordered eggs any way which comes with potatoes and a bagel. Nothing special about the dish. Service was subpar; ordered an americano as soon as I got seated and they forgot about it so I got my meal and still waited for my coffee. Half way to through i reminded my waiter and instead just ordered coffee. It tasted burnt- finished it either way. Many tables around me ordered the bagel salmon tower so maybe that's what keep this place busy but coffee was bad and my dish was average not worth they hefty price in my opinion

One of my fav brunch spots like EVERYTHING is amazing the food is good, the vibes are amazing and I am going to come back to try their french toast too! The salmon was so good. Definitely recommend making a reservation in advance!
Love this place the ambience is just great. Don't forget to try the smoked salmon bagel and the French toast. Despite being incredibly busy, the service was also good. Will be visiting soon.

The food was good but the overall experience wasn't great. For the prices, it wasn't worth it. Our table felt squished and waiters walking behind the chair kept bumping into my sister. Also there were many flies flying around which is very unappetizing. We even found one in the sauce that came with our pigs in a blanket. We notified the server who took it and brought us a new dish but I would have expected the side to have been comped or something, but they still charged us full price. Pretty gross experience. Prices weren't worth the experience

Literally the most PERFECT place to have brunch in Soho on the weekend! It has a cute little vintage feel I loved how you were also able to watch them make their bagels in the center of the restaurant. I was able to make a reservation in advance online for a Saturday and I would highly recommend doing so because this place was packed! The food is incredible and I loved the variety on the menu. The only downside is the seating arrangement. As a party of 2 we were stuck in a corner with an extremely small table that barely fit the 2 dishes we ordered and looking around it was the same case for other parties of 2.

As for the food, we ordered the smoked scottish tower and the leo omelette. I loved how thinly sliced the smoked salmon was and just because it's thinly sliced doesn't mean there wasn't a big portion of it!! Both the tower and omelette had a hefty amount of salmon and it was delicious!

Sadelle's is super hyped up and I think while it's not bad, it definitely doesn't live up to the hype. The ambiance is very nice and the service is great. The food was good, but not anything special. They're famous for their French toast, but I honestly found it to be extremely greasy and heavy, I wasn't a fan. The pancakes were pretty good but kinda dry. I didn't try the bagel tower but my dad thought it was just alright, nothing special. Overall, I would probably come back for the vibes and probably order some different things to try.

Visiting from Florida and going intoSOHO to shop so my daughter researched restaurant places to eat. We chose Sadelle's because we both like smoked fish and wanted to treat ours. We recently were elsewhere for it so were wanted to compare places. 
The interior is upscale and lovely, service was fine. We ordered the Nova lox for 2 and bagels. It came with sliced cucumbers, capers and cream cheese as well. Sesame bagels were lightly toasted. This is the first time I have had capers with the fish nd found it to be a very nice addition. The cucumbers were a nice palate cleanser. The fish however was a little disappointing. I understand it should be sliced on the thin side but being able to see thru the slices was quite disappointing.
Would I return, Maybe but not for the fish. The other offering looked interesting, so maybe.

Our favorite breakfast spot! Simple, cozy ambiance that leaves the French toast and smoked salmon as the main focal points of the meal. Service is always quick. We are impressed every time we come here! Cannot recommend the French toast enough. It's absolutely heavenly!!!

Deducting one star only bc it's so annoying to get a reservation here and impossible on a Sunday to walk in at actual lunchtime. 

Otherwise, gotta say that despite the sceneiness, Sadelle's is impossible to walk into for a reason! The salads are perhaps the platonic ideal of salads -- ingredients are all fresh, delicious and somehow chopped to precisely the right size to mix all together perfectly. The Cobb is one of my favorite lunches in the city, period. 

And the pancakes -- which somehow never show up on best in the city lists -- are, well, among the best in the city! Crunchy griddled butter flavor on the outside, fluffy and light on the inside, not heavy....perfect, from a pancake connoisseur!

The pigs in blankets are also amazing on every level and a must order every time. 

I keep doing Resy alerts (which do often work out) for weekend brunches here for a reason!
Sadelle's has a cute vibe! If you're looking for a fancy bagel with a cute lox tower, this is your spot. The Prosecco also was a nice addition to the meal! Great, quick service.
Ambiance, food and service were amazing! I go here every time I'm in NYC.  I went with three friends pretty much ordered one of everything.

Sadelle's is a great spot for a sit-down brunch. The presentation of the bagel tower was breathtaking, with a beautiful array of freshly baked bagels stacked high alongside an assortment of delectable toppings.

Each element of the Bagel Tower was meticulously crafted to perfection. The bagels themselves were flawlessly baked - crispy on the outside, soft and chewy on the inside, just as a great bagel should be. From the velvety cream cheeses to the savory smoked salmon, every component added its own burst of flavor and texture to the experience.

Perfect for any occasion, it's a must-try for bagel enthusiasts and brunch lovers alike. Trust me, you won't be disappointed!

This was my second time visiting Sadelle's and similar to my first time, thought food was good but not out of this world or anything living up to the hype. Service was great. Started with the pigs in the blanket which was solid as an app . Got the burger which was slightly disappointing to be honest  ; way too salty and not much else that was special about it. Ambiance is nice.

A NYC breakfast MUST! If you're looking for a fresh bagel, fresh lox, fluffy soft eggs and strong coffee - this is the spot! Super cozy ambiance, especially on a cold day. The decor is super cute, quaint and the service was also attentive and kind! Will definitely be returning!

My favourite brunch place in New York City! Love meeting my friends here so we can debrief on our week at brunch. service is friendly. Food is great just what you need to start your weekend or end your weekend!

Try to reserve super early. We tried to look up for reservation 2-3 weeks before our vacation to New York. But the only time available was at 8:30 AM. Fortunately, it's only few min walk from our hotel. Once we were fully seated, it's already half full in the big restaurant. 

We tried: 
- House Salmon( w/bagel, cucumber, tomato, cream cheese): I like how there is gluten free option bagel. But surprisingly this didn't end up to be my favorite. 

- Egg Any Style( sunny side up eggs w/ potato and bagel): potato's are super crispy but very flavorful. It's not like those barely cooked mushy potato. Recommend. 

- Tomato Soup: sweet tangy. My favorite item ordered from Sadelle. Highly recommend!

This is a busy spot for weekend brunch. We waited about an hour but once seated we were t disappointed. My daughter had eggs with potatoes a bagel and avocado. The potatoes are delish! I had French toast, which is a huge slice and very fresh. I prefer mine with a bit more egg flavor but it was tasty served with syrup and fruit compote. Service was great but be prepared for a long line at the restroom.

Once again, an nyc hotspot disappoints. Clearly more scene than substance. 

Don't get the pancakes. They can't even get a basic batter right. Extremely mealy and crumbles apart on the fork. I'll stick with my usual spots that are actually good. Honestly, even a place like Grey Dog does things better with considerably better value, and when places like Clinton Street Baking company are available, dining here makes zero sense.

To be contrarian, and because I loved it, I'm going to go five stars on this breakfast/brunch experience despite the high prices ($27 bagel with lox and cream cheese) the hostile "we won't seat you until the entire party arrives" policy, and the $50/person late-cancellation or no-show fee (which applies on cancellations less than 12h in advance).

Why?  The food was great, the bagels were made right next to our table in a glass-walled kitchen.  The smoked salmon was epic.  The service was great.  The scene was, well, the scene -- the kind of place where people wear pink shirts with linen jackets and Loro Piana baseball caps straight out of Succession.  And bring their dogs?

Reserve early, it's not easy to get a table.  Show up with the whole gang, otherwise you'll wait.  And beware that everything is pretty darn salty, which I liked but let's say they are liberal with the salt on everything (even the lox it seemed) so if you're not cutting it with the cream cheese it can be pretty salty.

A must visit spot if you're in NY! At Sadelles, brunch is elevated to an art form. The attention to detail, from the presentation with your bagel served in a towel to the exquisite flavors of the cream cheese and toppings, creates a culinary masterpiece. With impeccable ambiance and impeccable taste, Sadelles earns a well-deserved 5/5 rating as a top brunch destination.

Great atmosphere and the food was good, not great. Enjoyed the scenery and presentation but the place was a bit overrated. Service staff was very nice and attentive and the wait for our food wasn't too long. I do think this is a cute place for out of towners however not my number one spot to go back to for brunch in NY

I love this restaurant so so much! So many things about this restaurant is great! The food is the best thing ever! I really enjoyed the French toast. Service so so fast. I got my food in less than 10 minutes! The ambiance is insane. I love this restaurant!

Came here for friday brunch with some friends! I love how cute the vibe is here and getting to sit right next to where they were making the bagels fresh, was so cool. 

I highly recommend getting the salmon lox and whitefish salad, breakfast potatoes and sausage!

This is hands down the greatest brunch you probably ever will have. The FRENCH TOAST alone is absolutely to die for. Not to mention the incredible eggs Benedict. Both dishes are truly top tier culinary creations. You will NOT regret coming here.

The food was amazing. We had scrambled eggs , fried eggs with potatoes and blueberry pancakes. No complaints! Can't wait to visit again. 
Our waitress Charlie aas very friendly and always there when we needed her. Excellent service
Best breakfast place I've ever eaten. French toast is unreal, eggs bene with salmon. Of course you have to get a bagel.
Say yes to the bagels, bacon, and grapefruit. You can't go wrong. Wonderful service as usual. Cool ambiance.

Go for the French Toast. Seriously the best I've ever had. 

Everything else we ate was very mid and you can get better smoked fish and bagels at many places in NYC (at half the price)...but I will be dreaming about that French Toast. 

Service is efficient and it's a fun scene if you like dressing up for brunch.

We came here for the first time on a Sunday morning. Great salmon Benedict and bagel and lox. Their salmons are one of the best in the city. Service was also great and the ambiance is nice. Wish they had an espresso machine though.

I'm not gonna lie, I thought at this place might have been overly hyped because I came across it on TikTok. The bagel tower ended up being my favorite. It was everything I didn't know I wanted. It was so fresh and flavorful. I would go back here just to get their bagel tower. If you get the French toast, it was just so so. I think that the size is great, but because it's so thick, it can be a little mushy in the center. Whenever I'm in Soho on a Saturday, I'm definitely coming back here.

Absolutely 10 out of 10.  Came here for breakfast - note:  be sure to make a reservation - they opened at 9:00 and there was a line when I arrived.

I was seated promptly and I have to admit, the overall decor of the restaurant is very nice.  They even have outdoor seating for those that want to sit outside.

They have a bar area where you can get coffees and mimosas, etc.

I ordered the house smoked salmon on sesame bagel with coffee.  The coffee was nice and strong and I didn't have to wait long for my food.

The salmon with tomatoes and cucumbers are brought out on a tiered tray and the bagel with cream cheese was separate.  The salmon was very good and paired with the tomatoes, capers and cucumbers was amazing.  The bagel wasn't too big which was a good thing for me as they fill me up fast.  They do have other offerings such as eggs and French toast and when I go back again I will try one of them.

Can I take a minute to talk about the service?  It was amazing -my waitress checked me repeatedly and didn't allow my coffee cup or water glass to be empty.

It was a very nice experience and one I wouldn't mind experiencing again.

The food was so amazing! 5 stars for the food-- it came out in a decent amount of time and it was absolutely delicious! The ambiance was great! Nice vibes and the cleanliness of the restaurant was up to par. There was a tiny miscommunication where the waiter forgot to bring out part of our meal but other than that it was a great experience.

This was a good experience. We ordered the whitefish bagel, an order of latkes, and the "Freddy" salad. Our server, I believe, would've been named "Hannah," or something of that ilk. We didn't ask, she just had that vibe. Could've been another name. But she was a good server, I won't speculate any further about her life.

The white fish and the bagel was my favorite. I love smoked salmon, too, but recently I've been enjoying whitefish salad (perhaps even more...?) on a good bagel. I like it at Barney Greengrass, and I also recently had it at that new place Apollo Bagels (good there too.) 

The Freddy salad was g surprisingly good- surprising given how simple it is. I don't even like shrimp that much. Somehow, the artichoke hearts were extra tender. 

The latkes are great, small order, but great. I will advise that the sour cream is sort of buttery and salty, almost like an aioli.
Still mixes well with the applesauce. I'd recommend putting some of your whitefish salad on it, if there's some left after the bagel. 

Even though the individual menu items seem expensive at first glance, we ended up actually full, and only spent like $35 each before tip. That's pretty good. 

I score this experience 84 out of 100

Usually love but not this time. Perhaps the weekend is the worst time to enjoy. 

Bagel tasted like it was toasted and left out for half hour... whitefish had no flavor... latkes... I was felt like I was playing peek-a-boo with the potatoes.... It was all fried batter not potato... a fail.. they were all like that unfortunately.  

Sadelle's! We love you!! Get it together!!!

I was excited to try Sadelle's as I had heard good things about their brunch. I suggest making a reservation if you are going to their weekend brunch. 

We were sat upstairs and had a lovely view overlooking the downstairs part of the restaurant. 

Our table ordered several things not knowing how HUGE their portions are. The matzo ball soup is served in a bowl, not a cup, so keep that in mind when ordering. The tuna melt was delicious. Our table also enjoyed the triple decker sandwich. The star of the show were the veal dumplings. I would go back just for this dish! 

Our waitress was quite lovely and very kind. I would definitely recommend! I can't wait for my next visit!

One of, if not the #1 eating experiences we had while visiting The City.  We ordered the Blueberry Pancakes, The Cobb Salad, the Breakfast Sandwich (not the healthy breakfast sandwich) and the Chicken Sandwich.  We did not order the French Toast or The Tower and that might have been a mistake.  Also, for drinks we ordered the Cucumber Margarita and the Blood Orange Spritz... the Margarita was the winner!

Overall, everything we ordered was top notch! Our server (Jeff) was awesome! 

The only negative would be that there are only two (one person) bathrooms.  The line for the WC can get long and it's right outside the kitchen.  This is not a reason not to try this amazing spot.  We will go back the next time we visit The City.

I'm not a huge breakfast person but I LOVED this! The entire experience was great! The atmosphere was absolutely adorable and the food was delicious as well! I got the smoked salmon bagel and it came out on a tower! It was worth it just for the presentation, let alone the fact that everything it came with was delicious! We also had the salami omelet which was a first for me; I would have never thought to put salami and mustard in an omelet but it worked! This is the perfect spot for a celebration breakfast for a birthday or something!

Leaving review to warn people that a plain lemonade or arnold palmer is 15$ each .... Apparently it's the same button for any non alcoholic drink? Sounded wrong but she wasn't budging. Food is average at best, bagel extremely thin and not New Yorks best. Tuna melt was good and only 3$ more than a lemonade so do with that information what you will!

Got off a plane and went to Sadelle's really early to grab a table. They started turning away people after that so go early or get a reservation. Had to get the salmon stack and two extra bagels and it fed three people. Incredible but everything bagels in New York are crazy salted so warning if you're not used to that as in you but Costco or Trader Joe's everything bagels it will be different when you get them fresh.

Hostess with short black hair and nose piercings was super rude, Monday Oct. 14z wouldn't even let me get a yes or no answer out when asking me a question. Main reason why i'm leaving such a low review.

First asked for my name upon check in however i didn't give my name, just my number( i guess they use resy and i was unaware) and was saying " i didn't leave a name, but my number is..." and was proceeded to be cut off in an angry tone asking for my name again. After she found my name, she asked if outside is okay, and before i could even reply, she said "great!" in the most monotone, off putting-rude tone. I can't even say it's her personality because we heard her talking in a friendly tone to her coworkers. As someone in the industry, I never have wanted to leave a bad review but she left such a sour taste in our mouths at Sadelle's, especially when you are the one who's suppose to greet every customer.. And it didn't happen with just us, she did this with each group she sat.

Our server was nice and helped pick the french toast.

Bagel's are honestly really small though. I understand making profit but when a bagel is half the size of a normal one, for 20 bucks with just 1 egg, bacon and cheese, it's a bit of a rip off.

Walked in without a reservation on a Wednesday morning around 9:45am and was told there would be a 45 minute wait. We put our names down and walked around soho to kill some time. The wait ended up being closer to 70 minutes though. 

We got the sable and eggs Benedict, which both were delicious. The sable was perfectly smoky and paired well with the seasoned tomatoes, cucumbers and capers that came with it. The bagel was tiny. Like very tiny. But honestly, I was pleasantly satiated. The eggs Benedict with salmon was also tasty, but just a tad bit too salty. 

Food and vibes were good overall but I personally don't think it's worth the hype. Definitely recommend booking a reservation because I wouldn't say it's worth the wait at all as a walk in.
Love this place. On of my favorite for a good bagel and lox. The ambiance here is transformative. The food and service is some of the best. Brunch is a must!

Fabulous brunch place with delicious salmon and bagels elevated. There's also eggs, French toast, pancakes etc. everything is delicious and place is fancy. It costs a certain amount but is worth it for a special occasion. Service was good and would definitely recommend. Reservations needed a month in advance.

Came here for the bagel tower. We liked the salmon and it's a pretty good deal to split among 2 people. Also had the orange juice which was a bit steep at $8/glass and would probably skip next time. Service was good.

5 Stars

Sadelle's is a true gem in NYC, and their French toast is absolutely phenomenal! Hands down, the best I've had in the city. Each bite was a perfect balance of crunch on the outside and moist, fluffy perfection on the inside. The flavor was divine--just the right amount of sweetness without being overpowering.

I can't stop thinking about how delicious it was--like a little slice of heaven on a plate. If you're in the city and love French toast, Sadelle's should be at the very top of your list. I'll definitely be back for more!

A tourist trap -- brought to you by the Major Food Group, a chain of eateries that thinks all diners are suckers.

You know they think the customers are dopes when they unabashedly proclaim  on their website  -- without any reviews -- their's is "the best bagel in America".

Don't believe the hype.
 
I live nearby and went in today to do a simple task - buy a single wholewheat bagel to go. Well, they don't sell wholewheat, only sour dough. Weird , but , OK.

The tiny bagel (it weighed 100 gram on my kitchen scale, while most bagels weigh about 150 g.) cost $3.00!! Every other bagel store in NYC maxes out at $2.

But to add insult (or rip-off) to injury, they charge sales tax on the bagel. THAT IS AGAINST THE LAW. There is no sales tax on bread, or a single bagel to go. 

So the price was $3.27. I gave the clerk a $5 bill.

Without saying a word, he disappears to the back of the place and, after 5 minutes, brings the manager up front, who has to scrounge through the tip jar to give me my change = a dollar bill, six dimes, and three pennies - cluttering my pocket with change.

I mean, they couldn't just give 3 quarters = scrounging over pennies on an overpriced,  illegally tax, tiny bagel?

So, lesson is = this is totally unacceptable.

If you are a tourist seeking to be ripped off by this restaurant chain, shop here.

For the savvy, avoid it like you would avoid the other rip-off restaurants from this group, like Torrissi or Carboners. You know any restaurant that has an outlet in Vegas is purely for losers.

Do what we downtown NYers do, avoid this tourist trap.

I
nasty over price - eggs overcooked - don't waste your time so many other good breakfast foods around for half the cost

even for tuesday brunch you should probably make a resy! i was glad i did as there was a line but maybe it was because it was the tuesday before thanksgiving. the food was as good as I was hoping for and service was kind. this was the best lox i can remember tasting - omelette, bagel, cream cheese and drinks were great too. I enjoyed the chives in the cream cheese and sprinkled on top. Definitely a cute and trendy brunch spot and my only wish is that prices were a bit lower for the portions.

i got the sadelle's tower and the french toast. 

we went here at 8am---we put in full effort to get that bagel tower. 

i've heard great things about the french toast at this place, and it did NOT disappoint. it was so so delicious. honestly, probably one of my favorite french toasts i've ever had. the bread was so moist it almost had a donut like consistency, yet the slightest crisp on the outside. it was utterly delicious, especially with the berry compote. 

as for the bagel tower, it was so fun. we all fought over the everything bagels. we did not know it was unlimited bagels however--that somewhat, not close at all, but somewhat explains the $125 bagel tower. i do think $125 is a ridiculous price for this though. it also came with smoked salmon, tomatoes, tuna salad, salmon salad, cucumbers, capers, and other smoked fishes. although it was really fun to make my bagel have all different topping combinations and it was fun to eat, it definitely was overpriced for what it was. honestly the value should be more around $60. especially since i don't think people would eat MORE than two bagels each and eat all of the refilled bagels. oh well, i guess it was worth trying once. 

it had a great NY brunch ambience though, not sure how to describe that but i liked it.

The food was good but the service was terrible. You could tell our server did not give us much thought or care, I'm not sure if it is because of how we dressed or because we were there right when it opened so he was still trying to wake up. Our server half listened to us and our orders, he was in a rush and couldn't seem to be bothered by our table. Going as far as spilling hot coffee from my husbands mug, spilling it on my sister in law when he meant to remove the package of sugar on the table. He also moved my coffee mug back, before proceeding to pour my coffee, to its place it was when I tried moving it closer to him to help him out because the space was small. It took forever to get our bill, our server did not come and check on us to see how things were but a different server did. I had to ask multiple times for a glass of ice before getting one, from again not our server. It was a really disappointing experience for us and needless to say I will not go back nor recommend this to anyone, regardless of how good the food was. The service really spoke volumes about that place.

This is one of the best brunch spots I've been to. Aside from the amazing presentation, the food itself was so good. The bagel and lox were good but the tuna salad spread was even better. We also ordered the French toast. When it came out, I was a little surprised at how basic it looked. After taking a bite, I realized how good it was. Possibly one of the best French toast entrees I've ever tired. Outside was crunchy and inside was fluffy. Definitely the top dish there.
Food overpriced and a tourist trap. Had the French toast was incredibly disappointed. Definitely not worth your money or time

Sadelle's is such a cute iconic tourist spot in NYC. the food is delicious and brunch is just such a vibe here. Service is great but fairly quick since they're trying to seat and get people out quickly. I would recommend making reservations here when you plan to visit since it's always crowded.

A CLASSIC for a reason! Sadelle's is an absolute MUST VISIT when you're in NYC, doesn't matter if you've been before or have never tried, you have to make time in your trip to go. I'd recommend making a reservation beforehand so you don't have to worry about any wait times, and if you're coming straight from the airport like my girlfriends and I did, they let you store your luggage at the side of the restaurant so no worries there ;)

We ordered the bagel tower and french toast, both of which you cannot skip out on! Next time I come back, I'm getting the exact same thing - it's THAT good. For the bagel tower, we ordered 3 Everything bagels with the House Salmon and Whitefish Salad. Insane. Literally speechless. Both were perfectly seasoned and the combination of the House Salmon with the cucumbers, tomatoes, and capers was heavenly. The Whitefish Salad was not too fishy whatsoever and completely blew my mind! I didn't know what to expect, but it was amazing.

For the french toast, also a must order! It's famous for a reason. I'm not even a french toast girlie but theirs is on another level. It's not soggy and texture-less at all, which is why I'm usually not a fan... it's perfectly crunchy on the outside but fluffy and soft on the inside, SO GOOD. And with the syrup, wow, literally you cannot come here without ordering it.

So impressed by the food and super cute interior, and would highly highly recommend coming! I know I'll be bringing friends/family and stopping here each NYC trip I make!!

Came here for brunch with my kids before a show and service was wonderful, the atmosphere was beautiful, we were just left a little uninspired with our meal. Everything was good, don't get me wrong, it just wasn't amazing as I suppose I was hoping for. They did an excellent job accommodating a dairy allergy so that was appreciated. If in the need for some place fun and cute I would recommend this spot.

I arrived early and I was told to leave and come back at the appointed time which I did, however, I got a text 15 minutes early that my table was ready.  While waiting for my friend to arrive, I asked for coffee. The coffee poured to me was in a nice large cup, but was cold. I tried to get someone's attention to replace it for 15 minutes but they were otherwise engaged.  We were seated on the balcony, which is a very tight space and  a very small bistro table.   I ordered a Leo omelette and I asked our waitress the difference between the house cured salmon and the Scottish salmon.  I wanted the least salty of the two.  She didn't know the difference. My friend  told the waiter she had an onion allergy and she didn't want raw onions or any scallions on anything due to a food allergy. She ordered eggs Benedict with salmon and it arrived with chives all over it. She asked them to give her a new one without the chives. She also ordered a bagel instead of brioche with the eggs Benedict  and a side of avocado. When they brought the dish back, the bagel was covered in butter, the cream cheese had scallions in it,, and the side of avocado was covered in oil.  When she told the waiter that she didn't want butter on her bagel or oil on her avocado , he said there's no butter on there. She asked for some paper towels, and there were at least seven or eight paper towels that she was able to wipe the butter off with that were just drenched. no attempt was made to replace the avocado, or the bagel which was covered in oil and butter. Before we closed out our check, we asked for three sesame bagels to go. The waiter brought us a box and said I brought you half a dozen to make up for the error we made on your allergy and I gave you three sesame and three everything bagels (which have onions that she's allergic to) .The staff doesn't seem to understand food allergies or how the food is served on the menu so if you have a food allergy, perhaps don't go to this restaurant as the staff can't absorb what it means to be allergic to something and isn't clear about what's in the dishes .  I explained to the waiter that  anything allium affects her. The fact that the everything bagels have onion and touched the sesame bagels means she can't have it. They brought out another order of her sesame bagels. I handled the check and nothing was done on the check to make up for all these errors, although the manager did come to our table and apologized profusely.  I left a 20% tip anyway because I feel for people who have to make their living waiting tables however they did nothing to deserve this even lying to her saying there's no butter on the bagel or oil on the avocado. All the talk of the manager did nothing too although she was very nice. We asked to see a dessert menu and they just brought the regular menu and said dessert here is French toast, pancakes, or cheese blintzes. I had heard about their Babka, but they no longer serve that.  We left and went to Dominique Ansel for dessert although we would've liked to sit down somewhere.

Amazing house salmon bagel platter! We ordered the whitefish salad and house salmon platter- the whitefish salad was decent, but the house salmon stole the show with its delicious flavor and perfectly thin slices. Service was excellent, making the experience even better

My recent visit to Sadelle's for a Saturday brunch was nothing short of exceptional. From the moment I walked in, I was welcomed by the warm and inviting atmosphere, with the lively energy of the restaurant making it the perfect spot to start the weekend. I decided to try the Challah French Toast, and it was absolute perfection--each bite was wonderfully fluffy, with just the right amount of sweetness and a beautifully caramelized exterior. The flavors were rich and comforting, making it one of the best French toasts I've ever had. The service was equally impressive; the staff was incredibly attentive, ensuring that our drinks were always topped up and that we had everything we needed for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. Whether you're looking for a cozy brunch with friends, a special breakfast treat, or just a fantastic way to begin your weekend, Sadelle's delivers an experience that is both delicious and memorable. I can't wait to return!

I came here for the Bagel Tower, and it did not disappoint! Not only was the Tower an experience, but the pairings were delightful! The tower comes with dill, tomatoes, cucumber slices, and regular whipped cream cheese. Each protein you order will include 1 bagel but you could always order another one the side if you're sharing. The salmon serving was enough for 2 people to share.

Decided to try Sadelle's after reading great reviews and hearing about it on a celebrity gossip blog (apparently it's frequented by celebs in NY). I arrived 10 minutes just after they opened, as I wanted to make the most of my day and time in NYC, and I was surprised to find the restaurant almost half full already. I did not have a reservation but was happy to be seated quickly and attended to very well. The service was extremely attentive and professional and I knew from reviewing the menu I wanted the Leo omelette. And it was amazing! Simple with obviously eggs, caramelized onions, salmon and creme fraiche on top. Not too oniony or fishy with the salmon, just a good balance of flavors all around and a great breakfast to start my day. I had a side of rye toast with jam and butter but should have ordered the challah instead (just preference, the bread was fine) coffee and a mimosa that really didn't give me the buzz I wanted but the meal made up for it! 

I will add that the restaurant was extremely warm! I get it, it's winter and cold and rainy outside, but it was almost unbearable inside but I was too embarrassed to mention that to the waiters. From where I was sitting, I was placed closely in between two groups of people and didn't want to be that person complaining but idk if that's normal for the heat to be cranked up so high for a restaurant already small and practically full of people? Just a thought but glad I got to dine at Sadelle's and would recommend it as a great place to dine at.

The French toast still can't be beat and neither can the latke royale although the atmosphere continually gets worse.  This time we were shoved into a corner so that the person on the bench seat (me) was walled off by the wine cooler. The poor guy (separate party) next to me basically was in the person next to HIM (another separate party) lap to give me enough space to use utensils. Ugh, but I just can't give up the best French toast in town so it is what it is lol.

Although it was the most expensive breakfast I've ever had, it was worth it. The food items are wonderful, and we got to watch a true artist--the salmon slicer--preparing the most thinly slices lox in NYC.

The sole purpose of this review is because I miss New York. I miss my bestfriend, I miss Sadelle's. My best friend and I have eaten there several  times & every time it smacks !!! All the workers are super friendly. I look forward to my trip to NY this summer & eating at Sadelle's
Great food and drinks. Big portions. Attentive service. Ok prices for NYC. Only downside is a far too strong air conditioning, creating an unpleasant draft. Reservation needed.
The bagel flight was incredible. I got the smoked salmon with an onion bagel and yum yum yum! Definitely make a reservation cause it was busy!

Well worth the hype! exceptional service and quality. the interior is charming, and gives off an industrial cozy theme. and the food was rich and flavorful. mimosas were made with FRESH squeezed orange juice! the star of the show was the french toast. was decadent, thick, crispy and a creamy interior. also served with a berry compote. cannot wait to come back!

Like anyone and everyone else, I'm familiar with Sadelle's through social media and we decided to stop by during the weekend for brunch. It is certainly an aesthetic, IG friendly spot however will caution that it's hard to secure a reservation at a "normal" time i.e. 10AM/11AM. While fans of Apollo Bagels/Russ & Daughters, we ordered the below:

Sadelle's Tower
French Toast
Sadelle's Spritz
Bellini

The service was a bit lacking as it was initially hard to flag someone down to order, the bagels tasted and felt very store bought. I'd recommend dining here one time for the one time, but I truly don't get the hype.

I love this place--the vibe, the Instagram hype--it's all real! It's like if Ralph Lauren and a Jewish baker teamed up to create the perfect bagel shop, and the result is Sadelle's. The best part? Everything. From the atmosphere to the food, it's a must-visit!
Great food and presentation! The only thing I did not like was the trout roe. Tasted like rubber balls. Salmon roe is much better.
Very mediocre food (pancakes were dry, nothing was amazing), pretty long wait, pretty expensive, service was good
If you are in New York, you must try this place! The French toast is to die for, but the bagel and lox platters are incredible.

Amazing service , food and drinks! Must visit breakfast spot in NYC. We ordered for the drinks - Mimosas, was perfect with fresh juice. For breakfast we choose fresh salmon with everything bagel - it was super delicious! Highly recommended! Cheese pancakes, dumplings and eggs benny was good also too.

It's a beautiful place, crowded when we visited on a weekday at 1:30. We were looking for a great bagel place and made a reservation here after reading a recommendation. This was not the bagel/deli we had in mind--they make bagels but only a few kinds (flavors weren't even listed on the menu and only two kinds of cream cheese). Lots of beautiful lox and caviar towers, fancier than we expected (and more pretentious).

I got tea instead of coffee, and the hot water arrived in the mug, not in a teapot. I had to ask for a teaspoon.
My son ordered the French toast, which I thought was amazing but he considered the middle too wet and undercooked.
If you want a fancy lunch spot, this might be your place. We won't be back.
